    total_distinct_properties   38,365
    placeholder_excluded         4,245   DEFEASED, VARIOUS, -, N/A, NA, UNKNOWN
    geocodable_denominator      34,120
    geocoded                    33,219
    COVERAGE                    97.36%   of geocodable

THE REAL REMAINING GAP IS ABOUT 901 PROPERTIES, NOT ~24,700.

WHY THE FIGURES DIVERGE. The 51% number counts a denominator that includes addresses which
CAN NEVER GEOCODE -- defeased and placeholder entries whose address field is blank or
literal "VARIOUS". Excluding them is not generosity; it is the same denominator definition
br-1ni6's geo_coverage_pct uses, pinned to the same normalization macros so the two cannot
drift. A coverage rate computed over ungeocodable rows is not a coverage rate.
The 50,593 row count is also a different grain from 38,365 distinct properties, so the two
statements were never comparable to begin with.

WHAT THIS CHANGES IN THIS BEAD AND ACROSS THE EPIC:
1. GEOCODE COVERAGE IS NOT THE BINDING CONSTRAINT ON THE PROPERTY BOOK. I described it as a
   ceiling that "binds before canon geo does any work." At 97.36% of geocodable it does not.
   Strike that framing wherever it appears.
2. WHAT REMAINS A REAL LIMIT, UNCHANGED:
   - `Various` addresses genuinely never geocoded, and there are 4,245 placeholder identities.
     They still need the Annex A parse (edgar-elt br-6iii), not geometry, and they are still
     excluded-and-counted per OC-0048's denominator-honesty criterion.
   - Ginnie Mae still has no address field at its native pool grain.
   - The AGENCY tables are a separate and much larger population that is genuinely NOT
     geocoded yet -- cmdrvl-curves bd-25xz covers roughly 90,000 records (15,579 Ginnie
     street addresses plus 74,349 HUD FHA multifamily at city/state/zip). THAT is the real
     coverage gap for the agency corpora, and it is ON HOLD (bd-13mx).
3. bd-14hu's argument IMPROVES. Pre-resolving our own corpora looked weaker when half the
   property book appeared ungeocoded. At 97.36% the CMBS side is effectively ready to
   pre-resolve now, and the work concentrates on the agency tables rather than on backfill.

MEASURED GEOCODE HISTORY, for anyone sizing this work (2026-08-14, literal query):
WRGL_EDGAR_CMBS_GEOCODES__STRUCTURED -- 68,603 rows, 54,690 distinct PROPERTY_ADDRESS,
4,149 addresses appearing under more than one ASOF because the ETL appends rather than
upserts. Dominated by the 2025-01 initial load (45,114 rows) and an unexplained 2026-08
batch (14,714 rows / 14,242 distinct).

PROCESS NOTE: this is the fourth claim this session that came from prose rather than a
measured value, and the third that was wrong. The 51% figure was in a document I trusted;
the 97.36% figure was in a bead comment recording an actual query. WHEN TWO NUMBERS
DISAGREE, PREFER THE ONE WITH A RECORDED METHOD AND A DENOMINATOR DEFINITION.

title: [CANON-V1/P07.R6b] Score record-link evidence and align assignments through native link
description:
## Background
R6 needs structured evidence at source-record grain, then issuer resolution and assignment alignment as distinct outcomes. Surface-pair scoring alone collapses same-name assignments and cannot consume canon.evidence.v1 RecordLink targets.

## Technical Approach
Consume canon.entity.record_link_input.v1 sidecars in the native v1 block/evidence/run/link chain. Generate bounded cross-source record candidates inside declared scope, apply deterministic numeric/date/categorical primitives, emit hash-bound canon.evidence.v1 RecordLink records and a separate assignment-alignment sidecar, and aggregate only policy-approved evidence to issuer-pair support. Enforce one-to-one or declared-cardinality alignment with explicit tie/duplicate abstention. Profile cannot-link evidence must be emitted on the production path and hard veto must dominate every support score. Relation/context and crosswalk fields remain non-authoritative.

## Success Criteria
- Independent structured fields can carry an otherwise below-threshold issuer-name pair.
- Multiple assignments for one issuer align record-to-record without minting extra issuer identities.
- Ties, duplicate attributes, missingness, scale mismatch, and hard negatives abstain deterministically.
- Hard cannot-link is emitted in production and vetoes structured support.
- Public v1 artifacts bind record-input, candidate, evidence, assignment-alignment, profile, strategy, and upstream hashes.
- Shuffled inputs produce byte-identical public artifact bytes; no public command reads or writes legacy v0 entity artifacts.
- No assignment/crosswalk field becomes an alias or canonical identity.

## Test Plan
Run a neutral two-source multi-assignment fixture through public subprocess block, evidence, solve/run, and link. Include below-threshold names rescued by structured agreement, duplicate/tie abstention, near miss, unit mismatch, hard cannot-link, relation-only control, shuffled repeats, stale/tampered sidecars, budgets, and no-partial-write assertions.

- src/entity/run.rs

title: [CANON-V1/P04.2] Capture unresolved and ambiguous outcomes from every public workflow
description:
## Background
An inbox only compounds if all operator paths feed it consistently. Exact lookup, entity clustering, entity linkage, provider materialization, apply, and project runs currently expose different failure shapes.

## Technical Approach
Create one outcome-to-inbox mapping layer and integrate it with exact mapping artifacts, entity v1 artifacts, review results, provider conflicts, and project receipts. Capture is explicit in plan/manifest policy, writes atomically to an owned path, and records source artifact hashes. Refused commands and invalid inputs do not create misleading unresolved events.

## Success Criteria
- All supported unresolved, ambiguous, contradictory, review-deferred, and no-rule outcomes have stable inbox reason codes.
- Replaying the same artifact is idempotent; merging independent shards is commutative and deterministic.
- Read-only mode can emit inbox data to stdout or an explicit output but never mutates ambient state.
- Exact resolved rows and security/policy refusals are not misclassified as missing registry coverage.

## Test Plan
Exercise every producer with frozen artifacts, duplicate replay, concurrent shard capture, interruption, read-only mode, and malformed upstream references. Compare inbox bytes and event counts.

## RESERVATIONS
- `src/inbox/capture.rs`
- `src/lib.rs`
- `src/entity/output.rs`
- `tests/inbox_capture.rs`

## Considerations
Do not make ambient inbox state mandatory. Projects should own or explicitly reference the accumulating artifact.

title: Property-based invariant tests
description:
Write property-based tests in tests/properties.rs using proptest. Generate random registries and random inputs, then verify canon's five core invariants hold universally.

TARGET FILE: tests/properties.rs only.

=== GENERATORS ===

Registry generator (arb_registry):
- Generate 1-100 mapping entries with random input strings (ASCII printable, 1-20 chars), random canonical_id, canonical_type from fixed set (ticker/isin/lei/counterparty_id), rule_id from fixed set
- Write to a tempdir as valid registry: registry.json + one or more mapping files
- Sometimes generate duplicate input values across files (tests first-match-wins)
- Sometimes generate empty registry (zero entries)

Input generator (arb_csv_input):
- Generate CSV with 1-500 rows, header always includes the target column
- Column values drawn from: registry inputs (will resolve), random strings (won't resolve), empty strings, mix
- Sometimes include blank rows (all fields empty)
- Delimiter: randomly comma, tab, or pipe

Input generator (arb_jsonl_input):
- Generate JSONL with 1-500 lines
- Field values drawn from: registry inputs, random strings, null, missing field, nested objects/arrays, numbers, booleans
- Tests all five special reason paths

=== INVARIANTS (verified for every generated case) ===

1. COMPLETENESS: summary.total == summary.resolved + summary.unresolved
   Parse JSON output, check arithmetic identity.

2. DETERMINISM: run canon twice with identical input + registry, outputs are byte-identical.
   Run binary twice, compare stdout bytes.

3. PARTITION: every unique input value appears in exactly one of mappings[] or unresolved[], never both, never missing.
   Collect all inputs from mappings + unresolved, verify it's a partition of the unique input values.

4. TRACEABILITY: every mappings[].rule_id + mappings[].input references a real entry in the registry.
   Load the registry files, verify each mapping's input/rule_id pair exists as an entry.

5. CROSS-MODE CONSISTENCY: for CSV input, run both --emit json and --emit csv on the same input+registry. Verify:
   - Each resolved row's canonical column value matches the corresponding mappings[].canonical_id (after stripping u8: prefix)
   - Each unresolved row's canonical column is empty
   - Row count in CSV output matches input row count

=== TEST STRUCTURE ===

proptest! {
    #[test]
    fn invariant_completeness(reg in arb_registry(), input in arb_csv_input()) { ... }

    #[test]
    fn invariant_determinism(reg in arb_registry(), input in arb_csv_input()) { ... }

    #[test]
    fn invariant_partition(reg in arb_registry(), input in arb_csv_input()) { ... }

    #[test]
    fn invariant_traceability(reg in arb_registry(), input in arb_csv_input()) { ... }

    #[test]
    fn invariant_cross_mode(reg in arb_registry(), input in arb_csv_input()) { ... }

    #[test]
    fn invariant_jsonl_completeness(reg in arb_registry(), input in arb_jsonl_input()) { ... }

    #[test]
    fn invariant_jsonl_partition(reg in arb_registry(), input in arb_jsonl_input()) { ... }
}

=== PROPTEST CONFIG ===

Use ProptestConfig with cases=512 for CI (fast), PROPTEST_CASES env var for exhaustive local runs. Persist regressions to tests/proptest-regressions/ (tracked in git, NOT gitignored).

VERIFICATION: cargo test --test properties -- --test-threads=1
acceptance_criteria:
All tests in tests/properties.rs pass with ProptestConfig { cases: 512 }.
7 property tests: invariant_completeness (CSV), invariant_determinism (CSV), invariant_partition (CSV), invariant_traceability (CSV), invariant_cross_mode (CSV), invariant_jsonl_completeness, invariant_jsonl_partition.
Generators: arb_registry (0-100 entries, valid registry dir), arb_csv_input (1-500 rows, mixed resolve/unresolve/empty/blank), arb_jsonl_input (1-500 lines, all special reasons).
proptest-regressions/ tracked in git.
VERIFICATION: cargo test --test properties -- --test-threads=1
notes: Config: use ProptestConfig { cases: 512, .. } for CI. Set PROPTEST_CASES=2048 for thorough local runs. IMPORTANT: proptest-regressions/ directory MUST be tracked in git (NOT gitignored) — regression files are permanent test cases that prevent known-bad inputs from recurring. Add tests/proptest-regressions/.gitkeep.

title: canon geo: address parse forest — regular-grammar query-side parsing, all readings held as a domain, tested as PAD membership
description:
The query-side half of address matching, per section 7.1 and section 16.3 row 2. PAD (landed, verified) is the LOT-side reference: every legal address per lot, normalized, range/parity encoded. This bead is the QUERY side: parse messy CMBS address strings into ALL candidate readings via a declared, versioned token grammar (regular/DFA — deterministic, no CRF/libpostal), hold the readings alive as a domain, and test each as (a) PAD address-set membership and (b) tile-constraint compatibility. Wrong readings die by evidence, not by a parser's single choice.

WHAT THE GRAMMAR MUST COVER (from worked receipts): multi-address enumerations ('199, 201, 203, 205 First Avenue and 349 & 351 East 12th Street' — Case 4), slash/dash ranges ('241/249 West 74th Street', '107-109-111 North 9th'), Queens hyphenates as literals ('130-50 146 Street'), corner a/k/a alternation ('66 Crosby Street a/k/a 514 Broadway' — Case 5), directional/suffix/ordinal token equivalences (Appendix E normalizer as token classes), placeholder detection ('Various' etc.).
CHIMERA REJECTION IS THE POINT: a parsed reading asserted by NO source member (Case 4's synthesized '199 E 12th St') must be rejectable by membership — single-parse normalizers structurally cannot do this.

SIZING INPUT: bd-3ujr/bd-3sot's PAD rounds use simple range/parity/hyphenate predicates; their UNRESOLVED residual (keys that fail on parse complexity rather than absent addresses) is this bead's justified population — take the measured residual from those reports as the acceptance corpus. Also take the six Appendix I case addresses as mandatory fixtures (the corpus was built for this).
BOUNDARY: deterministic versioned grammar per canon doctrine; parse forest lives at evidence-admission (rho) level; no statistical components in the decision path (section 7.1). Consumers: bd-1zph address operators, bd-1a12 refutation (asserted-street extraction), section 16.3 row 2.

title: canon geo: choose the geometry dependency and prove exact predicates
description:
DECISION + SPIKE. Gates all downstream geo code, so it goes first.

TWO QUESTIONS:
1. Does the geometry dependency live in canon CORE, or in an out-of-tree
   extension? IDENTITY_ARCHITECTURE.md keeps domain expertise out of core
   (registries, profiles, strategies, extensions). Geometry is arguably domain
   machinery rather than domain knowledge -- decide deliberately and record the
   reasoning, because it sets the precedent for every future typed value.
2. Which library, judged on EXACT PREDICATES rather than features.

HARD REQUIREMENT -- EXACT GEOMETRIC PREDICATES.
Naive floating-point point-in-polygon is NON-DETERMINISTIC precisely on
boundary-adjacent points, and boundary-adjacent points are the entire
population canon geo cares about. Determinism is canon's core promise -- same
input and same tile digest must reproduce the same answer across platforms and
runs, forever. Adaptive-precision orientation/incircle predicates
(Shewchuk-style) are the bar.

EXIT CRITERIA:
- A written decision on core vs extension with reasoning.
- A chosen library with exact-predicate support demonstrated, not assumed.
- A property test proving identical PIP results for points ON and adjacent to
  polygon edges, across at least two platforms.
- A documented refusal path for invalid geometry (self-intersecting rings,
  unclosed polygons, mixed CRS) -- refuse rather than guess, per canon doctrine.

Parent: bd-2kjx
close_reason: Implemented and documented the exact tile-local integer predicate kernel; invalid rings and overflow refuse; Ubuntu/macOS boundary suites and full CI passed in run 33195783086. Projection admission and clipping remain in their named downstream beads.

comments.author: Zac
comments.text:
REALITY CHECK 2026-08-14 — QUESTION 1 IS A FALSE BINARY TODAY. DECIDE CORE.

THE FINDING: there is no extension runtime to choose. src/extensions/ is 12,346 LOC and
is NOT declared in src/lib.rs. Verified: the only thing that compiles it is
tests/domain_neutrality.rs via `#[path = "../src/extensions/mod.rs"]`. It is a set of
contract types with tests, entirely disconnected from the running binary. No CLI command
executes any of it.

So "core vs out-of-tree extension" as posed cannot be answered on the merits — choosing
extension means BUILDING THE EXTENSION HOST FIRST, which no bead scopes and which would
gate the entire epic behind an unrelated platform project.

THREE INDEPENDENT ARGUMENTS FOR CORE, RECORD THEM AS THE REASONING THIS BEAD ASKS FOR:

1. PRECEDENT. Core is already not domain-free. src/entity/profile.rs:833-851 ships
   strip_tenant_noise, strip_regab_noise, tenant_brand_fingerprint,
   drop_tenant_stopwords, expand_na_abbreviation, firm_core. The doctrine in
   IDENTITY_ARCHITECTURE.md is already breached in practice. Geometry is *machinery*
   (a typed value plus predicates over it), which is a weaker claim on the boundary than
   the domain *knowledge* the doctrine actually targets.

2. BYOP MAKES IT DECISIVE (operator decision 2026-08-14, see bd-2kjx). The client runs
   canon LOCALLY against their own licensed parcel layer. An out-of-tree extension means
   they install two artifacts and we cannot guarantee the predicate implementation that
   determinism depends on. Determinism is the product promise; do not put it behind a
   dependency the client assembles.

3. THE DOMAIN-NEUTRALITY GATE STILL BINDS, AND IS CHEAP TO SATISFY.
   src/extensions/mod.rs FORBIDDEN_EXTENSION_RUNTIME_TERMS lists cmbs/loan/servicer/
   collateral/cusip etc. `parcel`, `building`, `bbl`, `apn` are NOT on that list and
   MUST NOT BE ADDED — geometry primitives are neutral. What must stay out of core is
   the DOMAIN VOCABULARY (BBL semantics, condo parent/unit rules, Queens grid
   conventions), which belongs in profiles and strategies. Write the decision doc so it
   draws that line explicitly: PREDICATES IN CORE, CONVENTIONS IN PROFILES.

QUESTION 2 — LIBRARY, JUDGED ON EXACT PREDICATES:

  robust  (crate)  Shewchuk adaptive-precision orientation/incircle. This is the bar
                   this bead sets, implemented directly. Pure Rust, no C.
  geo     (crate)  builds on `robust` via its Kernel abstraction; gives you the
                   algorithm surface (contains, intersects, area) over exact kernels.
  h3o     (crate)  pure-Rust H3 port. No C bindings, deterministic. Confirms the
                   operator decision that client-layer H3 indexing lives in canon.
                   NOTE bd-2b9d: do NOT use Snowflake H3 helpers for anything a
                   decision depends on — they returned malformed boundaries and a bad
                   k-ring (edgar-elt br-2wir).

REQUIRED ADDITION — FILTERED PREDICATES, NOT NAIVE EXACT.
Running adaptive-precision predicates on every candidate pair is affordable at ~167
nodes/tile but not at national tile counts. Implement the standard two-stage cascade:
floating-point evaluation WITH AN ERROR BOUND, and fall through to the exact predicate
only when the filter is inconclusive. This is how CGAL achieves exactness at speed. The
filter must be provably conservative — a filter that returns a wrong definite answer is
a determinism bug, not an optimization.

REQUIRED ADDITION — THE PREDICATE REGIME IS PART OF THIS DECISION.
See the new predicate-regime reconciliation bead. In short: MapPLUTO was reprojected
EPSG:2263 -> WGS84, the bd-bmee baseline was computed with Snowflake ST_CONTAINS on
GEOGRAPHY (spherical), and canon will compute planar exact predicates on WGS84 degrees.
Three regimes. Determinism of canon's predicate does NOT imply agreement with the
baseline, and disagreement concentrates on boundary-adjacent points — the entire
population of interest. This bead must declare WHICH REGIME IS CANONICAL and record why.

EXIT CRITERIA — AMENDED:
- Written decision: CORE, with the predicates-in-core / conventions-in-profiles line
  drawn explicitly and the three arguments above recorded.
- Chosen crates with exact-predicate support DEMONSTRATED, not assumed.
- Property test: identical PIP results for points ON and adjacent to polygon edges,
  across at least two platforms (CI matrix: linux-x86_64 + macos-aarch64).
- A conservative floating-point filter with a proven error bound, plus a test that the
  filter never returns a definite answer that disagrees with the exact predicate.
- Documented refusal path for invalid geometry: self-intersecting rings, unclosed
  polygons, mixed CRS, antimeridian crossing, NaN/Inf coordinates, and empty geometry.
  Refuse rather than guess.
- A declared canonical predicate regime, with the reprojection provenance recorded.

comments.author: Zac
comments.text:
DESIGN RESULT NOT PREVIOUSLY WRITTEN TO THIS BEAD 2026-08-14 — A TILE-LOCAL METRIC FRAME
WITH INTEGER COORDINATES MAKES EXACT PREDICATES FREE, AND DEMOTES SHEWCHUK FROM HARD
REQUIREMENT TO FALLBACK.

It was reasoned through in the design session and only landed on bd-16r1 (canonical
coordinate encoding). It belongs here too, because it changes what this bead has to choose.

== STEP 1: PROJECT ONCE PER TILE INTO A LOCAL METRIC CRS ==
An r9 cell plus k-ring 1 is ~1 km across. Over that extent a local transverse-Mercator or
azimuthal projection centred on the tile has SUB-MILLIMETRE distortion. So the projection
choice, which is fraught at continental scale, IS FREE AT TILE SCALE. Project every source
into a tile-local metric CRS at tile build, pin the parameters in the tile artifact, and
content-address the POST-PROJECTION coordinates.

THIS ALSO FIXES A BUG NOBODY FLAGGED. Planar predicates on WGS84 DEGREES are fine for
point-in-polygon, which is topological, and WRONG for anything metric. At 40 degrees north a
degree of longitude is ~85 km against ~111 km for latitude, so distance_lt, area_ratio and
iou_gt are anisotropically wrong by roughly 1.3x in x. In a tile-local metric frame they are
simply correct.

== STEP 2: QUANTIZE TO FIXED-POINT MILLIMETRES. EXACTNESS FOLLOWS. ==
  tile extent ~1 km at 1 mm precision  ->  ~2^20 units, call it 21 bits with margin
  orientation test = 2x2 determinant of coordinate differences
      differences <= 2^21 | products <= 2^42 | determinant <= 2^43
  THAT FITS IN i64 WITH TWENTY BITS TO SPARE.
So orientation, point-in-polygon, segment intersection and polygon area (shoelace gives
exact 2*area as an integer) are ALL EXACT INTEGER ARITHMETIC. No floats anywhere in the
decision path, and no adaptive-precision machinery required -- exactness comes from the
coordinates being integers and the tile bounding their magnitude.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS BEAD'S EXIT CRITERIA: the `robust` crate (Shewchuk adaptive precision)
stops being the hard requirement this bead currently states and becomes the FALLBACK for
anything that escapes the integer frame. That is a real simplification, and it composes
exactly with bd-16r1's fixed-point recommendation -- in a local metric frame, integer
millimetres is the obvious canonical encoding and content-addressing becomes trivially
stable.

== ONE HONEST CAVEAT: POLYGON INTERSECTION IS NOT CLOSED OVER INTEGERS ==
Clipping two integer polygons creates new vertices at edge crossings, and those are RATIONAL,
not integer. So exact IoU needs either i128 rational arithmetic for the intersection area, or
an interval approach: bracket the IoU with integer bounds and ABSTAIN when the bracket
straddles the threshold.
RECOMMEND THE BRACKET-AND-ABSTAIN OPTION. An inconclusive predicate becoming an abstention
rather than a guess is canon's doctrine applied one level down, and it avoids dragging
rational arithmetic through the whole evidence path for one operator.

== AND THE REPROJECTION ITSELF IS PROVENANCE, NOT DECISION ==
The projection step is float and lossy. It happens ONCE, at tile build, is recorded with
library and version, and the INTEGER RESULT is what gets content-addressed. Replay never
re-projects. That keeps the lossy step out of the reproducibility surface entirely.

NOTE: MapPLUTO already carries GEOM_CRS and SOURCE_GEOM_CRS as projected columns, so the
EPSG:2263 -> WGS84 provenance this reasoning depends on is documented in the table rather
than needing archaeology.

comments.text:
ARCHITECTURE SUPERSEDED 2026-08-15 — see docs/PLAN_CANON_GEO.md.

An adversarial multi-model design session produced a materially different architecture,
which then survived a red team that destroyed two intermediate designs. The tile is modelled
as a BOUNDED UNIVERSE and every piece of evidence is a CONSTRAINT; propagation runs to a
fixpoint; the residual model set IS the answer. There is no proposer channel.

THE THREE PROPERTIES THAT MATTER:

  Cousot & Cousot 1977; Apt 1999), so determinism is a theorem rather than an engineering
  effort.
- MONOTONICITY. Constraints only add and domains only shrink, so a tile resolved with four
  sources today and six next year yields a TIGHTER residual, never a contradicting one. The
  earlier answer was never wrong, only less resolved.
- STRUCTURAL ABSTENTION. The residual model set is the answer. No threshold anywhere.

THE KEY DESIGN RULE IS rho, THE SOUNDNESS DISCIPLINE. Every source attribute enters the
solver only through a declared versioned relaxation mapping it to the WEAKEST constraint the
source can actually support. An interpolated geocode becomes a 150m disc rather than a
location. A parcel ADDRESS becomes "one of this lot's addresses" rather than functional
equality. OWNERNAME equal PERMITS an assemblage; OWNERNAME different constrains NOTHING.
Every noisy channel is admitted only in its sound direction — which is what dissolved the
proposer dilemma that broke the two earlier designs.

AND THE COMMERCIAL CONSEQUENCE: if every rho is sound, the true assignment is in the model
set, so AN EMPTY MODEL SET IS A PROOF that a named source violated its own published error
model — attributable, falsifiable, and mailable to the vendor.

title: [CANON-V1/P04] Unresolved inbox, impact analysis, and compounding review flywheel
description:
## Background
Canon emits honest unresolved results, but usage does not yet automatically become organized future registry knowledge. The product becomes genuinely accretive when unresolved evidence is safely accumulated, deduplicated, prioritized, reviewed once, promoted, and replayed across all affected data.

## Scope
Define a privacy-aware canonization inbox; ingest mapping and workbench artifacts; group repeated surfaces and ambiguities; rank review by blast radius, false-merge risk, reuse value, and coverage gain; simulate registry changes before mutation; provide machine and offline human review outputs; measure coverage and drift.

## Success Criteria
Repeated unresolved inputs converge into a stable queue. Operators can see why an item matters, what a decision changes, and how many rows/deals/datasets benefit. A reviewed promotion measurably reduces future unresolved coverage without silently widening identity semantics.

## Test Plan
Cross-run dedupe, redaction/retention, ranking determinism, impact simulation, stale queue refusal, review round trips, and a full ingest -> review -> promote -> replay flywheel E2E.
notes:
## Core review-flywheel boundary
P04 owns transport-neutral review packets, deterministic import, append-only decisions, conflict handling, replay, and promotion policy. It does not own email delivery, a UI, ticketing, active-learning selection, or another review transport. Those can layer on later without changing the core authority contract.

title: canon geo: geometry as a typed value — canonical encoding, normalization, refusals, size budget
description:
BLOCKS EVERY SPATIAL OPERATOR. FOUND BY REALITY CHECK 2026-08-14.

THE FINDING: geometry is not a value type anywhere in canon's evidence model, and nothing
in the epic scoped adding one. bd-15ba chooses a geometry LIBRARY; that is a different
question from how a polygon travels through prepare -> index -> block -> evidence ->
solve -> review -> artifact.

VERIFIED CURRENT STATE:
  src/entity/record_link.rs:153  RecordLinkFeatureKind = Numeric | Date | Categorical
  src/entity/record_link.rs:161  RecordLinkFeatureValue = Numeric{units,scaled_value,scale}
                                 | Date{value} | Categorical{value}
  src/entity/profile.rs:833      SUPPORTED_NORMALIZE_OPS — 19 entries, all string ops
  src/entity/score.rs            ScoreUnits(u32), ENTITY_SCORE_SCALE = 10_000 — the
                                 artifact boundary is integer, deliberately
There is no geometry variant, no coordinate type, and no normalization op that could
produce one.

WHY THE INTEGER BOUNDARY MAKES THIS SUBTLE AND IMPORTANT: canon's promise is that
"metric implementations may use floats internally, but this module is the artifact
boundary: thresholds, ordering, review output, and solver-visible values use only integer
units." Geometry is the first value type where the INPUT ITSELF is floating point.
That means the boundary must be drawn one level earlier than it is for strings: not just
the SCORE must be integer-quantized, but the COORDINATE REPRESENTATION must be canonical,
or two artifacts describing the same polygon will hash differently and content addressing
breaks.

TASK:
1. CANONICAL COORDINATE REPRESENTATION. Decide and specify how a coordinate is stored in
   an artifact such that it round-trips byte-identically. Options: fixed-point integers at
   a declared scale (e.g. 1e-9 degrees), or a canonical decimal string form with a fixed
   number of significant digits, or the source bytes retained verbatim with a separate
   computed form. RECOMMEND FIXED-POINT INTEGERS AT A DECLARED SCALE: it makes hashing,
   ordering, and equality trivially deterministic, it composes with ScoreUnits' existing
   integer discipline, and it makes the exact predicates of bd-15ba cheaper because
   adaptive-precision arithmetic over integers is simpler than over floats. MEASURE the
   precision loss against parcel-scale distances before adopting.
2. THE TYPED VALUE. Add a geometry variant to the feature/evidence value model —
   Point, Polygon, MultiPolygon — carrying CRS, the canonical coordinate encoding, a
   vertex count, and a bounding box. Bounding box is not redundant: it is the conservative
   filter stage bd-15ba requires.
3. CANONICAL GEOMETRY NORMALIZATION. Two polygons describing the same shape must produce
   the same bytes. Specify: ring orientation (exterior CCW, interior CW), starting vertex
   (lexicographically smallest), duplicate-vertex removal, closure convention (is the
   final vertex repeated), and ring ordering within a multipolygon. Without this, content
   addressing is a lottery. This is a NORMALIZATION OPERATOR in the geo profile's own
   vocabulary, parallel to entity's string normalizers.
4. REFUSAL SURFACE. Self-intersecting rings, unclosed rings, mixed CRS within one source,
   antimeridian crossing, NaN/Inf coordinates, empty geometry, and vertex counts above a
   declared budget. Refuse rather than repair — a silently repaired polygon is a decision
   canon did not disclose.
5. SIZE BUDGET. A single Manhattan superblock lot can carry thousands of vertices, and
   bd-101v requires DECISION-FIDELITY geometry retained for EVERY candidate including
   losers. Specify a per-tile geometry byte budget in the same shape as the existing
   candidate budget (src/entity/budget.rs), with refusal rather than silent truncation.
   Note the interaction with bd-1uld: display simplification is DERIVED and LABELLED, and
   must never be substituted for decision geometry.

DEPENDENCIES AND ORDER: this bead needs bd-15ba's library decision and the canonical
predicate regime decision to be in flight, but it should NOT wait for them to complete —
the representation question is largely independent of which crate computes the predicate,
and it blocks bd-gs6n which is on the critical path.

EXIT CRITERIA:
- Specified canonical coordinate encoding with measured precision loss at parcel scale
- Geometry variant added to the feature/evidence value model, with CRS and bbox
- Canonical geometry normalization specified and implemented as a geo normalization
  operator, with a property test: two encodings of the same shape hash identically
- Full refusal surface implemented with typed codes
- Per-tile geometry byte budget with refusal, wired to the existing budget machinery
- A negative test that a self-intersecting ring is refused rather than repaired

title: canon geo: address-independent ground truth via ACRIS and stratified adjudication — the precision number is circular without it
description:
THE PRECISION NUMBER IS CIRCULAR WITHOUT THIS. Promised during the 2026-08-14 design session
and not written down until now.

== THE PROBLEM ==
PLUTO's ground truth is ADDRESS -> BBL. The CMBS geocode's address came from Geocodio
parsing the Annex A address. So scoring "did we get the right BBL" against PLUTO IS ITSELF
AN ADDRESS JOIN. We would be using address matching to grade address matching.

Wherever the address is unambiguous the circularity is harmless -- and worthless, because
those rows were never in doubt. Wherever the address is AMBIGUOUS, which is the entire
population this outcome exists for, THE GROUND TRUTH IS WRONG IN THE SAME DIRECTION AS THE
THING BEING TESTED. A cascade that makes the same address error as the truth set scores as
correct.

This session measured exactly the failure modes that poison it: chimera parses that
synthesize an address no source asserts, a ROOFTOP-tier geocode parsed onto a street ~1.8 km
away, MapPLUTO carrying one address for a five-address property, corner buildings with two
legitimate and completely different addresses, and 756 Queens grid hyphenates a range rule
would destroy. Every one of those corrupts an address-derived truth set.

== THE FIX: TRUTH FROM EVIDENCE THAT DOES NOT COME FROM THE ADDRESS CHANNEL ==

SOURCE 1 -- ACRIS. LANDED, ~100.76M rows, release_dt 2026-08-10 (cmdrvl-context bd-3rfd).
A recorded mortgage on a BBL, matched to a known CMBS loan by ORIGINATION AMOUNT and
RECORDING DATE and LENDER, yields a BBL for that loan WITH NO USE OF THE ADDRESS AT ALL.
This is the strongest available and it is free and already in the warehouse.
CAVEATS, from OC-0048's own assessment: ACRIS party names are free text with uneven quality,
so it is strong evidence that A MORTGAGE EXISTS ON A BBL and much weaker evidence about WHO
the lender is without name resolution. For ground-truth purposes that asymmetry is fine --
we need the BBL, not the lender identity. Amount-plus-date matching will produce some
ambiguity of its own; require a match to be unique on (amount, date-window) before accepting
it as truth, and discard rather than adjudicate the rest. A smaller clean truth set beats a
larger contaminated one.
NOTE: ACRIS also closes the loop to OC-0047 (holder attribution). Nobody had noticed it is
ALSO how OC-0048 gets honest ground truth for itself.

SOURCE 2 -- STRATIFIED HUMAN ADJUDICATION. Expensive per row, cheap in aggregate if
stratified rather than sampled uniformly. Stratify by the populations that actually matter:
multi-containment, nearest_rooftop_match, interpolated tier, multi-address fields, corner
a/k/a properties, and the never-parsed rows. A few hundred adjudicated rows across those
strata is worth more than thousands drawn at random from the easy 95%.
THIS IS THE VISUAL EVIDENCE CARD'S FIRST REAL JOB. bd-101v stops being only a deliverable
and becomes the instrument that makes the evaluation affordable -- a reviewer judging "is
that the right building" from a rendered tile in seconds rather than reading a table.
Adjudicators must work from ZoLa and the rendered geometry, NOT from the address, or the
circularity returns through the human.

SOURCE 3 -- MULTI-SOURCE GEOMETRIC AGREEMENT, as a weak corroborator only. Where Overture,
FEMA and Microsoft footprints and the parcel layer all agree on a structure, that agreement
is independent of the address channel. It is NOT independent of the geometry channel the
cascade uses, so it CANNOT validate geometric resolution -- it can only cross-check the
address channel. Use it to flag suspects for adjudication, never as truth.

== HOW THE THREE COMPOSE ==
  PLUTO             use for the easy majority, and REPORT IT SEPARATELY, labelled as
                    address-derived. It is not wrong, it is just not informative about the
                    contested population.
  ACRIS             the primary independent truth set. Report precision against it as the
                    headline number.
  ADJUDICATION      the contested tail, stratified, rendered rather than read.
REPORT THE THREE SEPARATELY AND NEVER POOL THEM INTO ONE PRECISION FIGURE. A blended number
hides exactly the contrast that matters: how much worse the cascade does where the address
cannot be trusted.

== WHY THIS GATES bd-bmee ==
bd-bmee's kill criterion compares the cascade against baselines. If truth is address-derived
and the baselines are address-based, the comparison is partly self-referential. The
address-string baseline in particular would be scored against a truth set built the same way
it works, which flatters it in some places and penalises it in others, unpredictably.
DO NOT PUBLISH A PRECISION NUMBER FOR THE CONTESTED POPULATION UNTIL AN INDEPENDENT TRUTH
SET EXISTS FOR IT.

EXIT CRITERIA:
- ACRIS-derived truth set built by amount-plus-date-plus-window matching to known CMBS loans,
  with uniqueness required and non-unique matches discarded and counted
- Its size and coverage reported by borough and by geocode tier, so its representativeness is
  visible rather than assumed
- A stratified adjudication set across the six named contested populations, adjudicated from
  rendered geometry and ZoLa rather than from addresses
- Precision reported SEPARATELY against PLUTO, against ACRIS, and against adjudication, with
  the address-derived one explicitly labelled
- A written statement of how much the three disagree with each other -- that disagreement is
  itself a measurement of how unreliable address-derived truth is

title: [CANON-V1/P00.4] Wire executable artifact-backed entity index build
description:
## Background
Index construction exists in native modules and run orchestration, while public runbooks advertise an index command that Clap does not currently expose. The stage must become a real resumable command consuming prepared artifacts.

## Technical Approach
- Implement the request/response seam created by P00.3 without reopening shared CLI design.
- Load and validate prepare artifacts and surface streams; enforce profile, strategy, registry, and patch hashes.
- Build or reuse token, exact-view, IDF, and n-gram postings through the content-addressed cache contract.
- Write index artifacts atomically and emit human summary or structured JSON with cache diagnostics and next command.

## Success Criteria
- The checked-in index build command executes successfully.
- Stale, tampered, over-budget, or wrong-profile inputs refuse before writes.
- Unchanged reruns produce a verified cache hit and byte-identical artifact.
- Index output is consumable by artifact-backed block.

## Test Plan
- Unit tests for request validation and cache keys.
- CLI subprocess success/refusal tests.
- Corrupt cache rebuild/refusal matrix.
- Medium and measured large-corpus index telemetry.

## RESERVATIONS
- `src/entity/index.rs`
- `src/entity/index_io.rs`
- `src/entity/cache.rs`
- `src/entity/summary.rs`
- `tests/entity/index_cli.rs`

## Considerations
- Do not write cache files into the source registry.
- Keep physical batching independent from logical global index scope.
- Large postings must be bounded and diagnosed.
close_reason: Completed true public prepare.v1/index.v1 convergence: direct self-hashed artifacts, strict v0/tamper/profile/budget firewalls, atomic index bundle publish, verified byte-identical warm cache hits, canonical v1 operator/inventory contracts, and public CLI coverage. title: [CANON-V1/P13.1] Post-core starter pack: BDC issuer resolution
description:
## Background
Package the private BDC issuer deployment used to exercise bd-kkh5 R1-R5 as a standalone, out-of-tree Canon pack after the core v1 release. This is a production use case and worked example; it does not grant structured-finance awareness to Canon core.

## Scope
- Define domain-owned roles for issuer, filer, holding, and instrument or tranche.
- Map SOI-style rows into observations, assignments, relationships, and source provenance.
- Preserve raw, legal-name, and dba or operating-name views.
- Package conservative evidence and promotion policy plus an independently adjudicated starter corpus.
- Distribute through the signed P08 package contract.
- Exclude tournament parsing, source acquisition, proprietary data, and automatic promotion from the pack.

## Technical approach
Normalization may remove punctuation and well-justified legal suffixes in derived views, but it must preserve the original string and protected legal or organizational terms. It must never blanket-strip SPV, Bidco, Holdco, numbered-company, or similar tokens that may distinguish entities. Tranches remain assignments or instruments, not duplicate organizations. Industry and cross-filer co-holding are contextual evidence only; neither is identity authority or a universal cannot-link. Authoritative identifiers or reviewed constraints are the only hard veto sources.

The gold corpus must be human-adjudicated, provenance-bearing, sealed before evaluation, and separated from policy tuning and holdouts. The pack emits evidence through generic Canon contracts and cannot write registry truth directly.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Clean install runs the sealed BDC fixture without changing Canon core.
- R1-R5 are exercised with provenance and temporal/as-of behavior.
- Raw, legal, and dba views survive round-trip inspection.
- Known SPV/Bidco/Holdco and same-name/different-entity cases do not false-merge.
- Candidate and decision metrics meet declared thresholds on an untouched holdout.
- No domain vocabulary appears in core source.

## Test plan
- Golden tests for typed views, tranche separation, temporal aliases, and protected tokens.
- Must-link and cannot-link evaluation on the sealed corpus with leakage checks.
- Ablations for co-holding and industry context.
- Install/verify/run/uninstall tests through P08 signatures and digests.
- Domain-neutrality scan over Canon core.

## File and reservation boundaries
Implementation belongs in a standalone pack or private deployment repository plus public, license-safe fixtures. Reserve exact pack and documentation files; do not edit core to accommodate BDC rules.

## Considerations
The pack may contain private local acceptance data that cannot ship publicly. Public fixtures must be synthetic or appropriately licensed while preserving the same contract. A starter corpus is evidence, not truth by assertion.

title: canon registry default-id-scheme: persist prefix convention in registry.json
description:
Add `canon registry default-id-scheme` to persist a registry's self-authored canonical ID convention in `registry.json`.

Purpose:
- A self-authored registry usually has one canonical namespace such as `PPL`, `IC`, or `CPTY`. Storing the convention makes the registry self-describing and lets `next-id` and `mint` work without repeating `--prefix` every time.

CLI:
`canon registry default-id-scheme --registry <DIR> --prefix <PREFIX> [--zero-pad <N>] [--strict] [--bump patch|minor|major | --next-version <VER>] [--emit json|plain]`

Behavior:
- Read `registry.json` as a JSON object and set `default_id_scheme` to `{ "prefix": <PREFIX>, "zero_pad": <N> }`.
- Validate `PREFIX` as `^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]*$` and `zero_pad` as an integer from 1 through 20. Default width is 3.
- Preserve all existing `registry.json` fields and formatting can change only through pretty JSON serialization.
- Version update uses the same mutually exclusive `--next-version` or `--bump` rules as add-entry, defaulting to patch when the current version is bumpable.
- Increment no mapping entries. `entry_count` should remain unchanged because this is registry metadata, not a mapping addition.
- Inspect existing `canonical_id` values. By default, emit warnings for IDs that start with the prefix namespace but do not conform to the scheme. With `--strict`, refuse instead of writing.
- Write `registry.json` atomically or leave the original bytes unchanged on failure.
- Do not mutate mapping files or `_index.sqlite`.
- Do not add new witness behavior in this bead.
- Ensure `next-id` without a prefix and `mint` without `--canonical-id` or `--prefix` consume the configured scheme.

Output:
- Default `--emit json`: emit `canon_registry_default_id_scheme.v0` with registry version before/after, previous scheme, new scheme, warning counts, and touched file.
- `--emit plain`: print `<PREFIX>-<zero_pad width>` style summary plus newline, for example `PPL-3`.
acceptance_criteria:
- Setting the scheme writes `default_id_scheme` to `registry.json` and bumps the registry version without changing `entry_count`.
- Unknown `registry.json` fields survive unchanged.
- Invalid prefixes, zero padding outside 1..20, and unchanged/non-bumpable versions refuse with recovery guidance.
- `--strict` refuses when existing in-namespace canonical IDs do not conform; non-strict mode writes and records warnings in the JSON receipt.
- `canon registry next-id --registry <DIR>` uses the configured scheme when no prefix is supplied.
- `canon registry mint --registry <DIR> --canonical-type <TYPE> --with-alias ...` uses the configured scheme when no canonical ID or prefix is supplied.
- JSON receipt shape is covered by a golden fixture for `canon_registry_default_id_scheme.v0`.
- The command writes only `registry.json`; mapping files and `_index.sqlite` are unchanged.
- Quality gate passes: `cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo test`.
notes:
Target files:
- src/registry/id_scheme.rs (new)
- src/registry.rs (add module/export and extend metadata helpers; there is no src/registry/mod.rs in this repo)
- src/registry/next_id.rs (fallback behavior, if not already complete)
- src/registry/mint.rs (fallback behavior, if not already complete)
- src/cli.rs (wire subcommand)
- src/lib.rs (minimal dispatch only)
- operator.json (add command contract if implemented in this bead)
- tests/registry_id_scheme.rs (new)

Implementation notes:
- This bead should land after next-id and mint to avoid parallel edits to the same modules.
- `default_id_scheme` is metadata for self-authored registries. It must not alter lookup matching semantics.
- Keep the field optional; existing registries without it must continue to load and resolve exactly as before.
close_reason: Implemented canon registry default-id-scheme as a metadata-only registry.json writer. Validates prefix and zero_pad, bumps version without changing entry_count, preserves unknown registry fields, records non-strict warnings for in-namespace out-of-scheme IDs, supports --strict refusal, leaves mappings and _index.sqlite untouched, and proves next-id/mint consume the stored scheme. Evidence: cargo fmt --check; cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings; cargo test; target/debug/canon --describe includes default-id-scheme; br dep cycles --json returned count 0.

title: [CANON-V1/P13.2] Post-core starter pack: CMBS tenant resolution
description:
## Background
Build a second hand-authored starter pack for tenant-name resolution across rent rolls and leases. It exercises a different entity archetype from BDC issuers—chains, stores, franchisees, legal tenants, locations, and landlords—but remains a structured-finance-adjacent use case. It must not be presented as proof of cross-industry generality.

## Scope
- Define domain-owned roles and relationships for tenant, legal obligor, brand or chain, franchisee, store or location, landlord, lease, and source row.
- Preserve store numbers, location identifiers, dba relationships, and franchise relationships rather than collapsing them into names.
- Package source mappings, typed normalization views, evidence policy, and an adjudicated starter corpus.
- Distribute through P08 as an independent package.
- Exclude document extraction, rent-roll parsing, and automatic registry promotion.

## Technical approach
Map each source row into observations and typed assignments. Preserve raw strings and protected numeric or location features. Treat chain affiliation and franchise relationships as typed evidence, not identity equivalence. Legal tenant, operating brand, franchisee, and individual store can be related while remaining distinct entities. All scoring and decisions pass through generic Canon evidence, review, and promotion contracts.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A clean install resolves the sealed CMBS tenant fixture without core edits.
- Chain, franchisee, legal tenant, and store/location identities remain distinguishable.
- Store numbers and location signals improve disambiguation without becoming universal match keys.
- Holdout candidate recall and decision quality meet declared thresholds.
- Documentation accurately calls this a second finance archetype, not cross-domain proof.

## Test plan
- Golden tests for chain/franchise/store/legal-tenant relationship shapes.
- Adversarial same-brand/different-franchisee and same-name/different-location cases.
- Leakage-safe holdout evaluation and feature ablations.
- P08 install, signature, digest, compatibility, and uninstall checks.
- Domain-neutrality scan over Canon core.

## File and reservation boundaries
Implementation belongs in a standalone pack or deployment repository with license-safe fixtures. Reserve exact files and keep all CMBS vocabulary outside core.

## Considerations
Brand similarity can be strong relationship evidence while being dangerous identity evidence. The corpus must represent franchise and multi-location negatives, not only easy aliases.

title: canon geo: geocode plausibility — use the tile to refute its own input, and adjudicate competing geocodes
description:
OPERATOR INSIGHT 2026-08-14: THE TILE CAN REFUTE ITS OWN INPUT. THIS IS A CAPABILITY,
NOT AN ERROR PATH.

"Geocodes are hard to trust, and there is going to be some cases where the geocode we're
provided is just flat out wrong. It's not in the tile set at all. So it's an abstain or
refuse, and there's a lot of validity to when we're only looking at one tile and its
surrounding tiles being able to say: this geocode and this address are nowhere in here."

Everything else in canon geo runs FORWARD: take the geocode, pull the tile, generate
candidates, score, decide or abstain. This runs BACKWARD — it uses the tile as EVIDENCE
ABOUT THE INPUT. It is cheap, purely local, entirely deterministic, and it catches a
population that accuracy_type cannot.

== THE PROOF CASE, FROM REAL DATA ==
"241/249 West 74th Street" carries two geocodes from two different geocoding services:
  (40.7777640, -73.9755480)  range_interpolation  parsed "241 W 74th St"
  (40.7615050, -73.9859030)  ROOFTOP              parsed "241 W 49th St"  <- ~25 blocks off
The second is at the HIGHEST confidence tier and is flatly wrong.

Pull the tile plus k-ring at each point and ask a single question: DOES ANYTHING IN THIS
NEIGHBOURHOOD CARRY THE ASSERTED STREET? At the first point, West 74th Street is present.
At the second, it is not. THE TILE REFUTES THE GEOCODE. No ground truth, no external
service, no ML — just the tile the cascade already had to download.

== WHY TILE SCOPING IS WHAT MAKES IT WORK ==
Street names repeat across boroughs; there is a Broadway in every one. The question is not
"does this street name exist anywhere" (useless) but "DOES THIS STREET EXIST HERE"
(decisive). A res-9 cell plus k-ring 1 is ~1 km across, and a street that does not appear
anywhere in a 1 km neighbourhood is a street you are not standing on. The blocking unit
doubles as the plausibility window, which is the third distinct job the tile is doing —
after blocking (bd-2b9d) and the map viewport (bd-101v).

== THE CHECK, IN ORDER OF COST ==
1. STREET PRESENCE. Does any entity in the tile + k-ring carry the asserted street name
   (normalized)? Cheapest and strongest.
2. HOUSE-NUMBER RANGE. Does the asserted number fall within the range of numbers observed
   on that street in the neighbourhood? Catches "241 West 74th" pointing at the 1600 block.
3. ADDRESS-SET MEMBERSHIP. For multi-address assertions, does ANY member of the asserted
   set appear? (Requires the address-set source, bd-35qg, to be strong.)
4. ATTRIBUTE COHERENCE. Does anything in the neighbourhood plausibly match on size, type
   or year built? Weakest, but it is what discriminates the two failure directions below.

== IT DISCRIMINATES TWO FAILURE DIRECTIONS THAT NEED DIFFERENT REMEDIES ==
  GEOCODE IS WRONG    the tile has coherent content, but NOTHING matches the assertion on
                      ANY channel. Remedy: re-geocode. This is the 241/249 W 49th case.
  ADDRESS IS WRONG    the geocode lands cleanly on a rooftop and the tile has a coherent
                      property there matching on OTHER channels (size, type, name) but not
                      on address. Remedy: fix the source record.
  BOTH PLAUSIBLE      abstain.
Conflating these produces the wrong advice to the client, and the advice is the product.

== IT ADJUDICATES BETWEEN COMPETING GEOCODES ==
The geocode table's grain is property x SOURCE x ASOF — multiple geocoding services
appended, not upserted (verified 2026-08-14; see the correction on bd-tccn). So a property
may carry SEVERAL candidate points from INDEPENDENT services. That independence is
valuable: when two services disagree, the tile is a deterministic referee. Pull the tile at
each candidate, apply the checks above, and keep the point its own neighbourhood supports.
Where several survive or none do, abstain.
This is strictly better than the usual heuristics (highest accuracy_score, most recent
asof, preferred source), all of which pick a winner without evidence.

== THE EXPANDING SEARCH: DIAGNOSTICS, NOT REPAIR ==
When the geocode is refuted, expanding the k-ring can often find where the asserted address
actually is. That is genuinely valuable OUTPUT — "412 rows in your book have geocodes more
than 500 m from anything matching their address, and here is where each probably belongs"
is a report a client can act on the day they receive it, and no competing product produces
it.
BUT IT IS NOT RESOLUTION. Per canon doctrine the workbench proposes and review promotes. A
relocated point is a CANDIDATE carrying its displacement distance and its supporting
evidence, never a silent correction. Bound the expansion explicitly (a declared max k) and
refuse rather than searching outward indefinitely.

== ABSTENTION VOCABULARY ADDITIONS (extends bd-786w) ==
  GeocodeRefutedByTile      nothing in the neighbourhood supports the asserted address
  AddressRefutedByTile      the point is coherent but the assertion is not supported
  CompetingGeocodes         multiple candidate points, none decisively supported
  GeocodeUnlocatable        refuted, and the bounded expanding search found no better home
Each carries the tile id, the checks that ran, and what was found instead — so the card
(bd-101v) can render "we looked here and here is what is actually there."

== WHY THIS MAY BE THE HIGHEST-VALUE-PER-EFFORT ITEM IN THE EPIC ==
1. It needs NO data that is not already required — the tile and the client's own row.
2. It catches silent errors that accuracy_type provably misses. The proof case is ROOFTOP
   tier, which every tier-based calibration would trust.
3. It converts an unexplained miss into an ACTIONABLE finding with a named remedy, which is
   the difference between "we could not key 6% of your book" and "6% of your book has bad
   geocodes and here they are."
4. It is a REFUSAL, which is canon's native and strongest posture.

EXIT CRITERIA:
- The four checks implemented as geo evidence operators emitting structured (not prose)
  evidence
- Tile-scoped street presence proven on the 241/249 West 74th Street case: the W 49th point
  refuted, the W 74th point supported
- Both failure directions discriminated, with a fixture for each
- Competing-geocode adjudication, with a test that it beats highest-accuracy_score and
  most-recent-asof heuristics on a labelled set
- Bounded expanding search emitting candidates with displacement distance, never silent
  correction; refusal at the declared bound
- Four abstention reasons implemented and carried into the artifact
- Reported as a first-class rate alongside coverage, precision, abstention, multi-candidate
  and false-merge

comments.text:
CORRECTION 2026-08-14 (SECOND) — "COMPETING GEOCODING SERVICES" WAS NOT ESTABLISHED. IT
CAME FROM AN LLM INTERPRETATION, NOT FROM THE DATA. Operator caught it.

WHAT THE BEAD SAID: that the geocode table carries points from "SEVERAL candidate points
from INDEPENDENT services," and that their independence is what makes cross-source
disagreement valuable evidence.

THE PROVENANCE OF THAT CLAIM: Loom asserted "the ETL pipeline runs multiple geocoding
services (NYC and Census TIGER)." I did not verify it before writing it down. OC-0048
states plainly that the CMBS geocodes come from GEOCODIO — a single service — and records
a frozen Geocodio account (br-1zo6) as the backfill blocker.

THE LITERAL VALUES, NOW VERIFIED, for the two "241/249 West 74th Street" rows:
                   ROW 1                                          ROW 2
  SOURCE           "TIGER/Line(R) dataset from the US Census      "City of New York"
                    Bureau"
  ASOF             2025-01-01                                     2026-08-01
  CENSUS_YEAR      2024                                           2025
  PROPERTY_NAME    "Alfie Arms Corp."   (trailing period)         "Alfie Arms Corp"
  LAT/LON          40.7777640 / -73.9755480                       40.7615050 / -73.9859030
  ACCURACY_TYPE    range_interpolation                            rooftop
  ACCURACY_SCORE   1.00                                           0.92
  STREET           "W 74th St"                                    "W 49th St"

MOST LIKELY READING, STILL UNVERIFIED AND FLAGGED AS SUCH: those SOURCE strings are
GEOCODIO'S UNDERLYING-ADDRESS-DATASET ATTRIBUTION, not separate vendors. Geocodio returns a
per-result `source` naming the dataset that produced the match, and "TIGER/Line(R) dataset
from the US Census Bureau" is one of its stock strings. One service, two runs, different
underlying datasets matched.
DO NOT HARDEN THIS EITHER. Verify against Geocodio's documentation. It is the same class of
unverified-vendor-semantics problem bd-bmee already flags for accuracy_type ("asserted from
general knowledge, NOT verified against their documentation"), and both should be settled
in the same pass.

THE ACTUALLY VERIFIED AND MORE USEFUL FINDING — A TRAILING PERIOD DUPLICATES THE ROW.
PROPERTY_NAME is part of the table's grain. "Alfie Arms Corp." and "Alfie Arms Corp"
differ by ONE PUNCTUATION MARK, and that is what makes this two rows rather than one. Two
upstream records naming the same property slightly differently, geocoded 19 months apart,
landing 1.8 km apart.
This is a NAME-NORMALIZATION problem sitting upstream of the geo problem — and it is
squarely what canon entity's existing machinery is for (bd-2cbs rule 3). Deduplicating the
book by normalized property name BEFORE geo runs is cheap, uses shipped capability, and
directly shrinks the denominators bd-14co has to report. Add it to the corpus as its own
observation.

ALSO VERIFIED AND WORTH KEEPING: ACCURACY_SCORE and ACCURACY_TYPE DISAGREE about which row
to trust. Score says row 1 (1.00 vs 0.92); tier says row 2 (rooftop beats
range_interpolation). The tier — the field every convention trusts, and the one bd-bmee's
tier analysis is built on — points at the WRONG row. Neither field alone is a safe selector.

WHAT SURVIVES IN THIS BEAD, UNCHANGED AND STILL THE POINT:
The capability does not depend on WHY multiple rows exist. Whatever the mechanism —
separate vendors, one vendor across vintages, or duplicate upstream records — a property
can carry SEVERAL candidate points that disagree, and THE TILE CAN ADJUDICATE BETWEEN THEM
WITH EVIDENCE where accuracy_score, accuracy_type, most-recent-asof and preferred-source
all pick a winner without any. The 241/249 proof case stands exactly as written: the tile at
the West 49th point contains no West 74th Street and refutes it; the tile at the West 74th
point supports it.

REQUIRED EDIT: strike "independent services" from the adjudication section and replace with
"multiple candidate points for one property, whatever their provenance." Do not claim
independence as a property of the evidence until the mechanism is verified — independent
sources disagreeing IS stronger evidence than one source varying, but that strength has to
be earned by verification, not assumed.

PROCESS NOTE FOR THIS CORPUS: two claims in this session came from Loom's prose
interpretation rather than from returned values, and both were wrong. When building the
worked-case corpus (bd-tccn), TAKE LITERAL COLUMN VALUES AND RECORD THE QUERY. Prose
summaries from any LLM tool are a lead to verify, never a finding to cite. This matters
more here than usual because the corpus is meant to be the thing everything else is
designed against.

comments.author: Zac
comments.text:
VERIFIED FACTS FROM STRUCTURED TOOL OUTPUT 2026-08-14. Method: `cmdrvl --json orchestrator
query --tenant salt --raw`, reading `.data.response.tool_responses[].structuredContent`
rather than Loom's prose answer. The underlying tool is `data__edgar_data_run_query`, which
returns the literal SQL it ran plus `{ok, columns, rows}` or `{ok:false, error}`. Every
fact below is a literal returned value.

THIS METHOD CHANGE IS THE FINDING THAT MATTERS MOST. Three claims earlier in this session
came from Loom's prose and were wrong. The structured path caught the third one
immediately, and the skill documentation already prescribed it ("prefer
tool_responses[*].structuredContent from --raw over prose"). ALL CORPUS EXTRACTS MUST USE
THE STRUCTURED PATH AND RECORD THE EMITTED SQL.

=========================================================================
1. THE LANDED MapPLUTO TABLE PROJECTS A SUBSET OF FIELDS. `UNITSTOTAL` DOES NOT EXIST.
=========================================================================
A prior extract reported "UNITSTOTAL 178" for BBL 1014477501. The structured output shows
that query FAILED: `invalid identifier 'UNITSTOTAL'`. The value was fabricated in prose.

LITERAL COLUMN LIST of EDGAR_DB.SOURCE.NYC_DCP_MAPPLUTO_HOT:
  RELEASE, RELEASE_DT, VARIANT, SOURCE_ROW_NUMBER, VALID_FROM_RELEASE_DT,
  VALID_TO_RELEASE_DT, IS_CURRENT_RELEASE, COUNTRY, STATE, BOROUGH_PARTITION, OBJECTID,
  BOROUGH, BLOCK, LOT, BBL, ADDRESS, BLDGCLASS, LANDUSE, YEARBUILT, LOTAREA, BLDGAREA,
  NUMBLDGS, NUMFLOORS, OWNERNAME, PLUTOMAPID, GEOM_GEOG, CENTROID_GEOG, CENTROID_LON,
  CENTROID_LAT, BBOX_XMIN, BBOX_YMIN, BBOX_XMAX, BBOX_YMAX, H3_R7, H3_R8, GEOM_CRS,
  SOURCE_GEOM_CRS, SOURCE_CHANNEL, SOURCE_FILENAME, ROW_PAYLOAD, LOADED_AT

CONSEQUENCES:
- MapPLUTO publishes roughly ninety fields; the landed table projects about twenty and puts
  the remainder in ROW_PAYLOAD. Anything not projected requires digging into ROW_PAYLOAD,
  which is a different access pattern and a different cost.
- THE SIX-FIELD CLIENT CONTRACT IS SATISFIED BY PROJECTED COLUMNS, which is good news:
  building size -> BLDGAREA, year built -> YEARBUILT, property type -> BLDGCLASS + LANDUSE.
  No ROW_PAYLOAD dig needed for the core cascade.
- UNIT COUNTS (UnitsTotal, UnitsRes) ARE NOT PROJECTED. Assemblage subset-sum for
  multifamily (case 7) may want them. Confirm they exist in ROW_PAYLOAD before designing
  around them.

=========================================================================
2. BBL IS STORED AS A STRING WITH A TRAILING ".0" AND IS NOT JOIN-READY.
=========================================================================
Literal returned value: "BBL": "1014477501.0"

This is a direct problem for canon. Core lookup is EXACT BYTE MATCH AFTER ASCII-TRIM, so
"1014477501" would NOT resolve against "1014477501.0". Any registry built from this column
without normalization silently fails to match the identifier every other NYC source uses,
and every downstream join against ACRIS, PLUTO, or the footprints file has the same
exposure.
REQUIRED: BBL normalization is a declared, versioned step in the ingest, not an incidental
cast. It belongs in the geo profile's normalization vocabulary alongside the geometry
canonicalization, and it needs a negative test.

=========================================================================
3. CASE 6 IS A CONDO, AND THE CONDO TRAP IS LIVE IN IT.
=========================================================================
Literal rows for BBL prefix 10144775:

  BBL 1014477501.0  "305 EAST 72 STREET"  BLDGCLASS RM  LOTAREA 37,800
                    BLDGAREA 194,949  NUMBLDGS 2  NUMFLOORS 17  YEARBUILT 1961
                    OWNERNAME "305/72 CONDOMINIUM"
  BBL 1014477502.0  "1355 1 AVENUE"       BLDGCLASS RM  LOTAREA  5,100
                    BLDGAREA 102,719  NUMBLDGS 1  NUMFLOORS 31  YEARBUILT 2009
                    OWNERNAME "UNAVAILABLE OWNER"

FOUR THINGS THIS ESTABLISHES:
a) OWNERNAME "305/72 CONDOMINIUM" and the 75xx lot range confirm these are CONDO BILLING
   BBLs. The condo trap named in OC-0048 and measured in the multi-lot fan-out is present
   in the very property picked to illustrate a different case.
b) A PRIOR CLAIM IS CORRECTED. I wrote that five asserted addresses "resolve to ONE BBL."
   Not established. At least two condo BBLs sit here with DIFFERENT street frontages —
   East 72 Street and 1 Avenue. The property's a/k/a set names E 72nd, 2nd Avenue and
   E 73rd; 1 Avenue is a fourth frontage not in that set. The containment test still has to
   be run properly.
c) YEARBUILT 1961 vs 2009 ON ADJACENT CONDO LOTS IS A LIVE REDEVELOPMENT SIGNAL — exactly
   the case hypothesised on bd-gs6n, that a large year-built spread on overlapping or
   adjacent footprints is a TEMPORAL finding rather than a match failure. It is real and it
   is in the first property examined closely.
d) NUMBLDGS 2 on one condo BBL. The building level is still needed and the BBL-to-BIN
   bridge (landed, bd-397d) is still the next pull.

=========================================================================
4. THE TABLE IS STRUCTURALLY BITEMPORAL ALREADY.
=========================================================================
RELEASE, RELEASE_DT, VALID_FROM_RELEASE_DT, VALID_TO_RELEASE_DT, IS_CURRENT_RELEASE are all
present. The landing contract (cmdrvl-curves bd-qbno) was built for multiple releases even
though OC-0048 records that only the current one is loaded.
CONSEQUENCE: the as-of machinery bd-12gh and bd-1oy8 need does not require a schema change,
only additional releases. Check `SELECT DISTINCT RELEASE, RELEASE_DT` before assuming case
9's temporal arc is blocked — cmdrvl-curves bd-33t6 may be closer to done than the outcome
document states.

=========================================================================
5. REPROJECTION PROVENANCE IS ALREADY RECORDED. THIS DIRECTLY SERVES bd-3nc7.
=========================================================================
GEOM_CRS and SOURCE_GEOM_CRS are projected columns. So the EPSG:2263 -> WGS84 transform
that the predicate-regime bead has to reason about is documented in the table itself rather
than needing archaeology. Read those columns first when starting bd-3nc7.

=========================================================================
6. H3_R7 AND H3_R8 ARE PRESENT. H3_R9 IS NOT.
=========================================================================
The epic's default tile is res-9. It is not precomputed. Canon computes it itself, which is
what bd-2b9d already requires for a separate reason — the Snowflake H3 helpers returned
malformed boundaries and a bad k-ring (edgar-elt br-2wir). Both reasons now point the same
way: compute r9 in canon with a vetted Rust H3 library, and treat the warehouse H3 columns
as a coarse prefilter at most.

=========================================================================
7. GEOCODIO SOURCE SEMANTICS — CONFIRMED BY OPERATOR.
=========================================================================
Geocodio reports the underlying address dataset that produced each match. So SOURCE values
like "TIGER/Line(R) dataset from the US Census Bureau" and "City of New York" are
per-result attribution from ONE service, not competing vendors — and MULTIPLE SOURCED
GEOCODES PER PROPERTY ARE EXPECTED AND NORMAL.
This VINDICATES the capability in bd-1a12 while keeping the retraction of the mechanism.
SOURCE becomes usable EVIDENCE: a local authoritative dataset and a national interpolated
one carry different reliability.
BUT NOTE THE COUNTEREXAMPLE ALREADY IN HAND: on "241/249 West 74th Street" the
"City of New York" sourced row is the WRONG one (W 49th St, rooftop, score 0.92) and the
TIGER/Line row is right (W 74th St, range_interpolation, score 1.00). So SOURCE is not a
safe selector either, any more than ACCURACY_TYPE or ACCURACY_SCORE are. Three fields, none
individually decisive, all disagreeing — which is precisely the argument for letting the
tile adjudicate.

comments.author: Zac
comments.text:
ARCHITECTURE SUPERSEDED 2026-08-15 — see docs/PLAN_CANON_GEO.md.

An adversarial multi-model design session produced a materially different architecture,
which then survived a red team that destroyed two intermediate designs. The tile is modelled
as a BOUNDED UNIVERSE and every piece of evidence is a CONSTRAINT; propagation runs to a
fixpoint; the residual model set IS the answer. There is no proposer channel.

THE THREE PROPERTIES THAT MATTER:
- CONFLUENCE. The fixpoint is independent of the order constraints are applied (Tarski 1955;
  Cousot & Cousot 1977; Apt 1999), so determinism is a theorem rather than an engineering
  effort.
- MONOTONICITY. Constraints only add and domains only shrink, so a tile resolved with four
  sources today and six next year yields a TIGHTER residual, never a contradicting one. The
  earlier answer was never wrong, only less resolved.
- STRUCTURAL ABSTENTION. The residual model set is the answer. No threshold anywhere.

THE KEY DESIGN RULE IS rho, THE SOUNDNESS DISCIPLINE. Every source attribute enters the
solver only through a declared versioned relaxation mapping it to the WEAKEST constraint the
source can actually support. An interpolated geocode becomes a 150m disc rather than a
location. A parcel ADDRESS becomes "one of this lot's addresses" rather than functional
equality. OWNERNAME equal PERMITS an assemblage; OWNERNAME different constrains NOTHING.
Every noisy channel is admitted only in its sound direction — which is what dissolved the
proposer dilemma that broke the two earlier designs.

AND THE COMMERCIAL CONSEQUENCE: if every rho is sound, the true assignment is in the model
set, so AN EMPTY MODEL SET IS A PROOF that a named source violated its own published error
model — attributable, falsifiable, and mailable to the vendor.

Read PLAN_CANON_GEO.md before starting any geo work. Section 11 carries the bead-by-bead
supersession table. Appendix A covers frozen-weight observers and imagery sources. APPENDIX
B RECORDS THE FIRST HARD MEASUREMENT, WHICH FALSIFIED A LOAD-BEARING CLAIM — read it before
trusting any performance number in the plan.

Raw session artifacts, including the red team and the adversarial reviews, are preserved
under docs/geo_design_session/ with a reading guide.

comments.text: L.5 doctrine (operator, 2026-08-16): abstention is a reacquisition TRIGGER — tile refutation feeds a bounded re-geocode-and-retry outer loop, not a terminal state. E1 measured the population this serves: 40/79 labeled failures are wrong-location input averaging 7.1km. bd-s3i9 M3 is measuring the retry-loop ceiling from already-landed alternate geocode rows. This capability bead should implement refute -> reacquire -> retry as the operating shape.

comments.author: Zac
comments.text: Live n=1 retry-loop trial (operator-directed, via Loom geo MCP): re-geocoded the P4 proof-case address '241/249 West 74th Street, New York, NY' — the address whose landed rooftop geocode sits ~25 blocks away on W 49th. Result: match_quality=exact, matched '249 W 74TH ST 10023' (range form parsed correctly by usaddress; no W49 chimera recurrence), tract_geoid 36061016300 = the true W 74th location's tract, i.e. a DIFFERENT and correct-location geocode vs the bad landed point. Contract discovered: the geo MCP source_chain [usaddress, census_structured] returns TRACT-grain results (no lat/lon) — so as landed it serves the refutation/confirmation arm (tract disagreement corroborates abstention; tract agreement clears retry targeting) rather than direct PIP re-entry. Full recovery paths remain: coordinate-returning geocode pass, or PAD address->BBL (bd-28kn) which bypasses coordinates entirely. Retry loop validated in principle at n=1.

comments.author: Zac
comments.text: Retry loop demonstrated END-TO-END at n=1 on the P4 proof case, using only free public acquisition + landed data: (1) landed rooftop geocode refuted (2,161m away on W49 — abstain); (2) fresh acquisition via the free US Census Geocoder locations API (geocoding.geo.census.gov, no key, public domain; handles the raw '241/249' range form; benchmark Public_AR_Current, TIGER interpolation): returns (40.780793,-73.982580) on the correct street/block — also 669m from the LANDED range-interpolation row, which had placed the address at the wrong END of W74 (near CPW); (3) PIP on the fresh point returns 0 lots (roadbed — interpolation tier behaving per Case 2, honest); (4) address channel inside the tile finishes it: MapPLUTO '245 WEST 74 STREET' (representative address for the 241-249 range) = BBL 1011660007, 75,312 SF, 1 building, boundary 1.5m from the fresh point. The retry re-enters the pipeline at interpolation-tier rho and resolves via address membership + proximity corroboration — exactly the Case 2 shape. Census locations endpoint is a legitimate generic instance for evidence row 1 (coordinate-returning, national, free); geo MCP's geographies-style tract result is the cheap refutation cross-check. Both belong in the bd-1a12 capability design.

comments.author: Zac
comments.text: Operator design decision: TRACT-BOUNDED RETRY is the v1 loop — no coordinate API required. The tract is a bounded universe of the same epistemic shape as the tile (jurisdiction-defined, integer-keyed GEOID, versioned), so retry = refute -> address->tract via geo MCP as landed (exact match) -> assemble tract cells -> normal pipeline over the tract's candidate set with address as existential membership evidence. Measured bound for the trial tract 36061016300: 27 FEMA structures / 6 r9 cells (order ~100 buildings, ~200 parcels after FEMA dense-MN undercount). Census locations API is an optimization (6 cells -> 1), not a requirement. Bonus: tracts are population-normalized -> roughly constant candidate-set sizes by construction (relevant to Appendix G sizing). Guards: (1) chimera/parsed-address membership check BEFORE trusting tract (tract inherits address-string risk); (2) rho scales with match_quality (exact -> tract; weaker -> tract+neighbors); (3) PIN TRACT VINTAGE — 2010 vs 2020 GEOIDs (MapPLUTO CT2010-era vs FEMA 2020 TRACT_GEOID) is the same silent-join defect class as H3 INTEGER/TEXT; (4) representative-address gap persists until PAD (bd-28kn).

comments.author: Zac

title: [CANON-V1/P07.R6h] Credit exact prepared-surface collapse in native link decisions
description:
## Background
Public native link decision derivation flattens observation-to-surface bindings into reference and target ID sets before classifying targets. An exact shared prepared surface can therefore resolve to one incumbent with zero candidate support but still be emitted as unmatched. PLAN_CANON defines prepared_surface_collapse as a first-class attachment lane with no candidate-rank or recall credit.

## Technical Approach
Retain target/reference binding identity at prepared-surface grain in entity_link_decision_records_from_solve. Permit a match only when exactly one reference and the target share the exact hash-bound prepared surface, the solve entity is resolved_existing, and all hard-cannot-link, conflict, soft-warning, and multiple-reference guards pass. Keep ordinary threshold matching unchanged. Emit an explicit prepared_surface_collapse assertion/disposition with zero candidate score rather than pretending candidate evidence exists. Refresh strict alias-withholding fixture decisions from the updated solve and committed lineage.

## Success Criteria
- Exact shared-surface reference/target observations deterministically produce one match even with zero candidate support.
- Collapse receives no candidate-rank or candidate-recall credit and is explicitly distinguishable from threshold evidence matches.
- Distinct-surface zero-support cases remain unmatched.
- Hard/soft anti-merge and multiple-reference cases never auto-match.
- Review-export rederivation remains byte/semantic parity with emitted link decisions.
- Strict alias-withholding fixture has one collapse attach and one honest non-incumbent abstention under committed publication lineage.

## Test Plan
Add neutral public link coverage for shared-surface collapse and negative safety guards; rerun entity_alias_withholding, CLI smoke/link integration, fmt, strict Clippy, and full cargo test.

## RESERVATIONS
- src/lib.rs
- tests/cli_smoke.rs
- tests/entity_alias_withholding.rs
close_reason: Guarded exact prepared-surface collapse now attaches only one safe resolved incumbent, emits zero candidate credit, preserves anti-merge and multi-reference abstention, and passes neutral, alias-withholding, and full quality gates.

title: [CANON-V1/P09.10] Deferred decision: review delivery transports
description:
## Background
Agent-orchestrated email crowdsourcing is one plausible way to deliver Canon review packets to domain experts, but it is only an idea. Core review and promotion must not depend on email, a UI, a ticketing system, active learning, or any other transport.

## Scope
Retain the future choices: direct CLI/file review, agent-operated email, a third-party or OpenRefine-compatible client, ticketing/approval systems, a custom UI, or no additional delivery layer. Core owns stable review packets, structured decision import, ledger receipts, stale/tamper refusals, audit, promotion, and replay.

## Technical Approach
Do no transport implementation before final v1 acceptance. Later, choose from observed review volume, privacy/disclosure constraints, expert-routing needs, and operator workflow. A selected transport becomes an out-of-core sidecar or client over the generic artifacts. Email, if selected, requires authorization, redaction, thread/candidate binding, reply parsing, spoof/tamper defense, idempotency, bounce/timeout/reassignment, retention, and real-service E2E.

## Acceptance Criteria
- No review delivery transport blocks or appears in core acceptance.
- CLI and offline files alone complete review, import, audit, promotion, and replay.
- The decision document records all options without selecting email or forbidding future clients.
- Any later client has zero direct registry/promotion authority and uses stable generic contracts.
- This bead remains blocked until final v1 acceptance.

## Test Plan
Before any later selection, scan release dependencies and docs to prove transport independence. A future selected sidecar must add protocol, security, stale/tamper, idempotency, failure, and real-service E2E matrices.

## RESERVATIONS
- docs/DECISION_REVIEW_VIA_EMAIL_CROWDSOURCING.md

## Considerations
Transport-neutral artifacts maximize open-source adoption and let agent workflows evolve independently of Canon core.
