title: canon geo: attribute-anchored resolution — resolve through the tile, with tile-relative evidence weighting
description:
OPERATOR INSIGHT 2026-08-14: RESOLVE THROUGH THE TILE, NOT BETWEEN THE ROWS. THIS MAY BE
THE CENTRAL MECHANISM OF THE WHOLE PRODUCT.

"Assuming we knew it was an office building, ten thousand square feet, and we pulled our
geometry services and the tile from that geocode has an office building with ten thousand
square feet, then both of these would match that, and we would know they're the same
property — irrespective of their name or their address, because the characteristics of the
building match a building in the tile set, if not multiple buildings, because the tile
includes data from four or five sources."

== WHY THIS IS A DIFFERENT MECHANISM, NOT A NEW OPERATOR ==
Every solve mode scoped so far compares ROWS TO EACH OTHER. Cluster mode compares within a
corpus, link mode across two, assemblage compares an assertion to a subset. All pairwise or
subset-wise, all rooted in comparing client data to client data.

THIS COMPARES EACH ROW TO THE TILE INDEPENDENTLY, and equivalence falls out:
    row A  ->  tile entity X
    row B  ->  tile entity X
    therefore A and B denote the same physical thing
The tile entity is a SHARED REFERENT. No A-to-B comparison ever happens. This is canon's
own cluster doctrine — the cluster is the identity, source IDs are participants bound by
evidence — with the anchor SUPPLIED BY THE TILE rather than emerging from pairwise scoring.

== WHY IT MATTERS SO MUCH: IT ROUTES AROUND EVERY FAILURE WE HAVE MEASURED ==
Verified failures in this book, all of them name/address failures:
  chimera parses that synthesize an address no source asserts
  a ROOFTOP-tier geocode parsed onto the wrong street, ~1.8 km off
  MapPLUTO carrying one address for a five-address property
  corner buildings with two legitimate and completely different addresses
  a TRAILING PERIOD in a property name duplicating a row
  756 Queens grid hyphenates that a range rule would destroy
  the hardest rows never parsing at all (accuracy_type 'place', null number and street)
ATTRIBUTE-ANCHORED RESOLUTION NEEDS NONE OF IT. Geometry puts you in the tile; building
class, floor area, floor count and year built pick the entity. The address channel becomes
CORROBORATION rather than the spine — which is the right posture given how comprehensively
it fails.

== PREREQUISITE: THE TILE MUST SHIP PRE-RESOLVED ==
The operator's phrasing — "the tile includes data from four or five sources" — implies the
tile's own sources are ALREADY RECONCILED when it ships. That is a significant architectural
commitment and it should be explicit:

  AT TILE BUILD (our side, once per tile per vintage): reconcile Overture, FEMA USA
  Structures, Microsoft GlobalML and NYC footprints into BUILDING CLUSTERS with agreed
  characteristics and a minted cmdrvl:building:* id, plus the per-source disagreement
  retained.
  AT CLIENT RUN (their machine, once per book): attach client rows to ALREADY-RESOLVED
  ANCHORS, and reconcile the client's own parcel layer against them.

This is a large simplification and a large scaling win: the expensive N-source
reconciliation happens ONCE PER TILE rather than once per client run, and every client gets
the same anchors — which is also what makes cmdrvl:building:* ids stable and shareable
across clients at all.
IT ALSO CHANGES bd-1s4e. If the tile ships pre-resolved, the client run is not a symmetric
six-source problem; it is client-book + client-parcels against a pre-anchored building
layer. Revisit that bead's scope in light of this.

== THE HARD PART: EVIDENCE STRENGTH IS TILE-RELATIVE ==
"An office building at 10,000 SF" is DECISIVE in a tile containing three offices and NEARLY
WORTHLESS in a tile containing forty. The same attribute match means different things in
different tiles, and treating it as a fixed-weight operator will overmerge in dense tiles
and underperform in sparse ones.

THE TILE SUPPLIES ITS OWN DENOMINATOR. Because the tile bounds the population, the rarity
of an attribute tuple within it is exactly computable — no global corpus statistics, no
approximation. This is the same idea as the rarity weighting canon already implements for
names in src/entity/tfidf_evidence.rs, applied to ATTRIBUTE TUPLES instead of tokens, and
it is one of the few places where an existing canon component transfers to geo essentially
unchanged.

REQUIRED:
- Compute, per tile, the frequency of each attribute tuple actually used for anchoring
  (class x floor-area band x floor-count band x year band).
- Score matches by tuple RARITY IN THAT TILE, not by a global weight.
- ABSTAIN when the matched tuple is not discriminating — several tile entities match
  equally well. That is a genuine tie and it is the honest output.
- Report the tile's discriminating power as a diagnostic, so "we could not resolve this"
  distinguishes "the tile is too homogeneous" from "nothing matched."
This makes dense-urban behaviour principled rather than a tuning exercise, and it is
computable from data we already have.

== A DISTINCTION TO PRESERVE: SAME ANCHOR IS NOT SAME PROPERTY ==
Two rows landing on the same tile entity are the same BUILDING. Per the settled set model
(see bd-67wx / bd-1oid comments 2026-08-14) SAME PROPERTY additionally requires their
member sets to be equal. In the operator's example the two rows are the same property, and
that is correct — but the general rule must not collapse the two, because the case where it
matters is exactly the false-merge case in bd-1oy8: a REIT position and a CMBS position can
land on the same building and be DIFFERENT collateral. Anchoring gives same-building;
set equality gives same-property.

== IT ALSO STRENGTHENS THE GEOCODE-PLAUSIBILITY CHECK (bd-1a12) ==
That bead adjudicates competing geocodes by asking whether the asserted STREET appears in
the neighbourhood. Attribute anchoring is a stronger version of the same test: does the
neighbourhood contain an entity matching the asserted CHARACTERISTICS? On "241/249 West
74th Street" the two candidate points can be adjudicated by looking for an office/
residential building of the right size near each, with no reliance on street parsing at all
— which matters because street parsing is exactly what failed there.

EXIT CRITERIA:
- Attribute-anchoring as a named solve path: client row -> tile entity, with per-attribute
  structured evidence
- Equivalence derived from shared anchors, never from row-to-row comparison
- Tile-relative rarity weighting over attribute tuples, with the per-tile denominator
  computed and recorded
- Abstention when the matched tuple is not discriminating in that tile, with the tile's
  discriminating power reported
- Same-anchor and same-property kept distinct, with a test on a false-merge fixture
- A worked case resolving two rows to one building using NO name and NO address evidence,
  and a negative case where attributes alone are insufficient and the path abstains

comments.author: Zac
comments.text:
TILE PRE-STITCHING IS ALREADY UNDER WAY IN cmdrvl-curves, LANDING NOW 2026-08-14. Verified
by reading the in-progress beads. This confirms the pre-resolved-tile architecture and
supplies hard facts that change several canon geo assumptions.

== WHAT IS ACTUALLY LANDING ==

  cmdrvl-curves bd-30ho   OVERTURE MAPS, release 2026-07-22.0. Themes buildings,
                          building_parts, PLACES, addresses, divisions. Snowflake DDL
                          APPLIED (OVERTURE_MAPS_FEATURES_HOT / _EXT /
                          OVERTURE_MAPS_FEATURE_H3_COVERAGE plus 14 per-type views);
                          manifest scan running, 0 rows landed yet.
  cmdrvl-curves bd-1ssr   FEMA USA STRUCTURES, 135,321,228 features nationally. National
                          landing IN PROGRESS; DC / AK / AL complete, AR running.
                          FEMA_USA_STRUCTURES_HOT loaded and read back (DC = 64,701 rows).
  cmdrvl-curves bd-3fyv   MICROSOFT GLOBALML FOOTPRINTS, release 2026-07-24. Landing IN
                          PROGRESS: 179 of 2,415 US files, 5,219,860 rows at 14:45Z.
  cmdrvl-curves bd-11uu   HUD USPS ADDRESS VACANCIES -- **BLOCKED**, and not a tile source.
                          HUD restricts it to registered governmental/non-profit users and
                          the sublicense forbids selling, licensing or distributing the
                          data. DO NOT PLAN ANY CANON GEO CAPABILITY ON IT.

NOTE ON "FOURSQUARE OS PLACES": it arrives as OVERTURE'S PLACES THEME, not a separate
Foursquare landing. That is the POI level in bd-2cbs, and it is in the same table family as
Overture buildings.

== FINDING 1: THE LANDED H3 GRAIN IS r4 / r7 / r8. THERE IS NO r9. ==
All three sources partition by h3_r4 and carry H3_R7 and H3_R8 columns. The epic's default
tile is res-9 and it is NOT precomputed anywhere.

AND THERE IS A CONVENIENT COINCIDENCE WORTH DELIBERATELY EXPLOITING: an r8 cell is
approximately 0.737 km2 -- which is almost exactly the area the epic specifies for its WORK
UNIT (an r9 cell plus k-ring 1 = 7 cells = 0.737 km2). So the already-landed H3_R8 column is
essentially the intended work-unit size.
ACTION FOR bd-2b9d: reconsider r9-plus-k-ring versus r8-plus-k-ring as the work unit, now
that r8 is precomputed across every source and r9 is not. This does not change the
requirement to compute cells in canon with a vetted Rust library -- the Snowflake H3 helper
defects (edgar-elt br-2wir) still stand -- but it does mean the warehouse can prefilter at
r8 for free, and the resolution decision now has a third input alongside node count and
human legibility.

== FINDING 2: POLYGON-TO-CELLS RETURNS EMPTY FOR SMALL BUILDINGS. LIVE, MEASURED. ==
From bd-3fyv: "H3_POLYGON_TO_CELLS alone inserted only 116 coverage rows for 354,804 hot
rows because small buildings often contain no H3 r8 cell centroid." Fixed there by using a
guaranteed CENTROID_H3_R8 plus H3_TRY_POLYGON_TO_CELLS.

THIS IS DIRECTLY THE MEMBERSHIP QUESTION bd-10s2 AND bd-2b9d SPECIFY. At r8 or r9 a
building is much smaller than a cell, so "which cells does this polygon cover" is
degenerate: the standard polygon-to-cells contract returns cells whose CENTRES fall inside
the polygon, and for a building that set is almost always EMPTY.
CONSEQUENCE: membership must be CENTROID-ANCHORED with polygon coverage as a supplement for
the large-feature case (parcels, campuses, complexes), NOT the other way round. My earlier
recommendation on bd-10s2 -- "full intersection cover for membership plus a single
deterministic anchor cell" -- is right in intent but inverted in emphasis, and applying it
naively with polygon_to_cells would have silently produced empty membership for nearly every
building. Correct it there.

== FINDING 3: OUR OWN SOURCES CARRY LICENSE OBLIGATIONS. bd-pq5w IS SCOPED TOO NARROWLY. ==
I framed license containment entirely around the CLIENT's licensed parcel layer. The landed
research shows OUR side has obligations too, and they differ per source:
    Overture buildings, divisions      ODbL-1.0            <-- SHARE-ALIKE
    Overture places                    per-source mix of CDLA-Permissive-2.0, Apache-2.0,
                                       CC0-1.0; source license must be retained
    Overture addresses                 source-specific, incl. NAD Access and Usage License
    FEMA USA Structures                CC-BY-4.0, attribution to ORNL and FEMA Geospatial
                                       Response Office REQUIRED
    Microsoft GlobalML                 CDLA-Permissive-2.0 current release; older vintages
                                       need per-release revalidation
bd-30ho states plainly: "License segmentation by source array is REQUIRED before any derived
product ships. Treat as a build-time gate, not a later cleanup."

ODbL SHARE-ALIKE IS THE COMMERCIAL ISSUE AND IT NEEDS AN OPERATOR DECISION, NOT AN
ENGINEERING ONE. A tile is a derived product. If it mixes ODbL Overture buildings with
everything else, the derived tile may inherit share-alike obligations that are
incompatible with a paid distribution model. Options to evaluate deliberately:
  (a) segregate ODbL-derived features into a separately-licensed layer of the tile, with
      the license class carried per feature -- note OVERTURE_MAPS_FEATURES_EXT ALREADY HAS
      LICENSE_CLASS AND LICENSE_TERMS COLUMNS, so the substrate for this exists;
  (b) build the commercial tile from the permissive sources only (FEMA CC-BY, Microsoft
      CDLA) and treat Overture as an internal enrichment;
  (c) accept share-alike and publish the tile openly.
REQUIRED IN bd-pq5w AND bd-1uld: license class per FEATURE in the tile artifact, and a
declared per-tile license posture that composes our obligations with the client's. The
artifact license boundary now has TWO directions, not one.

== FINDING 4: THE ATTRIBUTE CHANNELS FOR bd-272d ARE REAL, AND ONE IS MODELLED ==
Attribute anchoring needs class, size, floors, year. What is actually arriving:
    FEMA        OCC_CLS, PRIM_OCC (occupancy class), SQFEET, PROP_ADDR, UUID, BUILD_ID
    Overture    building class, height, num_floors, GERS id
    Microsoft   height (subset only), confidence, NO ID
    MapPLUTO    BLDGCLASS, LANDUSE, BLDGAREA, LOTAREA, NUMBLDGS, NUMFLOORS, YEARBUILT
So the six-field client contract has a counterpart on the tile side for every field except
YEAR BUILT, which only MapPLUTO supplies -- meaning year-built anchoring works in NYC and
degrades outside it until a national year source exists. Record that as a known national
limitation rather than discovering it later.

CRITICAL: FEMA OCCUPANCY IS MODELLED, NOT SURVEYED. bd-1ssr requires a provenance flag
"so downstream never treats it as surveyed." Attribute anchoring MUST carry that flag into
the evidence and weight modelled attributes below observed ones. A modelled occupancy class
driving a hard eliminative filter (bd-2zdz's assemblage type filter) would be a silent error
generator -- the filter is HARD, so a wrong modelled class removes the correct candidate
before anything is scored. Use modelled occupancy as SUPPORT evidence, never as a hard
filter, unless corroborated.

== FINDING 5: NO STABLE ID CONFIRMED FOR TWO SOURCES ==
Microsoft has no id at all -- bd-3fyv derives "a deterministic feature hash because no
stable id." Overture ADDRESSES are alpha with no stable GERS id either. This confirms
bd-2cbs rule 4 (alias-less participants) and extends it: the alias-less set is Microsoft
footprints AND Overture addresses, not just Microsoft.
A derived feature hash is NOT an alias and must not be minted into a registry -- it will
change whenever the geometry changes, which violates the tile identifier stability contract
in bd-12gh.

== FINDING 6: OVERTURE ADDRESSES CANNOT BE THE ADDRESS-SET SOURCE ==
bd-30ho: "Addresses theme is ALPHA -- do not build a contract against it yet," no stable
GERS id, multi-source licensing including NAD terms. US count 127,719,691.
So bd-35qg's address-set acquisition is NOT solved by Overture. NYC PAD or the per-BIN
addresses in the landed footprints file (bd-397d) remain the path, and the national story
stays open. Do not let the size of the Overture addresses count create false confidence.

== WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE WORKED-CASE CORPUS (bd-tccn) ==
The corpus can now stage its non-MapPLUTO pulls against REAL TABLE NAMES rather than
placeholders:
    EDGAR_DB.SOURCE.FEMA_USA_STRUCTURES_HOT              partially loaded (DC, AK, AL)
    EDGAR_DB.SOURCE.MICROSOFT_GLOBALML_BUILDING_FOOTPRINTS_HOT   partially loaded
    EDGAR_DB.SOURCE.OVERTURE_MAPS_FEATURES_HOT           DDL applied, 0 rows
    plus the *_FEATURE_H3_COVERAGE tables for each
NEW YORK IS NOT YET LOADED IN ANY OF THE THREE. FEMA is alphabetical by state and is at AR;
Microsoft is 179/2415 files; Overture has not started landing. So the full-tile version of
every case remains blocked, exactly as the corpus bead predicted -- but the blocker is now
a KNOWN COMPLETION DATE rather than an unlanded dataset, and the table names and column
shapes are already fixed enough to write the extraction queries against.

comments.author: Zac
comments.text:
ARCHITECTURE SUPERSEDED 2026-08-15 — see docs/PLAN_CANON_GEO.md.

An adversarial multi-model design session produced a materially different architecture,
which then survived a red team that destroyed two intermediate designs. The tile is modelled
as a BOUNDED UNIVERSE and every piece of evidence is a CONSTRAINT; propagation runs to a
fixpoint; the residual model set IS the answer. There is no proposer channel.

THE THREE PROPERTIES THAT MATTER:
- CONFLUENCE. The fixpoint is independent of the order constraints are applied (Tarski 1955;
  Cousot & Cousot 1977; Apt 1999), so determinism is a theorem rather than an engineering
  effort.
- MONOTONICITY. Constraints only add and domains only shrink, so a tile resolved with four
  sources today and six next year yields a TIGHTER residual, never a contradicting one. The
  earlier answer was never wrong, only less resolved.
- STRUCTURAL ABSTENTION. The residual model set is the answer. No threshold anywhere.

THE KEY DESIGN RULE IS rho, THE SOUNDNESS DISCIPLINE. Every source attribute enters the
solver only through a declared versioned relaxation mapping it to the WEAKEST constraint the
source can actually support. An interpolated geocode becomes a 150m disc rather than a
location. A parcel ADDRESS becomes "one of this lot's addresses" rather than functional
equality. OWNERNAME equal PERMITS an assemblage; OWNERNAME different constrains NOTHING.
Every noisy channel is admitted only in its sound direction — which is what dissolved the
proposer dilemma that broke the two earlier designs.

AND THE COMMERCIAL CONSEQUENCE: if every rho is sound, the true assignment is in the model
set, so AN EMPTY MODEL SET IS A PROOF that a named source violated its own published error
model — attributable, falsifiable, and mailable to the vendor.

Read PLAN_CANON_GEO.md before starting any geo work. Section 11 carries the bead-by-bead
supersession table. Appendix A covers frozen-weight observers and imagery sources. APPENDIX
B RECORDS THE FIRST HARD MEASUREMENT, WHICH FALSIFIED A LOAD-BEARING CLAIM — read it before
trusting any performance number in the plan.

Raw session artifacts, including the red team and the adversarial reviews, are preserved
under docs/geo_design_session/ with a reading guide.

title: [CANON-V1/P02.1] Define the Canon project manifest and configuration boundary
description:
## Background
Operators need one durable declaration of inputs, registries, profiles, strategies, extensions, outputs, review policy, and resource limits. Today those choices are scattered across long command lines and ambient paths, making repeated identity runs difficult to audit or reproduce.

## Technical Approach
Specify a versioned `canon.project.v1` manifest with explicit project ID, source declarations, cluster/link modes, registry and strategy package references, profile parameters, output projections, review thresholds, temporal scope, resource budgets, and offline/network policy. Define path resolution relative to the manifest, schema evolution, environment interpolation, and a hard boundary preventing secrets from entering manifests or receipts.

## Success Criteria
- JSON Schema and Rust types reject unknown or contradictory fields with stable refusal codes.
- Every path, package, strategy, profile, output, and limit has one precedence rule.
- Secrets use typed external handles and are redacted from describe, plan, logs, and artifacts.
- Minimal neutral, multi-source, and unknown-extension projects validate without ambient configuration.

## Test Plan
Validate minimal, complete, malformed, path-traversal, secret-leak, incompatible-mode, unknown-extension, and future-version fixtures twice; compare diagnostics byte-for-byte and log fixture, exit/refusal code, and schema hash.

## RESERVATIONS
- `src/project/mod.rs`
- `src/project/manifest.rs`
- `schemas/canon.project.v1.schema.json`
- `tests/fixtures/project/minimal.toml`
- `tests/project_manifest.rs`

## Considerations
Keep the manifest declarative. It names desired work and immutable dependencies; it cannot embed executable code or silently discover mutable state.
close_reason: Implemented canon.project.v1 contract boundary and verified focused rustfmt/clippy/test gate

title: [CANON-V1/P07.R6j] Resolve review-export strategy replay from artifact context
description: Background: native link artifacts persist the strategy source display string exactly as supplied. Link-side binding replay is being made artifact-context aware and hash-bound, but native review export still loads a relative strategy source against the ambient process cwd. A valid committed artifact chain can therefore replay from one directory and refuse from another. Technical approach: resolve path-like relative strategy sources through deterministic link-artifact/work-dir context candidates, accept only a source whose id, version, and content hash match both run metadata and link decisions, and fail closed on missing, stale, ambiguous, or mismatched candidates. Do not relax artifact path guards or use cwd as authority. Success: review export is byte/semantic stable across cwd changes; tampered and unrelated cwd sources refuse before writes; absolute existing behavior remains compatible. RESERVATIONS: src/lib.rs and focused native review integration tests.

title: Wire run() orchestration
description:
Implement the run() function in src/lib.rs that wires all modules together. This bead depends on bd-1do ONLY and runs IN PARALLEL with Phase 1 features — it is written against the stub function signatures, not real implementations.

TARGET FILE: src/lib.rs (run() function only — do NOT modify shared types, mod declarations, or src/main.rs). Reserve src/lib.rs only.

The function calls each module stub in sequence (~50 lines):

1. Handle info commands (--version, --describe, --schema) — early return exit 0
2. Validate required args present (input, registry, column)
3. Warn on stderr if --map-out is set with --emit json (the mapping already IS stdout; ignore --map-out but warn)
4. Load registry: registry::load(&cli.registry)?
5. Hash input file bytes with blake3 for witness (BEFORE parse)
6. Parse input: input::parse(&cli.input, &cli.column, cli.max_rows, cli.max_bytes)?
7. Validate emit mode: if cli.emit == Csv && input_values.format == Jsonl => refuse E_EMIT_FORMAT
8. Resolve: lookup::resolve(&input_values, &registry)?
9. Determine outcome from summary (resolved==0 => Unresolved, unresolved==0 => Resolved, else Partial). NOTE: resolved==0 && unresolved==0 should never happen — the input module raises E_EMPTY_INPUT for that case. Add a debug_assert as a safety net.
10. Emit output:
   - JSON mode: json_str = output::json::emit(result, registry.meta); print json_str to stdout (no --map-out in this mode, already warned in step 3)
   - CSV mode: wrap stdout in a BLAKE3 hashing tee writer, then call output::csv::emit(&mut tee_writer, ...). The CSV module takes a generic writer (&mut impl Write), NOT stdout directly — this enables witness hashing. After emit, if --map-out is set, write output::json::emit(result, registry.meta) to the sidecar file.
11. Hash output bytes for witness (JSON: hash json_str bytes; CSV: finalize the tee_writer's hasher)
12. Record witness (unless --no-witness)
13. Return exit code: 0=Resolved, 1=Partial/Unresolved, 2=Refusal

Error handling: any Refusal from steps 4-8 is caught, serialized via refusal.to_canon_output(), routed to stdout (json mode) or stderr (csv mode), return exit 2.

IMPORTANT: This compiles against bd-1do's stubs. When Phase 1 agents replace stubs with real implementations, run() works WITHOUT MODIFICATION — the shared types are the contract. Do not change function signatures defined in stubs.

VERIFICATION: cargo check passes for entire project. cargo run -- --version prints version.
acceptance_criteria: cargo check passes. run() calls all module APIs in correct order. Refusal routing (stdout vs stderr) correct for both emit modes. Hashing tee for CSV output wired. --map-out sidecar wired. Outcome derivation from summary counts correct.
notes: IMPORTANT: Do NOT modify src/main.rs — it is already complete from bd-1do (parses Cli, calls run(), maps exit code). This bead ONLY modifies the run() function body in src/lib.rs. Reserve src/lib.rs only.
close_reason: Completed run() orchestration wiring in src/lib.rs, fixed refusal routing/error mapping, and validated with cargo check, cargo run -- --version, and full quality gate

title: [CANON-V1/P06.2] Define extensible role and relationship vocabularies
description:
## Background
Roles and relationships are domain knowledge, yet Canon must preserve them separately from identity so operators can model assignments, hierarchy, and context without accidental merges.

## Technical Approach
Define a vocabulary package with namespaced predicates/roles, subject/object type constraints, direction, cardinality hints, interval requirements, identity implication fixed to false by default, synonyms for intake, and extension compatibility. Generic relation artifacts validate against the pinned package but treat IDs opaquely.

## Success Criteria
- New role and relationship kinds require only a package, not a Canon release.
- Role synonyms normalize to stable IDs without resolving the parties involved.
- Relation-only facts cannot become aliases or same-as evidence unless a separate explicit identity policy consumes them as context.
- Unknown namespaced extensions survive import/export when the package is present.

## Test Plan
Use neutral invented role sets with transfers, co-assignees, invalid subject/object types, unknown extensions, synonym ambiguity, and cycles. Assert exact lookup is unchanged by relation-only facts.

## RESERVATIONS
- `src/extensions/vocabulary.rs`
- `schemas/canon.extension.vocabulary.v1.schema.json`
- `tests/extensions_vocabulary.rs`

title: canon strategy — frozen script resolution by schema shape + skill hash
description:
New resolution mode for canon: resolve a schema shape + skill hash to a frozen champion script.

## Concept

Canon resolves messy inputs to canonical outputs using versioned registries. Canon strategy extends this to resolve schema shapes to frozen scripts:

- Input: schema fingerprint (from profile stats) + skill hash (from the skill file that authored the script)
- Output: a frozen Python/shell script that passed verify + assess + airlock
- Registry: versioned, grows across clients, compounds per PRC-COMPOUND-006

## Resolution tiers

Same semantics as entity canon:
- EXACT: identical columns, types, cardinalities → run frozen champion
- COMPATIBLE: same columns, different cardinalities → run frozen champion (script still works)
- PARTIAL: overlapping columns, some missing → ESCALATE (LLM rewrites)
- UNRESOLVED: different domain → LLM authors new script, gates it, registers on success

## Registration flow

1. profile stats produces schema fingerprint
2. Skill file is hashed (the skill that authored the script is part of the lookup key)
3. canon strategy resolve checks registry for (schema shape, skill hash) tuple
4. If UNRESOLVED: LLM writes script → verify PASS → assess PROCEED → canon strategy register
5. If RESOLVED: frozen script runs directly, no LLM, deterministic output

## Why skill hash matters

The same schema could produce different scripts depending on which skill authored it. A procurement skill and a compliance skill both operating on the same CSV shape should resolve to different champion scripts. Hashing the skill into the lookup key prevents cross-skill contamination.

## Why this is canon, not a new primitive

- Registry is the moat (same as entity canon)
- Versioning is built in (canon already versions registries)
- Resolution semantics are identical (exact/compatible/partial/unresolved)
- Compounds across clients (PRC-COMPOUND-006)
- Dual-copy model applies (client gets output, CMD+RVL retains registry)

## Origin

Observed during procurement spine skill testing: four runs on the same data produced four different grand totals ($83K, $94K, $83K, different). All within sanity bounds, all using the same median fallback. The variation comes from the LLM writing slightly different Python each time. Canon strategy would freeze the first passing script and reuse it — same shape, same script, same numbers, every time.
close_reason: Implemented canon strategy resolve/register for frozen script resolution by schema shape plus skill hash; added docs/operator metadata and tests; validated with cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, and cargo test.

title: OpenFIGI provider for registry materializer
description:
## Summary

Implement the OpenFIGI provider for `canon registry build`. This is the first real provider — it queries the OpenFIGI API (https://www.openfigi.com/api) and materializes FIGI mappings into a standard canon registry.

## What is OpenFIGI

The Financial Instrument Global Identifier (FIGI) is an open standard published by the Object Management Group (OMG). OpenFIGI is Bloomberg's free API that maps between FIGIs and other identifier types (CUSIP, ISIN, SEDOL, ticker, composite FIGI). It is the canonical cross-reference for financial instrument identifiers.

**API details:**
- Endpoint: `https://api.openfigi.com/v3/mapping`
- Method: POST with JSON array of mapping jobs
- Rate limits: 25 requests/minute (free, no API key), 250 requests/minute (with free API key)
- Batch size: up to 100 identifiers per request
- No authentication required for basic use; optional API key via `X-OPENFIGI-APIKEY` header for higher rate limits

## Design

### Provider implementation

```rust
pub struct OpenFigiProvider {
    api_key: Option<String>,   // optional, from --provider-config or env OPENFIGI_API_KEY
    base_url: String,          // default: https://api.openfigi.com/v3/mapping
    id_type: String,           // "ID_CUSIP", "ID_ISIN", "ID_SEDOL", etc.
}
```

### API request format

```json
[
  {"idType": "ID_CUSIP", "idValue": "037833100"},
  {"idType": "ID_CUSIP", "idValue": "594918104"},
  {"idType": "ID_CUSIP", "idValue": "17275R102"}
]
```

### API response format

Each identifier returns zero or more FIGI records:

```json
[
  {"data": [{"figi": "BBG000B9XRY4", "name": "APPLE INC", "ticker": "AAPL", "exchCode": "US", "compositeFIGI": "BBG000B9XRY4", "securityType": "Common Stock"}]},
  {"data": [{"figi": "BBG000BPH459", "name": "MICROSOFT CORP", "ticker": "MSFT", ...}]},
  {"data": [{"figi": "BBG00QFYFL90", "name": "COINBASE GLOBAL INC", "ticker": "COIN", ...}]}
]
```

### Mapping extraction

From each OpenFIGI response, extract multiple mapping types into separate registry files:

| Registry file | Mapping | Example |
|--------------|---------|---------|
| cusip-to-figi.json | CUSIP → composite FIGI | 037833100 → BBG000B9XRY4 |
| cusip-to-ticker.json | CUSIP → ticker | 037833100 → AAPL |
| cusip-to-name.json | CUSIP → security name | 037833100 → APPLE INC |

Each mapping entry uses the standard canon format:
```json
{"input": "037833100", "canonical_id": "BBG000B9XRY4", "canonical_type": "composite_figi", "rule_id": "OPENFIGI_CUSIP_TO_FIGI"}
```

### Multi-result handling

OpenFIGI can return multiple FIGIs for a single CUSIP (different share classes, exchanges, security types). The provider must handle this:

- **composite_figi** is usually unique per identifier — prefer this as the primary mapping
- If multiple results, take the one matching the most common security type for the id type (e.g., "Common Stock" for equity CUSIPs)
- Record all results in _build.json for transparency, but the registry file gets the best single match
- If no clear winner, mark as ambiguous in _build.json and exclude from registry (conservative — don't guess)

### CLI integration

```bash
# Basic: materialize CUSIPs from a positions file
canon registry build --source openfigi \
  --seed positions.csv --seed-column cusip \
  --output registries/openfigi-cusip/ \
  --version "2026.03.05"

# With API key for higher rate limits
OPENFIGI_API_KEY=xxx canon registry build --source openfigi \
  --seed positions.csv --seed-column cusip \
  --output registries/openfigi-cusip/ \
  --version "2026.03.05"

# ISINs instead of CUSIPs
canon registry build --source openfigi \
  --seed positions.csv --seed-column isin \
  --provider-config id_type=ID_ISIN \
  --output registries/openfigi-isin/ \
  --version "2026.03.05"
```

### Rate limiting

- Free tier: 25 req/min, 100 IDs per request = 2,500 IDs/minute
- With API key: 250 req/min = 25,000 IDs/minute
- For a typical 5,000-CUSIP seed list: ~2 minutes (free) or ~12 seconds (with key)
- Provider reports rate limit status via the trait's rate_limit() method
- Framework handles backoff and retry on 429 responses

## Acceptance criteria

- OpenFIGI provider implements the RegistryProvider trait from bd-2zo
- Queries the real OpenFIGI API (integration tests can use a mock HTTP server)
- Respects rate limits (25/min free, 250/min with key)
- Batches identifiers (100 per request)
- Handles multi-result responses conservatively (composite FIGI preferred, ambiguous excluded)
- Supports CUSIP, ISIN, and SEDOL as seed id types via --provider-config
- Optional API key via env var or --provider-config
- Produced registry is a valid, standard canon registry that resolves normally
- _build.json includes: API calls made, identifiers submitted, resolved, failed, ambiguous, wall clock time
- Unit tests: mock HTTP responses for success, partial failure, rate limit, ambiguous multi-result
- Integration test: end-to-end with mock server → registry → canon resolution
close_reason: Added OpenFIGI provider support with provider-config plumbing, conservative multi-result handling, retry-aware HTTP fetches, provenance diagnostics, and end-to-end mock-server coverage

title: [CANON-V1/P06.8] Support related-but-distinct and hierarchy policy as extensions
description:
## Background
Near-name relations such as parent/child, brand/operator, predecessor/successor, branch/whole, or product/issuer appear in many domains. Canon needs a generic way to preserve relation evidence and prevent transitive over-merges.

## Technical Approach
Define packaged relationship constraints and review semantics over generic relation IDs: related-but-distinct vetoes, allowed identity implications only through explicit sourced equality facts, temporal succession, graph cardinality/cycle policy, and transitive merge guards. Store relation decisions and cannot-link patches independently.

## Success Criteria
- A new hierarchy vocabulary requires no core enum or special case.
- Known related-distinct pairs cannot auto-merge through similarity or shared context.
- Temporal succession does not silently collapse historical identities.
- Review can choose same, distinct, related, or uncertain with separate artifacts.

## Test Plan
Use invented parent/child, brand/operator, successor, shared-address, and graph-cycle cases. Test pair order, transitive closure pressure, temporal boundaries, and relation-only promotion.

## RESERVATIONS
- `src/extensions/relation_policy.rs`
- `schemas/canon.relation.policy.v1.schema.json`
- `tests/extensions_relation_policy.rs`

## Considerations
Canon enforces generic identity separation; it does not decide the legal significance of a relationship.

title: [CANON-V1/P07.3] Enforce a domain-neutral engine and extension firewall
description:
## Background
Canon's open-source value depends on being a reusable compiler, not an application with hidden industry assumptions. Configuration extensibility is insufficient if domain vocabulary or source behavior leaks into core code.

Define allowed dependencies between core engine, generic extensions, neutral fixtures, and out-of-tree deployments. Add compile-time/module boundaries where useful, a denylist/source scan for known shipped-domain vocabulary, schema tests using unknown opaque IDs, and a conformance harness that loads two unrelated neutral packages. - Core source contains no industry-specific enum, conditional, identifier list, thresholds, provider client, or ontology.
- An unknown domain package can exercise every stage without code changes.
- Removing all optional external deployment assets leaves build, tests, docs, and release unchanged.
- Any future domain leakage fails an automated architecture check with a precise path and rule.

Scan core and generated contracts, run multiple invented domains, deliberately inject a forbidden term/branch in a fixture of the checker, and verify public CI needs no private assets.

title: [CANON-V1/P04.5] Rank inbox work by deterministic expected coverage value
description:
## Background
A compounding workflow needs to tell the operator what registry improvement to make next and why. A black-box score would undermine that trust.

## Technical Approach
Create a versioned priority policy that combines recurrence, unique sources/deals/projects, role criticality, exposure band, downstream consumers, candidate readiness, ambiguity cost, review effort, age, and drift. Emit component scores, uncertainty flags, and sensitivity analysis. Support queue partitions by profile, registry, role, source, and privacy class.

## Success Criteria
- The ordering is stable with deterministic tie-breaks and fully decomposable scores.
- Policy changes produce an explainable rerank without rewriting source events.
- High-impact ambiguous items can outrank easy low-value aliases without being auto-decided.
- Unknown inputs and capped outliers have explicit contributions.

## Test Plan
Golden-test ranking, ties, missing signals, extreme values, policy revisions, and shuffled inputs. Add monotonic/metamorphic assertions for each component and snapshot explanations.

title: canon geo: H3 tile blocking with k-ring buffer and halo reconciliation
description:
Blocking by tile replaces ngram/postings blocking. It is EXACT where
name-trigram blocking is lossy in both directions: a feature in one cell never
matches one three cells away.

DESIGN:
- H3 res-9 default (0.105 km2, ~201m edge, roughly a city block). Confirm
  against REAL node-count distributions before fixing the default -- pull a
  dense Manhattan cell and a suburban cell and measure.
- Work unit is the cell PLUS its k-ring 1 neighbours (7 cells, 0.737 km2) so
  boundary features can resolve.
- HALO RECONCILIATION: keep only decisions anchored in the centre cell, discard
  the rest. Without this, boundary buildings either get orphaned or get resolved
  twice with different outcomes.
- Emit the block artifact in the same shape as entity/block_artifact.rs so
  diagnostics and candidate budgets work unchanged.

EXIT CRITERIA:
- Deterministic cell assignment and stable node ordering within a tile
- Halo decisions provably discarded; no double-minting across adjacent tiles
- Node-count distribution measured on real data, default resolution justified

Depends on: skeleton
Parent: bd-2kjx

comments.author: zac
comments.text:
TWO NOTES 2026-08-14.

1. THE TILE IS ALSO THE VIEWPORT. A res-9 cell plus k-ring 1 is 0.737 km2, roughly four city blocks — which is exactly the zoom at which a human can judge 'is that the right building'. The blocking unit and the natural rendering extent coincide. That is unusual and worth exploiting deliberately when choosing the default resolution: this bead already says to confirm res-9 against real node-count distributions, and HUMAN LEGIBILITY OF THE TILE AS A MAP EXTENT should be a second criterion alongside node count. See bd-101v (visual evidence card).

2. SNOWFLAKE H3 HELPERS RETURNED BAD GEOMETRY — do not build blocking on them without verifying. Asked for the r9 cell and k-ring for lon -73.977264 lat 40.753429 via H3_LATLNG_TO_CELL_STRING, H3_CELL_TO_BOUNDARY and H3_GRID_DISK. The cell id came back plausible (892a100d26bffff) but the BOUNDARY was wrong: its edges compute to roughly 27-48 m against an expected r9 edge of about 174 m, and the returned k-ring listed 892a100d26fffff THREE TIMES with rings that were not consistent hexagons. Filed against edgar-elt as br-2ovc with the full query and outputs.

Consequence for this bead: cell ASSIGNMENT may be fine while cell GEOMETRY is not, and halo reconciliation depends on neighbour identity being correct. Verify H3_GRID_DISK returns six distinct neighbours before relying on k-ring buffering, and prefer a vetted H3 library in the Rust path over warehouse helpers for anything the decision depends on.

comments.author: Zac
comments.text:
REALITY CHECK 2026-08-14 — BLOCKING IS NEW CODE, AND THE CLIENT LAYER IS NOW YOUR JOB.

1. "EMIT THE BLOCK ARTIFACT IN THE SAME SHAPE AS entity/block_artifact.rs" IS RIGHT.
   That part reuses cleanly — block_artifact.rs (1,193 LOC) plus budget.rs and the
   candidate/diagnostics path work unchanged.

2. BUT THE OPERATOR ITSELF IS NEW. src/entity/block.rs:52 defines
   `BlockCandidateOperator` as a CLOSED 3-VARIANT ENUM:
     NgramTopK | RareTokenOverlap | AliasPatchMatch
   All three are postings/text operators driven by EntityPostingIndex / EntityNgramIndex.
   There is no extension point, no trait object, no plugin. H3 tile blocking is a new
   variant (or, per bd-3ccc, geo's own parallel enum in src/geo/) plus a new index type
   that is a cell->member map rather than a postings index. Budget it as new.

3. H3 LIBRARY — SETTLED (operator decision 2026-08-14). Use a pure-Rust H3 port (h3o).
   No C bindings, deterministic, and it makes client-layer indexing possible inside
   canon, which is now a requirement rather than a nicety.

4. CLIENT-LAYER H3 INGEST IS CANON'S JOB (operator decision 2026-08-14, see bd-2kjx
   BYOP). Our tiles ship pre-indexed. The client's licensed parcel extract (ATTOM/Regrid)
   does NOT. The client must not be required to own H3 tooling. See the new client-layer
   tile ingest bead — this bead owns the blocking semantics, that one owns getting client
   geometry into the same cell space.

5. THE SNOWFLAKE H3 WARNING NOW HAS A SECOND CONSEQUENCE. The existing comment records
   that H3_CELL_TO_BOUNDARY returned edges of ~27-48 m against an expected ~174 m and
   that H3_GRID_DISK listed a neighbour three times. Beyond "prefer a vetted Rust
   library," note that MapPLUTO landed with h3_r7 and h3_r8 columns COMPUTED BY THOSE
   SAME SNOWFLAKE HELPERS (per the bd-35ae landing receipt). If cell ASSIGNMENT is also
   affected — not just boundary geometry — then the warehouse H3 columns are unsafe as a
   blocking key and canon must recompute cells from coordinates with h3o. VERIFY
   ASSIGNMENT PARITY between the warehouse h3_r7/h3_r8 columns and h3o before relying on
   the landed columns for anything. Add this as an explicit exit criterion.

6. RESOLUTION DEFAULT — THREE CRITERIA NOW, NOT TWO.
   (a) node-count distribution on real data (dense Manhattan cell vs suburban cell), as
       already written;
   (b) human legibility as a map extent, per the existing comment and bd-101v;
   (c) NEW — CLIENT COVERAGE GRANULARITY. Under BYOP the tile is also the unit at which
       "does the client's layer cover this area" is answered. A resolution that is much
       finer than the client's coverage boundaries produces a huge number of
       trivially-uncovered tiles; much coarser produces tiles that are partially covered,
       which is worse because it hides the gap. r9 is still the likely answer but the
       coverage-granularity criterion must be measured, not assumed.

7. HALO RECONCILIATION UNDER BYOP. "Keep only decisions anchored in the centre cell" is
   correct and becomes MORE important with two geometry sources: a client parcel whose
   centroid sits in a halo cell must not be minted twice when the neighbouring tile runs.
   The anchor rule must be defined on a DETERMINISTIC PROPERTY OF THE GEOMETRY (e.g.
   the cell containing the polygon's representative point under an exact predicate), not
   on which source supplied it or on iteration order.

EXIT CRITERIA — AMENDED:
- Deterministic cell assignment and stable node ordering within a tile
- Halo decisions provably discarded; no double-minting across adjacent tiles, PROVEN by
  running two adjacent tiles independently and asserting the union has no duplicate
  minted IDs and no orphaned boundary features
- Node-count distribution measured on real data; default resolution justified against
  all three criteria above
- h3o vs warehouse h3_r7/h3_r8 cell-assignment parity verified, or the warehouse columns
  explicitly declared unsafe for blocking
- Client-layer geometry lands in the same cell space as our tiles, verified on a fixture
  with deliberate coverage holes

comments.author: Zac
comments.text:
VERIFIED FACTS FROM STRUCTURED TOOL OUTPUT 2026-08-14. Method: `cmdrvl --json orchestrator
query --tenant salt --raw`, reading `.data.response.tool_responses[].structuredContent`
rather than Loom's prose answer. The underlying tool is `data__edgar_data_run_query`, which
returns the literal SQL it ran plus `{ok, columns, rows}` or `{ok:false, error}`. Every
fact below is a literal returned value.

THIS METHOD CHANGE IS THE FINDING THAT MATTERS MOST. Three claims earlier in this session
came from Loom's prose and were wrong. The structured path caught the third one
immediately, and the skill documentation already prescribed it ("prefer
tool_responses[*].structuredContent from --raw over prose"). ALL CORPUS EXTRACTS MUST USE
THE STRUCTURED PATH AND RECORD THE EMITTED SQL.

=========================================================================
1. THE LANDED MapPLUTO TABLE PROJECTS A SUBSET OF FIELDS. `UNITSTOTAL` DOES NOT EXIST.
=========================================================================
A prior extract reported "UNITSTOTAL 178" for BBL 1014477501. The structured output shows
that query FAILED: `invalid identifier 'UNITSTOTAL'`. The value was fabricated in prose.

LITERAL COLUMN LIST of EDGAR_DB.SOURCE.NYC_DCP_MAPPLUTO_HOT:
  RELEASE, RELEASE_DT, VARIANT, SOURCE_ROW_NUMBER, VALID_FROM_RELEASE_DT,
  VALID_TO_RELEASE_DT, IS_CURRENT_RELEASE, COUNTRY, STATE, BOROUGH_PARTITION, OBJECTID,
  BOROUGH, BLOCK, LOT, BBL, ADDRESS, BLDGCLASS, LANDUSE, YEARBUILT, LOTAREA, BLDGAREA,
  NUMBLDGS, NUMFLOORS, OWNERNAME, PLUTOMAPID, GEOM_GEOG, CENTROID_GEOG, CENTROID_LON,
  CENTROID_LAT, BBOX_XMIN, BBOX_YMIN, BBOX_XMAX, BBOX_YMAX, H3_R7, H3_R8, GEOM_CRS,
  SOURCE_GEOM_CRS, SOURCE_CHANNEL, SOURCE_FILENAME, ROW_PAYLOAD, LOADED_AT

CONSEQUENCES:
- MapPLUTO publishes roughly ninety fields; the landed table projects about twenty and puts
  the remainder in ROW_PAYLOAD. Anything not projected requires digging into ROW_PAYLOAD,
  which is a different access pattern and a different cost.
- THE SIX-FIELD CLIENT CONTRACT IS SATISFIED BY PROJECTED COLUMNS, which is good news:
  building size -> BLDGAREA, year built -> YEARBUILT, property type -> BLDGCLASS + LANDUSE.
  No ROW_PAYLOAD dig needed for the core cascade.
- UNIT COUNTS (UnitsTotal, UnitsRes) ARE NOT PROJECTED. Assemblage subset-sum for
  multifamily (case 7) may want them. Confirm they exist in ROW_PAYLOAD before designing
  around them.

=========================================================================
2. BBL IS STORED AS A STRING WITH A TRAILING ".0" AND IS NOT JOIN-READY.
=========================================================================
Literal returned value: "BBL": "1014477501.0"

This is a direct problem for canon. Core lookup is EXACT BYTE MATCH AFTER ASCII-TRIM, so
"1014477501" would NOT resolve against "1014477501.0". Any registry built from this column
without normalization silently fails to match the identifier every other NYC source uses,
and every downstream join against ACRIS, PLUTO, or the footprints file has the same
exposure.
REQUIRED: BBL normalization is a declared, versioned step in the ingest, not an incidental
cast. It belongs in the geo profile's normalization vocabulary alongside the geometry
canonicalization, and it needs a negative test.

=========================================================================
3. CASE 6 IS A CONDO, AND THE CONDO TRAP IS LIVE IN IT.
=========================================================================
Literal rows for BBL prefix 10144775:

  BBL 1014477501.0  "305 EAST 72 STREET"  BLDGCLASS RM  LOTAREA 37,800
                    BLDGAREA 194,949  NUMBLDGS 2  NUMFLOORS 17  YEARBUILT 1961
                    OWNERNAME "305/72 CONDOMINIUM"
  BBL 1014477502.0  "1355 1 AVENUE"       BLDGCLASS RM  LOTAREA  5,100
                    BLDGAREA 102,719  NUMBLDGS 1  NUMFLOORS 31  YEARBUILT 2009
                    OWNERNAME "UNAVAILABLE OWNER"

FOUR THINGS THIS ESTABLISHES:
a) OWNERNAME "305/72 CONDOMINIUM" and the 75xx lot range confirm these are CONDO BILLING
   BBLs. The condo trap named in OC-0048 and measured in the multi-lot fan-out is present
   in the very property picked to illustrate a different case.
b) A PRIOR CLAIM IS CORRECTED. I wrote that five asserted addresses "resolve to ONE BBL."
   Not established. At least two condo BBLs sit here with DIFFERENT street frontages —
   East 72 Street and 1 Avenue. The property's a/k/a set names E 72nd, 2nd Avenue and
   E 73rd; 1 Avenue is a fourth frontage not in that set. The containment test still has to
   be run properly.
c) YEARBUILT 1961 vs 2009 ON ADJACENT CONDO LOTS IS A LIVE REDEVELOPMENT SIGNAL — exactly
   the case hypothesised on bd-gs6n, that a large year-built spread on overlapping or
   adjacent footprints is a TEMPORAL finding rather than a match failure. It is real and it
   is in the first property examined closely.
d) NUMBLDGS 2 on one condo BBL. The building level is still needed and the BBL-to-BIN
   bridge (landed, bd-397d) is still the next pull.

=========================================================================
4. THE TABLE IS STRUCTURALLY BITEMPORAL ALREADY.
=========================================================================
RELEASE, RELEASE_DT, VALID_FROM_RELEASE_DT, VALID_TO_RELEASE_DT, IS_CURRENT_RELEASE are all
present. The landing contract (cmdrvl-curves bd-qbno) was built for multiple releases even
though OC-0048 records that only the current one is loaded.
CONSEQUENCE: the as-of machinery bd-12gh and bd-1oy8 need does not require a schema change,
only additional releases. Check `SELECT DISTINCT RELEASE, RELEASE_DT` before assuming case
9's temporal arc is blocked — cmdrvl-curves bd-33t6 may be closer to done than the outcome
document states.

=========================================================================
5. REPROJECTION PROVENANCE IS ALREADY RECORDED. THIS DIRECTLY SERVES bd-3nc7.
=========================================================================
GEOM_CRS and SOURCE_GEOM_CRS are projected columns. So the EPSG:2263 -> WGS84 transform
that the predicate-regime bead has to reason about is documented in the table itself rather
than needing archaeology. Read those columns first when starting bd-3nc7.

=========================================================================
6. H3_R7 AND H3_R8 ARE PRESENT. H3_R9 IS NOT.
=========================================================================
The epic's default tile is res-9. It is not precomputed. Canon computes it itself, which is
what bd-2b9d already requires for a separate reason — the Snowflake H3 helpers returned
malformed boundaries and a bad k-ring (edgar-elt br-2wir). Both reasons now point the same
way: compute r9 in canon with a vetted Rust H3 library, and treat the warehouse H3 columns
as a coarse prefilter at most.

=========================================================================
7. GEOCODIO SOURCE SEMANTICS — CONFIRMED BY OPERATOR.
=========================================================================
Geocodio reports the underlying address dataset that produced each match. So SOURCE values
like "TIGER/Line(R) dataset from the US Census Bureau" and "City of New York" are
per-result attribution from ONE service, not competing vendors — and MULTIPLE SOURCED
GEOCODES PER PROPERTY ARE EXPECTED AND NORMAL.
This VINDICATES the capability in bd-1a12 while keeping the retraction of the mechanism.
SOURCE becomes usable EVIDENCE: a local authoritative dataset and a national interpolated
one carry different reliability.
BUT NOTE THE COUNTEREXAMPLE ALREADY IN HAND: on "241/249 West 74th Street" the
"City of New York" sourced row is the WRONG one (W 49th St, rooftop, score 0.92) and the
TIGER/Line row is right (W 74th St, range_interpolation, score 1.00). So SOURCE is not a
safe selector either, any more than ACCURACY_TYPE or ACCURACY_SCORE are. Three fields, none
individually decisive, all disagreeing — which is precisely the argument for letting the
tile adjudicate.

comments.author: Zac
comments.text:
TILE PRE-STITCHING IS ALREADY UNDER WAY IN cmdrvl-curves, LANDING NOW 2026-08-14. Verified
by reading the in-progress beads. This confirms the pre-resolved-tile architecture and
supplies hard facts that change several canon geo assumptions.

== WHAT IS ACTUALLY LANDING ==

  cmdrvl-curves bd-30ho   OVERTURE MAPS, release 2026-07-22.0. Themes buildings,
                          building_parts, PLACES, addresses, divisions. Snowflake DDL
                          APPLIED (OVERTURE_MAPS_FEATURES_HOT / _EXT /
                          OVERTURE_MAPS_FEATURE_H3_COVERAGE plus 14 per-type views);
                          manifest scan running, 0 rows landed yet.
  cmdrvl-curves bd-1ssr   FEMA USA STRUCTURES, 135,321,228 features nationally. National
                          landing IN PROGRESS; DC / AK / AL complete, AR running.
                          FEMA_USA_STRUCTURES_HOT loaded and read back (DC = 64,701 rows).
  cmdrvl-curves bd-3fyv   MICROSOFT GLOBALML FOOTPRINTS, release 2026-07-24. Landing IN
                          PROGRESS: 179 of 2,415 US files, 5,219,860 rows at 14:45Z.
  cmdrvl-curves bd-11uu   HUD USPS ADDRESS VACANCIES -- **BLOCKED**, and not a tile source.
                          HUD restricts it to registered governmental/non-profit users and
                          the sublicense forbids selling, licensing or distributing the
                          data. DO NOT PLAN ANY CANON GEO CAPABILITY ON IT.

NOTE ON "FOURSQUARE OS PLACES": it arrives as OVERTURE'S PLACES THEME, not a separate
Foursquare landing. That is the POI level in bd-2cbs, and it is in the same table family as
Overture buildings.

== FINDING 1: THE LANDED H3 GRAIN IS r4 / r7 / r8. THERE IS NO r9. ==
All three sources partition by h3_r4 and carry H3_R7 and H3_R8 columns. The epic's default
tile is res-9 and it is NOT precomputed anywhere.

AND THERE IS A CONVENIENT COINCIDENCE WORTH DELIBERATELY EXPLOITING: an r8 cell is
approximately 0.737 km2 -- which is almost exactly the area the epic specifies for its WORK
UNIT (an r9 cell plus k-ring 1 = 7 cells = 0.737 km2). So the already-landed H3_R8 column is
essentially the intended work-unit size.
ACTION FOR bd-2b9d: reconsider r9-plus-k-ring versus r8-plus-k-ring as the work unit, now
that r8 is precomputed across every source and r9 is not. This does not change the
requirement to compute cells in canon with a vetted Rust library -- the Snowflake H3 helper
defects (edgar-elt br-2wir) still stand -- but it does mean the warehouse can prefilter at
r8 for free, and the resolution decision now has a third input alongside node count and
human legibility.

== FINDING 2: POLYGON-TO-CELLS RETURNS EMPTY FOR SMALL BUILDINGS. LIVE, MEASURED. ==
From bd-3fyv: "H3_POLYGON_TO_CELLS alone inserted only 116 coverage rows for 354,804 hot
rows because small buildings often contain no H3 r8 cell centroid." Fixed there by using a
guaranteed CENTROID_H3_R8 plus H3_TRY_POLYGON_TO_CELLS.

THIS IS DIRECTLY THE MEMBERSHIP QUESTION bd-10s2 AND bd-2b9d SPECIFY. At r8 or r9 a
building is much smaller than a cell, so "which cells does this polygon cover" is
degenerate: the standard polygon-to-cells contract returns cells whose CENTRES fall inside
the polygon, and for a building that set is almost always EMPTY.
CONSEQUENCE: membership must be CENTROID-ANCHORED with polygon coverage as a supplement for
the large-feature case (parcels, campuses, complexes), NOT the other way round. My earlier
recommendation on bd-10s2 -- "full intersection cover for membership plus a single
deterministic anchor cell" -- is right in intent but inverted in emphasis, and applying it
naively with polygon_to_cells would have silently produced empty membership for nearly every
building. Correct it there.

== FINDING 3: OUR OWN SOURCES CARRY LICENSE OBLIGATIONS. bd-pq5w IS SCOPED TOO NARROWLY. ==
I framed license containment entirely around the CLIENT's licensed parcel layer. The landed
research shows OUR side has obligations too, and they differ per source:
    Overture buildings, divisions      ODbL-1.0            <-- SHARE-ALIKE
    Overture places                    per-source mix of CDLA-Permissive-2.0, Apache-2.0,
                                       CC0-1.0; source license must be retained
    Overture addresses                 source-specific, incl. NAD Access and Usage License
    FEMA USA Structures                CC-BY-4.0, attribution to ORNL and FEMA Geospatial
                                       Response Office REQUIRED
    Microsoft GlobalML                 CDLA-Permissive-2.0 current release; older vintages
                                       need per-release revalidation
bd-30ho states plainly: "License segmentation by source array is REQUIRED before any derived
product ships. Treat as a build-time gate, not a later cleanup."

ODbL SHARE-ALIKE IS THE COMMERCIAL ISSUE AND IT NEEDS AN OPERATOR DECISION, NOT AN
ENGINEERING ONE. A tile is a derived product. If it mixes ODbL Overture buildings with
everything else, the derived tile may inherit share-alike obligations that are
incompatible with a paid distribution model. Options to evaluate deliberately:
  (a) segregate ODbL-derived features into a separately-licensed layer of the tile, with
      the license class carried per feature -- note OVERTURE_MAPS_FEATURES_EXT ALREADY HAS
      LICENSE_CLASS AND LICENSE_TERMS COLUMNS, so the substrate for this exists;
  (b) build the commercial tile from the permissive sources only (FEMA CC-BY, Microsoft
      CDLA) and treat Overture as an internal enrichment;
  (c) accept share-alike and publish the tile openly.
REQUIRED IN bd-pq5w AND bd-1uld: license class per FEATURE in the tile artifact, and a
declared per-tile license posture that composes our obligations with the client's. The
artifact license boundary now has TWO directions, not one.

== FINDING 4: THE ATTRIBUTE CHANNELS FOR bd-272d ARE REAL, AND ONE IS MODELLED ==
Attribute anchoring needs class, size, floors, year. What is actually arriving:
    FEMA        OCC_CLS, PRIM_OCC (occupancy class), SQFEET, PROP_ADDR, UUID, BUILD_ID
    Overture    building class, height, num_floors, GERS id
    Microsoft   height (subset only), confidence, NO ID
    MapPLUTO    BLDGCLASS, LANDUSE, BLDGAREA, LOTAREA, NUMBLDGS, NUMFLOORS, YEARBUILT
So the six-field client contract has a counterpart on the tile side for every field except
YEAR BUILT, which only MapPLUTO supplies -- meaning year-built anchoring works in NYC and
degrades outside it until a national year source exists. Record that as a known national
limitation rather than discovering it later.

CRITICAL: FEMA OCCUPANCY IS MODELLED, NOT SURVEYED. bd-1ssr requires a provenance flag
"so downstream never treats it as surveyed." Attribute anchoring MUST carry that flag into
the evidence and weight modelled attributes below observed ones. A modelled occupancy class
driving a hard eliminative filter (bd-2zdz's assemblage type filter) would be a silent error
generator -- the filter is HARD, so a wrong modelled class removes the correct candidate
before anything is scored. Use modelled occupancy as SUPPORT evidence, never as a hard
filter, unless corroborated.

== FINDING 5: NO STABLE ID CONFIRMED FOR TWO SOURCES ==
Microsoft has no id at all -- bd-3fyv derives "a deterministic feature hash because no
stable id." Overture ADDRESSES are alpha with no stable GERS id either. This confirms
bd-2cbs rule 4 (alias-less participants) and extends it: the alias-less set is Microsoft
footprints AND Overture addresses, not just Microsoft.
A derived feature hash is NOT an alias and must not be minted into a registry -- it will
change whenever the geometry changes, which violates the tile identifier stability contract
in bd-12gh.

== FINDING 6: OVERTURE ADDRESSES CANNOT BE THE ADDRESS-SET SOURCE ==
bd-30ho: "Addresses theme is ALPHA -- do not build a contract against it yet," no stable
GERS id, multi-source licensing including NAD terms. US count 127,719,691.
So bd-35qg's address-set acquisition is NOT solved by Overture. NYC PAD or the per-BIN
addresses in the landed footprints file (bd-397d) remain the path, and the national story
stays open. Do not let the size of the Overture addresses count create false confidence.

== WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE WORKED-CASE CORPUS (bd-tccn) ==
The corpus can now stage its non-MapPLUTO pulls against REAL TABLE NAMES rather than
placeholders:
    EDGAR_DB.SOURCE.FEMA_USA_STRUCTURES_HOT              partially loaded (DC, AK, AL)
    EDGAR_DB.SOURCE.MICROSOFT_GLOBALML_BUILDING_FOOTPRINTS_HOT   partially loaded
    EDGAR_DB.SOURCE.OVERTURE_MAPS_FEATURES_HOT           DDL applied, 0 rows
    plus the *_FEATURE_H3_COVERAGE tables for each
NEW YORK IS NOT YET LOADED IN ANY OF THE THREE. FEMA is alphabetical by state and is at AR;
Microsoft is 179/2415 files; Overture has not started landing. So the full-tile version of
every case remains blocked, exactly as the corpus bead predicted -- but the blocker is now
a KNOWN COMPLETION DATE rather than an unlanded dataset, and the table names and column
shapes are already fixed enough to write the extraction queries against.

              its representative point. Reliable for every feature at every size, and it
              doubles as the deterministic anchor cell that halo reconciliation (bd-2b9d)
              needs for mint-once semantics.
  SUPPLEMENT  POLYGON COVERAGE for LARGE features only — parcels, campuses, complexes,
              anything genuinely spanning cells. This is where the original intent was
              right; it is simply the exception rather than the rule.
  REFUSE      a coverage computation that returns empty for a non-empty geometry. That is
              the defect above, and it should surface as a refusal rather than as silently
              absent membership.

The anchor rule must still be a deterministic property of the geometry, never of input
order or of which source supplied the feature.

NOTE FOR THE INGEST CONTRACT: this applies to the CLIENT's layer too. A client parcel
extract will contain both small lots (centroid suffices) and large assemblages (coverage
needed), so the ingest must apply both and record which rule produced each membership row.

comments.author: Zac
comments.text:
ARCHITECTURE SUPERSEDED 2026-08-15 — see docs/PLAN_CANON_GEO.md.

An adversarial multi-model design session produced a materially different architecture,
which then survived a red team that destroyed two intermediate designs. The tile is modelled
as a BOUNDED UNIVERSE and every piece of evidence is a CONSTRAINT; propagation runs to a
fixpoint; the residual model set IS the answer. There is no proposer channel.

THE THREE PROPERTIES THAT MATTER:
- CONFLUENCE. The fixpoint is independent of the order constraints are applied (Tarski 1955;
  Cousot & Cousot 1977; Apt 1999), so determinism is a theorem rather than an engineering
  effort.
- MONOTONICITY. Constraints only add and domains only shrink, so a tile resolved with four
  sources today and six next year yields a TIGHTER residual, never a contradicting one. The
  earlier answer was never wrong, only less resolved.
- STRUCTURAL ABSTENTION. The residual model set is the answer. No threshold anywhere.

THE KEY DESIGN RULE IS rho, THE SOUNDNESS DISCIPLINE. Every source attribute enters the
solver only through a declared versioned relaxation mapping it to the WEAKEST constraint the
source can actually support. An interpolated geocode becomes a 150m disc rather than a
location. A parcel ADDRESS becomes "one of this lot's addresses" rather than functional
equality. OWNERNAME equal PERMITS an assemblage; OWNERNAME different constrains NOTHING.
Every noisy channel is admitted only in its sound direction — which is what dissolved the
proposer dilemma that broke the two earlier designs.

AND THE COMMERCIAL CONSEQUENCE: if every rho is sound, the true assignment is in the model
set, so AN EMPTY MODEL SET IS A PROOF that a named source violated its own published error
model — attributable, falsifiable, and mailable to the vendor.

Read PLAN_CANON_GEO.md before starting any geo work. Section 11 carries the bead-by-bead
supersession table. Appendix A covers frozen-weight observers and imagery sources. APPENDIX
B RECORDS THE FIRST HARD MEASUREMENT, WHICH FALSIFIED A LOAD-BEARING CLAIM — read it before
trusting any performance number in the plan.

Raw session artifacts, including the red team and the adversarial reviews, are preserved
under docs/geo_design_session/ with a reading guide.

comments.author: Zac
comments.text:
MEASURED ON REAL DATA 2026-08-15 — see PLAN_CANON_GEO.md Appendix B. Two findings that
change this bead directly.

1. CENTROID PROXIMITY DOES NOT DECOMPOSE A DENSE TILE AT ANY RADIUS.
Real tile: 100 MapPLUTO parcels + 93 NYC building footprints within 150m of the 305 E 72nd
rooftop geocode. Bipartite centroid graph swept from 10m to 150m:

    r=10   64 comps  max 17     r=30   12 comps  max 49
    r=20   33 comps  max 34     r=35    7 comps  max 59
    r=25   24 comps  max 37     r=60    1 comp   max 193  <- percolation

There is no plateau. At the best radius (25m) only 9 of 24 components fall in the 6-20 band
and the max is already 37. THE TILE PERCOLATES AT ~60m, well inside the 150m tile radius.
Any design that assumes a proximity filter will decompose the work unit is unvalidated for
dense urban geography.

2. A FIXED RADIUS IS THE WRONG SHAPE OF FILTER.
Equal-area disc radius sqrt(A/pi) per parcel, a hard floor on centroid-to-boundary distance:

    median  8.7m     p90  18.6m     max  33.4m
    parcels exceeding 25m:  4 / 100  =  4%

The 33.4m maximum is BBL 1014477501 — the answer parcel, LOTAREA 37,800, the largest in the
tile. So a fixed 25m radius is adequate for 96% of parcels and FAILS SPECIFICALLY AND
SILENTLY ON THE ~4% THAT ARE LARGE ASSEMBLAGES, which are exactly the hard cases this
product exists to solve.

REQUIRED: any geometric filter must NORMALISE BY PARCEL EXTENT — half-diagonal from
LOTFRONT/LOTDEPTH, or the equal-area radius above — never a constant. And the tile/halo
design must account for percolation: a radius large enough to catch boundary features on a
dense block merges the entire block into one component.

SCOPE HONESTLY: n=1 and it is the dense extreme. Midtown-adjacent Manhattan is the worst
case for percolation; a suburban or agency-multifamily tile will decompose far more readily.
The claim is falsified for dense urban, not universally. Measure across a stratified tile
sample before concluding anything general.

ALSO MEASURED: an edge effect this bead should own. Parcels whose centroid falls inside a
150m window can have footprints whose centroids fall outside it. Halo reconciliation must be
computed PER LEVEL, not once for the tile.

title: [CANON-V1/P00.4a] Centralize direct v1 artifact construction and hash binding

## Background
The v1 contract catalog and validator exist, but lifecycle builders keep stage metadata/self-hash helpers in review.rs and use placeholder schema hashes. Prepare/index and later stages need one direct construction seam before any public v1 writer can be faithful.

## Technical Approach
Centralize domain-neutral helpers for registered stage descriptors, canonical descriptor/schema digests, workdir layout, sorted validated upstream references, metadata construction, and self-hash finalization. Generalize existing lifecycle consumers to this shared seam. Builders must operate on real v1 artifacts and in-memory stage payload data only; they must never point at, persist, or deserialize a legacy v0 backing artifact. - Every registered v1 stage can obtain deterministic descriptor/schema/workdir metadata from one helper.

- Upstream references are sorted and byte-stable.
- Review/audit/promote/explain behavior remains green after adopting the shared seam.
- No public command behavior or legacy reader is added in this bead.

## Test Plan
Unit-test all stage descriptors, canonical digest stability, key-order invariance, unsorted/legacy upstream refusal, self-hash validity, and existing lifecycle fixtures.

- src/entity/review.rs
- src/entity/audit.rs
- src/entity/promote.rs
- src/entity/explain.rs
- tests/entity_schema_snapshots.rs

This bead is a construction seam only. bd-17q8 owns prepare/index emission; bd-32y0 owns block/evidence/solve/run emission.
