title: canon geo: the entity-level model — per-source levels, same-level equivalence, cross-level containment
description:
OPERATOR INSIGHT 2026-08-14 — THE ORGANIZING PRINCIPLE OF THE WHOLE TILE. Read this before
bd-3ccc.

THE FRAMING: a tile is a SLICE OF EVERY DATASET AT ONCE — Foursquare OS Places, Overture
Maps, FEMA USA Structures, Microsoft GlobalML footprints, MapPLUTO (or the client's
licensed parcel layer), and the client's property book. The work is STITCHING THEM
TOGETHER: this Foursquare place is in this building, which is this BIN, which sits on this
BBL. But the stitching is not one resolution problem, because THE DATASETS DO NOT ALL
DESCRIBE THE SAME KIND OF THING.

  LEVEL          NATIVE SOURCES                              IDENTIFIER
  poi/unit       Foursquare OS Places, tenant rows,          fsq_place_id, none
                 commercial condo units
  building       Overture buildings, FEMA USA Structures,    GERS, FEMA UUID, BIN,
                 Microsoft GlobalML, NYC footprints          (Microsoft: NONE)
  parcel         MapPLUTO, ATTOM, Regrid, county assessor    BBL, APN, vendor parcel id
  property       the client's book                           document-scoped; a SET over
                                                             the levels above

EACH SOURCE HAS A NATIVE LEVEL AND MUST DECLARE IT. Resolution happens WITHIN a level;
relationships happen ACROSS levels. That single rule is what keeps the whole thing honest.

== RULE 1: SAME LEVEL IS same_as. CROSS LEVEL IS NEVER same_as. ==
A Foursquare place is not the same_as a building — it is WITHIN one. A building is not the
same_as a parcel — it is ON one. Collapsing a cross-level relationship into an equivalence
is the single most damaging error available here, and it is exactly what a wide crosswalk
does (bd-67wx rejects it for this reason).
canon ALREADY ENFORCES THIS and the fit is unusually good: ScoreLane::RelationHint
contributes ZERO merge score by construction, and src/entity/relation.rs deliberately
refuses to emit same_as. What was previously read as a limitation of relation.rs (see the
2026-08-14 comment on bd-3soj) is, under the level model, exactly the right semantics — it
just needs a typed vocabulary rather than prose strings.

== RULE 2: THE TILE IS SHARED; BLOCKING IS NOT PER-LEVEL WORK ==
All levels share the same H3 cell, so one tile blocks every level simultaneously. This is
what makes "a slice of each dataset" a coherent unit of work rather than four separate
pipelines. bd-2b9d's blocking serves all levels; only the EVIDENCE differs.

== RULE 3: EACH LEVEL HAS DIFFERENT RESOLUTION PHYSICS. Do not build one operator set. ==
  PARCEL     Polygons. Authoritative geometry. APN/BBL equality is string equality.
             Within-source mutual exclusion is FALSE where condo aggregation exists
             (measured on MapPLUTO). Overlap between a unit lot and its parent is part_of,
             not a distinctness violation.
  BUILDING   Polygons. Footprint IoU, area ratio, height. Within-source mutual exclusion is
             TRUE (two Overture buildings are not the same building). This is the level
             where the epic's "hard negatives exist" claim is cleanest.
  POI/UNIT   POINTS, not polygons — so IoU and area ratio DO NOT APPLY. Names carry the
             signal here.

RULE 3 HAS AN IMPORTANT CONSEQUENCE FOR THE REUSE QUESTION. The 2026-08-14 reality check
established that canon entity is a NAME resolver and that its machinery does not transfer
to geometry. AT THE POI/UNIT LEVEL THAT FINDING INVERTS: name resolution is precisely what
is needed, and canon's existing namekit / rapidfuzz / tfidf_cosine / alias_patch_match
machinery, plus the cmbs_tenant_label profile pattern, TRANSFERS UNCHANGED. The correct
statement is level-scoped: geometry levels need new operators; the POI level reuses the
existing ones. Both halves of that are true and the epic should say so.

== RULE 4: NOT EVERY SOURCE CAN CONTRIBUTE AN ALIAS ==
bd-67wx's scheme assumes each source contributes a role-namespaced alias to a cluster.
MICROSOFT GLOBALML HAS NO STABLE IDENTIFIERS — verified in OC-0047 against the Overture
GERS bridge-file spec, which excludes it explicitly because it has "no meaningful IDs for
reverse lookup." So it is a GEOMETRY-AND-ATTRIBUTE-ONLY PARTICIPANT: it can contribute a
footprint and a height (and height feeds gross area, which feeds the assemblage subset-sum),
but it can never be an alias in a registry.
REQUIRED: the ID scheme must model a participant that supplies evidence but no alias. Do
not synthesize a surrogate identifier for it — a minted id for an unstable source would be
reassigned on every refresh and would violate the tile identifier stability contract.

== RULE 5: GEOMETRY IS THE ONLY JOIN KEY, WHICH IS WHY THE LADDER EXISTS ==
Verified in OC-0047: Foursquare fsq_place_id is not a bridged GERS source, Microsoft is
excluded, FEMA is not an Overture source, and no parcel theme exists anywhere so there is
no APN. THERE IS NO CROSS-DATASET IDENTIFIER BRIDGE AT ANY LEVEL. The level ladder IS the
bridge: resolve within a level using that level's physics, then relate across levels by
containment. That is how "this Foursquare place -> this building -> this BBL" gets built
without a universal ID, and it is the core mechanism of the outcome.

== RULE 6: SOURCES HAVE DIFFERENT VINTAGES, AND DISAGREEMENT MAY BE TEMPORAL ==
Overture, FEMA, Microsoft, Foursquare and MapPLUTO all refresh on different cadences. A
tile is therefore a COMPOSITE OF SOURCES AT DIFFERENT POINTS IN TIME, and per-source
vintage must live in the tile provenance (bd-1uld already requires per-source provenance
blocks; this is why it matters).
THE FAILURE MODE THIS CREATES: a building demolished in 2020 appears in a 2019 FEMA release
and is absent from a 2022 Overture release. The cascade sees source disagreement and will
score it as a quality or coverage problem WHEN IT IS ACTUALLY A DEMOLITION. Year-built,
per-source vintage, and presence/absence together can detect this. Treat cross-source
presence disagreement as a candidate TEMPORAL finding, not automatically as error — and
where it cannot be distinguished, abstain.

== HOW THIS COMPOSES WITH THE PROPERTY SET MODEL ==
Property sits above the ladder as a SET over resolved members at whatever levels the
document implies (see the 2026-08-14 comments on bd-67wx and bd-1oid). So the full picture
is: resolve within each level, relate across levels, then constitute the property as a
membership set AT A POINT IN TIME. All the uncertainty is spent in the first two steps; the
third is exact set algebra.

EXIT CRITERIA:
- A declared LEVEL for every source, required at ingest, with refusal on absence
- Level recorded on every surface, cluster and minted id
- A hard invariant, tested: no cross-level pair can produce same_as or accumulate support
  score. Negative test with a POI and its containing building.
- Per-level operator sets, with the POI level explicitly reusing canon entity's existing
  name machinery rather than reimplementing it
- Alias-less participants supported (Microsoft GlobalML), with a test that no surrogate id
  is minted for them
- Per-source vintage in tile provenance; a temporal-disagreement detector distinguishing
  demolition from coverage error, abstaining where it cannot
- A worked fixture stitching one location across all levels: Foursquare place -> Overture/
  FEMA/Microsoft building -> BIN -> BBL, with the typed relations at each hop

comments.author: Zac
comments.text:
TILE PRE-STITCHING IS ALREADY UNDER WAY IN cmdrvl-curves, LANDING NOW 2026-08-14. Verified
by reading the in-progress beads. This confirms the pre-resolved-tile architecture and
supplies hard facts that change several canon geo assumptions.

== WHAT IS ACTUALLY LANDING ==

  cmdrvl-curves bd-30ho   OVERTURE MAPS, release 2026-07-22.0. Themes buildings,
                          building_parts, PLACES, addresses, divisions. Snowflake DDL
                          APPLIED (OVERTURE_MAPS_FEATURES_HOT / _EXT /
                          OVERTURE_MAPS_FEATURE_H3_COVERAGE plus 14 per-type views);
                          manifest scan running, 0 rows landed yet.
  cmdrvl-curves bd-1ssr   FEMA USA STRUCTURES, 135,321,228 features nationally. National
                          landing IN PROGRESS; DC / AK / AL complete, AR running.
                          FEMA_USA_STRUCTURES_HOT loaded and read back (DC = 64,701 rows).
  cmdrvl-curves bd-3fyv   MICROSOFT GLOBALML FOOTPRINTS, release 2026-07-24. Landing IN
                          PROGRESS: 179 of 2,415 US files, 5,219,860 rows at 14:45Z.
  cmdrvl-curves bd-11uu   HUD USPS ADDRESS VACANCIES -- **BLOCKED**, and not a tile source.
                          HUD restricts it to registered governmental/non-profit users and
                          the sublicense forbids selling, licensing or distributing the
                          data. DO NOT PLAN ANY CANON GEO CAPABILITY ON IT.

NOTE ON "FOURSQUARE OS PLACES": it arrives as OVERTURE'S PLACES THEME, not a separate
Foursquare landing. That is the POI level in bd-2cbs, and it is in the same table family as
Overture buildings.

== FINDING 1: THE LANDED H3 GRAIN IS r4 / r7 / r8. THERE IS NO r9. ==
All three sources partition by h3_r4 and carry H3_R7 and H3_R8 columns. The epic's default
tile is res-9 and it is NOT precomputed anywhere.

AND THERE IS A CONVENIENT COINCIDENCE WORTH DELIBERATELY EXPLOITING: an r8 cell is
approximately 0.737 km2 -- which is almost exactly the area the epic specifies for its WORK
UNIT (an r9 cell plus k-ring 1 = 7 cells = 0.737 km2). So the already-landed H3_R8 column is
essentially the intended work-unit size.
ACTION FOR bd-2b9d: reconsider r9-plus-k-ring versus r8-plus-k-ring as the work unit, now
that r8 is precomputed across every source and r9 is not. This does not change the
requirement to compute cells in canon with a vetted Rust library -- the Snowflake H3 helper
defects (edgar-elt br-2wir) still stand -- but it does mean the warehouse can prefilter at
r8 for free, and the resolution decision now has a third input alongside node count and
human legibility.

== FINDING 2: POLYGON-TO-CELLS RETURNS EMPTY FOR SMALL BUILDINGS. LIVE, MEASURED. ==
From bd-3fyv: "H3_POLYGON_TO_CELLS alone inserted only 116 coverage rows for 354,804 hot
rows because small buildings often contain no H3 r8 cell centroid." Fixed there by using a
guaranteed CENTROID_H3_R8 plus H3_TRY_POLYGON_TO_CELLS.

THIS IS DIRECTLY THE MEMBERSHIP QUESTION bd-10s2 AND bd-2b9d SPECIFY. At r8 or r9 a
building is much smaller than a cell, so "which cells does this polygon cover" is
degenerate: the standard polygon-to-cells contract returns cells whose CENTRES fall inside
the polygon, and for a building that set is almost always EMPTY.
CONSEQUENCE: membership must be CENTROID-ANCHORED with polygon coverage as a supplement for
the large-feature case (parcels, campuses, complexes), NOT the other way round. My earlier
recommendation on bd-10s2 -- "full intersection cover for membership plus a single
deterministic anchor cell" -- is right in intent but inverted in emphasis, and applying it
naively with polygon_to_cells would have silently produced empty membership for nearly every
building. Correct it there.

== FINDING 3: OUR OWN SOURCES CARRY LICENSE OBLIGATIONS. bd-pq5w IS SCOPED TOO NARROWLY. ==
I framed license containment entirely around the CLIENT's licensed parcel layer. The landed
research shows OUR side has obligations too, and they differ per source:
    Overture buildings, divisions      ODbL-1.0            <-- SHARE-ALIKE
    Overture places                    per-source mix of CDLA-Permissive-2.0, Apache-2.0,
                                       CC0-1.0; source license must be retained
    Overture addresses                 source-specific, incl. NAD Access and Usage License
    FEMA USA Structures                CC-BY-4.0, attribution to ORNL and FEMA Geospatial
                                       Response Office REQUIRED
    Microsoft GlobalML                 CDLA-Permissive-2.0 current release; older vintages
                                       need per-release revalidation
bd-30ho states plainly: "License segmentation by source array is REQUIRED before any derived
product ships. Treat as a build-time gate, not a later cleanup."

ODbL SHARE-ALIKE IS THE COMMERCIAL ISSUE AND IT NEEDS AN OPERATOR DECISION, NOT AN
ENGINEERING ONE. A tile is a derived product. If it mixes ODbL Overture buildings with
everything else, the derived tile may inherit share-alike obligations that are
incompatible with a paid distribution model. Options to evaluate deliberately:
  (a) segregate ODbL-derived features into a separately-licensed layer of the tile, with
      the license class carried per feature -- note OVERTURE_MAPS_FEATURES_EXT ALREADY HAS
      LICENSE_CLASS AND LICENSE_TERMS COLUMNS, so the substrate for this exists;
  (b) build the commercial tile from the permissive sources only (FEMA CC-BY, Microsoft
      CDLA) and treat Overture as an internal enrichment;
  (c) accept share-alike and publish the tile openly.
REQUIRED IN bd-pq5w AND bd-1uld: license class per FEATURE in the tile artifact, and a
declared per-tile license posture that composes our obligations with the client's. The
artifact license boundary now has TWO directions, not one.

== FINDING 4: THE ATTRIBUTE CHANNELS FOR bd-272d ARE REAL, AND ONE IS MODELLED ==
Attribute anchoring needs class, size, floors, year. What is actually arriving:
    FEMA        OCC_CLS, PRIM_OCC (occupancy class), SQFEET, PROP_ADDR, UUID, BUILD_ID
    Overture    building class, height, num_floors, GERS id
    Microsoft   height (subset only), confidence, NO ID
    MapPLUTO    BLDGCLASS, LANDUSE, BLDGAREA, LOTAREA, NUMBLDGS, NUMFLOORS, YEARBUILT
So the six-field client contract has a counterpart on the tile side for every field except
YEAR BUILT, which only MapPLUTO supplies -- meaning year-built anchoring works in NYC and
degrades outside it until a national year source exists. Record that as a known national
limitation rather than discovering it later.

CRITICAL: FEMA OCCUPANCY IS MODELLED, NOT SURVEYED. bd-1ssr requires a provenance flag
"so downstream never treats it as surveyed." Attribute anchoring MUST carry that flag into
the evidence and weight modelled attributes below observed ones. A modelled occupancy class
driving a hard eliminative filter (bd-2zdz's assemblage type filter) would be a silent error
generator -- the filter is HARD, so a wrong modelled class removes the correct candidate
before anything is scored. Use modelled occupancy as SUPPORT evidence, never as a hard
filter, unless corroborated.

== FINDING 5: NO STABLE ID CONFIRMED FOR TWO SOURCES ==
Microsoft has no id at all -- bd-3fyv derives "a deterministic feature hash because no
stable id." Overture ADDRESSES are alpha with no stable GERS id either. This confirms
bd-2cbs rule 4 (alias-less participants) and extends it: the alias-less set is Microsoft
footprints AND Overture addresses, not just Microsoft.
A derived feature hash is NOT an alias and must not be minted into a registry -- it will
change whenever the geometry changes, which violates the tile identifier stability contract
in bd-12gh.

== FINDING 6: OVERTURE ADDRESSES CANNOT BE THE ADDRESS-SET SOURCE ==
bd-30ho: "Addresses theme is ALPHA -- do not build a contract against it yet," no stable
GERS id, multi-source licensing including NAD terms. US count 127,719,691.
So bd-35qg's address-set acquisition is NOT solved by Overture. NYC PAD or the per-BIN
addresses in the landed footprints file (bd-397d) remain the path, and the national story
stays open. Do not let the size of the Overture addresses count create false confidence.

== WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE WORKED-CASE CORPUS (bd-tccn) ==
The corpus can now stage its non-MapPLUTO pulls against REAL TABLE NAMES rather than
placeholders:
    EDGAR_DB.SOURCE.FEMA_USA_STRUCTURES_HOT              partially loaded (DC, AK, AL)
    EDGAR_DB.SOURCE.MICROSOFT_GLOBALML_BUILDING_FOOTPRINTS_HOT   partially loaded
    EDGAR_DB.SOURCE.OVERTURE_MAPS_FEATURES_HOT           DDL applied, 0 rows
    plus the *_FEATURE_H3_COVERAGE tables for each
NEW YORK IS NOT YET LOADED IN ANY OF THE THREE. FEMA is alphabetical by state and is at AR;
Microsoft is 179/2415 files; Overture has not started landing. So the full-tile version of
every case remains blocked, exactly as the corpus bead predicted -- but the blocker is now
a KNOWN COMPLETION DATE rather than an unlanded dataset, and the table names and column
shapes are already fixed enough to write the extraction queries against.

comments.author: Zac
comments.text:
ARCHITECTURE SUPERSEDED 2026-08-15 — see docs/PLAN_CANON_GEO.md.

An adversarial multi-model design session produced a materially different architecture,
which then survived a red team that destroyed two intermediate designs. The tile is modelled
as a BOUNDED UNIVERSE and every piece of evidence is a CONSTRAINT; propagation runs to a
fixpoint; the residual model set IS the answer. There is no proposer channel.

THE THREE PROPERTIES THAT MATTER:
- CONFLUENCE. The fixpoint is independent of the order constraints are applied (Tarski 1955;
  Cousot & Cousot 1977; Apt 1999), so determinism is a theorem rather than an engineering
  effort.
- MONOTONICITY. Constraints only add and domains only shrink, so a tile resolved with four
  sources today and six next year yields a TIGHTER residual, never a contradicting one. The
  earlier answer was never wrong, only less resolved.
- STRUCTURAL ABSTENTION. The residual model set is the answer. No threshold anywhere.

THE KEY DESIGN RULE IS rho, THE SOUNDNESS DISCIPLINE. Every source attribute enters the
solver only through a declared versioned relaxation mapping it to the WEAKEST constraint the
source can actually support. An interpolated geocode becomes a 150m disc rather than a
location. A parcel ADDRESS becomes "one of this lot's addresses" rather than functional
equality. OWNERNAME equal PERMITS an assemblage; OWNERNAME different constrains NOTHING.
Every noisy channel is admitted only in its sound direction — which is what dissolved the
proposer dilemma that broke the two earlier designs.

AND THE COMMERCIAL CONSEQUENCE: if every rho is sound, the true assignment is in the model
set, so AN EMPTY MODEL SET IS A PROOF that a named source violated its own published error
model — attributable, falsifiable, and mailable to the vendor.

Read PLAN_CANON_GEO.md before starting any geo work. Section 11 carries the bead-by-bead
supersession table. Appendix A covers frozen-weight observers and imagery sources. APPENDIX
B RECORDS THE FIRST HARD MEASUREMENT, WHICH FALSIFIED A LOAD-BEARING CLAIM — read it before
trusting any performance number in the plan.

Raw session artifacts, including the red team and the adversarial reviews, are preserved
under docs/geo_design_session/ with a reading guide.

title: [CANON-V1/REVIEW] Enforce strict BLAKE3 digest encoding in persisted contracts
description:
## Background
5.5 review found placeholder-friendly digest validation in persisted v1 contracts. Inbox and registry package validators accept any non-empty `blake3:` suffix, while identity facts require canonical 64-hex BLAKE3 strings.

## Evidence
- `src/inbox/mod.rs` accepts non-empty `blake3:` suffixes.

title: [SPLINK-STEAL/S8] diagnostics: unlinkables report (intrinsic match ceiling per surface)
description:
## Problem this solves
Some records can never auto-link regardless of threshold tuning: their populated fields are too sparse or degraded to reach backbone/attach thresholds even against a perfect duplicate of themselves. Knowing that fraction up front (a) sets honest auto-accept expectations per corpus BEFORE the grind (so "82% auto-accept" is recognized as the data ceiling, not a strategy failure), and (b) routes structurally hopeless records straight to enrichment or the inbox instead of wasting review passes on them.

## Build
canon entity diagnose unlinkables (or a report section in run/link artifacts):
- Per prepared surface, compute the maximum attainable support score: score the surface against a hypothetical perfect twin under the active strategy (every configured operator fires at full strength given the fields actually populated on that surface).
- Report the distribution of max-attainable scores vs the solver thresholds; list surfaces whose ceiling < attach/backbone thresholds, with missing-field reasons (which absent fields cost how many units).
- Surface the result as ranking context for the inbox (bd-fung consumes it as one more deterministic signal).

## Splink reference (clone at /Users/zac/Source/opensource/splink)
- splink/internals/unlinkables.py — self-match ceiling concept ("proportion of records with insufficient information to link to themselves")
- docs/topic_guides/evaluation/overview.md — how unlinkables frames intrinsic data-content limits

## How to test
- Sparse-row fixture (name-only, no anchors, no context) flagged with correct ceilings and correct missing-field attributions.
- Ceiling correctness property: for each surface, ceiling equals the evidence stage's actual score for (surface, exact clone of surface) under the same strategy.
- Determinism replay across runs and shuffles.
- Report-only: no artifact chain or outcome semantics change (byte-identical run artifacts with the feature unused).

## Doctrine constraints
Deterministic read-only diagnostics; integer units; no solver or outcome changes.

## RESERVATIONS

- tests/entity_unlinkables.rs

title: [CANON-V1/P05.1] Define bitemporal identity facts with provenance and trust
description:
## Background
Identity claims change over time: names change, identifiers retire or recycle, objects merge or split, data arrives late, and sources correct earlier assertions. A timeless alias map cannot answer what was believed when or valid as of a date.

## Technical Approach
Define domain-neutral `canon.identity.fact.v1` with subject/object IDs, typed predicate, valid interval, recorded-at interval or transaction sequence, source locator, materialization digest, assertion status, trust-policy reference, supersession/retraction linkage, and optional scope. Specify boundaries, open ends, canonical serialization, fact identity, and conflict representation.

## Success Criteria
- The model distinguishes event validity from when Canon learned/corrected it.
- Accepted, retracted, and superseded facts retain immutable provenance.
- Equivalent facts deduplicate; contradictory facts coexist explicitly.
- Current date or file mtime never affects semantics.

## Test Plan
Round-trip invented facts across boundaries, late arrivals, corrections, duplicate/conflicting sources, and clock-independent serialization; property-test interval and supersession invariants.

## RESERVATIONS
- `src/temporal/mod.rs`
- `src/temporal/fact.rs`
- `schemas/canon.identity.fact.v1.schema.json`
- `tests/temporal_fact.rs`

## Considerations
Facts are assertions, not automatically trusted truth. Acceptance policy and compiled snapshots remain explicit.
close_reason: Defined bitemporal identity fact v1 contract with provenance/trust; validated with cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, and cargo test.

title: Registry diff and changelog (canon registry diff)
description:
## Summary

Add `canon registry diff` to compare two registry versions and report what changed. Essential operational tooling for materialized registries — when you re-materialize from OpenFIGI weekly, you need to know what changed before you start resolving against the new version.

## Motivation

Materialized registries are snapshots. When you re-materialize, identifiers get added (new instruments issued), removed (instruments delisted), or changed (corporate actions — ticker changes, mergers). Without diff, you are resolving against a new registry version blind. With diff, you know exactly what shifted and can assess impact before updating your pipeline.

This also feeds the spine: `canon registry diff` output can be piped to `rvl` for materiality analysis — "of the 47 mappings that changed, which ones affect positions I actually hold?"

## Design

### Subcommand

```bash
canon registry diff \
  --old registries/openfigi-cusip-v2026.02/ \
  --new registries/openfigi-cusip-v2026.03/ \
  [--emit json|summary]
```

### Output (JSON)

```json
{
  "version": "canon_registry_diff.v0",
  "old": { "id": "openfigi-cusip", "version": "2026.02.28" },
  "new": { "id": "openfigi-cusip", "version": "2026.03.05" },
  "summary": {
    "total_old": 4183,
    "total_new": 4210,
    "added": 34,
    "removed": 7,
    "changed": 12,
    "unchanged": 4157
  },
  "added": [
    { "input": "92936U101", "canonical_id": "BBG01ABCDEF0", "canonical_type": "composite_figi", "rule_id": "OPENFIGI_CUSIP_TO_FIGI" }
  ],
  "removed": [
    { "input": "78462F103", "canonical_id": "BBG000BVG4K0", "canonical_type": "composite_figi", "reason": "not_in_new_registry" }
  ],
  "changed": [
    {
      "input": "931142103",
      "old": { "canonical_id": "BBG000BJ2GK0", "canonical_type": "composite_figi" },
      "new": { "canonical_id": "BBG00XXXXXXX", "canonical_type": "composite_figi" },
      "change_type": "figi_change"
    }
  ]
}
```

### Summary mode

```bash
$ canon registry diff --old v2026.02/ --new v2026.03/ --emit summary
openfigi-cusip: 2026.02.28 → 2026.03.05
  +34 added, -7 removed, ~12 changed, =4157 unchanged
  Notable: 3 ticker changes (corporate actions), 7 delistings
```

### Composability with the spine

```bash
# What changed in the registry?
canon registry diff --old v2026.02/ --new v2026.03/ > evidence/registry-diff.json

# Which changes affect my positions?
# (extract changed input IDs, filter positions file, run rvl)
canon registry diff --old v2026.02/ --new v2026.03/ \
  | jq -r '.changed[].input' > /tmp/changed-cusips.txt

# Seal the evidence
pack seal evidence/ --note "Registry update 2026.02 → 2026.03"
```

## Acceptance criteria

- `canon registry diff --old <dir> --new <dir>` compares two registry versions
- Reports added, removed, changed, unchanged counts
- JSON output includes full detail for each category
- Summary mode (--emit summary) gives human-readable one-liner
- Both registries must have the same id (refuse if comparing apples to oranges)
- Handles registries with different mapping file sets (old has cusip-to-figi.json only, new adds cusip-to-ticker.json)
- Deterministic output: same two registries = same diff, always
- Tests: known registries with specific additions, removals, and changes
close_reason: Implemented canon registry diff with deterministic effective-entry comparisons, summary output, refusals, and tests

title: [CANON-V1/P02.2] Lock all project inputs, packages, strategies, and policy hashes
description:
## Background
A manifest can point at mutable tags and local inputs, so it is not by itself a reproducibility proof. Identity decisions must be replayable months later against the exact source bytes, strategy, registry, policy, extension packages, and executable contract.

## Technical Approach
Define `canon.project.lock.v1` as a deterministic sorted lockfile containing content digests and resolved identities for every input, registry, strategy, provider snapshot, profile, ontology/vocabulary, policy, schema, and relevant Canon build. Add generation, verification, stale detection, and explicit refresh; ordinary runs never rewrite it.

## Success Criteria
- Equivalent projects produce byte-identical lockfiles independent of enumeration order.
- Changed bytes, retagged packages, missing dependencies, and tool-contract drift fail before execution with actionable diffs.
- Refresh is explicit and leaves an auditable before/after receipt.
- No credential, host-local absolute path, nondeterministic timestamp, or private raw value contaminates the lock hash.

## Test Plan
Use shuffled manifests and copied workspaces; mutate one dependency class at a time; assert exact stale reasons; and prove read-only lock checking leaves content, mtimes, and directory inventory unchanged.

## RESERVATIONS
- `src/project/lock.rs`
- `schemas/canon.project.lock.v1.schema.json`
- `tests/project_lock.rs`

## Considerations
Distinguish a human-edited manifest from a machine-generated lock. Mutable tags may be recorded for provenance, but execution pins resolved digests.

title: [CANON-V1/P05.5] Compile as-of identity facts into immutable exact lookup snapshots
description:
## Background
Production lookup must remain exact and fast even when source truth is temporal and contested. Runtime traversal of a fact graph would violate Canon's deliberately boring lookup kernel.

## Technical Approach
Implement a deterministic compiler that accepts fact packages, trust/conflict policy, scope, `--as-of`, `--known-as-of`, and parent snapshot; selects valid accepted identity aliases; abstains on unresolved conflicts; and emits a normal immutable registry package plus a compilation proof. Relationships are emitted as sidecars/projections and never affect exact mapping unless policy accepted an identity fact.

## Success Criteria
- A frozen fact set and policy compile to byte-identical registry snapshots.
- Every emitted mapping points to the exact facts, intervals, scope, and policy clause that authorized it.
- Ambiguous/conflicting facts are omitted with structured diagnostics, never last-write-wins.
- The resulting registry works through unchanged exact lookup, row-preserving apply, dbt seed, and searchable index backends.

## Test Plan
Compile boundary dates, known-as-of corrections, scope subsets, conflicts, retractions, and relation-only facts; compare exact query results and proof references. Shuffle inputs and repeat.

## RESERVATIONS
- `src/temporal/compile.rs`
- `schemas/canon.temporal.compile.v1.schema.json`
- `tests/temporal_compile.rs`

## Considerations
Compilation turns rich evidence into boring exact truth for a declared slice. It must never claim that one snapshot is timeless.

title: [CANON-V1/P08.6] Specify the filesystem-first publication backend seam
description:
## Background
Existing wrapper-managed object-store sync exposed the real requirement: registry publication must detect divergent writers. The open-source engine does not need built-in awareness of any cloud provider, and the prior decision was to remain filesystem-first and cloud-free by default.

## Technical Approach
Specify the minimal publication backend trait used by immutable package and channel operations: read by digest, create immutable object if absent, inspect head, compare-and-swap channel/head, list declared ancestry where supported, and return typed capability/refusal information. Implement the local filesystem backend as default with atomic rename/create semantics. Evaluate an optional generic object-store/OCI backend only after CAS and OCI contracts are stable; do not shell out to vendor CLIs or add provider SDKs to the default binary.

## Success Criteria
- Core lookup and local project execution have no cloud dependency or ambient network access.
- Registry mutations require expected base digest regardless of backend.
- Backends that cannot enforce required CAS refuse mutation rather than race.
- External wrappers can use immutable package push/pull safely because mutable head changes are an explicit transaction.
- The design records why native provider-specific URI handling remains deferred.

## Test Plan
Run the backend conformance suite against filesystem and the local OCI test backend; exercise create-if-absent, identical writes, stale/divergent heads, crash boundaries, read-only mode, capability refusal, and concurrent subprocess writers. Log operations, expected/actual digests, and filesystem/object inventories.

## RESERVATIONS
- `src/distribution/backend.rs`
- `src/registry/transaction.rs`
- `tests/publication_backend_conformance.rs`
- `docs/OCI_ARTIFACTS.md`

## Considerations
This resolves the original S3-versus-wrapper question in favor of generic correctness: filesystem-first core, immutable OCI distribution, and a narrow capability seam. A provider-specific backend is future optional work only if repeated external demand justifies its dependency and maintenance cost.

title: Funds registry: deterministic mint from NPORT structured IDs — string workbench explicitly deferred
description:
Decision record (2026-07-07, operator + assessment): do NOT run the string entity-resolution workbench on fund names. NPORT-P provides a native identity spine — registrant CIK -> seriesId (S000...) -> LEI at registrant AND series level (regName/regLei/seriesName/seriesId/seriesLei all already extracted in edgar-elt stg_edgar_nport) — so fund identity is deterministic-key territory, not fuzzy-matching territory. Fund names are also maximally collidable ('Growth Fund', 'Income Fund II'): pointing the workbench at them is the false-merge corpus par excellence (NEWMARK lesson) with no upside when keys exist.

What to build instead (when demand arrives, not before — depth-before-breadth gates): a deterministic funds registry, deal-registry pattern: mint from (CIK, seriesId, LEI); accumulate seriesName/regName variants as time-stamped aliases KEYED BY structured id as filings arrive (fund renames become alias history, zero matching judgment); registry then rides the standard rails — dbt-seed export (bd-t1ay), search-index (bd-2mwa), IRI->holon front door (cmdrvl-context bd-2pmk).

Where string ER WOULD earn its keep later, demand-driven: (1) NPORT holdings issuer names where lei/cusip/isin are N/A (loans, repos, swaps, privates) -> canon ORGs; (2) external name-only sources joining into the funds registry. Neither is scheduled.

The high-value cross-product needs NO name ER: NPORT holdings -> CUSIP/FIGI -> unified bond table -> deal_ref = which funds hold which CMBS deals — pure identifier joins riding edgar-ddp br-k3y + edgar-elt br-2yun/br-2fnd. Capture-only: no build scheduled.
notes: This remains an operator deployment decision, not a Canon-core feature. It is related to the generic out-of-tree extension acceptance bead bd-doe2, but it does not block the open-source program and must not introduce fund, filing, or structured-finance semantics into Canon.

title: [SPLINK-STEAL/S5] external-candidate decision-import recipe (disposable Splink bridge; docs+fixtures only)
description:
## Problem this solves
Until S1/S3/S6 land, multi-column corpora (BDC loan/investment names: issuer + coupon + maturity + type — the shape Splink is genuinely good at) can use Splink's EM-calibrated scoring as a BOOTSTRAP candidate oracle. What canon lacks is a documented, fixture-tested recipe for importing externally-authored decisions through the EXISTING review import — with zero new runtime surface — so the bridge is disposable and core stays standalone. Keeps bd-3ofg (generic adapter contract) correctly deferred: no adapter runtime enters canon.

## Build (docs + fixtures only — no core code)
A doc (docs/EXTERNAL_CANDIDATE_IMPORT.md) specifying the full recipe:
1. Run canon entity run/link to produce artifacts + review queue as normal.
2. External scorer runs OUTSIDE canon (Splink, fully seeded: estimate_u(seed=...), EM from deterministic rules; the saved model JSON committed next to the decisions for provenance).
3. A conversion script (operator-owned, out of tree) authors decision files (match/distinct/defer) ONLY for items above an operator-set probability with no cannot-link conflict; everything else stays defer.
4. canon entity review import validates hashes and applies; audit + promote exactly as normal.
5. Sampled spot-check protocol: operator reviews N% of mechanically-authored decisions before promotion; document the sampling rule.
Include: a committed fixture pair (tiny corpus + pre-scored decisions file) proving the import path end-to-end offline; an explicit caveat that Splink is unsuitable for single-column vocabularies per its own docs ("not designed for a single bag-of-words column") — servicers, sponsors, instrument types stay pure canon; and a retirement clause: this recipe is scaffolding to be retired once S1/S3/S6 close the calibration gap.

## Splink reference (clone at /Users/zac/Source/opensource/splink)
- splink/internals/linker_components/training.py — estimate_u seed parameter (reproducibility requirement for any run feeding decisions)
- splink/internals/linker_components/misc.py — save_model_to_json (provenance artifact to commit)
- splink/internals/realtime.py — compare_records (scoring review-queue pairs directly)
- docs/index.md — the single-column unsuitability statement to quote

## How to test
- Fixture decisions import cleanly through the existing validator; receipts correct.
- Tampered/stale decision file -> atomic refusal (proves external authorship gets no special trust).
- Doc walkthrough is executable offline: canon-side test needs no network and no Python (fixtures are pre-generated and committed).

## Doctrine constraints
Zero canon code changes; the external tool has zero decision/registry/promotion authority — every decision flows through the existing validated import, audit, and promotion gates. This bead must not evolve into an adapter runtime (that is bd-3ofg, deferred).

title: [SPLINK-STEAL/S2] review export: evidence-signature grouping (decide patterns, not pairs)
description:
## Problem this solves
Review queues scale with item count, but most escrowed items share a handful of evidence signatures (same lanes/operators hit, same score band, same contradiction class). Reviewing item-by-item makes the CMBS tenant long tail humanly infeasible; deciding per-signature collapses thousands of decisions to dozens. This is the review-ergonomics half of the grind problem (S1 is the calibration half).

## Build
- Deterministic evidence-signature computation per review item: sorted (lane, operator, view/field) hit vector + banded score + contradiction class. Signature definition documented in the artifact schema.
- --group-by signature on canon entity review export (both queue and native-review artifacts): items grouped; each group carries signature, member count, deterministic sample members (first-N by stable ID), and aggregate score stats.
- Import side: accept group-level decisions that expand to per-member decisions inside the typed patch receipt — every member listed individually, per-item decision IDs and hash bindings preserved, per-member overrides win over the group decision.
- No new renderer or import format: extend the bd-14m6 native review substrate exactly as bd-fung mandates (single renderer, single validator).

## Splink reference (clone at /Users/zac/Source/opensource/splink)
- splink/internals/splink_comparison_viewer.py + comparison_vector_distribution.py — browse distinct agreement patterns with example rows; one look covers hundreds of pairs. This is the concept to port into the review artifact itself.

## How to test
- Fixture where 500 synthetic pairs collapse to <= 10 signatures; assert group counts and sample determinism.
- Group-decision import expands to exact per-member patches; replay import -> identical receipt.
- Tamper one member's binding -> atomic import refusal (existing staleness semantics unchanged).
- Per-member override coexists with group decision and wins.
- Signature stability under input row-order shuffle.
- Offline HTML projection renders groups with a network-disabled browser.

## Doctrine constraints
Grouping changes presentation and import ergonomics only — zero auto-accept, no change to decision authority, audit gates, or patch semantics.

## RESERVATIONS
- src/entity/review_export.rs
- src/entity/review_import.rs
- src/entity/review.rs
- tests/entity_review_signature_groups.rs
Note: S7 (waterfall) also touches review_export.rs — serialize if both in flight.

title: Refusal system (10 codes)
description:
Implement the refusal type system and helper constructors in src/refusal.rs.

This module defines types and serialization only. It does NOT decide which stream (stdout/stderr) to write to — that routing is the caller's responsibility (run() checks emit mode).

Types:
- RefusalCode enum with all 10 codes (E_IO, E_ENCODING, E_CSV_PARSE, E_BAD_REGISTRY, E_COLUMN_NOT_FOUND, E_PARSE, E_EMPTY_INPUT, E_TOO_LARGE, E_EMIT_FORMAT, E_COLUMN_EXISTS). Serializes to string (e.g. "E_IO").
- Refusal struct: code (RefusalCode), message (String), detail (serde_json::Value), next_command (Option<String>).

JSON envelope: wraps Refusal into a full CanonOutput with outcome=REFUSAL, registry=null, summary=null, mappings=[], unresolved=[], refusal=Some({...}). Uses the shared CanonOutput type from lib.rs.

Helper constructors for each code, e.g.:
- Refusal::column_not_found(column: &str, available: &[String]) -> Refusal
- Refusal::bad_registry(path: &str, reason: &str) -> Refusal
- Refusal::io_error(path: &str, err: &str) -> Refusal
- etc.

Each constructor populates message, detail, and next_command with actionable recovery guidance per PLAN_CANON.md.

Convenience method: Refusal::to_canon_output() -> CanonOutput (wraps into the full envelope for serialization).

title: [CANON-V1/P03.4] Put strategy audit behind a bounded, isolated execution runner
description:
## Background
Current strategy audit executes scripts without a complete timeout, resource, environment, filesystem, or network boundary. That is too much ambient authority for a standalone package that may ingest third-party procedures.

## Technical Approach
Create one strategy runner with explicit runtime allowlist, wall and CPU deadlines, memory/output/process/file limits, empty-by-default environment, owned scratch directory, read-only package and fixtures, closed stdin, and network denied by policy. Capture deterministic stdout/stderr digests and structured termination reasons. Refuse platforms where the declared isolation contract cannot be enforced rather than silently degrading.

## Success Criteria
- Infinite loops, fork/process storms, oversized output, filesystem escape, network access, and environment reads terminate or refuse within documented bounds.
- Audit cannot mutate strategy packages, fixtures, registries, project inputs, or arbitrary host paths.
- Termination artifacts distinguish fixture failure from timeout, resource limit, policy denial, and runner failure.
- Normal audited fixtures remain deterministic and usable offline.

## Test Plan
Run adversarial fixture executables for each capability and limit; inspect process trees and filesystem deltas; repeat under read-only and concurrent audits. Log runner policy, commands, exit status, signal/limit reason, and artifact hashes.

## RESERVATIONS
- `src/strategy/audit.rs`
- `src/strategy/runner.rs`
- `tests/strategy_sandbox.rs`

## Considerations
Portable isolation is difficult. State the enforceable contract per supported platform and fail closed; do not advertise a sandbox based only on conventions.

title: EPIC: canon geo — geospatial resolution as a first-class sibling to canon entity
description:
Build GEOSPATIAL RESOLUTION as a first-class workbench alongside canon entity. Designed natively for the geo problem, NOT bolted onto canon resolve (that two-tape CMBS tape matcher is the wrong substrate -- see bd-3g5q, closed).

== THESIS ==
canon entity resolves entities from graph structure and attribute evidence.
canon geo resolves PHYSICAL LOCATIONS from spatial structure and geometric evidence.
Same doctrine -- clusters are the unit of identity, source-namespaced IDs are participants bound by evidence, uncertain work happens in a workbench, review promotes, runtime lookup stays exact. Different evidence domain and different blocking key.

== WHY canon entity IS THE RIGHT PARENT ==
The mature machinery already exists and most of it transfers unchanged:
  multisource.rs   N-SOURCE link materialization with source names, comparison
                   graph validation, pair budgets, source-aware consistency
                   diagnostics. A geo tile carries six sources; this is solved.
  anti_merge.rs    distinctness / hard negatives -- exactly what spatial
                   exclusion needs (two buildings 500m apart are NOT the same;
                   two footprints in one source are NOT the same)
  relation.rs      typed relationships -- same_as vs contains vs part_of, which
                   the geo answer requires and a boolean cannot express
  block/index/postings/block_artifact   blocking machinery
  candidates.rs + budget.rs             bounded candidate generation
  evidence.rs, evidence_ir.rs, edge.rs, edge_artifact.rs   evidence model
  ledger.rs + ledger_replay.rs          replay
  promote / review / publication / inbox   the accepted-knowledge path
  explain.rs, patches.rs, audit.rs, lint.rs, diagnostics.rs

== WHAT IS GENUINELY NEW (the actual scope) ==
1. TILE BLOCKING. H3 cell membership replaces ngram/postings blocking. It is
   EXACT where name-trigram blocking is lossy both ways: a building in one cell
   never matches one three cells away. Buffered by k-ring 1 (7 cells) so
   boundary features resolve; halo decisions discarded. H3 res-9 = 0.105 km2,
   ~201m edge, roughly a city block, ~167 nodes across six sources.
2. GEOMETRY AS A TYPED VALUE. Points and polygons as first-class column types.
   Decision needed: geometry dependency in core, or out-of-tree extension per
   IDENTITY_ARCHITECTURE.md's domain-expertise boundary.
   HARD REQUIREMENT: EXACT geometric predicates (adaptive-precision orientation,
   Shewchuk-style), NOT naive float. Naive float point-in-polygon is
   non-deterministic precisely on boundary-adjacent points, which is the entire
   population of interest. This is a determinism bug, not a rounding detail.
3. SPATIAL EVIDENCE OPERATORS. within, intersects, distance_lt, area_ratio,
   iou_gt, constellation_consistent -- same shape as the existing exact /
   tolerance_pct / range / prefix operators, expressed in the strategy surface
   so core stays domain-free.
4. ADDRESS OPERATORS -- TWO, NOT ONE.
   address_match  normalization (case, abbreviation expansion, unit handling)
   address_range  parse '100-101 Main' as [100,101] and test containment
   The motivating case ('100 Main' vs '100-101 Main') CANNOT be decided by
   string similarity -- edit distance says near-identical, but they may be one
   property or two different buildings. Range parsing plus geometry decides it.
5. TILE ARTIFACT + PROVIDER. Content-addressed tile served by a geo MCP server
   (acquisition, network) then consumed by an OFFLINE provider emitting typed
   facts -- PROVIDER_SDK.md forbids network access inside a provider build.
   Subset predicate = the H3 cell set, so 'why is this row in my tile' is
   answerable by construction.
6. ABSTENTION AS A REPORTED RATE. 'Zero matches is a finding, not a failure'
   already holds; geo needs the abstention rate as a first-class metric because
   it is an OC-0048 success criterion and dense urban will be ambiguous often.

== WHY GEO IS EASIER THAN PERSON ER ==
1. HARD NEGATIVES EXIST. Distance gives definitive non-matches. Person ER has
   no equivalent; name similarity generates none. anti_merge already models this.
2. WITHIN-SOURCE MUTUAL EXCLUSION. Two Overture buildings are not the same
   building. Two CRM rows CAN be the same person.
3. CARDINALITY PRIOR. A tile has approximately N buildings; a clustering
   producing 3N is wrong by construction.
4. CONSTELLATION CONSISTENCY. Relative arrangement survives across sources even
   when coordinates, counts and attributes differ. Right matching aligns the
   whole block under one transform; wrong matching does not. A global check no
   attribute-based ER can perform.
5. EMBARRASSINGLY PARALLEL. A feature in tile X never matches one in tile Y.
   Person ER is globally connected. Geo shards perfectly.

== NO HEAVY MATH IN v1 ==
At ~167 nodes exhaustive evaluation is affordable, hard constraints prune most
pairs, and the evidence is near-dispositive rather than fuzzy (point-in-polygon
is a boolean; APN equality is string equality; IoU 0.95 is done). Ship a
DETERMINISTIC OPERATOR CASCADE with abstention. Then MEASURE THE RESIDUAL. Only
if the residual justifies it, add permutation synchronization / correlation
clustering / Sinkhorn assignment -- and only in the workbench as candidate
generation and scoring, never in runtime. canon already forces this boundary.

== ENTITY TYPES ==
Buildings and parcels resolve LOCALLY per tile. Chains, brands, sponsors and
owners are ORG entities and resolve GLOBALLY through canon entity. Both land in
one registry. Two entity types, two blocking strategies, one identity model.

== OPEN DESIGN DECISIONS ==
- src/geo/ as a sibling module to src/entity/, or a geo profile/strategy inside
  entity? Leaning sibling module reusing entity's artifact and review path.
- Geometry dependency in core vs out-of-tree extension.
- Tile unit: H3 res-9 default; confirm against real node-count distributions.
- How typed containment edges map onto the existing edge/relation artifacts.
- Whether the tile artifact is a DataBook.

== DRIVEN BY ==
cmdrvl-context OC-0048 (Location Master) -- proving ground is BBL on every CMBS
property in NYC, scored against PLUTO. Upstream of OC-0045, OC-0046, OC-0047,
none of which can join their corpora without this.
NYC acquisition: cmdrvl-context bd-1g1h; channels registered under
data_provider://nyc open data with T2/T3 beads in cmdrvl-gtm and cmdrvl-curves.

== CHILDREN NOT YET CUT ==
Architecture decisions above come first.

OC-0045/0046/0047 all assume they can be joined, so this is UPSTREAM of all three and should be sequenced first. Newmark, CRED iQ and others are demand, not the reason.

comments.author: zac
comments.text:
CORRECTION TO THE EPIC 2026-08-14, from measured NYC data (baseline on bd-bmee).

The section 'WHY GEO IS EASIER THAN PERSON ER' claim 2 states: 'WITHIN-SOURCE MUTUAL EXCLUSION. Two Overture buildings are not the same building.' THIS IS SOURCE-DEPENDENT AND IS FALSE FOR NYC TAX LOTS.

MapPLUTO legitimately carries condo UNIT billing BBLs that overlap the condo PARENT lot, in the same source and the same release. Measured: a single CMBS geocode point lands inside more than one MapPLUTO polygon often enough to make row counts disagree across query formulations (6,682 rows / 6,255 distinct points / 6,388 in-lot, with a by-borough Manhattan in-lot count of 5,494 against a 3,420 total).

The correct statement is that within-source mutual exclusion is a PER-SOURCE PROPERTY that must be declared, not a global geo invariant. It holds for building footprints. It does not hold for parcel/tax-lot sources with condo aggregation. Overlap in such a source is a part_of relation (bd-3soj), not an anti_merge distinctness violation — treating it as the latter would suppress a true relationship.

Claim 3 (CARDINALITY PRIOR: 'a tile has approximately N buildings') needs the same qualification: a tile has approximately N BUILDINGS but an unbounded number of overlapping LEGAL parcels once condos are included, so the prior applies per entity type, not per tile.

The other three claims — hard negatives from distance, constellation consistency, embarrassing parallelism — are unaffected.

REALITY CHECK 2026-08-14 (code-verified) + ARCHITECTURE SETTLED: BRING-YOUR-OWN-PARCEL.

== PART 1: THE REUSE CLAIM IS SUBSTANTIALLY WRONG. Verified against source. ==

This epic says "the mature machinery already exists and most of it transfers unchanged."
That is true for the PLUMBING and false for the MATCHING LAYER. canon entity is a NAME
resolver. Its operator vocabularies are closed const arrays in core, and every entry is
textual:

  src/entity/profile.rs:833-886 -- four closed `const &[&str]` arrays:
    SUPPORTED_NORMALIZE_OPS      19 entries, all string ops
    SUPPORTED_SUPPORT_OPS         6 entries: exact_view, token_overlap,
                                  string_similarity, tfidf_cosine,
                                  alias_patch_match, reviewed_alias
    SUPPORTED_CANNOT_LINK_OPS    10 entries, all lexical
    SUPPORTED_RELATION_HINT_OPS   8 entries, all org-hierarchy semantics
  NOT ONE OPERATOR TAKES A NUMBER, let alone a coordinate.

  src/entity/block.rs:52 -- BlockCandidateOperator is a closed 3-variant enum
    (NgramTopK | RareTokenOverlap | AliasPatchMatch). All postings/text.
  src/entity/record_link.rs:153 -- RecordLinkFeatureKind = Numeric|Date|Categorical.
    No geometry variant.
  Cargo.toml -- ELEVEN dependencies, ZERO geospatial. The matching engine is
    `rapidfuzz`, a string-similarity crate.

WHAT ACTUALLY TRANSFERS (genuinely excellent, ~30K LOC): artifact chain + content
hashing, ledger + ledger_replay, promote/review/publication/inbox, budget enforcement,
explain/audit/lint/diagnostics, ScoreUnits(u32) integer boundary, the three-lane
evidence model.

WHAT IS NEW CONSTRUCTION (not reuse): every blocking operator, every evidence operator,
every normalization operator, the geometry typed value, the typed relation vocabulary,
spatial anti-merge.

CONSEQUENCE: bd-3ccc, bd-gs6n, bd-3soj and part of bd-2b9d are written as "reuse X"
where X does not do what is claimed. They have been corrected individually. Do not let
an implementing agent discover this mid-build.

== PART 2: THREE MORE VERIFIED FINDINGS ==

1. THERE IS NO EXTENSION RUNTIME. src/extensions/ is 12,346 LOC and is NOT declared in
   src/lib.rs. The only thing that compiles it is tests/domain_neutrality.rs via
   `#[path = "../src/extensions/mod.rs"]`. It is contract types with tests,
   disconnected from the binary. bd-15ba's "core vs out-of-tree extension" is a FALSE
   BINARY today -- choosing extension means building the host first, which no bead
   scopes.

2. CORE IS ALREADY NOT DOMAIN-FREE. src/entity/profile.rs ships strip_tenant_noise,
   strip_regab_noise, tenant_brand_fingerprint, drop_tenant_stopwords. The doctrine is
   already breached in practice, so geometry-in-core has precedent. Make the call
   explicitly rather than discovering it.

3. multisource.rs IS THE ONE REUSE CLAIM THAT HOLDS UP -- BUT IT IS LIBRARY-ONLY.
   EntityMultisourceInput carries per-source name/role/local_id_column/anchor_namespace;
   EntitySourceRole = {CanonicalReference,Reference,Target,Peer}; EntitySourceComparison
   budgets each source pair independently; EntityAnchorConflict abstains on
   disagreement. Excellent fit for a multi-source tile. HOWEVER: grep for `multisource`
   in cli.rs/lib.rs/main.rs returns NOTHING. The only caller is
   tests/entity_multisource.rs. The CLI is strictly two-tape
   (`canon entity link <REFERENCE> <TARGET>`). N-source CLI wiring is UNSCOPED and is
   now ON THE CRITICAL PATH.

== PART 3: GOOD NEWS, VERIFIED BY RUNNING THE PIPELINE ==

Ran canon entity run on tests/fixtures/entity/cmbs/small_book/observations.csv:
15 rows -> 14 surfaces -> 23 candidate pairs -> 23 EVIDENCE RECORDS. LOSING CANDIDATES
ARE ALREADY RETAINED, including pairs scoring zero, each with per-hit lane /
operator_id / reason_code / score_units / hard_cannot_link / explanation. bd-101v calls
this "the big one" and flags it for verification -- IT IS ALREADY SATISFIED at the
evidence stage. Do not rebuild it.

Also verified working: ScoreUnits(u32) scale 10,000 integer artifact boundary;
`--profile <path>` loads profiles from YAML files; 404/404 library tests pass.

== PART 4: ARCHITECTURE SETTLED 2026-08-14 -- BRING YOUR OWN PARCEL (BYOP) ==

OPERATOR DECISION. canon geo is PARCEL-SOURCE AGNOSTIC. Clients bring their own
licensed parcel layer (one client subscribes to ATTOM). We never redistribute an APN
corpus -- already the stated non-goal in OC-0048.

  OUR SIDE (geo MCP serves content-addressed H3 tiles of OUR datasets, 4-5 at launch):
  Overture building GERS, FEMA USA Structures, Microsoft GlobalML footprints, NYC Open
  Data / MapPLUTO where free. Plus MSCI RCA where licensed.

  CLIENT SIDE: their licensed parcel geometry (ATTOM/Regrid/LightBox), which may be
  PARTIAL -- clipped, county-limited, or subscription-scoped -- plus their property
  book.

  CANON: composes the graph across both, locally, on the client's machine.

THIS RESOLVES THE NATIONAL PARCEL BLOCKER. It stops being our acquisition problem and
becomes a client input contract question. It also STRENGTHENS geometry-in-core for
bd-15ba: the client runs canon locally against their own licensed data, so an
out-of-tree extension means they install two things and we cannot guarantee the
predicate that determinism depends on.

CLIENT INPUT CONTRACT -- SETTLED, SIX FIELDS (operator decision 2026-08-14). These are
what can reasonably be expected from ANY source:
  geocode (lat/lon)   address   geometry   building size   year built   property type
The first three drive geometry; the last three are independent attribute channels that
REJECT wrong matches rather than find right ones. OC-0048's Client input contract
section currently lists only address + geocode + soft disambiguators and must be
amended to make geometry required-or-declared.

H3 INDEXING OF THE CLIENT LAYER HAPPENS IN CANON (operator decision 2026-08-14).
Pure-Rust H3 ports exist (h3o); no C bindings, deterministic. The client must not need
their own H3 tooling.

== PART 5: SIX NEW REQUIREMENTS BYOP CREATES, NONE PREVIOUSLY BEAD-COVERED ==

1. COVERAGE ABSTENTION vs NO-MATCH ABSTENTION. The sharpest one.
   EntityMultisourceAbstentionReason has EXACTLY ONE VARIANT: AnchorConflict. With
   partial boundaries the cascade MUST distinguish "the client's layer does not cover
   this tile" from "no parcel contains this point." Conflating them is a silent-error
   mode and is precisely the class OC-0048 forbids.
2. TWO GEOMETRY SOURCES WITH ASYMMETRIC TRUST. bd-1uld models one. The subset predicate
   becomes an INTERSECTION of our tile's H3 cell set and the client's coverage
   predicate.
3. CLIENT-LAYER H3 INGEST. Our tiles ship pre-indexed; their extract does not.
4. ARTIFACT LICENSE CONTAINMENT. bd-101v requires geometry at DECISION FIDELITY in the
   artifact. Client parcel geometry in the artifact makes it license-encumbered and
   unable to round-trip to us -- no hosted debugging, no scoring their runs, no hosted
   evidence-signature review (bd-2jfj).
5. TWO-REGISTRY COMPOSITION + TILE-REFRESH ID STABILITY. bd-67wx models one registry and
   says minting is a promotion event. Tile-shipped cmdrvl:building:* IDs are minted at
   OUR promotion, before the client ever runs. If a tile refresh reassigns them, every
   client registry breaks.
6. THE PROVING GROUND TESTS A DIFFERENT CONFIGURATION THAN THE PRODUCT. bd-bmee has us
   supplying MapPLUTO. Fine as a cascade proof; nothing tests the BYOP path.

== PART 6: THE RESIDUAL CONSTRAINT IS NOT PARCELS. IT IS GEOCODE COVERAGE. ==

PROPERTY_MART.PROPERTY_DIM: 50,593 rows, 25,884 geocoded (51%), backfill blocked on a
frozen Geocodio account (br-ppnr blocked on br-1zo6). Ginnie's native key is a POOL
NUMBER WITH NO ADDRESS FIELD AT ALL. Annex A `Various` addresses never geocoded.
Geometry cannot key what has no location. This ceiling binds before canon geo does any
work and must be reported in every coverage denominator.

== PART 7: SEQUENCING DEFECT -- THE KILL CRITERION CANNOT BE EVALUATED ==

bd-bmee says "BASELINE FIRST: run plain address-string matching and record its
precision and recall. That is the number the deterministic cascade must beat." WHAT WAS
ACTUALLY MEASURED on 2026-08-14 is GEOMETRY-ONLY point-in-polygon hit rate (95.49%,
tier-broken-out) -- not address-string precision/recall. THE KILL-CRITERION COMPARATOR
HAS NEVER BEEN MEASURED. Meanwhile OC-0048 says Phase 0 "Not yet run" while bd-bmee's
comments show a baseline was run. Both are half right; the half that matters is missing.

Worse, the chain is four deep and the cheapest falsifying experiment sits at the bottom:

  bd-67wx --+
            +--> bd-3ccc --+--> bd-2b9d --+
  bd-15ba --+              +--> bd-1zph   +--> bd-bmee   <-- kill criterion lives here
                           +--> bd-gs6n --+

YOU CANNOT FAIL FAST ON THIS PLAN. The address-string baseline has been cut as its own
READY bead with no dependencies -- it is SQL only, no canon, no code.

== PART 8: THE AMBITION LANE IS NOW SCOPED, AND STILL GATED ON THE RESIDUAL ==

This epic's "NO HEAVY MATH IN v1 ... ship a DETERMINISTIC OPERATOR CASCADE with
abstention, then MEASURE THE RESIDUAL" discipline is CORRECT and is retained unchanged.
What was missing is that the post-residual layer was named but never scoped, so it read
as aspiration rather than plan. It is now a real bead chain, every member gated behind
an explicit residual-measurement harness that must justify it:

  optimal assignment (Hungarian/JV)  -- deterministic, polynomial, exact. The honest
                                        baseline the fancy methods must beat.
  constellation consistency          -- spectral graph matching over a geometric
                                        affinity matrix. The missing v1 operator.
  correlation clustering             -- the correct objective for canon's +/- evidence
                                        lanes. Deterministic pivot/LP rounding.
  permutation synchronization        -- multi-source global consistency across the
                                        6-7 named sources in a BYOP tile.
  entropic OT / Sinkhorn             -- soft assignment under cardinality priors.
                                        Determinism risk; fixed-iteration + integer
                                        quantization required.

None of these may enter runtime lookup. All are workbench candidate generation and
scoring only, per the boundary canon already enforces.

CORRECTION 2026-08-14 — THE "51% GEOCODED" FIGURE IS WRONG. I cited it repeatedly this
session, including in this bead. Operator questioned it and was right.

WHAT I REPEATED, sourced from OC-0048: "PROPERTY_MART.PROPERTY_DIM holds 50,593 rows with
only 25,884 geocoded (51%) ... that is a hard coverage ceiling."

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY MEASURED (edgar-elt br-ppnr, 2026-07-23, against
WRGL_EDGAR_CRE_PROPERTIES__DEDUPED, applying the br-351x identity normalization and the
committed placeholder seed list):
    total_distinct_properties   38,365
    placeholder_excluded         4,245   DEFEASED, VARIOUS, -, N/A, NA, UNKNOWN
    geocodable_denominator      34,120
    geocoded                    33,219
    COVERAGE                    97.36%   of geocodable

THE REAL REMAINING GAP IS ABOUT 901 PROPERTIES, NOT ~24,700.

WHY THE FIGURES DIVERGE. The 51% number counts a denominator that includes addresses which
CAN NEVER GEOCODE -- defeased and placeholder entries whose address field is blank or
literal "VARIOUS". Excluding them is not generosity; it is the same denominator definition
br-1ni6's geo_coverage_pct uses, pinned to the same normalization macros so the two cannot
drift. A coverage rate computed over ungeocodable rows is not a coverage rate.
The 50,593 row count is also a different grain from 38,365 distinct properties, so the two
statements were never comparable to begin with.

WHAT THIS CHANGES IN THIS BEAD AND ACROSS THE EPIC:
1. GEOCODE COVERAGE IS NOT THE BINDING CONSTRAINT ON THE PROPERTY BOOK. I described it as a
   ceiling that "binds before canon geo does any work." At 97.36% of geocodable it does not.
   Strike that framing wherever it appears.
2. WHAT REMAINS A REAL LIMIT, UNCHANGED:
   - `Various` addresses genuinely never geocoded, and there are 4,245 placeholder identities.
     They still need the Annex A parse (edgar-elt br-6iii), not geometry, and they are still
     excluded-and-counted per OC-0048's denominator-honesty criterion.
   - Ginnie Mae still has no address field at its native pool grain.
   - The AGENCY tables are a separate and much larger population that is genuinely NOT
     geocoded yet -- cmdrvl-curves bd-25xz covers roughly 90,000 records (15,579 Ginnie
     street addresses plus 74,349 HUD FHA multifamily at city/state/zip). THAT is the real
     coverage gap for the agency corpora, and it is ON HOLD (bd-13mx).
3. bd-14hu's argument IMPROVES. Pre-resolving our own corpora looked weaker when half the
   property book appeared ungeocoded. At 97.36% the CMBS side is effectively ready to
   pre-resolve now, and the work concentrates on the agency tables rather than on backfill.

MEASURED GEOCODE HISTORY, for anyone sizing this work (2026-08-14, literal query):
WRGL_EDGAR_CMBS_GEOCODES__STRUCTURED -- 68,603 rows, 54,690 distinct PROPERTY_ADDRESS,
4,149 addresses appearing under more than one ASOF because the ETL appends rather than
upserts. Dominated by the 2025-01 initial load (45,114 rows) and an unexplained 2026-08
batch (14,714 rows / 14,242 distinct).

PROCESS NOTE: this is the fourth claim this session that came from prose rather than a
measured value, and the third that was wrong. The 51% figure was in a document I trusted;
the 97.36% figure was in a bead comment recording an actual query. WHEN TWO NUMBERS
DISAGREE, PREFER THE ONE WITH A RECORDED METHOD AND A DENOMINATOR DEFINITION.

comments.author: Zac
comments.text:
ARCHITECTURE SUPERSEDED 2026-08-15 — see docs/PLAN_CANON_GEO.md.

An adversarial multi-model design session produced a materially different architecture,
which then survived a red team that destroyed two intermediate designs. The tile is modelled
as a BOUNDED UNIVERSE and every piece of evidence is a CONSTRAINT; propagation runs to a
fixpoint; the residual model set IS the answer. There is no proposer channel.

THE THREE PROPERTIES THAT MATTER:
- CONFLUENCE. The fixpoint is independent of the order constraints are applied (Tarski 1955;
  Cousot & Cousot 1977; Apt 1999), so determinism is a theorem rather than an engineering
  effort.
- MONOTONICITY. Constraints only add and domains only shrink, so a tile resolved with four
  sources today and six next year yields a TIGHTER residual, never a contradicting one. The
  earlier answer was never wrong, only less resolved.
- STRUCTURAL ABSTENTION. The residual model set is the answer. No threshold anywhere.

THE KEY DESIGN RULE IS rho, THE SOUNDNESS DISCIPLINE. Every source attribute enters the
solver only through a declared versioned relaxation mapping it to the WEAKEST constraint the
source can actually support. An interpolated geocode becomes a 150m disc rather than a
location. A parcel ADDRESS becomes "one of this lot's addresses" rather than functional
equality. OWNERNAME equal PERMITS an assemblage; OWNERNAME different constrains NOTHING.
Every noisy channel is admitted only in its sound direction — which is what dissolved the
proposer dilemma that broke the two earlier designs.

AND THE COMMERCIAL CONSEQUENCE: if every rho is sound, the true assignment is in the model
set, so AN EMPTY MODEL SET IS A PROOF that a named source violated its own published error
model — attributable, falsifiable, and mailable to the vendor.

Read PLAN_CANON_GEO.md before starting any geo work. Section 11 carries the bead-by-bead
supersession table. Appendix A covers frozen-weight observers and imagery sources. APPENDIX
B RECORDS THE FIRST HARD MEASUREMENT, WHICH FALSIFIED A LOAD-BEARING CLAIM — read it before
trusting any performance number in the plan.

Raw session artifacts, including the red team and the adversarial reviews, are preserved
under docs/geo_design_session/ with a reading guide.

title: canon geo: E4 factorized residual solver and component-budget fallback
description: Replace the E4 residual kernel global 2^N assignment materialization with an exact deterministic factorized solver. Compile a constraint-incidence graph from building-to-parcel structural relations and every hard constraint referenced members; any live constraint spanning variables keeps them in the same component. Solve independent components exactly, represent unconstrained variables symbolically, and combine exact residual cardinality and backbone without enumerating the Cartesian product. For oversized connected components, use deterministic propagation or backtracking with partial-feasibility pruning and declared budgets; budget exhaustion returns a typed component-budget fallback with recovery guidance. Preserve the workbench-only truth firewall, exact-runtime boundary, conflict provenance, and byte determinism. Do not add NYC-specific identifiers, source names, thresholds, or demo-path special cases. Code and behavioral tests ship in this bead.
design: Compile one deterministic incidence graph over candidate variables, structural relations, and hard constraints. Stable component identity and traversal order derive only from canonical member and constraint identifiers. A constraint that references variables across a proposed partition merges those variables; no hard constraint may be evaluated component-locally unless its full support is in that component. Free variables are exact symbolic factors. Small constrained components are enumerated exactly. Large constrained components use deterministic propagation and partial-feasibility pruning under explicit work and materialization budgets. The artifact records the factorization, exact checked global residual count, exact global backbone, local counts, work statistics, and whether model materialization is exhaustive. If compact output changes wire meaning, bump the declared contract version rather than silently reinterpreting residual_models. Soft evidence may produce a deterministic bounded k-best presentation over the frozen hard residual but cannot change feasibility, backbone, status, or promotion.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The checked-in 15-case E4 population evaluates to exact resolved or ambiguous factorized artifacts with zero assignment-budget-exceeded cases; it preserves abstention and zero false merges, and reports candidate reach and truth recall separately rather than treating missing truth candidates as solver error.
2. A positive case whose unconstrained global model count exceeds the old 65,536 assignment ceiling returns the exact count and backbone without materializing the full Cartesian product. A positive parcel-star case with independent local factors does the same.
3. Small factorized cases match a brute-force oracle for status, exact residual count, backbone, conflict provenance, and deterministic bounded soft ranking. Input and constraint permutations produce byte-identical canonical output.
4. A hard cardinality or integer-sum constraint spanning variables is never split into independent factors. Contradictory constraints return Conflict with deterministic minimal conflict identifiers. A deliberately oversized connected hard component returns the typed component-budget fallback with component ID, variables, constraints, measured work, configured limit, and a recovery command or parameter.
5. Compact artifacts cannot imply that a partial residual_models list is exhaustive: factorization and materialization state are explicit and contract-versioned. All counts use checked integer arithmetic and overflow is typed.
6. Production code contains no fixture IDs, NYC source names, learned thresholds, or case-specific branches. The workbench truth firewall and exact promoted-registry replay boundary remain intact.
7. cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, and cargo test pass.
close_reason: Exact factorized residual solver acceptance restored and adversarially verified across width, overflow, saturation, budget, incidence, provenance, determinism, and fallback cases; full repository quality gate passed.

title: [CANON-V1/P08.2] Implement deterministic local pack, unpack, inspect, and verify
description:
## Background
Operators need complete offline control before any remote publishing exists. A package must be inspectable and verifiable without trusting filename, tag, or ambient cache.

## Technical Approach
Implement local OCI-layout and single-file archive operations over canonical package bytes. Normalize paths/modes/order, reject links/path traversal/duplicates, verify every digest and semantic contract, unpack only into an explicit empty owned target, and expose structured inventory, provenance, licenses, dependencies, and required capabilities.

## Success Criteria
- Equivalent trees produce identical package and layout digests across workspaces.
- Verify detects content, manifest, path, mode, dependency, and schema tampering.
- Inspect and verify work read-only and offline without writing inside source packages.
- Unpack never overwrites existing content or escapes the target.

## Test Plan
Pack twice, compare bytes, mutate every layer/metadata class, exercise malicious archives, read-only inspection, non-empty targets, Unicode paths, and interruption. Record filesystem deltas.

- `src/distribution/package.rs`
- `src/cli.rs`
- `tests/package_local.rs`

## Considerations
Reuse one safe archive implementation across package kinds; do not proliferate near-identical packers.

title: [CANON-V1/P01] Immutable registry substrate and deployment export backends
description:
## Background
Registry files are Canon's durable product. Existing dbt-seed and searchable SQLite index exports are valuable deployment backends and must be retained. Today normal lookup may write _index.sqlite inside the registry and invalidate it with mtimes, which conflicts with immutable packaging and read-only deployment.

## Scope

## Success Criteria
A registry can be mounted read-only, verified by digest, queried with identical semantics, and exported deterministically to dbt seed or search index with package/version/provenance metadata. Existing export consumers require no loss of functionality.

## Test Plan
Read-only filesystem tests, cache corruption/invalidation tests, concurrent builders, byte-stable exports, dbt fixture execution, SQLite query goldens, canonical IRI parity, and old-versus-new regression fixtures.

The native engine handles demanding unknown-domain workloads without Python, hosted services, optional adapters, or industry branches. Every candidate, veto, decision, and abstention can be inspected, reproduced, and routed to review.

title: [CANON-V1/P12.8] Prove identity knowledge accretes across sequential registry snapshots
description:
## Background
Canon is intended to compile uncertain identity work into an exact reusable registry. That claim is stronger than resolving one batch: reviewed knowledge must make later batches cheaper and more exact without making history irreproducible or propagating a bad merge.

## Technical Approach
Create a sequential evaluation protocol over versioned batches and registry snapshots. Resolve batch A from a pinned registry, review and promote accepted aliases, links, relationships, and explicit non-equivalence constraints into a new immutable snapshot, then resolve later batches B through N. Report exact-first coverage, non-exact candidate recall, auto-link, review, abstention, correction rate, and human decisions per unique surface at each step. Include versioned corrections, supersession, rollback by digest, temporal validity, and relationship changes without mutating earlier artifacts. Compare cold-start and accrued-registry runs on identical future observations.

## Success Criteria
- Accepted knowledge from batch A increases exact or high-confidence coverage on later batches by a measured amount.
- Replaying any batch with its original registry and policy digest is byte-stable.
- A correction creates a new snapshot and can suppress a bad alias prospectively without rewriting historical evidence.
- Accretion is measured per unique observation surface, not inflated by repeated physical rows.
- New aliases cannot silently broaden into parent, subsidiary, successor, or related-party equivalence.
- The report makes review burden and marginal knowledge gain visible for every snapshot.

## Test Plan
Use sequential fixtures containing recurring aliases, previously unseen aliases, successor changes, parent-subsidiary ambiguity, a deliberately wrong promotion followed by correction, and repeated rows. Run cold and warm sequences, rollback to an earlier digest, shuffle within batches, and verify deterministic outputs and append-only lineage.

## RESERVATIONS
- src/entity/eval.rs
- src/entity/registry.rs
- src/entity/promote.rs
- tests/entity_accretion.rs
- tests/fixtures/canon_v1/quality/sequential/
- docs/ENTITY_REGISTRY_LIFECYCLE.md

## Considerations
Accretion is the core economic loop: review should purchase durable exactness. A growing registry that merely accumulates unverified aliases or hides regressions is negative compounding.

title: canon registry export --format search-index: standard SQLite search artifact for serving endpoints
description:
Second member of the registry-export family (sibling of bd-t1ay dbt-seed): export any versioned registry as a standard, self-describing SQLite search index that consumers can drop behind a search endpoint (first target: cmdrvl-receipts find_deals; the pattern generalizes to any registry behind any lookup endpoint).

Motivation: the same search grammar is now hand-rolled in >=3 places — canon resolve (Rust), cmdrvl-receipts ReceiptsStore.resolveDeal, and findDealsInCoveredDeals's five-tier scorer (exact/prefix/contains/reverse-contains/raw text with field weights). Same tiers, same normalization idea, three codebases, guaranteed drift. Precedent in embryo: canon already builds registries/firms/_index.sqlite (registry.rs) but as a PRIVATE exact-input cache (input->canonical_id, version+mtime metadata) — this feature promotes that into a consumer-facing artifact.

Design requirements:
- SQLite single-file artifact (readable Node/Python/Rust, no services; FTS5 for contains/fuzzy). Determinism: content-hash the logical dump, not the file bytes.
- Tables: entities (canonical_id, display fields, external keys e.g. CIK), aliases (alias, alias_kind: name|short|ticker|variant, normalized_key), optional FTS5/trigram table.
- Scoring spec travels IN the artifact as data (tier->score map, field weights, alias-kind weights) so consumers share semantics without sharing code.
- Normalization function spec'd + versioned in artifact metadata (normalizeDealName-style uppercase/strip is duplicated in TS and Rust today; index-build vs query-time mismatch silently kills recall).
- Metadata: registry name, version, content hash, normalization spec version, generated-at — same drift-tripwire doctrine as the dbt seed.
- Identity only: no coverage/serving data in the index; consumers intersect with their own scope (receipts: 539 covered of 2062 registered) and attach domain data from their own stores.

Refs: bd-t1ay (dbt-seed sibling), bd-2exe (S3 IO), cmdrvl-receipts bd-1mr + new consumer bead, edgar-elt br-1mly (alias flow via manifest — the index supersedes manifest-alias search if adopted). Capture-only: no build scheduled.
