title: Lookup engine (exact match)
description:
Implement the lookup engine in src/lookup.rs.

Takes InputValues (from input module) and Registry (from registry module), resolves each unique value against the SQLite index, returns ResolveResult.

Process:
1. Open SQLite connection to Registry.db_path.
2. For each value in InputValues.values: query entries table for exact byte match on input column. First match wins (ORDER BY source_file ASC, entry_order ASC LIMIT 1).
3. If match found: create Mapping { input (raw), canonical_id, canonical_type, rule_id, confidence: "deterministic" }.
4. If no match: create UnresolvedEntry { input: Some(raw_value), reason: "no matching rule" }.
5. For each SpecialReason in InputValues.special (where count > 0): create UnresolvedEntry { input: None, reason: special_reason.to_string() }. At most one entry per distinct reason regardless of count.
6. Build Summary: total = mappings.len() + unresolved.len(), resolved = mappings.len(), unresolved_count = unresolved.len(). Invariant: total == resolved + unresolved_count.
7. Determine outcome (not stored in ResolveResult — derived by caller from summary counts).

Performance: batch queries where possible. For large InputValues, consider prepared statement reuse.
acceptance_criteria: TARGET FILE: src/lookup.rs only. Include #[cfg(test)] mod tests. Test: exact match lookup, no-match unresolved, special reason entries (one per distinct reason), summary invariant (total == resolved + unresolved), first-match-wins precedence. VERIFICATION: cargo test -- lookup
close_reason: Lookup engine complete - comprehensive SQLite-based exact match resolution with prepared statements, proper precedence (ORDER BY source_file ASC, entry_order ASC LIMIT 1), special reason handling, summary invariant verification, and 7 passing tests covering all scenarios.

title: Fix add-entry stale-plan lost-update race and make proof deterministic
description: Aggregate cargo test exposed a production atomicity defect, not only a harness flake. In src/registry/add_entry.rs, plan_add_entry builds proposed bytes from one registry snapshot, but commit_add_entry_plan rereads current files and uses those commit-time bytes as the expected hashes. A stale writer can therefore plan Beta against an empty registry, observe Alpha at commit time, validate Ready, then overwrite Alpha while both calls report success. TopazMill documented the interleaving in Agent Mail message 6740. Fix the optimistic write plan so expected state is bound to the bytes/snapshot used during planning and validated under the mutation guard before any write. Add a scheduler-independent same-module proof that precomputes two conflicting plans, commits the first, and proves the second refuses E_BAD_REGISTRY with field write_plan_hash and writes_performed=false while final state retains only the winner. Replace or tighten the integration concurrency assertion so it permits only safe outcomes and always detects lost updates; do not use mkfifo, lsof, platform-specific tools, longer sleeps, or entered-thread counters as the proof. RESERVATIONS: src/registry/add_entry.rs; tests/registry_concurrency.rs. Preserve identical-plan idempotence, atomic rollback, lint behavior, exact registry semantics, and existing public output. No other production files.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Plan expected hashes/state derive from the exact plan-time source snapshot, never commit-time rereads. 2. Deterministic same-module conflicting-plan test proves first commit succeeds, second stale plan refuses E_BAD_REGISTRY/write_plan_hash/writes_performed=false, final aliases length is one, version is 1.0.1. 3. Public concurrent integration test accepts only safe serialization or stale-refusal outcomes and fails any lost update. 4. Identical plans remain idempotent and no partial writes occur. 5. rustfmt, focused clippy/tests, repeated registry_concurrency stress, git diff --check, then aggregate cargo test pass. 6. Exact Agent Mail leases and start/finish/review evidence; no commits or pushes by workers.
close_reason: Fixed add-entry stale-plan lost updates with guarded plan snapshots, safe lease publication, deterministic private proofs, portable public safety assertions, stress, and adversarial PASS.

title: [CANON-V1/P05.3] Model source-scoped aliases, anchor validity, and conflict policy
description:
## Background
An alias can be valid only for one source, product line, or period; an anchor can be reassigned, corrected, or recycled. Flattening these claims too early creates false exact matches.

## Technical Approach
Define identity predicates for name/identifier aliases and trusted anchors with scope and intervals. Create deterministic conflict classes for overlapping exclusive anchors, alias-to-multiple-entity claims, source disagreement, recycled identifiers, and retractions. Bind resolution to a versioned trust/conflict policy that can abstain rather than overwrite.

## Success Criteria
- Overlapping exclusive anchors refuse acceptance or compilation unless a named policy resolves them.
- Source-local aliases do not leak into global lookup without explicit promotion.
- Retractions and corrections affect the appropriate as-of/known-as-of snapshots while history remains queryable.
- Conflict artifacts expose all claims and policy clauses used.

## Test Plan
Exercise renamed firms, recycled IDs, late corrections, simultaneous conflicting sources, local aliases, interval gaps, and policy revisions. Verify deterministic abstention and explanation.

## RESERVATIONS
- `src/temporal/alias.rs`
- `src/temporal/conflict.rs`
- `tests/temporal_alias.rs`

## Considerations
Anchor trust is policy and provenance, not a magic namespace list. Domain packs may recommend precedence but projects pin the policy.

title: JSON output emission (canon.v0 schema)
description:
Implement JSON output emission in src/output/json.rs.

TARGET FILE: src/output/json.rs ONLY. Do not touch src/output/csv.rs or src/output/mod.rs.

Takes a ResolveResult + RegistryMeta, builds a CanonOutput, and serializes to JSON.

IMPORTANT: Mapping.input and Mapping.canonical_id in the ResolveResult hold RAW values. This module MUST apply identifier encoding before JSON serialization:
- u8:<value> if the value is valid UTF-8 with no ASCII control bytes (0x00-0x1F, 0x7F)
- hex:<lowercase-hex-bytes> otherwise

This means you CANNOT just derive(Serialize) on CanonOutput and call serde_json::to_string. You need a wire/serialization struct (or custom Serialize impl) that transforms Mapping fields at serialization time.

UnresolvedEntry.input: same encoding rules. If None (special reasons), serialize as JSON null.

Outcome derivation:
- summary.resolved > 0 && summary.unresolved == 0 => RESOLVED
- summary.resolved > 0 && summary.unresolved > 0 => PARTIAL
- summary.resolved == 0 && summary.unresolved > 0 => UNRESOLVED

For REFUSAL outcomes: use Refusal::to_canon_output() from the refusal module. This module only handles RESOLVED/PARTIAL/UNRESOLVED.

Output is a single JSON object on stdout (compact, no trailing newline). The same format is used for --map-out sidecar files (CSV mode's JSON artifact).

UNIT TESTS: Include #[cfg(test)] mod tests in src/output/json.rs. Test:
- encode_identifier() for u8: and hex: cases
- Outcome derivation from summary counts
- Full JSON serialization round-trip for a known ResolveResult
- Refusal envelope structure

VERIFICATION: cargo test -- output::json
acceptance_criteria:
Emits single JSON object to stdout matching canon.v0 schema exactly.
version field is always 'canon.v0'.
outcome derived from summary: RESOLVED if unresolved==0, UNRESOLVED if resolved==0, PARTIAL otherwise.
registry object populated from RegistryMeta (id, version, source as CLI arg verbatim).
summary.total == summary.resolved + summary.unresolved (invariant enforced).
Identifier encoding: u8:<val> for valid UTF-8 with no ASCII control bytes, hex:<lowercase-hex> otherwise.
mappings[] has one entry per resolved unique input value.
unresolved[] has one entry per unresolved unique value (input=null JSON for special reasons).
refusal is null for non-REFUSAL outcomes; populated for REFUSAL with registry=null, summary=null, mappings=[], unresolved=[].
Exports pub fn emit(result: ResolveResult, registry: RegistryMeta) -> Result<String, Error>.
close_reason: Implemented JSON emission with identifier encoding, deterministic ordering, outcome derivation; added unit tests; cargo test -- output::json passed

title: Resolve v0 registry write-back
description:
Implement explicit registry write-back for canon resolve matched ID pairs.

- Use canonical_type from strategy entity_type or a deterministic mapping such as loan_id.
- Use rule IDs such as IDENTITY:reference and STRUCTURAL_MATCH:<strategy_id>.
- Never write unmatched or ambiguous records.
- Refuse or no-op safely on alias overwrite/conflicting existing entries using existing registry semantics.

title: [CANON-V1/P06.16] Project extension data through generic dbt and search backends
description:
## Background
Preserving dbt-seed and searchable-index generation requires a clean way for unknown ontology, identifier, relation, and assignment data to appear downstream without forking exporters.

## Technical Approach
Extend the deterministic backend interface with schema-declared projection packages. Base entity/alias/unresolved tables remain generic; packages may add namespaced identifier, relation, assignment, provenance, or domain-view tables and search fields using safe declarative expressions. All projections bind one registry/snapshot digest.

## Success Criteria
- Unknown extensions export without Rust changes or loss of IDs/provenance.
- Identity mappings remain separate from relations and assignments.
- dbt seeds and SQLite search agree on canonical IDs and extension rows.
- Unsafe SQL, collisions, nondeterministic expressions, and incompatible schemas refuse at plan time.

## Test Plan
Export two neutral extension packages, load/query dbt-compatible tables, query SQLite filters/joins, test schema collisions and injection, and rebuild byte-for-byte. Exercise empty, redacted, and large datasets.

## RESERVATIONS
- `src/registry/export_projection.rs`
- `schemas/canon.export.projection.v1.schema.json`
- `tests/export_extensions.rs`

## Considerations
Declarative projections must remain bounded; arbitrary user SQL belongs downstream, not inside the trusted compiler.

title: [CANON-V1/P09] Deferred matcher techniques and reconciliation interoperability
description:
## Background
Canon must ship a strong native entity-resolution core without waiting for a decision about Dedupe, Splink, OpenRefine, learned models, active learning, email, or another review client. Those tools and techniques may later add value, but choosing among them before P12 empirical acceptance would let speculative integration work outrun measured matching failures.

## Scope
Maintain a post-core decision space with four options: port a technique or model into Rust using a source-pinned oracle-parity program; integrate a bounded external matcher; expose standard reconciliation interoperability such as the W3C Entity Reconciliation API; or do nothing if native quality and scale are sufficient. Review delivery transports are similarly optional. Concrete OpenRefine, Splink, and Dedupe adapter beads remain closed as historical superseded proposals.

## Technical Approach
Block this epic and every open child on final Canon v1 acceptance. Preserve only transport-neutral observation, candidate, evidence, review, decision-ledger, and promotion contracts in core. Revisit an option only from a reproducible P12 failure slice, measured scale limit, real operator model/workflow, or compelling interoperability need. A selected option receives a new or reopened packet with pinned sources, files, invariants, errors, test matrices, commands, and lift gates.

## Success Criteria
- No P09 issue blocks release preflight, final acceptance, sec10d, or native offline operation.
- Canon v1 passes with no named matcher, model runtime, reconciliation client, email provider, or UI.
- The option register documents native-port, adapter, standard-protocol, and no-integration choices without claiming one is selected.
- A later option has zero promotion authority and must prove marginal lift on the sealed P12 methodology.
- Terminology, dependencies, and priorities consistently describe this lane as post-v1.

## Test Plan
Validate the graph is acyclic; verify all open P09 children are blocked by final v1 acceptance; run release planning with all P09 functionality absent; scan active docs and bead notes for claims that a concrete integration or email workflow is committed.

## RESERVATIONS
- docs/DECISION_PORT_TECHNIQUES_OVER_ADAPTERS.md
- docs/DECISION_REVIEW_VIA_EMAIL_CROWDSOURCING.md

## Considerations
Deferral preserves optionality without promising parity. A full Rust port may live in a separate repository, following the cmdrvl-tabfm source-pin, oracle, parity, provenance, discrepancy, and negative-evidence discipline.

title: [SPLINK-STEAL/S6] entity calibrate em: unsupervised weight suggestion emitting proposed strategy YAML
description:
## Problem this solves
When gold labels are thin (new corpus families with no benchmark yet), support-evidence weights are pure guesswork. Fellegi-Sunter expectation-maximisation over agreement patterns estimates how discriminating each evidence operator actually is in THAT corpus — unsupervised — turning weight authoring into weight review. Complements S1: S1 selects thresholds when gold exists; S6 proposes weights when it does not.

## Build
canon entity calibrate em <EVIDENCE.jsonl> --strategy <YAML> [--emit json|summary]
- Collapse per-pair lane evidence into agreement vectors; aggregate to distinct-pattern counts (Splink's key perf trick: EM iterates over pattern counts, never raw pairs).
- Run EM for m/u per evidence operator: fixed iteration cap, documented convergence epsilon, deterministic iteration order, fixed-point/integer-scaled arithmetic so results are platform-stable (no float drift across artifact boundaries).
- Report: per-operator m/u, implied log-odds weights mapped onto NAMEKIT_SCORE_SCALE-compatible integer scores, convergence diagnostics, degenerate-cell warnings.
- Emit a PROPOSED strategy YAML fragment (support scores only). Operator reviews, edits, freezes. Nothing executes from it automatically.

## Splink reference (clone at /Users/zac/Source/opensource/splink)
- splink/internals/expectation_maximisation.py — EM over aggregated agreement patterns (count_agreement_patterns_sql; convergence default 1e-4, max 25 iterations)
- splink/internals/em_training_session.py — session mechanics, blocking-adjusted lambda (:367)
- splink/internals/estimate_u.py — u estimation approach (here: derive from full evidence artifacts or deterministic hash-sample, never RNG)
- docs/topic_guides/training/training_rationale.md — hybrid regime rationale (direct u, EM for m)

## How to test
- Synthetic corpus with planted ground-truth m/u: EM recovers parameters within declared tolerance.
- Determinism: byte-identical report across runs, platforms (integer arithmetic), and shuffled input order.
- Degenerate fixtures: constant field, zero-count cell, non-convergence -> typed warnings and NO weight proposal for the affected operator (never silent bad weights).
- Proposed YAML fragment round-trips through existing strategy validation.
- Leakage guard: command refuses if pointed at a sealed acceptance/holdout suite path (mirror bd-20vz tournament hygiene).

## Doctrine constraints
Offline; consumes existing evidence artifacts only — no new scoring runtime, no runtime evidence operator. THIS IS NOT bd-1rlk: bd-1rlk is the deferred full Fellegi-Sunter/EM *evidence operator* with per-pair uncertain evidence at solve time; this bead is an offline calibration assist with zero runtime presence and zero authority, and must not grow into bd-1rlk.

- tests/entity_calibrate_em.rs

title: canon geo: E3 — pairwise candidate test, the headroom number (section 17)
description:
Section 17 stage E3 — the architecture's claim in measurable form: for the labeled failures, does JOINT evidence rank the true lot strictly above the wrong PIP lot?

Rebuild the Gate V2 labeled set (GROUNDTRUTH_ACRIS_BD179B.md exact CTEs). For each lot-incorrect point (and a matched sample of lot-correct points as control), build the PAIR (pip_lot, true_lot) — for multi-BBL truth, score against the nearest/best true member and report multi-BBL cases as a separate slice. Then score BOTH lots of each pair on every landed evidence row from section 16.3 EXCEPT ACRIS (row 8 is the truth source — using it as evidence is circular and forbidden here):
  - geocode: point-to-lot distance / containment depth under the tier's disc radius
  - address: parsed street matches lot's address street; house number within lot's observed range; house-number exact agreement (use the Appendix E normalizer; grammar-lite is acceptable, record its limits)
  - footprints: NYC footprint majority-linked on lot; footprint count vs NUMBLDGS agreement; FEMA count where covered
  - asserted attributes: SF band-consistency asserted-vs-BLDGAREA per lot (coordinate with E1+E2 bead comments for the discovered field names; do not block on it — discover independently if needed)
  - parcel attributes: NUMBLDGS, units consistency where fields exist
Per evidence row report the pairwise 3-way split over pairs: true lot wins / tie / PIP lot wins. Then the JOINT readouts: (1) simple vote across rows; (2) any-single-row-decisive rate; (3) the headline — fraction of incorrect points where the joint evidence ranks true strictly above PIP (ties broken by nothing — a tie is a residual doubleton, which is an honest abstention, count it separately). Control check: on the correct-point sample the PIP lot (which IS the true lot) must not lose to a random same-component neighbor — run that as the null comparison so the test has a falsification arm.

INTERPRETATION GATE: your headline number is folded only alongside E1's taxonomy (some failure classes are unaddressable by tile evidence — gross geocode errors with the true lot outside the tile must be reported as out-of-scope-for-pairwise, not as losses). title: [CANON-V1/P12.10] Publish downstream migration conformance protocol and consumer contract
description:
## Background
A downstream migration is not proven by an in-repository fixture or a helper that happens to compile against private internals. sec10d currently demonstrates the danger: its helper emits removed canon org commands while Canon tests reject that surface, and static tests still approve the stale invocation. Consumers need a capability-negotiated, artifact-pinned protocol that fails before mutating data.

## Technical Approach
Publish a public-binary migration protocol covering capability discovery, version compatibility, extension-package loading, project initialization, exact-first lookup, unresolved-tail preparation and execution, review export and import, promotion, audit, application or projection, and registry replay. Define a machine-readable consumer manifest that pins Canon version, command-contract version, artifact schemas, package digest, profile and ontology identifiers, registry digest, projection contract, resource budgets, and rollback snapshot. Provide dry-run and dual-run modes plus a conformance kit that invokes only the installed public executable. Unknown flags, removed command families, incompatible schemas, missing capabilities, and ignored arguments must be hard errors.

## Success Criteria
- A consumer can determine compatibility from machine output before running a project.
- The protocol preserves generate-dbt-seed and generate-searchable-index as registry projections rather than removing them.
- Canonical registry strategy, immutable snapshots, exact lookup, review, promotion, and replay remain the center of the migration.
- Public subprocess tests catch the current stale org-command class and any silently ignored option.
- Extension packages and consumer projections remain outside core while their versions and digests appear in artifacts.
- Dry-run reports exact filesystem and output mutations; rollback selects a prior immutable registry and package digest.
- At least one out-of-tree consumer completes conformance without importing Canon source modules or using repository-relative defaults.

## Test Plan
Run the kit against compatible, too-old, too-new, unknown-profile, missing-package, tampered-package, stale-registry, removed-command, unknown-flag, partial-output, interrupted, and read-only cases. Compare dual-run outputs byte-for-byte where parity is required. Execute from a clean installed-binary environment with no Canon source checkout present.

## RESERVATIONS
- src/cli.rs
- src/entity/describe.rs
- schemas/canon.consumer.manifest.v1.schema.json
- tests/entity_consumer_conformance.rs
- docs/ENTITY_MIGRATION_PROTOCOL.md
- docs/CLI_CONTRACT.md

## Considerations
This protocol may break obsolete pre-v1 helpers rather than preserve compatibility shims. The migration seam is artifacts and declared capabilities, not downstream knowledge inside Canon.
notes:
## Cross-repository acceptance
sec10d bd-277 freezes the compatibility matrix, bd-2az migrates the helper to exact-first plus a deduplicated unresolved tail, and bd-14w replaces stale org documentation and static-only tests. This Canon bead is not operationally complete until the public conformance kit catches the currently stale org commands and sec10d can execute from an installed binary without sibling-repository defaults.

title: strategy v1 contract: typed keys, grades, and lifecycle semantics
description: Define the canonical contract before code changes. This bead updates docs/PLAN_CANON.md, the source of truth for canon behavior, so future implementation beads do not invent strategy v1 behavior. The contract must cover typed strategy keys, task-key syntax, grade values, attestation provenance, lifecycle states, update semantics, deprecate/remove semantics, promotion semantics, resolve outcomes, registry version bumps, deterministic ordering, and refusal behavior. Background: existing docs specify schema-shape plus skill hash and proof-gated register only; bd-a43 requires intent-keyed champions and operator-attested grade in the same registry. RESERVATIONS: docs/PLAN_CANON.md.
design:
Recommended contract: strategy entries have entry_schema_version = canon_strategy_entry.v1 and a typed key object with key.type = schema or task. Schema entries preserve current schema_fingerprint plus schema plus skill_hash behavior. Task entries use exact task string after ASCII trim plus skill_hash; no fuzzy matching, aliases, normalization, or shape tiers. Grade strings are exactly operator-attested and proof-attested in JSON. Status strings are exactly active and deprecated.

Operator-attested entries require provenance: operator, attested_at, reason, script content hash, and attestation hash. Proof-attested entries require existing verify/assess/airlock references and hashes. Existing pre-v1 entries load as schema-keyed proof-attested active entries through an explicit compatibility/migration rule, not a loose best-effort parser.

Active resolution ignores deprecated entries. Update, promote, and deprecate are in-place registry mutations with explicit next-version; entries are never physically deleted. Mutating commands emit deterministic receipts with before/after registry hashes and append witness records under canon's normal witness policy. Read-only resolve/list/explain never execute scripts and do not append mutation witness records.

Operator discovery is part of the contract: strategy list and strategy explain, or exactly equivalent named commands, must expose registry entries, provenance, grade/status, source file/entry order, and active-resolution reasoning.
acceptance_criteria: Acceptance: PLAN_CANON documents task resolve/register/update/promote/deprecate/list/explain CLI forms; states task resolve is EXACT or UNRESOLVED only; states existing schema-keyed proof-attested behavior remains supported product behavior; defines JSON fields sufficiently for implementation without consulting bd-a43; defines entry schema versioning and legacy entry loading; defines mutation receipt fields and witness semantics; defines refusals for missing task/schema, invalid grade/status/key type, missing attestation fields, proof failures, duplicate active keys, stale versions, deprecated entries, malformed catalog filters, and malformed mixed registries.
notes: Do not edit code in this bead. Keep it as the contract bead all implementation beads depend on; include list/explain, receipts, witness policy, schema versioning, and the mixed-registry matrix in the written contract.

title: [CANON-V1/P07.R6a] Preserve record-grain comparison views across source mapping and prepare
description:
## Background
The deterministic structured comparison primitives cannot prove R6 while all prepared views are derived from the primary entity surface and same-name rows collapse before evidence. Multi-assignment records need a separate, hash-bound comparison input that never becomes identity.

## Technical Approach
Compile source-mapped observations and typed assignments into a domain-neutral canon.entity.record_link_input.v1 sidecar. Preserve one stable record per source row with source-side/scope IDs, issuer observation reference, opaque assignment reference, typed comparison views, declared units/scale, source-mapping/profile/input digests, and privacy-safe provenance. Keep entity surfaces and assignment records separate; comparison fields must never create aliases, canonical IDs, or assignment-as-identity behavior. The sidecar must preserve multiple same-issuer records and deterministic ordering under shuffled source rows.

## Success Criteria
- Independent numeric/date/categorical source fields survive intake at record grain.
- Same issuer plus multiple assignments remains multiple comparison records while pointing to one issuer observation.
- Units and scale are explicit and caller-owned; no conversion is inferred.
- Missing, malformed, duplicate, unknown, and incomparable fields fail closed or quarantine under declared policy.
- Output is byte-stable, hash-bound, schema-validated, and contains no BDC-specific fields/defaults.

## Test Plan
Use neutral two-source fixtures with same-name multi-assignment rows, shuffled order, missing/overflow values, explicit scale mismatch, duplicate record IDs, and assignment/identity firewall negatives. Validate source-mapping digest continuity and byte-identical sidecars.

title: [CANON-V1/P05.8] Prove temporal identity snapshots with metamorphic and E2E tests
description:
## Background
Temporal identity bugs hide at interval boundaries and correction sequences. Example-only tests cannot establish compiled exact snapshot integrity.

title: [ENTITY-ATOMICITY] Publish multi-file v1 stage sets transactionally
description:
## Background
The v1 entity workbench publishes block, evidence, solve, and run as multi-file stage sets. Validation and tamper refusals are preflighted before writes, but a late filesystem failure can still leave a mixed stage set because files are written sequentially to stable final paths. Per-file atomic rename does not make the whole set atomic. Warm-cache execution intentionally reruns in the same work_dir, so requiring final stage directories to be absent is not acceptable.

## Technical approach
Design and implement a versioned, recoverable stage-set publication protocol that preserves current public artifact paths or introduces an explicitly versioned migration. It must support same-work-dir warm-cache reruns, deterministic replay, concurrent readers, interruption recovery, and truthful writes_performed reporting. Explore append-only/content-addressed generations plus a verified commit marker or another portable transaction design. Do not rely on unsafe platform-specific directory swaps. Any cleanup or deletion behavior requires explicit written permission and a documented ownership boundary.

## Success criteria
- Readers observe either the complete previous stage set or the complete next stage set, never a mixed generation.
- I/O failure and process interruption at every publication boundary produce an actionable, truthful refusal and recover without corrupting the last committed stage.
- Warm enabled/disabled cache reruns in the same work_dir remain supported.
- Manual block/evidence/solve and full run retain byte/semantic parity.
- Publication is offline, deterministic, portable, and hash-bound.
- No hidden garbage collection or file deletion is introduced without explicit authorization.

## Test plan
Add fault injection at every write/sync/commit boundary, crash-restart recovery tests, concurrent reader/writer tests, same-work-dir cache replay, stale staging/commit marker tests, and full fmt/clippy/test gates.

## Reservations
Reserve exact implementation and test files after the publication protocol is approved; likely src/entity/run.rs plus a dedicated existing integration harness.
close_reason: Transactional content-addressed stage publication now provides complete committed generations, warm no-write replay, stale-parent refusal, failpoint recovery, concurrent reader/writer safety, and committed-byte consumers; 28 protocol tests and full quality gate pass.

Immutable objects plus a self-hashed generation manifest must be fully written, synced, read-back validated, then exposed by one atomic commit-marker creation. Readers snapshot one generation and resolve every logical path by manifest hash. Warm replay is idempotent and no-write; cache mode/status participate in generation identity; failures report writes_performed and committed state truthfully; orphan attempts are ignored and never deleted; no garbage collection or cleanup. Include deterministic fault-injection, concurrent reader/writer, same-generation race, tamper, crash-state, and warm-rerun tests. title: [CANON-V1/P10.1] Stabilize an embeddable Rust API around immutable artifacts

title: [CANON-V1/P12.5] Run entity-disjoint and time-forward discovery benchmarks
description:
## Background
Withheld aliases test attachment to known entities, but Canon must also cluster previously unseen entities and generalize to future sources. Random row splits cannot prove either behavior.

## Technical Approach
Run two sealed benchmark families through the public binary. Entity-disjoint trials place all observations for a canonical entity exclusively in tune or holdout and evaluate novel clustering plus related-distinct safety. Time-forward trials build a registry and policy only from observations available before a cutoff, then evaluate later documents, renamed surfaces, new firms, and changed relationships without future leakage. Include directional cross-source linkage where a reference and target dataset have different fields. Report results by evidence availability, source family, name difficulty, entity frequency, and relation class.

## Success Criteria
- No holdout entity or future observation contributes aliases, anchors, thresholds, dictionaries, or patches to the evaluated snapshot.
- Novel-cluster and time-forward metrics meet the quality contract or produce a versioned failure report that blocks release claims.
- Hard-negative hierarchy and lookalike cases have zero severity-critical false merges.
- Results expose head-versus-tail and easy-versus-hard performance rather than one aggregate score.
- The benchmark can run on an invented public corpus and an operator-owned private corpus through the same command.

## Test Plan
Create planted leakage and temporal-reversal controls; run clean entity-disjoint and chronological splits; shuffle physical rows; repeat with exact cache disabled/enabled; test missing timestamps and conflicting temporal facts. Verify public subprocess commands, hashes, exit codes, and output queries.

## RESERVATIONS
- src/evaluation/generalization.rs
- tests/entity_generalization.rs
- tests/fixtures/extensions/neutral-domain/time_forward/

## Considerations
An entity-disjoint test asks whether Canon can form a new cluster, not whether it can invent a globally authoritative identity from names alone. Promotion still requires policy and review.

Owns the time-forward evaluation side of R5. Include rename and temporal-alias cases where only evidence available as of the cutoff may be used. Report identity continuity, abstention, and false-link behavior across time rather than collapsing all aliases into an atemporal gold.

title: Witness protocol
description:
Implement the witness protocol in src/witness.rs. ~100-150 LOC.

Purpose: append an immutable ledger record for every canon run, enabling audit trail and reproducibility verification.

Hashing:
- input_hash: BLAKE3 hash of the input file bytes (read the file once, hash all bytes).
- output_hash: BLAKE3 hash of the output bytes. JSON mode: hash the entire JSON string. CSV mode: hash the CSV bytes incrementally as they stream through stdout (wrap the stdout writer in a BLAKE3 hashing tee).

Ledger record (one JSON line appended to .canon-witness.jsonl):
{
  "tool": "canon",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "timestamp": "2026-02-25T12:34:56.789Z",
  "input_path": "tape.csv",
  "input_hash": "blake3:abc123...",
  "output_hash": "blake3:def456...",
  "registry_id": "cusip-isin",
  "registry_version": "3.2.1",
  "outcome": "PARTIAL",
  "summary": { "total": 100, "resolved": 95, "unresolved": 5 }
}

Ledger location: .canon-witness.jsonl in the current working directory.

Error handling: witness failures NEVER block the main pipeline. If the ledger file can't be opened/written, log a warning to stderr and continue. The tool's primary output (JSON or CSV) is never affected by witness failure.

--no-witness: if set, skip the entire witness step (no hashing, no file write).
acceptance_criteria: TARGET FILE: src/witness.rs only. Include #[cfg(test)] mod tests. Test: ledger record JSON structure, BLAKE3 hash computation, --no-witness skips entirely, witness failure does not affect exit code. VERIFICATION: cargo test -- witness

title: canon geo: assemblage resolution — subset selection as a third solve mode (cluster, link, assemble)
description:
OPERATOR INSIGHT 2026-08-14: THE PROPERTY QUESTION IS A SUBSET-SELECTION PROBLEM, AND
canon HAS NO SOLVE MODE FOR IT.

canon has two solve modes today, both PAIRWISE:
  cluster mode   find same-entity groups within one corpus
  link mode      align a reference corpus to a target corpus
Both produce per-PAIR evidence. EdgeEvidenceRecord is keyed on left_surface_id and
right_surface_id. Everything scoped for canon geo so far inherits that shape.

THE ASSEMBLAGE PROBLEM IS NEITHER. Given one asserted property —
"100-105 Broadway, office, 340,000 SF" — and a tile full of resolved parcels and
buildings, the question is WHICH SUBSET OF THE TILE CONSTITUTES THIS PROPERTY. The
evidence is not per-pair; it is PER-SUBSET: does this subset's building area sum to the
asserted size, is it contiguous, does it span the address interval, is it type-consistent.
There is no artifact shape in canon for subset-level evidence. That is the gap this bead
fills.

WHY THIS IS NOT A COMBINATORIAL EXPLOSION. It looks like 2^N over the tile's ~167 nodes.
Four constraints collapse it, applied in this order:

1. TYPE IS A HARD ELIMINATIVE FILTER, NOT A WEIGHT. An office property removes the retail
   candidates outright before anything is scored. N drops from ~167 to single digits.
2. ADDRESS RANGE IS AN INTERVAL, NOT AN ARBITRARY SUBSET. Order the surviving candidates
   by address along the frontage; "100-105" is a contiguous interval in that order.
   Interval count over N items is N(N+1)/2 — at N=8 that is 36 candidate subsets rather
   than 256. This is semantically correct, not merely convenient: a range address IS an
   interval by definition.
3. CONTIGUITY. A property is a physically contiguous assemblage. Even allowing corner
   wraps where adjacency is not a clean path, this enumerates connected subgraphs of a
   small planar graph, not the power set. Contiguity must be SOFT-WITH-ABSTENTION, not a
   hard refusal — non-contiguous assemblages exist (air rights, released parcels).
4. SIZE IS AN ADDITIVE CONSTRAINT OVER THE SUBSET — subset-sum with tolerance.
   340,000 SF against candidates of 150k/130k/120k/80k/60k. At this N, exhaustive
   enumeration is EXACT.

RESULT: hard filter -> interval structure -> contiguity -> subset-sum scoring, fully
exhaustive, fully deterministic, fully explainable. Every candidate subset is scored and
the losers are retained exactly as losing pairs already are. NO HEAVY MATH IN V1 HOLDS FOR
ASSEMBLAGE TOO.

DO NOT POINT THE AMBITION LANE AT THIS. Correlation clustering and optimal assignment
address the PAIRWISE problem. Assemblage is constrained subset enumeration — a different
problem family. If tiles ever become dense enough to break exhaustion, the honest
escalation is a deterministic integer program, not Sinkhorn.

== FOUR TRAPS, ALL MEASURED OR STRUCTURAL ==

1. ODD/EVEN PARITY. In Manhattan 101/103/105 is one side of the street and 102/104 the
   other. An office property recorded as "100-105" whose candidates are all odd is almost
   certainly a one-side assemblage with a sloppy range endpoint. Parity is real signal and
   it is a JURISDICTION CONVENTION — it belongs in bd-1zph's locale table beside the
   Queens hyphenate rule, never hardcoded.
2. SIZE DEFINITIONS DIFFER SYSTEMATICALLY. CMBS building size is frequently NRA (net
   rentable area); PLUTO's BldgArea is gross. That is a structural 10-20% gap IN A KNOWN
   DIRECTION. Subset-sum with a naive symmetric tolerance will reject correct assemblages
   or accept wrong ones. The MEASURE must be declared per source (bd-uilx) and the
   tolerance must model the definitional offset rather than treating it as noise.
3. THE ANSWER MAY BE ONE BUILDING OVER THREE LOTS, NOT THREE BUILDINGS. 101/103/105
   Broadway is very often a single tower built over an assemblage of older tax lots — the
   most common Manhattan pattern. Then the property is one BUILDING which is
   contained-by three PARCELS. A BBL column cannot express this and neither can a boolean.
   This is why bd-3soj's typed relations are load-bearing.
4. CONDOS BREAK ADDITIVITY. A commercial condo is a FRACTION of one parcel, so the subset
   is not always whole parcels and building areas do not sum. That population needs its
   own path or an explicit abstention. Do not let it silently produce a wrong subset.

== ARTIFACT REQUIREMENTS ==
- A subset-evidence record: subset membership, per-constraint outcomes (interval span,
  contiguity, type consistency, size sum vs asserted with the measure declared), total
  score in ScoreUnits, and the abstention state.
- ALL CANDIDATE SUBSETS RETAINED, not only the winner — the same doctrine that already
  holds for losing pairs, and bd-101v's card needs the runners-up to be evidence rather
  than assertion.
- The margin between the best and second-best subset, which is the natural tie detector
  and comes free from exhaustive enumeration.

EXIT CRITERIA:
- Subset-evidence artifact contract, versioned, in the geo contracts module
- The four-stage constraint cascade implemented, with the enumeration count reported per
  run so the tractability claim stays visible
- Contiguity soft-with-abstention; non-contiguous assemblage fixture
- Parity handled via the locale convention table, not hardcoded
- Size measure declared per source; asymmetric NRA-vs-gross tolerance
- Condo/fractional population detected and routed to abstention
- All candidate subsets retained with margin-to-next-best
- Worked fixture: the 100-105 Broadway shape — mixed office/retail, both parities, with a
  correct answer of one building over three parcels

Bespoke interval enumeration must not be built. Remaining genuine work is adjudicating composition residuals against the multi-BBL population (H.4: 79 non-condo multi-parcel candidates) — tracked by the new E4-adjudication bead. comments.author: Zac
comments.text:
CORRECTION 2026-08-14 — THE INTERVAL TRACTABILITY CLAIM IS TOO NARROW. Surfaced by case 4
of the worked-case ladder (bd-tccn) BEFORE any code was written, which is exactly what that
corpus exists to do.

WHAT THIS BEAD CLAIMS: "Order the surviving candidates by address along the frontage;
'100-105' is a contiguous interval in that order. Interval count over N items is N(N+1)/2 —
at N=8 that is 36 candidate subsets rather than 256."

THE HIDDEN ASSUMPTION: that a property has ONE frontage, so candidates admit a single total
order. Operator case 4 (a comma-separated address on two different streets) and case 5 (one
building with legitimate frontages on two corners) both violate it. Corner and
through-block properties are common, not exotic — the measured NYC data already contains
them (bd-1zph: geocode "9 WEST FORDHAM ROAD" against MapPLUTO "2167 GRAND CONCOURSE").

THE CORRECTED FORMULATION. Candidates order along EACH FRONTAGE SEPARATELY. A property's
member set is then an interval on frontage A, optionally unioned with an interval on
frontage B, and so on:

  enumeration bound = product over frontages f of [ n_f * (n_f + 1) / 2 ]
                      plus the single-frontage cases

  2 frontages at n=5 each   ->  15 x 15 = 225        fine
  3 frontages at n=5 each   ->  3,375                fine
  4 frontages at n=6 each   ->  21^4 = 194,481       still enumerable, but budget it
  wide frontages            ->  grows fast

STILL TRACTABLE AT REALISTIC SIZES, and the hard type filter and contiguity constraint both
still apply and still prune first. But it is NO LONGER TRIVIALLY SMALL, and the bound is now
a product rather than a sum. REQUIRED CHANGES:

1. FRONTAGE IS AN EXPLICIT CONCEPT, not an implicit ordering. Each candidate parcel or
   building declares which street(s) it fronts. That is derivable from the address channel
   and, better, from geometry — which edges of the polygon abut a street centreline.
2. THE ENUMERATION IS BUDGETED AND REFUSES RATHER THAN EXPLODING. Wire it to the existing
   budget machinery (src/entity/budget.rs) exactly as candidate generation already is.
   Report the enumeration count on every run so the tractability claim stays visible rather
   than assumed.
3. CONTIGUITY ACROSS FRONTAGES IS A DIFFERENT TEST. Two intervals on two streets form a
   valid corner assemblage only if they MEET at the corner. Disjoint intervals on two
   parallel streets are a through-block property (valid) or two unrelated properties
   (invalid) — and geometry decides which, not the address.
4. A THROUGH-BLOCK PROPERTY IS A REAL AND SEPARATE SHAPE. Frontage on two parallel streets
   with the parcel spanning between them. It is neither a corner nor a single-frontage run,
   and it is common in Manhattan. Do not let the corner model swallow it.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT CHANGE: the constraint cascade order (type filter, then structure, then
contiguity, then subset-sum), the exhaustive-and-deterministic posture, or the conclusion
that no heavy math is needed in v1. The enumeration is larger than first claimed and is
still enumerable. It just has to be budgeted honestly rather than asserted to be small.

METHODOLOGICAL NOTE WORTH KEEPING: this correction came from writing down a case shape, not
from writing code or from further argument. It is the first concrete evidence that the
worked-case corpus (bd-tccn) pays for itself, and it is a point in favour of finishing that
corpus before bd-3ccc rather than in parallel with it.

comments.author: Zac
comments.text:
ARCHITECTURE SUPERSEDED 2026-08-15 — see docs/PLAN_CANON_GEO.md.

An adversarial multi-model design session produced a materially different architecture,
which then survived a red team that destroyed two intermediate designs. The tile is modelled
as a BOUNDED UNIVERSE and every piece of evidence is a CONSTRAINT; propagation runs to a
fixpoint; the residual model set IS the answer. There is no proposer channel.

THE THREE PROPERTIES THAT MATTER:
- CONFLUENCE. The fixpoint is independent of the order constraints are applied (Tarski 1955;
  Cousot & Cousot 1977; Apt 1999), so determinism is a theorem rather than an engineering
  effort.
- MONOTONICITY. Constraints only add and domains only shrink, so a tile resolved with four
  sources today and six next year yields a TIGHTER residual, never a contradicting one. The
  earlier answer was never wrong, only less resolved.
- STRUCTURAL ABSTENTION. The residual model set is the answer. No threshold anywhere.

THE KEY DESIGN RULE IS rho, THE SOUNDNESS DISCIPLINE. Every source attribute enters the
solver only through a declared versioned relaxation mapping it to the WEAKEST constraint the
source can actually support. An interpolated geocode becomes a 150m disc rather than a
location. A parcel ADDRESS becomes "one of this lot's addresses" rather than functional
equality. OWNERNAME equal PERMITS an assemblage; OWNERNAME different constrains NOTHING.
Every noisy channel is admitted only in its sound direction — which is what dissolved the
proposer dilemma that broke the two earlier designs.

AND THE COMMERCIAL CONSEQUENCE: if every rho is sound, the true assignment is in the model
set, so AN EMPTY MODEL SET IS A PROOF that a named source violated its own published error
model — attributable, falsifiable, and mailable to the vendor.

Read PLAN_CANON_GEO.md before starting any geo work. Section 11 carries the bead-by-bead
supersession table. Appendix A covers frozen-weight observers and imagery sources. APPENDIX
B RECORDS THE FIRST HARD MEASUREMENT, WHICH FALSIFIED A LOAD-BEARING CLAIM — read it before
trusting any performance number in the plan.

Raw session artifacts, including the red team and the adversarial reviews, are preserved
under docs/geo_design_session/ with a reading guide.

title: canon: register email_hash as an alias type in the resolver
description:
Extend canon's existing alias mechanism to accept type=email_hash so cmdrvl context resolve --type email_hash <hash> returns the canon entity. No new resolution machinery — this registers a new alias TYPE within the existing resolver.

## Design

Person markdown frontmatter (canon-side, lives in cmdrvl-context):

```yaml
---
id: PPL-022
name: Christian Ruiz
firm: SaltDataStudio
aliases:
  - { type: handle, value: christian }
  - { type: email_hash, value: "sha256:8a4f..." }
  - { type: email_hash, value: "sha256:b2c1..." }
  - { type: linkedin, value: christian-ruiz-1234 }
---
```

The canon spine tool already indexes aliases into the registry DB (alias_candidates, aliases tables). This bead adds:

1. type=email_hash recognized in alias schema validation.
2. Validation pattern: ^sha256:[a-f0-9]{64}$.
3. Indexed for fast lookup by canon resolve.
4. cmdrvl context resolve --type email_hash <hash> [--catalog salt] returns the canon entity (id, name, firm) or empty.

## Out of scope

- Adding email_hashes to existing person markdowns. Canon is curated; populating frontmatter with hashes is curation work, not platform work. This bead enables the mechanism; population happens organically as operators promote contacts.
- Hash normalization rule. Documented in cmdrvl-context bd-2o0h.1; this bead just validates the format.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Canon spine tool builds without error when person frontmatter contains type=email_hash aliases.
- [ ] cmdrvl context resolve --type email_hash <known_hash> returns the expected entity.
- [ ] cmdrvl context resolve --type email_hash <unknown_hash> returns empty / null cleanly (not an error).
- [ ] Validation rejects invalid hash patterns (non-sha256, missing prefix, wrong hex length).
- [ ] Test fixture: at least one synthetic person markdown with a known email_hash alias resolves correctly.
- [ ] Canon spine tool docs updated to list email_hash among recognized alias types.

## Lineage

- Parent (cross-repo): cmdrvl-context#bd-2o0h.
- Sibling (cross-repo): SaltIO/cmdrvl-cli — contacts extract command depends on this resolver primitive.
- Sibling (cross-repo): cmdrvl/pack#bd-3ue.6 — LinkedIn proof depends on canon hits being countable.
close_reason: Closed as no-op. Canon kernel needs no changes — registering email_hash as a new alias type was a misframing of the work. Canons alias-resolution registry type already supports exactly this use case (each alias is a separate registry entry mapping input to canonical_id). Implementation moves to cmdrvl-context#bd-2o0h.2 (seed registry) and SaltIO/cmdrvl-cli (br-12vs extract, br-28o5 promote). Canon stays focused on its purpose: exact byte-match identifier resolution against versioned JSON registries.

title: Registry materializer framework (canon registry build)
description:
## Summary

Add a `canon registry build` subcommand that materializes external data sources into standard canon registry directories. This is the framework — provider-specific implementations (OpenFIGI, etc.) are separate beads.

## Motivation

Canon resolves identifiers against static, versioned, local registries. This is the right design — determinism, reproducibility, offline use, diffability. But building those registries by hand is tedious and error-prone. Industry-standard identifier databases (OpenFIGI, GLEIF/LEI, EDGAR CIK) already exist as public APIs. The materializer bridges the gap: query the API once, snapshot the results as a versioned canon registry, then resolve against the snapshot thousands of times with full determinism.

The key principle: **canon never calls an API at resolution time.** The materializer is a separate step that produces a registry. Canon consumes it like any other registry. Same input + same registry version = same output. Always.

## Design

### Subcommand

```bash
canon registry build \
  --source openfigi \
  --seed positions.csv --seed-column cusip \
  --output registries/openfigi-cusip/ \
  --version "2026.03.05"
```

### Seed list

The materializer needs to know which identifiers to look up. A seed file (CSV or JSONL) provides the input population. The --seed and --seed-column flags extract unique identifiers from the seed file — same dedup logic canon already uses for resolution. This means the registry is scoped to what you actually need, not the entire universe.

### Provider trait

```rust
pub trait RegistryProvider {
    fn name(&self) -> &str;
    fn fetch(&self, identifiers: &[&str], config: &ProviderConfig) -> Result<Vec<MappingEntry>>;
    fn id_types(&self) -> &[&str]; // e.g., ["cusip", "isin", "ticker", "sedol"]
    fn rate_limit(&self) -> Option<RateLimit>;
}
```

Each provider implements fetch, which takes a batch of identifiers and returns mapping entries. The framework handles: batching (respecting provider rate limits), dedup, progress reporting, error handling (partial failures → report which identifiers failed), and writing the output registry directory.

### Output

Standard canon registry directory:

```
registries/openfigi-cusip/
├── registry.json                # { id, version, source: "openfigi", materialized_at, seed_count, resolved_count }
├── cusip-to-figi.json           # Primary mappings
├── cusip-to-ticker.json         # Secondary mappings (if provider returns them)
└── _build.json                  # Build metadata: seed file hash, provider version, API calls made, failures
```

registry.json includes standard fields (id, version) plus materializer-specific metadata: source (provider name), materialized_at (ISO timestamp), seed_count (unique identifiers submitted), resolved_count (identifiers that got at least one mapping).

_build.json is build provenance — not used by canon during resolution, but useful for debugging and auditing. Includes: seed file content hash, provider name and config, number of API calls, identifiers that failed to resolve, wall clock time.

### Incremental builds

```bash
# First build: full materialization
canon registry build --source openfigi --seed tape.csv --seed-column cusip \
  --output registries/openfigi-cusip/ --version "2026.03.05"

# Incremental: only query identifiers not already in the registry
canon registry build --source openfigi --seed tape-updated.csv --seed-column cusip \
  --output registries/openfigi-cusip/ --version "2026.03.06" --incremental
```

--incremental reads the existing registry, diffs against the seed list, and only queries identifiers that are new. Existing mappings carry forward. Version bumps.

## Key files

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| src/registry/build.rs | Subcommand entry point, orchestration |
| src/registry/provider.rs | Provider trait definition |
| src/registry/seed.rs | Seed list extraction (reuse input parsing) |
| src/registry/writer.rs | Registry directory writer (registry.json + mapping files) |

## Acceptance criteria

- `canon registry build --source <name> --seed <file> --seed-column <col> --output <dir> --version <ver>` produces a valid canon registry directory
- The produced registry passes canon resolution with no changes — it is a standard registry
- Provider trait is generic — adding a new provider means implementing one trait
- --incremental correctly diffs and only fetches new identifiers
- _build.json records full provenance
- Seed dedup uses the same logic as canon's input dedup
- Rate limiting is provider-configurable and respected
- Partial API failures produce warnings + the registry contains whatever succeeded
- Tests: mock provider that returns canned results, verify output registry structure
close_reason: Added canon registry build framework with mock provider, incremental materialization, provenance output, and end-to-end coverage

title: [CANON-V1/P01.1] Specify content-addressed registry package v1
description:
## Background
Plain JSON directories are inspectable and valuable, but distribution, immutable verification, attached proofs, and concurrency need a canonical package identity that does not replace the flat registry model.

## Technical Approach
- Define package manifest fields for registry id/version, canonical content digest, entry/effective mapping counts, file descriptors, schema version, canonical IRI namespace, build provenance, dependency references, and allowed sidecars.
- Specify canonical byte ordering and hash exclusions; derived caches must never affect identity.
- Represent audit, gold, strategy, signature, relation, escrow, and export artifacts as typed attachments rather than lookup mapping files.
- Define directory and archive layouts while keeping existing registry directories loadable through explicit compilation/migration, not a compatibility shim.

## Success Criteria
- Two copies with identical logical files have the same package digest regardless of path or mtime.
- Any mapping/provenance/declared sidecar change alters the correct digest.
- The package can be verified offline and compiled to the existing flat exact lookup view.
- dbt and search exports are named first-class deployment projections.

## Test Plan
- Canonicalization/hash golden vectors.
- Unknown/duplicate/path-traversal descriptor refusals.
- Round trips between directory and package layout.
- Cross-platform ordering fixtures.

## RESERVATIONS
- `src/registry.rs`
- `src/registry/package.rs`
- `tests/registry_package.rs`
- `tests/fixtures/registry_package/minimal/registry.json`
- `tests/fixtures/registry_package/minimal/mappings.json`

## Considerations
- Package identity must not include mutable caches.
- Secrets and provider credentials never enter package manifests.
- New package files are justified as genuinely new functionality.
close_reason: Implemented content-addressed registry package v1 contract; validated with cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, and cargo test.

title: [CANON-V1/P13.4] Post-core pack catalog over signed OCI packages
description:
## Background
Once multiple independently installable packs exist and P08 package trust semantics are proven, add discoverability metadata over the existing OCI distribution. The catalog is an index of packages, not new artifact storage or a new trust root.

## Scope
- Publish searchable metadata for package identity, digest, signature, publisher, compatibility, capabilities, license, provenance, security status, and revocation.
- Resolve an install request to the exact P08 OCI digest.
- Document publisher and consumer trust policy.
- Exclude billing, hosted marketplace workflow, new registry infrastructure, and automatic trust of catalog entries.

## Technical approach
Catalog records are signed or bound to signed package manifests and never float independently from immutable digests. Installation continues through P08 verification. Compatibility ranges are machine-checkable. Revocation and supersession preserve historical auditability. Search ranking has no effect on trust or identity decisions.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A consumer can discover a pack and install the exact verified digest through P08.
- Tampered metadata, signature mismatch, incompatible Canon versions, revoked packs, and unacceptable licenses fail closed.
- The catalog does not duplicate blobs or bypass package verification.
- Both finance packs and the neutral/non-finance proof are represented with accurate capability claims.

## Test plan
- End-to-end discover/resolve/verify/install tests.
- Negative tests for tampering, revoked keys or packages, stale compatibility, license-policy failure, and digest mismatch.
- Offline verification of already-resolved manifests.
- Audit test proving search order cannot alter the installed digest.

## File and reservation boundaries
Add catalog metadata/schema/client files only after P08 stabilizes. Reserve exact files. Do not modify the package trust root or add a second transport.

## Considerations
Open-core or premium-pack economics remain a future business choice. Catalog presence is not endorsement, correctness, or permission to promote records.

title: [CANON-V1/P01.8] Design semantic registry diff and three-way merge planning
description:
## Background
Content-addressed publication and multiple writers need more than directory copying. Operators must see alias, canonical target, metadata, temporal fact, sidecar, and attachment conflicts before choosing a new version.

## Technical Approach
- Extend diff around effective mappings and package descriptors rather than raw file positions.
- Implement a read-only three-way merge planner over base, ours, and theirs.
- Classify additive, idempotent, alias-target conflict, canonical-type conflict, deletion, temporal overlap, sidecar scope, and provenance changes.
- Emit a proposed deterministic write plan but require explicit mutation through normal registry commands.

## Success Criteria
- Non-conflicting additions merge deterministically.
- Conflicting identity assertions never auto-resolve.
- The plan explains blast radius and required operator decision.
- No input tree is changed during planning.

## Test Plan
- Three-way fixture matrix.
- Order/path independence properties.
- Concurrent version-chain scenarios.
- Integration with impact analysis and publication receipts.

## RESERVATIONS
- `src/registry.rs`
- `src/registry/package.rs`
- `tests/registry_merge.rs`

## Considerations
- Do not treat last-write-wins as identity policy.
- File layout differences must not become semantic conflicts.
- Actual remote CAS lands in P08.
close_reason: Completed package-aware read-only semantic registry diff and three-way merge planner with focused validation: rustfmt scoped check, cargo test --test registry_merge, cargo clippy --test registry_merge -- -D warnings, and cargo test --test registry_package.

title: [CANON-V1/P03.1] Define typed strategy kinds and canonical strategy doctrine
description:
## Background
`canon strategy` is worth keeping because it captures reusable procedural knowledge: a frozen, audited way to turn a known input shape or task into deterministic evidence. Its current schema and task entries, however, can blur selection keys, entity profiles, linkage field maps, and executable transformations.

## Technical Approach
Write the canonical model for typed strategy kinds such as `identity-evidence`, `record-linkage`, `schema-transform`, and `task-transform`. For each kind define selection key, allowed inputs, declared outputs, capability requirements, execution policy, audit fixtures, compatibility relation, and promotion semantics. Replace generic stringly contracts with a tagged `canon.strategy.v1` schema and unambiguous vocabulary: strategies are selected, entities are linked or clustered, identifiers are looked up.

## Success Criteria
- Every existing strategy entry maps to exactly one typed kind or is rejected with an actionable migration reason.
- Cross-kind selection is impossible even when hashes or schema shapes coincide.
- Help, schemas, artifacts, and docs use one vocabulary and state what a strategy can execute.
- The doctrine preserves local deterministic selection and never makes strategy execution part of exact lookup.

## Test Plan
Round-trip typed fixtures for every kind; fuzz unknown tags and incompatible fields; snapshot selection/explain output; confirm old mixed-kind ambiguity is rejected deterministically.

## RESERVATIONS
- `src/strategy/types.rs`
- `schemas/canon.strategy.v1.schema.json`
- `docs/IDENTITY_ARCHITECTURE.md`
- `tests/strategy_contract.rs`

## Considerations
Keep the strategy subsystem, but make it canonical procedural knowledge rather than a bag of scripts. Domain profiles and review policy remain separately versioned inputs.

title: [CANON-V1/P00.5] Wire artifact-backed block, evidence, solve, and run stages
description:
## Background
Native artifact-backed modules are well tested directly, but public block/evidence/solve paths still route through legacy or incompatible types. The final pipeline must operate on prepared observations and one chained artifact family.

## Technical Approach
Connect `block` to verified prepare/index artifacts and emit bounded candidates plus compact exact-bucket assertions. Expose the public `evidence` stage over the shared typed evidence IR while retaining pair/hyperedge structure internally. Connect `solve` to verified evidence/buckets, enforce signed-graph constraints, reconcile incumbents, and emit review seeds/ledger events. Make `run`, `entity link`, and project execution compose these exact stage entry points.

## Success Criteria
- Manual stages and run/project wrappers produce semantically and byte-equivalent artifacts.
- No raw-row O(n²) path exists.
- Hard cannot-link evidence vetoes merge; relation/context signals never add hidden authority.
- Outputs carry complete upstream hashes and actionable next commands.
- “Edge” is an internal graph concept, not a competing public artifact/command vocabulary.

## Test Plan
Run per-stage CLI subprocesses, batch/wrapper/manual metamorphic equivalence, cluster/link mode parity, budget/refusal/no-partial-write matrices, and hard-negative/exact-bucket stress goldens.

title: [CANON-V1/P02.7] Enforce workspace ownership, path, and mutation safety
description:
## Background
A project runner touches many user-supplied paths and may eventually invoke optional providers or adapters. A bad manifest or interrupted run must not overwrite source data, escape the workspace, follow a dangerous symlink, or blur read-only and mutating commands.

## Technical Approach
Create one workspace-safety policy for canonicalization, symlink handling, owned output roots, collision detection, atomic writes, permissions, quotas, temp placement, and read-only enforcement. Require every planned node to declare its mutation set and validate that set again at execution. Refuse implicit current-directory outputs and inputs that alias outputs.

## Success Criteria
- Path traversal, symlink escape, hard-link aliasing, input/output overlap, and undeclared writes are rejected before mutation.
- Read-only commands demonstrably leave files, mtimes, permissions, and Beads state unchanged.
- Interrupted atomic publication preserves the previous valid artifact.
- Diagnostics name the offending logical field and safe remediation without exposing secrets.

## Test Plan
Run adversarial filesystem fixtures on supported platforms, including nested symlinks, Unicode normalization, permission errors, quota/disk exhaustion, and concurrent output claims. Capture pre/post inode metadata and directory manifests.

## RESERVATIONS
- `src/project/workspace.rs`
- `src/fs_safety.rs`
- `tests/project_workspace_safety.rs`

## Considerations
Never solve safety by deleting unexpected content. All cleanup and replacement behavior must respect the repository's explicit no-deletion rule.

title: canon geo: land an address-SET source (NYC PAD or per-BIN) — bd-1zph's corroboration channel has no data
description:
ORPHANED ACQUISITION GAP. BLOCKS bd-1zph's STATED PURPOSE. FOUND BY REALITY CHECK
2026-08-14.

THE PROBLEM, MEASURED: bd-1zph depends on an address channel that corroborates geometry.
Its own 2026-08-14 comment establishes that the obvious source — MapPLUTO's ADDRESS field —
is NOT ADEQUATE, because MapPLUTO carries ONE representative address per tax lot while
large and corner lots legitimately carry many. Measured cases where the point is almost
certainly on the correct lot yet the addresses differ:
    geocode 1633 BROADWAY          vs MapPLUTO 1657 BROADWAY
    geocode 1540 BROADWAY          vs MapPLUTO 1568 BROADWAY
    geocode 330 WEST 42ND STREET   vs MapPLUTO 334 WEST 42 STREET
    geocode 388 BRIDGE STREET      vs MapPLUTO 360 BRIDGE STREET
    geocode 9 WEST FORDHAM ROAD    vs MapPLUTO 2167 GRAND CONCOURSE  (corner, two frontages)
Comparing against a single canonical lot address MANUFACTURES DISAGREEMENT on exactly the
large multi-address and corner lots that dominate the CMBS book.

WHY IT IS ORPHANED: bd-1zph's comment names NYC PAD (Property Address Directory, DCP) or
the building footprints file's per-BIN addresses as candidates, states NEITHER IS LANDED,
and points at cmdrvl-context bd-1g1h. VERIFIED: OC-0048 marks bd-1g1h "superseded
2026-08-14: all three gaps closed" — and the three gaps closed were MapPLUTO, Building
Footprints, and ACRIS. THE ADDRESS-SET GAP IS NOT AMONG THEM. No open bead owns it.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS: OC-0048 identifies the address channel as the mechanism
that recovers the INTERPOLATED GEOCODE TIER — the population where the point sits in the
right-of-way and no lot contains it, which is where geometry alone cannot reach and where
the cascade earns its keep against the geometry-only baseline. If the address channel has a
high false-disagreement rate, the cascade cannot beat the baseline on the one population
that justifies building it.

TASK:
1. LAND AN ADDRESS-SET SOURCE FOR NYC. Evaluate and land whichever is better:
   - NYC PAD (Property Address Directory, DCP) — purpose-built as the address-to-BBL/BIN
     directory, which is exactly the shape needed.
   - Building Footprints per-BIN addresses — already landed (bd-397d), so this may be
     partially free. CHECK FIRST whether the landed footprints file carries usable
     addresses before acquiring anything new.
   Prefer the cheaper path if it is adequate; measure adequacy rather than assuming.
2. RE-MEASURE THE ADDRESS DISAGREEMENT RATE against the address SET rather than the single
   MapPLUTO ADDRESS. The prior naive comparison scored the five cases above as mismatches;
   they are not. Quantify how much of the measured 2,107 house-number disagreements
   dissolves once a set is available. This number directly sizes bd-1zph's value.
3. DEFINE THE ADDRESS-SET SEMANTICS for the operator: a match against ANY member of the
   lot's address set is agreement; the operator emits WHICH member matched as structured
   evidence, so the card can show it.
4. NATIONAL POSTURE UNDER BYOP. NYC PAD is a NYC solution. Nationally, the client's own
   parcel layer may or may not carry an address set — ATTOM and Regrid typically carry a
   situs address, often one per parcel, with the same single-address pathology. So the
   six-field client input contract must model address as POSSIBLY-A-SET, and the operator
   must degrade honestly when only one address is available: a single-address source
   produces WEAKER corroboration, and that weakness must be reflected in the decision band
   rather than hidden. Record this as a limitation of the national product, not a bug.

EXIT CRITERIA:
- Footprints file checked for usable per-BIN addresses BEFORE new acquisition
- An address-set source landed for NYC with a receipt (row counts, vintage, coverage)
- Re-measured disagreement rate against the set, compared to the single-address baseline
- Address-set semantics specified for bd-1zph's operator, emitting the matched member
- Client input contract updated to model address-as-set with honest degradation when the
  client's layer carries only one

  cmdrvl-curves bd-1ssr   FEMA USA STRUCTURES, 135,321,228 features nationally. National
                          landing IN PROGRESS; DC / AK / AL complete, AR running.
                          FEMA_USA_STRUCTURES_HOT loaded and read back (DC = 64,701 rows).
  cmdrvl-curves bd-3fyv   MICROSOFT GLOBALML FOOTPRINTS, release 2026-07-24. Landing IN
                          PROGRESS: 179 of 2,415 US files, 5,219,860 rows at 14:45Z.
  cmdrvl-curves bd-11uu   HUD USPS ADDRESS VACANCIES -- **BLOCKED**, and not a tile source.
                          HUD restricts it to registered governmental/non-profit users and
                          the sublicense forbids selling, licensing or distributing the
                          data. DO NOT PLAN ANY CANON GEO CAPABILITY ON IT.

NOTE ON "FOURSQUARE OS PLACES": it arrives as OVERTURE'S PLACES THEME, not a separate
Foursquare landing. That is the POI level in bd-2cbs, and it is in the same table family as
Overture buildings.

== FINDING 1: THE LANDED H3 GRAIN IS r4 / r7 / r8. THERE IS NO r9. ==
All three sources partition by h3_r4 and carry H3_R7 and H3_R8 columns. The epic's default
tile is res-9 and it is NOT precomputed anywhere.

AND THERE IS A CONVENIENT COINCIDENCE WORTH DELIBERATELY EXPLOITING: an r8 cell is
approximately 0.737 km2 -- which is almost exactly the area the epic specifies for its WORK
UNIT (an r9 cell plus k-ring 1 = 7 cells = 0.737 km2). So the already-landed H3_R8 column is
essentially the intended work-unit size.
ACTION FOR bd-2b9d: reconsider r9-plus-k-ring versus r8-plus-k-ring as the work unit, now
that r8 is precomputed across every source and r9 is not. This does not change the
requirement to compute cells in canon with a vetted Rust library -- the Snowflake H3 helper
defects (edgar-elt br-2wir) still stand -- but it does mean the warehouse can prefilter at
r8 for free, and the resolution decision now has a third input alongside node count and
human legibility.

== FINDING 2: POLYGON-TO-CELLS RETURNS EMPTY FOR SMALL BUILDINGS. LIVE, MEASURED. ==
From bd-3fyv: "H3_POLYGON_TO_CELLS alone inserted only 116 coverage rows for 354,804 hot
rows because small buildings often contain no H3 r8 cell centroid." Fixed there by using a
guaranteed CENTROID_H3_R8 plus H3_TRY_POLYGON_TO_CELLS.

THIS IS DIRECTLY THE MEMBERSHIP QUESTION bd-10s2 AND bd-2b9d SPECIFY. At r8 or r9 a
building is much smaller than a cell, so "which cells does this polygon cover" is
degenerate: the standard polygon-to-cells contract returns cells whose CENTRES fall inside
the polygon, and for a building that set is almost always EMPTY.
CONSEQUENCE: membership must be CENTROID-ANCHORED with polygon coverage as a supplement for
the large-feature case (parcels, campuses, complexes), NOT the other way round. My earlier
recommendation on bd-10s2 -- "full intersection cover for membership plus a single
deterministic anchor cell" -- is right in intent but inverted in emphasis, and applying it
naively with polygon_to_cells would have silently produced empty membership for nearly every
building. Correct it there.

== FINDING 3: OUR OWN SOURCES CARRY LICENSE OBLIGATIONS. bd-pq5w IS SCOPED TOO NARROWLY. ==
I framed license containment entirely around the CLIENT's licensed parcel layer. The landed
research shows OUR side has obligations too, and they differ per source:
    Overture buildings, divisions      ODbL-1.0            <-- SHARE-ALIKE
    Overture places                    per-source mix of CDLA-Permissive-2.0, Apache-2.0,
                                       CC0-1.0; source license must be retained
    Overture addresses                 source-specific, incl. NAD Access and Usage License
    FEMA USA Structures                CC-BY-4.0, attribution to ORNL and FEMA Geospatial
                                       Response Office REQUIRED
    Microsoft GlobalML                 CDLA-Permissive-2.0 current release; older vintages
                                       need per-release revalidation
bd-30ho states plainly: "License segmentation by source array is REQUIRED before any derived
product ships. Treat as a build-time gate, not a later cleanup."

ODbL SHARE-ALIKE IS THE COMMERCIAL ISSUE AND IT NEEDS AN OPERATOR DECISION, NOT AN
ENGINEERING ONE. A tile is a derived product. If it mixes ODbL Overture buildings with
everything else, the derived tile may inherit share-alike obligations that are
incompatible with a paid distribution model. Options to evaluate deliberately:
  (a) segregate ODbL-derived features into a separately-licensed layer of the tile, with
      the license class carried per feature -- note OVERTURE_MAPS_FEATURES_EXT ALREADY HAS
      LICENSE_CLASS AND LICENSE_TERMS COLUMNS, so the substrate for this exists;
  (b) build the commercial tile from the permissive sources only (FEMA CC-BY, Microsoft
      CDLA) and treat Overture as an internal enrichment;
  (c) accept share-alike and publish the tile openly.
REQUIRED IN bd-pq5w AND bd-1uld: license class per FEATURE in the tile artifact, and a
declared per-tile license posture that composes our obligations with the client's. The
artifact license boundary now has TWO directions, not one.

== FINDING 4: THE ATTRIBUTE CHANNELS FOR bd-272d ARE REAL, AND ONE IS MODELLED ==
Attribute anchoring needs class, size, floors, year. What is actually arriving:
    FEMA        OCC_CLS, PRIM_OCC (occupancy class), SQFEET, PROP_ADDR, UUID, BUILD_ID
    Overture    building class, height, num_floors, GERS id
    Microsoft   height (subset only), confidence, NO ID
    MapPLUTO    BLDGCLASS, LANDUSE, BLDGAREA, LOTAREA, NUMBLDGS, NUMFLOORS, YEARBUILT
So the six-field client contract has a counterpart on the tile side for every field except
YEAR BUILT, which only MapPLUTO supplies -- meaning year-built anchoring works in NYC and
degrades outside it until a national year source exists. Record that as a known national
limitation rather than discovering it later.

CRITICAL: FEMA OCCUPANCY IS MODELLED, NOT SURVEYED. bd-1ssr requires a provenance flag
"so downstream never treats it as surveyed." Attribute anchoring MUST carry that flag into
the evidence and weight modelled attributes below observed ones. A modelled occupancy class
driving a hard eliminative filter (bd-2zdz's assemblage type filter) would be a silent error
generator -- the filter is HARD, so a wrong modelled class removes the correct candidate
before anything is scored. Use modelled occupancy as SUPPORT evidence, never as a hard
filter, unless corroborated.

== FINDING 5: NO STABLE ID CONFIRMED FOR TWO SOURCES ==
Microsoft has no id at all -- bd-3fyv derives "a deterministic feature hash because no
stable id." Overture ADDRESSES are alpha with no stable GERS id either. This confirms
bd-2cbs rule 4 (alias-less participants) and extends it: the alias-less set is Microsoft
footprints AND Overture addresses, not just Microsoft.
A derived feature hash is NOT an alias and must not be minted into a registry -- it will
change whenever the geometry changes, which violates the tile identifier stability contract
in bd-12gh.

== FINDING 6: OVERTURE ADDRESSES CANNOT BE THE ADDRESS-SET SOURCE ==
bd-30ho: "Addresses theme is ALPHA -- do not build a contract against it yet," no stable
GERS id, multi-source licensing including NAD terms. US count 127,719,691.
So bd-35qg's address-set acquisition is NOT solved by Overture. NYC PAD or the per-BIN
addresses in the landed footprints file (bd-397d) remain the path, and the national story
stays open. Do not let the size of the Overture addresses count create false confidence.

== WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE WORKED-CASE CORPUS (bd-tccn) ==
The corpus can now stage its non-MapPLUTO pulls against REAL TABLE NAMES rather than
placeholders:
    EDGAR_DB.SOURCE.FEMA_USA_STRUCTURES_HOT              partially loaded (DC, AK, AL)
    EDGAR_DB.SOURCE.MICROSOFT_GLOBALML_BUILDING_FOOTPRINTS_HOT   partially loaded
    EDGAR_DB.SOURCE.OVERTURE_MAPS_FEATURES_HOT           DDL applied, 0 rows
    plus the *_FEATURE_H3_COVERAGE tables for each
NEW YORK IS NOT YET LOADED IN ANY OF THE THREE. FEMA is alphabetical by state and is at AR;
Microsoft is 179/2415 files; Overture has not started landing. So the full-tile version of
every case remains blocked, exactly as the corpus bead predicted -- but the blocker is now
a KNOWN COMPLETION DATE rather than an unlanded dataset, and the table names and column
shapes are already fixed enough to write the extraction queries against.
