comments.text:
SECOND, COMPOUNDING PATH TO THE ADDRESS SET 2026-08-14 — see bd-14hu. (No dependency added:
bd-35qg already blocks bd-1zph which blocks bd-bmee which bd-14hu depends on, so the edge
would be a cycle. The relationship is informational.)

This bead treats the address set as an ACQUISITION problem: land NYC PAD or the per-BIN
addresses in the landed footprints file, because MapPLUTO carries one representative address
per lot and comparing against it manufactures disagreement on exactly the large and corner
lots that dominate the CMBS book.

THERE IS A SECOND PATH, AND IT COMPOUNDS. Pre-resolving our own property corpora (HUD,
Fannie, Freddie, CMBS conduit, REIT Schedule III, NAIC) TEACHES ADDRESSES PER BUILDING. When
a HUD project asserting "305 EAST 72 STREET" and a CMBS deal asserting "1355 1 AVENUE"
resolve to the same building cluster, we have LEARNED an address set MapPLUTO does not
carry -- and that learning promotes into registry knowledge like any other accepted fact.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND NYC: PAD is a New York solution. Nationally, under
bring-your-own-parcel, the client's vendor layer typically carries one situs address per
parcel with the same single-address pathology, and there is no national PAD equivalent.
ACCRETION IS THE ONLY PATH THAT SCALES NATIONALLY, because it does not depend on any
jurisdiction publishing an address directory.

THIS DOES NOT REPLACE THE ACQUISITION. PAD and per-BIN addresses are AUTHORITATIVE and
available now; accretion is derived and starts empty. Land the authoritative source, and
treat accretion as the compounding supplement that extends coverage everywhere the
authoritative source does not exist.

ONE DESIGN REQUIREMENT THIS ADDS: an accreted address must carry its PROVENANCE and its
CONFIDENCE distinctly from an authoritative one. "This address is valid for this building
because PAD says so" and "because a HUD project and a CMBS deal both resolved here" are
different warrants, and a reviewer must be able to tell them apart. Do not blend them into
one address-set column.

comments.author: Zac
comments.text:
CORRECTION 2026-08-14 — THE ACCRETION FLYWHEEL DOES NOT SPIN FROM CLIENT USAGE. I overstated
it, and the operator caught it.

"We're not gonna get to keep our clients' properties. We're gonna run canon on their side.
We could offer it as an empty MCP server and get the info for ourselves, but we're mostly
offering for them to run canon on their side, so we won't be picking up addresses."

WHAT I IMPLIED: that resolving corpora compounds generally, as though every run added to the
registry.
WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE: accretion is bounded to CORPORA WE HOLD AND RESOLVE OURSELVES.
Canon runs on the client's machine, their artifacts are license-encumbered (bd-pq5w), and
their book never comes back. So:

  ACCRETES     HUD, Ginnie, Fannie, Freddie, CMBS conduit, REIT Schedule III, NAIC --
               everything we acquire and resolve on our own compute.
  DOES NOT     bank balance sheets, CRE CLOs, SASBs, and every other client corpus. Every
               client BENEFITS from our accretion; NO client CONTRIBUTES to it.

THE MOAT THEREFORE COMPOUNDS WITH ACQUISITION, NOT WITH ADOPTION. That is a real flywheel and
a weaker one than I described. It grows when we land another corpus, not when we sign
another client. Worth stating plainly because it changes what investment actually widens the
lead: buying and resolving more property corpora, not selling more seats.

TWO CONSEQUENCES THAT NEED HANDLING.

1. THE ADDRESS-SET ACCRETION PATH IS BOUNDED TOO (see bd-35qg). It still works -- HUD plus
   the agencies plus CMBS conduit is a large share of US institutional CRE addresses, and it
   is genuinely national. But it will never reach the addresses that exist only in client
   books, so it cannot fully substitute for landing an authoritative address-set source.
   The two paths remain complementary rather than one superseding the other.

2. WE ARE BLIND TO OUR OWN PRODUCT'S PERFORMANCE, AND THIS IS THE SERIOUS ONE.
   This bead makes the STAGE-1 HIT RATE against a real client book "the number that decides
   how much this actually buys." UNDER CLIENT-SIDE EXECUTION WE CANNOT MEASURE IT. Same for
   precision, abstention rate, coverage and false merges on live books -- bd-pq5w already
   records that we cannot debug or score a client's run centrally, and this is the same
   blindness applied to the metrics that would tell us where to improve.

   MITIGATION, AND IT IS ALREADY SCOPED: bd-pq5w's field classification separates SHAREABLE
   from ENCUMBERED. Evidence scores, operator ids, reason codes, abstention states, coverage
   states, candidate counts and tile ids are all shareable; client geometry and row values
   are not. So an OPT-IN REDACTED RUN SUMMARY gives us hit rates, abstention distributions
   and residual taxonomy WITHOUT their data ever leaving their machine.
   REQUIRED: make that redacted telemetry a first-class, opt-in, clearly-labelled output of
   the client run rather than something bolted on later. Design it as part of the artifact
   contract, and make what it contains inspectable by the client before they send it --
   trust is the product here, and a telemetry channel that is not fully legible would cost
   more than the metrics are worth.

   PROXY IN THE MEANTIME: hold out one of our own corpora, resolve the rest, and measure
   stage-1 hit rate of the held-out set against the accreted registry. That is a real
   number we can compute without any client, and it bounds the expected benefit before the
   first deployment.

3. THE HOSTED-MCP ALTERNATIVE IS A DELIBERATE PRODUCT DECISION, NOT A FALLBACK. Offering a
   hosted server that resolves on our side WOULD let us capture addresses -- and it inverts
   the privacy posture that the client-side design exists to provide. It is a different
   product with a different trust story and a different licensing exposure (their parcel
   vendor's terms may forbid sending the layer to us at all). Do not let it arrive by
   accident as a support convenience; if it is offered, it is offered explicitly.

comments.author: Zac
comments.text:
ARCHITECTURE SUPERSEDED 2026-08-15 — see docs/PLAN_CANON_GEO.md.

An adversarial multi-model design session produced a materially different architecture,
which then survived a red team that destroyed two intermediate designs. The tile is modelled
as a BOUNDED UNIVERSE and every piece of evidence is a CONSTRAINT; propagation runs to a
fixpoint; the residual model set IS the answer. There is no proposer channel.

THE THREE PROPERTIES THAT MATTER:
- CONFLUENCE. The fixpoint is independent of the order constraints are applied (Tarski 1955;
  Cousot & Cousot 1977; Apt 1999), so determinism is a theorem rather than an engineering
  effort.
- MONOTONICITY. Constraints only add and domains only shrink, so a tile resolved with four
  sources today and six next year yields a TIGHTER residual, never a contradicting one. The
  earlier answer was never wrong, only less resolved.
- STRUCTURAL ABSTENTION. The residual model set is the answer. No threshold anywhere.

THE KEY DESIGN RULE IS rho, THE SOUNDNESS DISCIPLINE. Every source attribute enters the
solver only through a declared versioned relaxation mapping it to the WEAKEST constraint the
source can actually support. An interpolated geocode becomes a 150m disc rather than a
location. A parcel ADDRESS becomes "one of this lot's addresses" rather than functional
equality. OWNERNAME equal PERMITS an assemblage; OWNERNAME different constrains NOTHING.
Every noisy channel is admitted only in its sound direction — which is what dissolved the
proposer dilemma that broke the two earlier designs.

AND THE COMMERCIAL CONSEQUENCE: if every rho is sound, the true assignment is in the model
set, so AN EMPTY MODEL SET IS A PROOF that a named source violated its own published error
model — attributable, falsifiable, and mailable to the vendor.

Read PLAN_CANON_GEO.md before starting any geo work. Section 11 carries the bead-by-bead
supersession table. Appendix A covers frozen-weight observers and imagery sources. APPENDIX
B RECORDS THE FIRST HARD MEASUREMENT, WHICH FALSIFIED A LOAD-BEARING CLAIM — read it before
trusting any performance number in the plan.

Raw session artifacts, including the red team and the adversarial reviews, are preserved
under docs/geo_design_session/ with a reading guide.

comments.author: Zac
comments.text:
THIRD INDEPENDENT CONFIRMATION 2026-08-15 — this is now the most-cited missing input in the
entire geo epic.

It has been named as the decisive gap by three separate analyses that did not share context:
1. The red team, which concluded "most of the parse forest exists to compensate for a
   missing data source. You do not have an address-point layer, and you need one."
2. The ground-truth test on the real 305 E 72nd tile, whose value-of-information answer was
   an authoritative BBL, else a versioned PAD/Geosupport table mapping the a/k/a ranges
   301-305 E 72 ST, 1392-1396 2 AVE, 1398-1402 2 AVE and 300-302 E 73 ST to BBL 1014477501.
3. The measured tile itself: MapPLUTO carries exactly ONE address for that lot, so four of
   the five asserted addresses are unverifiable against landed data — which is why the case
   resolves to a strong candidate but ABSTAINS at proof grade.

PAD / Geosupport already encodes every legal address per lot including all frontages and
a/k/a's, already handles the Queens grid semantics, and already knows that 9 West Fordham
Road and 2167 Grand Concourse are the same lot. It is deterministic, integer-keyed,
explainable, contains no model, and is maintained by the jurisdiction that DEFINES the
answer.

With it, work currently scoped as elaborate machinery collapses to lookup. Without it, the
address channel cannot corroborate anything on multi-address lots, which is the population
that matters.

PRIORITISE ACCORDINGLY. This is cheap acquisition standing in front of expensive
engineering.

title: canon org adjudication queue — turn unresolved clusters into review artifacts
description:
Add an adjudication export/import workflow for unresolved, abstained, or contradictory org identity clusters.

Context:
canon org can resolve, escrow, audit, promote, and explain. The remaining serious entity-resolution workflow gap is human review: operators need a deterministic artifact that presents unresolved evidence and lets reviewed decisions become auditable registry inputs.

Acceptance Criteria:
- CLI: canon org review export <RESULT.json> [--emit json|csv] [--include resolved|escrow|contradictions|all].
- Export includes source_row_ids, observed names, anchors, incumbent overlaps, evidence scores, contradiction reasons, and proposed review actions with stable IDs.
- CLI: canon org review import <REVIEW.json|csv> --registry <DIR> --next-version <VER> [--audit <AUDIT.json>] [--emit json|summary].
- Import refuses malformed decisions, duplicate review IDs, anchor conflicts, stale registry snapshots, and unaudited promotion paths where required.
- Imported decisions produce alias/anchor/escrow patches with proof hashes and preserve current org promotion invariants.
- Tests cover export determinism, clean import, conflict refusal, stale registry refusal, and CSV round trip.
close_reason: Implemented canon org review export/import with JSON/CSV artifacts, import validation, patch/proof writes, docs/operator contract updates, and passing fmt/clippy/test gate.

title: CSV output emission (--emit csv)
description:
Implement CSV output mode (--emit csv) in src/output/csv.rs.

TARGET FILE: src/output/csv.rs ONLY. Do not touch src/output/json.rs or src/output/mod.rs.

This module does ONE job: re-read the original CSV and append a canonical column using a pre-resolved map. It does NOT parse input values or resolve lookups — those are done by the input and lookup modules before this is called.

Pre-condition: run() has already validated that input format is CSV (not JSONL). This module can assume CSV input.

Input: original CSV file path, resolve_map: HashMap<String, Option<String>> mapping raw input values to canonical IDs (None for unresolved), column name, canonical column name, detected delimiter (from InputValues.delimiter), and a writer (&mut impl Write) for output.

IMPORTANT: The emit function takes a generic writer, NOT stdout directly. run() wraps stdout in a BLAKE3 hashing tee for witness protocol, then passes that writer to this module. This module writes CSV bytes to whatever writer it receives.

Behavior:
- Re-read original CSV row by row.
- Append header with canonical column name (default: <COLUMN>__canon, overridable via --canon-column).
- Pre-check: if canonical column name already in header => E_COLUMN_EXISTS refusal.
- For each data row: look up the column value in resolve_map. If Some(id), append raw canonical_id (no u8: prefix). If None, append empty string.
- Blank records: passed through with empty canonical column.
- Preserve original delimiter and quoting.
- Write to the provided writer (NOT directly to stdout).

Note: --map-out sidecar JSON is handled by run() calling the json output module, NOT by this module.

Exit codes: 0 (all resolved), 1 (partial/unresolved), 2 (refusal — no CSV written, refusal JSON to stderr).

UNIT TESTS: Include #[cfg(test)] mod tests in src/output/csv.rs. Test:
- Column appended correctly with right name
- Custom --canon-column name
- Unresolved rows get empty canonical column
- Blank rows passed through
- Delimiter preserved (comma, tab, pipe)
- Writes to a Vec<u8> writer (not stdout) in tests

VERIFICATION: cargo test -- output::csv
acceptance_criteria:
Appends canonical column as last column in header + every data row.
Default column name: <COLUMN>__canon. --canon-column overrides.
Resolved rows: raw canonical_id (no u8: prefix). Unresolved: empty string.
Blank records passed through with empty canonical column.
Delimiter and quoting match input file's detected format (uses InputValues.delimiter).
Receives pre-resolved HashMap, does NOT call lookup engine directly.
Emit function signature: pub fn emit(writer: &mut impl Write, ...) — takes a generic writer, NOT stdout directly.
Refusal E_COLUMN_EXISTS: canonical column name already exists in input header.
Refusal (exit 2): no CSV written, refusal JSON to stderr (handled by caller).
PARTIAL (exit 1): CSV fully written, unresolved rows visible not dropped.
NOTE: E_EMIT_FORMAT check is done by run() BEFORE calling this module. This module can assume input is CSV.
NOTE: --map-out sidecar JSON is handled by run(), NOT by this module.
close_reason: Implemented CSV emission to generic writer with delimiter/header handling, unresolved/blank row behavior, E_COLUMN_EXISTS precheck, and unit tests; cargo test -- output::csv passed

title: [CANON-V1/P08.4] Verify signatures, attestations, and promotion trust policy
description:
## Background
A digest proves integrity but not who reviewed or promoted a registry or strategy. Operators need deployable trust decisions without making signatures mandatory for local experimentation.

## Technical Approach
Define pluggable signature/attestation verification over OCI subjects and local packages, a trust-policy schema for accepted identities/issuers/thresholds/expiry/revocation/offline roots, and promotion attestations binding audit/review/source digests. Support a two-person rule as policy. Verification emits a deterministic receipt and fails closed when required material is unavailable.

## Success Criteria
- Required signatures and attestations are checked before project planning or deployment.
- Trust-policy changes are pinned and invalidate verification receipts.
- Unsigned local workflows remain possible only when policy explicitly permits them.
- Signature verification never substitutes for semantic package verification.

## Test Plan
Test valid, wrong subject, altered manifest, expired/revoked/untrusted signer, missing transparency/network, offline root, threshold approvals, stale audit, and policy change. Use local test keys only.

## RESERVATIONS
- `src/distribution/trust.rs`
- `schemas/canon.trust.policy.v1.schema.json`
- `tests/package_trust.rs`

## Considerations
Choose standard ecosystems during implementation based on current primary documentation; keep the core verification interface independent of one hosted service.
close_reason: Completed deterministic trust policy, signature/attestation verification, fail-closed receipt, and focused tests.

title: [CANON-V1/P07.4] Render an evidence waterfall for every decision and abstention
description:
## Background
Operators need to see not just a total score but how candidates were generated, which evidence supported or opposed them, which vetoes applied, what was missing, and which policy clause decided the outcome.

## Technical Approach
Build a deterministic explanation model from evidence IR, candidate/solver artifacts, policy, and registry snapshot. Render JSON plus concise human summaries for exact-existing, new cluster, linked, ambiguous, contradictory, blocked-by-veto, below-threshold, and review-overridden outcomes. Include counterfactual threshold and competing-candidate context without recomputing evidence.

## Success Criteria
- Every decision and unresolved item has a complete machine-readable reason trail.
- Vetoes and contextual evidence are visually and structurally distinct from positive score contributions.
- Explanations are derived from frozen artifacts and never invoke live enrichment.
- Large explanations paginate deterministically and redact sensitive payloads by policy.

## Test Plan
Golden-test all outcome classes, ties, missing evidence, stale references, redaction, large candidate sets, and byte stability. Cross-check explanation totals and clauses against solver decisions.

## RESERVATIONS
- `src/entity/explain.rs`
- `src/evidence/explain.rs`
- `schemas/canon.entity.explain.v1.schema.json`
- `tests/evidence_explain.rs`

## Considerations
Explanation should expose policy mechanics without pretending that heuristic evidence is objective truth.

title: [CANON-V1/P07.R6] Add deterministic structured comparison support operators
description:
## Background
The owner-provided ARCC/GSBD parse-vs-XBRL slice makes R6 executable, but current public profile support is limited to exact_view, string_similarity, TF-IDF, and reviewed aliases. Precomputed exact buckets can admit candidates and seed labels, but cannot truthfully prove numeric/date attribute corroboration or multi-tranche alignment.

## Technical Approach
Add domain-neutral profile operators numeric_within_tolerance, date_exact, date_near, and categorical_match over declared views. Parse decimal and ISO-date inputs deterministically without floating-point-dependent ordering. Numeric configuration must declare absolute tolerance and may declare relative basis-point tolerance; it never infers units or scale. Date-near declares a maximum whole-day distance. Categorical matching is exact after the profile-declared normalization pipeline. Emit ordinary typed support-lane evidence with deterministic ScoreUnits and existing combination/solver authority; missing, malformed, overflow, incomparable, or unconfigured values fail closed with explicit diagnostic/refusal semantics. No operator names, fields, defaults, thresholds, or scale rules may be BDC-specific.

## Success Criteria
- Structured non-name evidence can contribute support when name similarity is below threshold, while no single assignment/crosswalk field silently becomes issuer identity.
- Same declared views, parameters, and inputs yield byte-identical hits/artifacts under shuffled row order.
- Numeric/date boundary, tie, missingness, malformed input, overflow, and negative-control cases are explicit and deterministic.
- Unit/scale provenance remains caller-owned; a parse-million versus XBRL-dollar comparison refuses or emits no support until the caller supplies comparable normalized views.
- Hard cannot-link still vetoes; relation/context remains non-authoritative; existing string operators are unchanged.
- Public run/link artifacts bind operator/profile/upstream hashes and expose the per-field evidence waterfall.

## Test Plan
Unit-test fixed decimal and date boundary semantics, invalid/missing inputs, score saturation, and stable diagnostics. Integration-test a neutral multi-assignment fixture where structured agreement carries an otherwise ambiguous name, duplicate/tied attributes abstain, one near-miss stays separate, and shuffled input produces identical artifacts. Re-run focused profile/evidence/run tests, fmt, clippy, then the full quality gate after bd-32y0 public-stage wiring lands.

## RESERVATIONS
- src/entity/profile.rs
- src/entity/evidence.rs
- src/entity/run.rs
- tests/entity_structured_support.rs

## Considerations
Reuse existing ScoreUnits accumulation and typed edge artifacts. Do not implement Fellegi-Sunter/EM, implicit unit conversion, domain adapters, or promotion authority in this bead. The owner-only ARCC/GSBD execution and privacy-sanitized metrics remain bd-12px.

title: [CANON-V1/P01.3] Make registry index and mutation paths atomic under concurrent processes
description:
## Background
Airflow, operator laptops, and concurrent local agents can read or mutate related registry state. Derived index races and partial registry writes must not corrupt the version chain.

## Technical Approach
- Introduce lock/lease semantics scoped by package digest for derived index builders.
- Use write-plan validation followed by atomic file replacement for registry mutations.
- Detect competing version/snapshot changes immediately before commit and refuse with expected/actual hashes.
- Guarantee cleanup/recovery of abandoned temporary artifacts without deleting user-authored files.

## Success Criteria
- Concurrent readers never observe partial index or mapping state.
- Exactly one of two conflicting promotions succeeds; the loser receives an actionable stale-snapshot refusal.
- Idempotent identical writes converge without duplicated entries.
- Crash recovery leaves the prior registry valid.

## Test Plan
- Multi-process race harness.
- Failpoint tests around every write boundary.
- Idempotent retry and stale writer tests.
- Windows/macOS/Linux atomicity smoke coverage.

## RESERVATIONS
- `src/registry.rs`
- `src/registry/add_entry.rs`
- `src/registry/mint.rs`
- `src/entity/promote.rs`
- `tests/registry_concurrency.rs`

## Considerations
- No destructive cleanup without explicit safety proof.
- Remote publication concurrency is handled in P08 but shares these receipts.
- Locks are derived state, not package content.
close_reason: Implemented reserved atomicity slice and validated targeted concurrency/add-entry/mint/promote tests plus clippy

What changed:
- added advisory lease files for registry index builders and registry mutations
- validated planned writes against expected/proposed BLAKE3 hashes before commit
- made conflicting mutation retries refuse with actionable stale expected/actual hashes
- treated identical concurrent add-entry replays as idempotent at commit time
- switched add-entry/promote temp writes to unique crash-safe temp names so abandoned tool temp artifacts do not block later writes
- added focused concurrency coverage for stale builder lease recovery, conflicting add-entry stale-plan refusal, identical add-entry convergence, abandoned temp artifact non-blocking behavior, conflicting promote stale-snapshot refusal, and mint smoke after the atomicity changes

Validation:

title: [ENT-P00.6] Define artifact-chain hash continuity and stale-input refusal contract
description:

Purpose/background:
Hash continuity is the safety rail that lets large entity runs reuse artifacts without accidentally applying evidence from the wrong profile, strategy, registry snapshot, patch set, or input corpus. This bead defines the shared chain-of-custody contract used by every stage.

The contract must name which hash changes invalidate which downstream artifacts, which commands may rebuild caches, and which commands must refuse stale input. It must distinguish cache misses, artifact-contract refusals, registry-snapshot refusals, review-import refusals, audit-gate refusals, and successful solver abstentions.

Contract IDs:
Invariants I03, I04, I16, I18, I20, I21, I22, I24. Errors E_ENTITY_REGISTRY_SNAPSHOT, E_ENTITY_CACHE_MISMATCH, E_ENTITY_ARTIFACT_CONTRACT, E_ENTITY_REVIEW_IMPORT, E_ENTITY_AUDIT_GATE, E_ENTITY_APPLY_UNRESOLVED, E_ENTITY_IO_BUDGET. Threats T06, T07, T08. Gates G09, G10, G13, G14, G15.

title: [CANON-V1/P06.5] Model typed assignments independently from entity identity
description:
## Background
Many domains need to say that an entity held a role for a subject during an interval. That assertion must not be confused with the question of whether two observations identify the same entity.

## Technical Approach
Define a generic assignment fact over the temporal relationship contract: typed subject, opaque role ID, entity object or unresolved observation, valid/known interval, source locator, status, and provenance. Support multiple assignees, succession, disagreement, and domain policy constraints supplied by vocabulary packages.

## Success Criteria
- Identity can be accepted while an assignment remains disputed, and an assignment can remain unresolved without inventing an entity.
- Assignment promotion never writes an alias unless an independent identity review did so.
- All domain semantics enter through pinned ontology/vocabulary/policy packages.
- Generic projections retain raw disclosed values and source locators.

## Test Plan
Use neutral fixtures for co-assignment, transfer, conflicting sources, unresolved assignee, invalid cardinality, and late correction. Assert exact mappings remain independent.

## RESERVATIONS
- `src/temporal/assignment.rs`
- `schemas/canon.identity.assignment.v1.schema.json`
- `tests/identity_assignment.rs`

## Considerations
Assignment is a reusable graph primitive; Canon should not ship a catalog of real-world roles.
notes:
## Demanding-deployment requirement ownership
Owns R2. A source row may describe one organization plus multiple facilities, tranches, holdings, roles, or other assignments. Model one issuer observation and N typed assignment or relationship facts; do not manufacture duplicate entities from instrument structure.

title: canon geo [ambition-2]: constellation consistency — exhaustive transform fit, then spectral graph matching
description:
THE OPERATOR bd-gs6n DEFERRED AND NOBODY CUT. IT IS ONE OF THE EPIC'S FIVE PILLARS.

bd-2kjx lists CONSTELLATION CONSISTENCY as reason 4 of five for why geo is easier than
person ER: "Relative arrangement survives across sources even when coordinates, counts and
attributes differ. Right matching aligns the whole block under one transform; wrong
matching does not. A GLOBAL CHECK NO ATTRIBUTE-BASED ER CAN PERFORM."
bd-gs6n lists constellation_consistent among its operators and says "deferred to its own
bead; harder and not v1." THAT BEAD WAS NEVER CREATED. Found by reality check 2026-08-14.

BLOCKED ON THE RESIDUAL HARNESS — specifically on category (c), the tie population. If
ties are rare, this does not get built.

THE PROBLEM: two sources describe the same city block with different coordinates (vendor
capture error, different generalization, different datum epoch), different counts (one
vendor merges adjoining structures), and different attributes. Pairwise geometry cannot
distinguish "these two footprints are the same building" from "these two footprints are
neighbours" when the offset between sources exceeds the spacing between buildings — which
is common in dense urban cores and is exactly where the CMBS book concentrates.
BUT THE ARRANGEMENT IS INVARIANT. If the matching is right, ONE rigid or similarity
transform aligns the whole block. If it is wrong, no single transform does.

THE METHOD — SPECTRAL GRAPH MATCHING (Leordeanu & Hebert, 2005), and it is the right tool
for four reasons:
1. It formulates matching as finding the strongest cluster in an AFFINITY GRAPH over
   candidate correspondences, where affinity between two correspondences (a->a', b->b')
   encodes GEOMETRIC CONSISTENCY — e.g. how well dist(a,b) agrees with dist(a',b').
   Pairwise distance is exactly the invariant that survives across vendors.
2. The solution is the PRINCIPAL EIGENVECTOR of the affinity matrix, followed by greedy
   discretization. Polynomial, and at ~167 nodes the affinity matrix is small.
3. It naturally produces a CONFIDENCE per correspondence (the eigenvector component), which
   maps onto ScoreUnits and therefore onto canon's existing evidence model — this is a
   scored operator, not an oracle.
4. It degrades honestly: a block with no consistent arrangement produces a flat
   eigenvector, which is a detectable ABSTENTION SIGNAL rather than a confident wrong
   answer.

DETERMINISM IS THE HARD PART AND MUST BE SOLVED, NOT ASSUMED:
- Eigen-decomposition is iterative and float. Two runs on different platforms can produce
  different eigenvectors, and sign is arbitrary. REQUIRED: a fixed iteration count (power
  iteration, not a library eigensolver with adaptive convergence), a deterministic
  starting vector, a canonical sign convention, and QUANTIZATION TO ScoreUnits AT THE
  ARTIFACT BOUNDARY. Per src/entity/score.rs the discipline already exists: floats
  internally, integers at the boundary. Follow it exactly.
- DEGENERATE CASES: repeated eigenvalues (a symmetric block — a row of identical townhouses
  is the canonical example and is common) make the principal eigenvector ill-defined.
  DETECT AND ABSTAIN. A symmetric arrangement is genuinely ambiguous and canon should say
  so; this is a feature, not a limitation.
- The greedy discretization step must have specified tie-breaking on a total order of
  surface ids.

SIMPLER ALTERNATIVE TO TRY FIRST, AND IT MAY BE ENOUGH: estimate a single transform by
exhaustive evaluation over minimal correspondence sets. A similarity transform needs two
correspondences; with hard distance constraints pruning most pairs, the candidate set per
tile may be small enough to enumerate EXACTLY and deterministically — no eigensolver, no
float convergence, no degeneracy handling. TRY THIS FIRST AND MEASURE. Do not use RANSAC:
it is randomized, which breaks replay, and a seeded RANSAC is just a worse exhaustive
search.

OUTPUT SHAPE: constellation consistency is a GLOBAL check that produces PER-PAIR evidence.
Each candidate correspondence gets a hit with the operator id, the residual under the fitted
transform, the transform's parameters, and how many correspondences supported it. All of
that is renderable on bd-101v's card and is exactly the "point at assertion scores"
explainability canon requires.

EXIT CRITERIA:
- Exhaustive minimal-set transform estimation attempted and measured FIRST
- If spectral is needed: fixed-iteration power method, deterministic start, canonical sign,
  integer quantization at the boundary
- Degenerate/symmetric arrangements detected and abstained on, with a test using a row of
  identical structures
- Per-pair evidence emitted with transform parameters and residuals
- Cross-platform determinism test
- Residual re-measured; the tie category must move materially or this is reverted

Appendix L (E1-E3, 2026-08-16): point re-ranking is not the dominant failure mode (0/7 tile-addressable wins; 72/79 labeled failures unreachable/representation cases), so the residual harness gate this lane waited on resolved AGAINST it. title: [SPLINK-STEAL/S3] evidence: value-level frequency weighting with rare-value floor
description:
## Problem this solves
An exact firm_core hit on a very common value ("Wells Fargo"-grade) currently scores the same as a hit on a rare value, so thresholds must assume the common-name-collision worst case and the long tail over-escrows. Value-level frequency weighting lets rare-name matches auto-accept confidently while common-name matches demand anchors — directly targeting the CMBS tenant/sponsor long tail, the corpus family with the worst review-burden projection.

## Build
- Persist per-view value-frequency tables at the posting/index stage (counts derivable from the existing posting dictionary; TfidfTerm postings already exist in src/entity/postings.rs).
- New strategy-configurable support-evidence modifier: frequency band scales exact_view and similarity support scores. Band table (rare/uncommon/common/very_common thresholds + integer multipliers) is authored in strategy YAML — no learned weights in this bead.
- Rare-value floor (Splink tf_minimum_u_value analog): values below a minimum corpus count cap at the uncommon band, so singleton misspellings cannot masquerade as ultra-rare strong evidence.
- Fuzzy-hit semantics: use the MORE frequent side's band (corruption assumption — one side is a typo of the other).
- Record band + count in evidence artifacts so explain/waterfall (S7) can show them.

## Splink reference (clone at /Users/zac/Source/opensource/splink)
- splink/internals/term_frequencies.py — TF table computation and join mechanics
- docs/topic_guides/comparisons/term-frequency.md — per-level weights, tf_minimum_u_value floor, greater-of-two-TF on fuzzy levels (lines ~118-211)

## How to test
- Skewed-distribution fixture: rare exact match auto-links while common exact match escrows under the same strategy.
- Floor test: singleton typo value does NOT get the rare-band boost.
- Fuzzy greater-side test: (common, rare-typo) pair uses the common band.
- Frequency tables are hash-bound: stale table vs current index -> typed refusal (mirror registry-snapshot staleness semantics).
- Absent-config no-op: strategies without a band table produce byte-identical artifacts to today (regression guard).
- Determinism replay across runs and row shuffles.

## Doctrine constraints
Integer units; frequency tables are hash-bound artifacts; band table is versioned strategy input; frequency weighting cannot elevate evidence past cannot-link, protected-token, or anchor-conflict facts; feature entirely inert unless configured.

## RESERVATIONS
- src/entity/postings.rs
- src/entity/value_frequency.rs (new)
- src/entity/evidence.rs
- tests/entity_value_frequency.rs

title: canon geo: WHO reconciles the tile's own four sources — curves at landing, canon at consumption, or canon at tile build?
description:
UNRESOLVED ARCHITECTURAL BOUNDARY. IT GATES FIVE EXISTING BEADS AND I ASSUMED AN ANSWER
WITHOUT ASKING. Filing it as the open question it actually is.

== WHAT IS ESTABLISHED ==
cmdrvl-curves is CO-LOCATING the big four by H3 cell right now (bd-30ho Overture, bd-1ssr
FEMA, bd-3fyv Microsoft, plus the landed MapPLUTO). Every source carries h3_r4 partitioning
and H3_R7/H3_R8 columns, and each has a `*_feature_h3_coverage` table. Operator 2026-08-14:
"we can take one H3 tile and get all four datasets."

CO-LOCATION IS NOT RESOLUTION. Having four sources indexed to the same cell tells you they
are in the same place. It does NOT tell you that Overture building X, FEMA structure Y and
Microsoft footprint Z ARE THE SAME BUILDING.

== THE QUESTION ==
WHO RECONCILES THE TILE'S OWN SOURCES INTO BUILDING CLUSTERS, AND WHERE?

  OPTION A -- cmdrvl-curves / Snowflake, at landing time.
    Tiles ship with building clusters already formed and cmdrvl:building:* ids minted.
    Canon geo never performs multi-source building ER; it attaches client rows to
    pre-existing anchors.
    FOR: the expensive N-source reconciliation runs once per tile per vintage rather than
    once per client run; every client gets identical anchors, which is what makes minted
    ids stable and shareable at all; the client's machine does far less work.
    AGAINST: identity resolution in dbt/SQL is exactly what canon exists to do properly --
    versioned registries, typed evidence, abstention, review, replay. Doing it in Snowflake
    means reimplementing canon's discipline in a substrate with none of it, and the
    provenance would not survive into canon's artifacts.

  OPTION B -- canon geo, at tile consumption.
    The tile ships co-located but unresolved. Canon resolves all sources including ours in
    one run.
    FOR: one resolution engine, one evidence model, one review path, full provenance.
    AGAINST: every client re-resolves the same public buildings independently, wasting
    work and -- worse -- producing DIFFERENT ANSWERS per client, which destroys the
    stable-shared-anchor property that bd-67wx's identifier scheme depends on.

  OPTION C -- canon geo, at tile BUILD, run by us.
    We run canon over the four sources once per tile per vintage and ship the resulting
    registry and artifacts inside the tile. The client runs canon again over their own two
    inputs against those anchors.
    FOR: canon's discipline everywhere, resolution happens once, anchors are stable and
    shared, provenance survives, and the tile carries real canon artifacts rather than a
    SQL side-effect.
    AGAINST: requires canon to run at national tile scale on our side, which is a
    throughput question nothing has sized.

RECOMMEND OPTION C. It is the only one that keeps identity resolution inside the tool
built for it while preserving the stable-shared-anchor property. But this is an OPERATOR
DECISION about where a boundary sits, not a technical preference, and the throughput
question is real and unsized.

== WHY THIS IS URGENT: IT ALREADY MISDIRECTED WORK ==
In bd-272d I asserted "the tile must ship pre-resolved" as though settled. That inference
is probably right in spirit and it INVALIDATED THE PREMISE OF AN ENTIRE BEAD before anyone
checked it:
  bd-3h2p (permutation synchronization) was scoped for "six to seven named sources in one
  BYOP tile." Under A or C the client run has THREE participants -- pre-resolved buildings,
  client parcels, client book -- and triangle consistency across three is trivial. Under B
  the original premise holds. The bead is CLOSED as superseded pending this decision; if B
  wins it should be reopened.

FOUR MORE BEADS DEPEND ON THE ANSWER AND ARE BLOCKED ON IT:
  bd-1uje  optimal assignment          which side runs it, and over what
  bd-3d8p  constellation consistency   almost certainly a TILE-BUILD problem, not a
                                       client-run one -- aligning four vendors' footprints
                                       is our job, not the client's
  bd-1c96  correlation clustering      same question
  bd-3ul7  entropic OT                 already lowest priority; a pre-resolved tile makes
                                       it less likely still
  bd-1s4e  N-source CLI wiring         under A or C the client run is 3 sources, not 7, so
                                       the justification and the scale both change

== WHAT THE ANSWER MUST SPECIFY ==
1. Where multi-source building reconciliation runs, with the reasoning recorded.
2. Whether cmdrvl:building:* ids are minted by us at tile build (A/C) or by the client
   (B). bd-67wx assumes stable shared anchors, which only A and C provide.
3. What the tile carries as a result: bare co-located features, or clusters plus the
   evidence and the retained losers. bd-101v's card needs the losers, so under A the
   Snowflake path would have to emit them -- which it currently does not.
4. If C: a throughput estimate for running canon over the built-up US at the chosen
   resolution, and whether that is a batch job we can actually afford.
5. Whichever option wins, HOW THE FOUR SOURCES' DISAGREEMENTS SURVIVE INTO THE CLIENT'S
   ARTIFACT. Cross-vendor disagreement is evidence, not noise, and collapsing it at tile
   build to ship a clean answer would discard exactly the material the visual evidence
   card is built to show.

EXIT CRITERIA:
- A written decision naming A, B or C with reasoning recorded
- Minting authority settled and reconciled with bd-67wx
- Tile contents specified for the chosen option, including retained losing candidates
- If C, a sized throughput estimate
- The five dependent beads re-scoped or reopened against the decision

comments.author: Zac
comments.text:
OPERATOR DECISION 2026-08-14: OPTION B. Canon reconciles the tile's sources AND the client's
data in one pass, at run time.

"All the tile's data is one pull from the geo MCP server for an H3 and its surrounding H3s.
It brings back a whole bunch of JSON, and canon reconciles that along with the client data
when it runs. The tile data is pre-assembled in Snowflake, but canon consumes it and the
client data and reconciles everything on the spot."

So the boundary is: SNOWFLAKE PRE-ASSEMBLES (co-location by cell, one pull, JSON out).
CANON RESOLVES (all sources, one pass, one evidence model, full provenance).

== MY OBJECTION TO B WAS WRONG. RETRACTING IT. ==
I argued B would mean "every client re-resolves the same public buildings independently,
producing DIFFERENT ANSWERS per client, which destroys the stable-shared-anchor property
bd-67wx depends on."

That is false, for two reasons.

1. DETERMINISM ALREADY GIVES THE SHARED-ANCHOR PROPERTY. Canon's core promise is that the
   same inputs plus the same versions reproduce byte-identical output. Two clients running
   over the same content-addressed tile digest, the same strategy hash, the same profile
   version and the same canon version get the SAME CLUSTERS. There is nothing to
   coordinate; the pinning canon already does IS the coordination.

2. CLIENTS DO NOT NEED THE SAME MINTED ID -- THEY NEED SHARED ALIASES, AND THEY HAVE THEM.
   bd-67wx's own doctrine is that the cluster is the identity and SOURCE IDS ARE
   PARTICIPANTS. Two clients determine that their clusters denote the same building because
   both contain building:overture:gers:X, not because both minted the same opaque id. The
   minted id is a LOCAL convenience. OC-0048 already states this outright: "The client mints
   their own IDs in their own registry. We supply evidence; we never impose an identifier."

So minting stays local, aliases carry cross-client comparability, and determinism carries
reproducibility. The objection dissolves.

== B HAS A REAL ADVANTAGE I DID NOT CREDIT ==
CLIENT DATA CAN IMPROVE TILE RECONCILIATION. If the client's licensed parcel layer is
better than anything we hold for that county, it may disambiguate buildings our four public
sources could not. A hard pre-resolve (Option C) FREEZES THAT OUT -- the decision would
already be made before their evidence arrives. Under B the client's evidence participates
on equal terms. That is strictly better resolution, and it is the kind of thing that would
have been very annoying to discover after building C.

== ON THE TWO-MODE IDEA: DO NOT BUILD TWO MODES. BUILD ONE PIPELINE WITH A CACHEABLE PREFIX ==
The operator asked whether canon could have a mode that builds a more efficiently
reconciled tile upfront, with client reconciliation as a second pass. The instinct is right
and there is a better shape for it than two modes.

THE KEY OBSERVATION: tile-internal reconciliation is a PURE FUNCTION OF (tile digest,
strategy hash, profile version). It does not depend on client data at all. Anything that is
a pure function of pinned inputs is CACHEABLE, and a cache is shippable.

CANON ALREADY HAS THIS MACHINERY. src/entity/cache.rs, EntityCacheStage,
EntityCacheDecision, cache receipts recorded in the run artifact, and
`--cache-mode enabled|disabled` on both `entity run` and `entity link`. The artifact chain
(src/entity/artifact_chain.rs, EntityChainEnforcement) already refuses stale or mismatched
stage hashes. This is not new architecture; it is the existing cache applied to a new
prefix.

SO: the "pre-built tile" is a CACHE ENTRY, not a mode.
  - We can compute it centrally and SHIP IT INSIDE THE TILE.
  - If present and hash-valid, canon skips recomputation and records a cache receipt.
  - If absent, stale, or the strategy changed, canon recomputes locally AND GETS THE
    IDENTICAL ANSWER, because determinism.
  - The cache is therefore an OPTIMIZATION THAT CAN NEVER CHANGE A RESULT -- which is the
    only kind of cache worth having in a tool whose product is reproducibility.
Two modes would mean two code paths, two sets of bugs, and a divergence risk between the
fast path and the correct path. One pipeline with a verifiable cache has none of that.

== THE SHARP PART: CACHE THE EVIDENCE, NOT THE VERDICT ==
Do NOT cache tile-internal DECISIONS. Cache the expensive DETERMINISTIC WORK that precedes
them:
    CACHE      cell assignment, blocking, candidate generation among tile sources,
               geometry predicate results, pairwise evidence scores between tile sources,
               the tile's attribute-rarity denominators (bd-272d)
    DO NOT     the solve, the clusters, the minted ids, the abstentions
Reason: if the tile's decisions were cached, the client's evidence could not participate in
them, and the advantage in the previous section evaporates -- we would have rebuilt Option C
by the back door. Caching at the evidence layer means the client's parcel layer joins a
FULLY-SCORED CANDIDATE GRAPH and the solve runs ONCE, over everything, with all evidence
present.

That is the whole design in one line: PRE-SCORE, NEVER PRE-DECIDE.

== CONSEQUENCES, PROPAGATED ==
1. bd-3h2p IS REOPENED. Its premise -- six to seven named sources in one client run -- is
   CORRECT under B, and I closed it against an assumption. The reopen condition recorded on
   that bead was "if bd-3foo decides Option B, reopen unchanged." It fired.
2. bd-1s4e's re-scope is REVERTED. The client run genuinely is 6-7 participants, and the
   original reasoning to leave CANONICAL_REFERENCE unused stands -- nothing in the tile is
   globally canonical when everything is being resolved together.
3. bd-1uje, bd-3d8p, bd-1c96, bd-3ul7 are UNBLOCKED from this decision. They are client-run
   problems as originally scoped. They remain gated on bd-8z0y's residual measurement,
   which is the gate that always mattered.
4. NEW WORK THIS CREATES: the cacheable-prefix design itself -- what exactly is cached, how
   it is hash-bound to the tile digest and strategy, how it ships inside the tile artifact
   (bd-1uld), and how canon proves a shipped cache is valid rather than trusting it.
5. THROUGHPUT MOVES TO THE CLIENT and needs sizing. A dense Manhattan tile pulled as JSON
   across four-plus sources, reconciled on a laptop, for every tile covering a client's
   book. That is a real performance question and it is now on the critical path in a way it
   would not have been under C. Size it against a real Manhattan tile before the format
   freezes.

title: [CANON-V1/P04.7] Simulate registry changes against frozen projects before promotion
description:
## Background
Resolving an inbox group may improve coverage but also redirect an existing alias, merge distinct firms, change historical snapshots, or affect many downstream rows. Promotion should show that blast radius.

## Technical Approach
Implement `canon registry impact` to apply a proposed patch to an in-memory candidate registry version, replay frozen lookup/link/cluster corpora and declared project samples, and emit exact before/after mappings, newly resolved, newly unresolved, changed canonical IDs, conflicts, temporal effects, and downstream projection deltas. Never write the candidate during simulation.

## Success Criteria
- Every changed mapping is attributable to a proposed patch entry and affected source rows/projects.
- No-change and additive-only patches are distinguished from remaps, merges, splits, and deletions.
- Simulation uses the same compiled lookup semantics as final promotion and records all input digests.
- A refused or failed impact run leaves registries and caches untouched.

## Test Plan
Test additive alias, unsafe remap, parent/subsidiary collision, temporal boundary, bulk patch, stale base, and dbt/search projection differences. Compare simulation with an explicitly promoted temporary registry.

## RESERVATIONS
- `src/registry/impact.rs`
- `schemas/canon.registry.impact.v1.schema.json`
- `tests/registry_impact.rs`

## Considerations
Impact is only as complete as declared frozen consumers; report coverage of the simulation corpus instead of claiming global safety.

title: EPIC: revive canon resolve — structural resolution Phase 5 + the five open questions
description:
Revive PLAN_STRUCTURAL_RESOLUTION.md (docs/, 976 lines, revised 2026-05-06). canon resolve shipped v0 and then stalled. OC-0048 (Location Master) now supplies the demand that makes finishing it worthwhile, and four of the plan's five open questions are exactly what the geo workbench needs.

== WHERE IT STOPPED ==
  Phase 1  Strategy parser + assertion operators (~450 LOC)      COMPLETE
  Phase 2  Tape loader + graph hydration (~350 LOC)              COMPLETE
  Phase 3  Scoring + resolve orchestration + CLI (~400 LOC)      COMPLETE
  Phase 4  Gold scoring + write-back (~200 LOC)                  COMPLETE
  Phase 5  Tournament validation                                 'NEXT' -- NEVER RAN

Phase 5 exit criteria as written: pick one deal with trustee + servicer tapes, have an analyst build a 50-100 loan gold cross-reference, author an initial strategy from domain knowledge, run the tournament (mutate strategy -> canon resolve -> score -> promote/revert), then validate the promoted strategy generalizes to a second deal.

That is a REAL blocker, not a formality: nothing in canon resolve has been validated against live CMBS tapes with a human-built gold set. Everything downstream inherits that unproven-ness.

== THE FIVE OPEN QUESTIONS, RE-RANKED BY THE OC-0048 DRIVER ==
The plan lists these as deferred. The geo workbench (bd-2kjx) forces four of them, which changes their priority from 'someday' to 'required'.

  Q1 MORE THAN TWO TAPES -- REQUIRED BY GEO.
     v0 takes exactly two tapes; a third means running pairwise and accumulating
     into one registry. A geo tile carries SIX tapes (Overture buildings, FEMA
     USA Structures, Foursquare places, CMBS Annex A, Schedule III, client
     parcels). Decide: native n-tape, or repeated pairwise plus a consistency
     pass? The plan's own note already anticipates 'future: native multi-tape'.

  Q2 BIPARTITE CONSTRAINT -- REQUIRED BY GEO.
     v0 is greedy (best match per target, independently) and can let two targets
     claim one reference, flagged only as a warning. Geo has HARD mutual
     exclusion -- two Overture buildings are not the same building -- so greedy
     conflicts are wrong answers, not warnings. The plan names Hungarian for v1.
     Note the geo case is easier than general: at ~167 nodes per tile an exact
     assignment is affordable.

  Q3 ADDRESS NORMALIZATION -- REQUIRED BY GEO, AND BY THE ORIGINATING PROBLEM.
     The plan calls exact-match on addresses brittle ('123 Main St' != '123 MAIN
     STREET') and defers an address_match operator. OC-0048's motivating case is
     harder still: '100 Main Street' vs '100-101 Main Street', where string
     similarity CANNOT decide and range parsing plus geometry must. Scope this as
     TWO operators, not one: address_match (normalization) and address_range
     (parse and containment).

  Q4 CANONICAL ID FOR MULTI-SOURCE -- REQUIRED BY GEO.
     v0 says the first/reference tape wins. Geo has NO natural winner: GERS,
     FEMA UUID, fsq_place_id, APN/BBL, BIN are all source-namespaced and none is
     primary -- verified 2026-08-13 that no universal ID exists. The plan's own
     v1 answer (configurable canonical ID strategy) is the right shape, and it
     must permit the CLIENT to mint their own, which OC-0048 requires.

  Q5 COLUMN TYPE INFERENCE -- not geo-forced. Lowest priority of the five.

== WHAT ELSE NEEDS FLESHING OUT ==
  - Geometry as a first-class column type. The plan assumes scalar/string
    columns; spatial predicates need polygons and points as typed values, plus
    a decision on whether geometry lives in core or an out-of-tree extension.
    Determinism requires EXACT predicates (adaptive precision), not naive float.
  - Typed relationship output. Plan output is match/no-match. OC-0048 needs
    same_as vs contains vs part_of, which the Provider SDK independently
    requires by keeping identity and relationship facts in separate fact
    families. A bare boolean is the wrong contract.
  - Blocking by tile. canon resolve applies a candidate filter; H3 cell
    membership is the geo blocking key and is exact where name-trigram blocking
    is lossy.
  - Abstention semantics at scale. 'Zero matches is a finding' must survive
    n-tape and be reportable as a rate, since it is an OC-0048 success metric.

== RELATIONSHIP TO bd-2kjx ==
bd-2kjx (geo resolution workbench) is the DEMAND. This epic is the SUBSTRATE.
Q1-Q4 must land here before the geo strategy operators have anything to sit on.
Sequencing: this epic first, or at minimum Q1/Q2 first.

== CHILDREN NOT YET CUT ==
Deliberate. Phase 5 needs an operator decision (which deal, whose analyst builds the gold set), and Q1 needs the native-vs-pairwise architecture call. Cut children after those two decisions.

Related: cmdrvl-context OC-0048, OC-0046, OC-0047; canon bd-2kjx; docs/PLAN_STRUCTURAL_RESOLUTION.md, docs/PROVIDER_SDK.md, docs/IDENTITY_ARCHITECTURE.md.
close_reason:
WRONG SUBSTRATE -- operator redirect 2026-08-13.

canon resolve is a TWO-TAPE cross-tape matcher built for CMBS trustee/servicer reconciliation. Generalizing it (n-tape, geometry column types, typed relationship output, tile blocking) would bend a tool toward a job it was not designed for.

The correct parent is canon entity, which is far more mature and already solves what this epic proposed to add:
  multisource.rs  -- 'Deterministic N-SOURCE entity-link materialization' with
                     source names, comparison graph validation, pair budgets and
                     source-aware consistency diagnostics. Open Question 1
                     (more than two tapes) is ALREADY ANSWERED in entity.
  anti_merge.rs   -- distinctness / hard negatives, exactly what spatial
                     exclusion needs
  relation.rs     -- typed relationships, i.e. same_as vs contains vs part_of
  block / block_artifact / index / postings -- blocking machinery
  candidates / budget -- bounded candidate generation
  evidence / evidence_ir / edge / edge_artifact -- evidence model
  ledger / ledger_replay, promote / review / publication, explain, patches

Geospatial resolution is therefore a FIRST-CLASS SIBLING TO canon entity, designed natively, not an extension of canon resolve. Redesign lives in bd-2kjx.

FINDING PRESERVED (independent of geo, not being actioned here): canon resolve stopped at Phase 5 (tournament validation) and has NEVER been validated against live CMBS tapes with a human-built gold cross-reference. Phases 1-4 shipped. If canon resolve is ever relied on for CMBS tape reconciliation, that gap is real and should be re-opened on its own merits.

title: [CANON-V1/P10] Embeddable lookup, agent interfaces, and additional deployment projections
description:
## Background
The CLI is the primary operator surface, but exact registry knowledge should be embeddable in pipelines, agents, browsers, and services without reimplementing semantics. This lane extends deployment while keeping one core contract.

## Scope
Establish stable Rust library boundaries; add agent-safe MCP/JSON-RPC resources and mutation gates; compile registry snapshots to additional deterministic projections such as WASM/static lookup, Parquet/Arrow, and JSON-LD where justified; document serving patterns built on the existing search-index export.

## Success Criteria
Embedded consumers return the same mappings, refusal semantics, version, and provenance as the CLI. New projections are generated from verified registry packages and do not become alternate truth stores.

## Test Plan
Cross-interface conformance, WASM/browser fixtures, language binding smoke tests if adopted, MCP permission tests, projection round trips, and byte/semantic parity with CLI lookup.

title: Improve JSON ergonomics for encoded UTF-8 values
description:
Canon JSON currently emits explicit UTF-8 values as strings like `u8:037833100` and `u8:BBG000B9XRY4`. This is defensible for lossless audit output, but confusing for common securities workflows where users expect plain CUSIP/FIGI strings. CSV mode already emits plain values.

Context: resolving CUSIP `037833100` through an OpenFIGI-built registry returns `canonical_id: "u8:BBG000B9XRY4"`, while users naturally expect `BBG000B9XRY4`.

Acceptance criteria:
- Decide and document the JSON contract for human/CLI workflows vs lossless audit workflows.

title: canon geo [ambition-4]: multi-source consistency — cycle-consistency filter first, permutation synchronization only if justified
description:
MULTI-WAY CONSISTENCY ACROSS THE 6-7 NAMED SOURCES IN A BYOP TILE.

BLOCKED ON THE RESIDUAL HARNESS AND ON THE OPTIMAL-ASSIGNMENT BEAD. Bipartite exactness
first; only reach for multi-way when pairwise-plus-reconciliation is measurably insufficient.

THE PROBLEM: a BYOP tile carries Overture GERS, FEMA USA Structures, Microsoft GlobalML,
NYC/MapPLUTO where free, the client's licensed parcel layer, and the client's property book.
Pairwise matching between each pair produces C(n,2) matchings that need not be MUTUALLY
CONSISTENT: A matches B, B matches C, but A does not match C. Every triangle that fails to
close is a contradiction sitting in the artifact.

canon already DETECTS this — EntityAnchorConflict plus EntityMultisourceAbstentionReason::
AnchorConflict in src/entity/multisource.rs abstain when sources disagree on a canonical id
for an anchor key. That is the correct conservative behaviour and it should REMAIN THE
DEFAULT. The question this bead asks is narrower and must be answered with data: HOW OFTEN
DOES THE CONTRADICTION ARISE, AND IS IT RESOLVABLE RATHER THAN MERELY DETECTABLE? If
abstention on cycle-inconsistency is rare, this bead is not worth building and should be
closed unbuilt.

THE METHOD — PERMUTATION SYNCHRONIZATION (Pachauri, Kondor, Singh, 2013): given noisy
pairwise matchings between N sets, recover globally consistent matchings by projecting onto
the space of matchings that DO compose transitively. The standard solution is a spectral
relaxation — stack the pairwise permutation matrices into a block matrix, take the leading
eigenvectors, and round to permutations. It is the natural generalization of the bipartite
assignment bead to N sources, and the epic already names it by name.

DETERMINISM CONSTRAINTS — same discipline as the constellation bead, and they are not
optional:
- Fixed-iteration power method, deterministic start vector, canonical sign convention,
  integer quantization at the artifact boundary per src/entity/score.rs.
- Rounding to permutations is an assignment problem per block — REUSE THE HUNGARIAN/JV
  IMPLEMENTATION from the optimal-assignment bead rather than writing a second one. That
  dependency is real and is why this bead is ordered after it.
- Repeated eigenvalues (symmetric source configurations) must abstain, not tie-break
  arbitrarily.

TRY THE CHEAP THING FIRST AND MEASURE IT: enumerate triangles among the pairwise matchings
and count how many fail to close. If the inconsistency rate is low, a deterministic
CYCLE-CONSISTENCY FILTER — drop or downweight correspondences that participate in a broken
triangle, and abstain where dropping is ambiguous — captures most of the value at a
fraction of the complexity and with no eigensolver at all. THAT MAY WELL BE THE RIGHT
ANSWER. Report the triangle-inconsistency rate before building anything spectral.

BYOP-SPECIFIC SUBTLETY — SOURCES ARE NOT EXCHANGEABLE, AND THE MATH ASSUMES THEY ARE.
The client's parcel layer is authoritative FOR PARCELS WITHIN ITS COVERAGE. Our footprint
sources are peers with no authority over parcels. The client's property book is the target
being keyed, not a peer at all. Standard permutation synchronization treats all sets
symmetrically. REQUIRED: a weighting or constraint scheme that respects the role semantics
already declared in EntitySourceRole {CanonicalReference, Reference, Target, Peer}. Applying
symmetric synchronization would let three mediocre footprint vendors outvote the client's
authoritative parcel layer — a wrong answer that would look mathematically principled, which
is the most dangerous kind.

ALSO: SOURCES COVER DIFFERENT SUBSETS. Permutation synchronization in its classic form
assumes matchings between sets of equal size with full correspondence. Here every source has
partial, unequal coverage — and under BYOP the client's layer may not cover the tile at all.
Partial permutations must be handled natively, and a source absent from a tile must reduce
the problem rather than corrupt it.

EXIT CRITERIA:
- Triangle-inconsistency rate measured on real multi-source tiles BEFORE any spectral work
- Deterministic cycle-consistency filter implemented and measured first
- If spectral is justified: fixed-iteration, deterministic, integer-quantized, reusing the
  Hungarian implementation for rounding
- Role-aware weighting so peers cannot outvote a declared authority
- Partial coverage and absent sources handled natively
- Existing AnchorConflict abstention preserved as the fallback, never replaced
- Residual re-measured or reverted
close_reason: SUPERSEDED — ambition lane retired by measurement. Appendix L (E1-E3, 2026-08-16): point re-ranking is not the dominant failure mode (0/7 tile-addressable wins; 72/79 labeled failures unreachable/representation cases), so the residual harness gate this lane waited on resolved AGAINST it. PLAN_CANON_GEO.md section 11: assignment and clustering become named global constraints with exact propagators; bd-2kjx.3's factorized exact residual solver (src/geo/composition.rs) now does exact composition without search. Any revival must come from a measured E4/E5 residual that names this technique, not from this bead.

comments.author: Zac
comments.text:
REFINEMENT 2026-08-14 — DETERMINISM TESTS WERE UNDER-SPECIFIED. Adding them explicitly,
because this bead is the highest determinism risk of the three spectral/iterative methods.

REQUIRED TESTS:
1. CROSS-PLATFORM BYTE PARITY. The same tile produces byte-identical synchronized matchings
   on the CI matrix (linux-x86_64 and macos-aarch64). Not "equivalent" — identical. If the
   spectral path cannot achieve this, the cycle-consistency filter ships and the spectral
   path does not.
2. SOURCE-ORDER INVARIANCE. Permuting the order in which sources are supplied must not
   change the result. This is the single most likely determinism bug in a multi-source
   method and it will not surface in normal use, because sources are usually supplied in
   the same order. Test it deliberately with a shuffled-order fixture.
3. DEGENERATE SYMMETRY ABSTAINS. A configuration with repeated eigenvalues (identical
   sources, or a symmetric arrangement) must abstain rather than tie-break arbitrarily.
   Fixture: three sources carrying identical geometry.
4. ROLE WEIGHTING IS EFFECTIVE. Construct a case where three peer footprint sources agree
   on a wrong correspondence and the declared-authority parcel layer disagrees. Assert the
   authority is NOT outvoted. This is the specific failure mode noted in the bead body and
   it must have a test, because a wrong answer here looks mathematically principled.
5. PARTIAL COVERAGE AND ABSENT SOURCES. A source absent from a tile must reduce the problem
   cleanly. Assert results with source S absent equal results computed without S at all.
6. FALLBACK PRESERVED. Assert that when synchronization abstains, the existing
   EntityMultisourceAbstentionReason::AnchorConflict path still fires and the run still
   produces a valid artifact. The new method must never be able to leave the run in a
   state the old path could not represent.

LOGGING: emit the triangle-inconsistency rate and the number of correspondences dropped by
the cycle-consistency filter on every run, so the justification for the spectral path stays
visible over time rather than being decided once.

comments.author: Zac
comments.text:
CLOSED AS SUPERSEDED 2026-08-14 — THE PREMISE WAS INVALIDATED BY THE PRE-RESOLVED-TILE
ARCHITECTURE. Not closed because the technique is wrong; closed because the problem it
solves may not exist at the layer this bead placed it.

THIS BEAD'S PREMISE: "a BYOP tile carries six to seven named sources in one run — Overture
GERS, FEMA USA Structures, Microsoft GlobalML, NYC/MapPLUTO, the client's licensed parcel
layer, and the client's property book. Pairwise matching between each pair produces C(n,2)
matchings that need not be mutually consistent."

WHAT CHANGED: operator 2026-08-14 established that the tile is PRE-STITCHED — cmdrvl-curves
is co-locating the big four by H3 cell now (bd-30ho, bd-1ssr, bd-3fyv), and the resolution
architecture assumes the tile arrives with its own sources already reconciled into building
clusters.

Under that architecture the CLIENT RUN has THREE participants, not seven: pre-resolved
building anchors, the client's parcel layer, and the client's property book. Triangle
consistency across three is trivial and needs no synchronization machinery.

WHERE THE TECHNIQUE MIGHT STILL LIVE: aligning FOUR VENDOR FOOTPRINT SOURCES at TILE BUILD
is a genuine multi-way consistency problem — but that is a different layer, a different
owner, and possibly a different repository. It is not this bead.

REOPEN CONDITION: bd-3foo decides where tile reconciliation runs. If it lands on Option B
(canon resolves everything, including our four sources, at tile consumption), THIS BEAD'S
ORIGINAL PREMISE HOLDS AND IT SHOULD BE REOPENED UNCHANGED. If it lands on A or C, this
work belongs at tile build and should be re-cut there with the correct source count and
owner.

Recorded rather than deleted so the reasoning survives. Nothing in the bead body was
wrong on its own terms — the cycle-consistency-filter-before-spectral discipline and the
determinism requirements are good and should be carried into whatever replaces it.

title: [CANON-V1/P06.6] Package evidence-preserving normalization without domain dictionaries
description:
## Background
Different domains need different punctuation, legal-form, capacity-phrase, transliteration, token-protection, and source-cleaning rules. Hardcoded dictionaries would make generic name handling brittle and biased.

## Technical Approach
Define a declarative normalization bundle composed from audited generic namekit primitives. Bundles create named token/string views, preserve raw values and step traces, declare protected features, and are content-addressed. Add a constrained extension mechanism only for primitives that can run deterministically and safely through the strategy runner.

## Success Criteria
- Unknown valid bundles run without domain-specific branches.
- Every transformation has a rule ID and trace back to the raw observation.
- Protected differences remain available to anti-merge evidence.
- Cluster and link modes consume the same named views.

## Test Plan
Golden-test two unrelated bundles, Unicode/punctuation variations, protected-token differences, empty/noisy values, bundle upgrades, and malicious/unsupported primitives. Add metamorphic tests for declared safe transformations.

## RESERVATIONS
- `src/extensions/normalization.rs`
- `schemas/canon.normalization.bundle.v1.schema.json`
- `tests/extensions_normalization.rs`

## Considerations
Known aliases belong in registries and operator dictionaries belong in external packages, never core source.
notes:
## Demanding-deployment requirement ownership
Owns R1 typed normalization views and the normalization side of R3. Preserve the raw source string alongside legal-name, dba or operating-name, and other derived views. Protected legal and organizational tokens remain inspectable; never blanket-strip SPV, Bidco, Holdco, numbered-company, or similar terms. Industry is contextual evidence, not a universal veto.

title: [CANON-V1/P05.7] Integrate temporal facts with projects, packages, review, and exports
description:
## Background
Temporal semantics will fragment if each provider, entity profile, project, and export invents its own dates and relationship sidecars.

## Technical Approach
Wire fact packages, scope vocabularies, trust policies, as-of compilation nodes, temporal review decisions, snapshot proofs, relation projections, and temporal diffs into the project manifest/lock/DAG and registry package/export contracts. Require all time-bearing inputs to use the shared interval model and pin timezone/calendar assumptions.

## Success Criteria
- A project declares its as-of and known-as-of policy once and every stage records it.
- Provider facts and reviewed facts merge through the same immutable contract.
- dbt/search/Parquet/RDF projections identify their compiled snapshot and preserve relationship validity where supported.
- A timeless project remains a valid explicit mode rather than an accidental missing date.

## Test Plan
Run multi-provider projects with late facts, reviewed corrections, temporal compile, promotion, and all exports; validate cross-artifact hashes and time metadata. Test incompatible calendars/timezones and stale locks.

## RESERVATIONS
- `src/project/manifest.rs`
- `src/project/plan.rs`
- `src/registry/export.rs`
- `tests/temporal_project.rs`

## Considerations
Prefer date/instant semantics that sources actually support. Do not fabricate precise timestamps from date-only disclosures.

title: Expose provider option schemas for agent-discoverable registry builds
description:
Context:
canon registry build has generic --provider-config KEY=VALUE plumbing, and OpenFIGI v0.6.2 now supports provider-specific mapping filters such as exchCode, micCode, currency, marketSecDes, securityType, securityType2, includeUnlistedEquities, coupon, maturity, etc. Today those keys are discoverable only through README/docs/source and a prose hint in operator.json. Agents cannot ask canon for a structured provider contract.

Problem:
Provider config is generic transport, but provider option semantics are provider-owned. That is the right design, but the allowed keys, types, enum values, secret redaction status, defaults, mutual exclusions, and examples need to be machine-discoverable. Without a structured provider schema, skills and downstream agents must hard-code or scrape docs, which is brittle and can silently drift from implementation.

Implementation goal:
Add a provider catalog/schema contract for registry build providers. The contract should let agents discover which providers exist and which --provider-config keys are valid for each provider without reading prose or source.

Suggested CLI/API shape:
- canon registry providers --emit json|summary
- canon registry provider-schema <PROVIDER> --emit json|summary
- Include the same structured provider metadata in canon --describe/operator.json, either under registry build or a top-level providers section.

OpenFIGI schema should include at least:
- provider id/name/description
- seed column support: cusip, isin, sedol
- id_type enum: ID_CUSIP, ID_ISIN, ID_SEDOL, with inference rules from seed-column
- base_url: URL/string, non-secret, local twin/testing use
- api_key: string, secret, env fallback OPENFIGI_API_KEY
- string filters: exchCode, micCode, currency, marketSecDes, securityType, securityType2, optionType
- bool filters: includeUnlistedEquities
- numeric interval filters: strike, contractSize, coupon
- date interval filters: expiration, maturity
- mutual exclusion: exchCode and micCode
- accepted interval encoding: JSON array of exactly two values, null allowed for open bound, at least one bound required
- examples for US equity disambiguation and bond/note cohorts

Design constraints:
- Keep CLI/provider boundary clean: generic registry build plumbing transports provider_options; each provider owns its option schema and validation.
- Do not make OpenFIGI-specific flags on canon registry build.
- Provider schemas must be deterministic, JSON-serializable, and suitable for skills/agents to consume directly.
- Secret fields must be marked so agents know not to echo values and _build.json redaction remains aligned.
- Unknown provider options can keep current runtime behavior unless this bead explicitly decides to tighten validation; if tightened, document the migration and add tests.

Acceptance criteria:
1. canon registry providers --emit json lists implemented providers, including openfigi and mock if appropriate, with source ids and short descriptions.
2. canon registry provider-schema openfigi --emit json emits a stable schema containing option keys, types, required/optional status, enum values, examples, secret flags, defaults/env fallbacks, and mutual exclusions.
3. canon --describe/operator.json exposes the provider catalog or links each registry-build provider to its schema so agent discovery works from the compiled operator contract.
4. Tests prove OpenFIGI schema contents match the implementation constants/validation, including exchCode/micCode mutual exclusion and interval filter typing.
5. README.md and docs/PLAN_CANON.md document the discovery commands and state that provider-specific config semantics are discoverable through canon, not only prose.
6. The existing OpenFIGI registry build tests continue to pass, and the provider schema tests do not contact api.openfigi.com.

Downstream value:
The xew-identity-fragility skill and future agent workflows can dynamically discover that OpenFIGI supports exchCode=US and other filters, split corpus builds into provider-filter cohorts, and avoid hard-coded provider option lists.
close_reason: Implemented in b52ac37: canon registry providers + provider-schema, operator.json providers catalog (+--describe), OpenFIGI schema sourced from resolver constants with secret flag, unknown-provider refusal with next_command, README+PLAN_CANON docs, drift+contract tests (no network). All 6 acceptance criteria met.

title: [ENT-P02.12] Adopt audited native similarity strategy and parity benchmarks
description:
ENT packet/reference: ENT-P02 child bead under parent bd-3k3. Labels: entity-workbench, child, ent-p02, namekit, similarity, rapidfuzz, licensing.

Purpose/background:
String metrics are useful support evidence, but implementation choice matters for determinism, speed, license, and API fit. RapidFuzz Rust is a strong candidate because it is native Rust, exposes Levenshtein/Jaro-Winkler style metrics, supports byte fast paths, score_cutoff, score_hint, and batch comparators, and is MIT/Apache licensed.

Exact scope:
Evaluate whether to adopt a pinned Rust crate (`rapidfuzz`, `strsim`, or another minimal crate) or implement internal metrics. The decision must include license compatibility, transitive dependency size, determinism, no unsafe policy, ASCII byte path behavior, Unicode char path behavior, cutoff/hint semantics, batch comparator reuse, and benchmark/parity expectations.

Suggested RESERVATIONS:
Cargo.toml; Cargo.lock; src/namekit/similarity.rs; benches/namekit_similarity.rs; tests/namekit/similarity.rs; docs/namekit/similarity-decision.md if a decision note is created.

Acceptance criteria:
- Dependency decision is recorded before code imports a metric crate.
- If adopting RapidFuzz Rust, score_cutoff and score_hint are tested for short-circuit/correctness and cannot change match semantics.
- ASCII byte path is used only when normalization proves ASCII-safe; Unicode path remains correct for non-ASCII fixtures.
- Metric outputs are normalized to stable canon score units with documented rounding.
- Metrics only produce support evidence; they cannot bypass cannot-link or solver constraints.

Verification commands:
cargo test namekit_similarity -- --nocapture; cargo test rapidfuzz_cutoff_hint_parity -- --nocapture; cargo test metric_ascii_unicode_parity -- --nocapture; cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings

acceptance_criteria: A dependency decision is recorded before Cargo.toml changes; accepted metrics have parity fixtures for ASCII, Unicode, empty, long, cutoff, score_hint, and batch reuse behavior; metric outputs are normalized into deterministic integer score units; any unsafe/native/transitive-risk concern is escalated before import.

Prefer a pinned native Rust metric crate only after license, unsafe-code, dependency-size, byte/Unicode, cutoff/hint, and determinism audits pass. title: [ENT-P02.21] Lock high-recall namekit source-parity implementation decisions
description:
Purpose/background:
The adversarial pass found that namekit is the highest-leverage place to accidentally underbuild the system. A minimal fuzzy matcher would be easier but would produce worse entity-resolution results. This bead locks the quality-oriented implementation decisions before downstream tokenization, sparse indexing, similarity, evidence, and benchmark beads start.

Default decisions:
- Use recall-rich native Rust primitives: word tokens, char n-grams, sparse TF-IDF, rare-token weighting, deterministic top-k, protected-token/cannot-link lanes, and source-parity fixture coverage.
- Dense vectors are forbidden for large corpora. Use integer dictionaries, sorted posting lists, CSR-like offset arrays where useful, and posting-list derived top-k retrieval.
- Sorted-neighborhood is supplemental recall machinery only when deterministic key/window/cap diagnostics are specified; it is not authoritative merge evidence.
- Prefer a pinned native Rust metric crate only after license, unsafe-code, dependency-size, byte/Unicode behavior, cutoff/hint, and parity audits pass. If audit fails, implement required metrics internally rather than weakening parity.
- Scores crossing module/artifact boundaries are deterministic integer score units. No float debug output belongs in artifacts.

title: [ENT-P02.7] Build namekit source-library research dossier and port map
description:
