MEASURED GEOCODE HISTORY, for anyone sizing this work (2026-08-14, literal query):
WRGL_EDGAR_CMBS_GEOCODES__STRUCTURED -- 68,603 rows, 54,690 distinct PROPERTY_ADDRESS,
4,149 addresses appearing under more than one ASOF because the ETL appends rather than
upserts. Dominated by the 2025-01 initial load (45,114 rows) and an unexplained 2026-08
batch (14,714 rows / 14,242 distinct).

PROCESS NOTE: this is the fourth claim this session that came from prose rather than a
measured value, and the third that was wrong. The 51% figure was in a document I trusted;
the 97.36% figure was in a bead comment recording an actual query. WHEN TWO NUMBERS
DISAGREE, PREFER THE ONE WITH A RECORDED METHOD AND A DENOMINATOR DEFINITION.

comments.author: Zac
comments.text:
THE KILL-CRITERION COMPARATOR, MEASURED 2026-08-15. This bead's central deliverable. From
returned structured results, not prose.

== NAIVE ADDRESS-STRING BASELINE ==

Method: deduplicate to distinct (PROPERTY_ADDRESS, COUNTY_FIPS) across the five boroughs.
Map COUNTY_FIPS to MapPLUTO BOROUGH (36005=BX, 36047=BK, 36061=MN, 36081=QN, 36085=SI).
Normalize BOTH sides identically and deliberately stupidly — uppercase, strip all
non-alphanumerics, collapse whitespace. Join on exact normalized equality, scoped by
borough. Borough scoping is required: NYC reuses street names across boroughs, so an
unscoped join would manufacture matches.

  distinct CMBS addresses in scope        5,269
  matched at least one MapPLUTO lot       1,522   =  28.9%
  matched exactly one                     1,522
  matched more than one                       0
  max lots per address                        1

**NAIVE ADDRESS-STRING MATCHING ACHIEVES 28.9% COVERAGE ON THE FIVE-BOROUGH CMBS BOOK.**

The operator predicted 30-40% before any measurement. The measured answer is 28.9%.

== READING IT HONESTLY ==

1. THIS IS COVERAGE, NOT PRECISION. We do not yet know how many of the 1,522 are correct.
   But every match is an exact normalized string equality within the correct borough against
   a lot's own recorded address, so precision on the matched subset should be high. That is
   the characteristic profile of address matching: PRECISE WHERE IT FIRES, AND IT RARELY
   FIRES.

2. ZERO AMBIGUITY, WHICH IS ITSELF INFORMATIVE. No address matched more than one lot. That
   is a consequence of MapPLUTO storing exactly ONE address per lot — exact equality against
   a single stored string either hits or misses, it cannot be ambiguous. So the baseline has
   no ambiguity to resolve and no abstention to make; it simply answers 28.9% of the time
   and is silent otherwise.

3. THE 71.1% THAT DO NOT MATCH ARE THE ENTIRE PRODUCT. That population is where every
   measured failure lives — multi-address strings, Queens grid hyphenates, ranges, corner
   a/k/a alternates, and the large and corner lots whose true address is not the one
   MapPLUTO stored.

== THE TWO BASELINES SIDE BY SIDE ==

  naive address-string    28.9% coverage, unique when it fires, precision unmeasured
  geometry-only PIP       ~95% coverage (directional, needs fan-out correction on distinct
                          points), precision unmeasured, 157 five-borough points land in
                          more than one lot

These are two points on a coverage/precision plane, not two numbers to beat separately. Per
the risk-coverage framing, THE CASCADE MUST PASS ABOVE BOTH POINTS: higher precision than
geometry-alone at geometry's coverage, and materially more coverage than 28.9% at
address-grade precision. A cascade that merely raises coverage above 28.9% has beaten
nothing, because point-in-polygon already does that.

== WHAT REMAINS ON THIS BEAD ==
- Precision for both baselines, which requires the address-independent ground truth in
  bd-179b — scoring against PLUTO alone is circular because PLUTO's truth is address-to-BBL
  and the CMBS address is the thing being tested
- The geometry-only rate re-derived fan-out-aware on the 4,076 distinct points rather than
  on rows
- Tier-by-tier breakdown, with nearest_rooftop_match as its own slice
- The corrected chimera rate after two-sided normalization
- The property-cardinality distribution

title: [CANON-V1/P12.9] Extract current domain special cases through extension packages with parity
description:
## Background
Canon core currently contains Reg AB, CMBS, sec10d, BDC, tenant, and structured-finance-aware profiles, fixtures, commands, defaults, or apply assumptions. They helped bootstrap the architecture, but they make the open-source engine appear coupled to one use case and make downstream ownership ambiguous. Extraction is safe only after non-exact quality is measured and parity is explicit.

## Technical Approach
Produce a machine-readable inventory of every domain-bearing symbol, literal, profile, fixture, schema field, documentation promise, command branch, default path, and test. Classify each as generic engine capability, neutral example, external extension package, downstream adapter, historical plan, or removable duplicate. Define a versioned extension-package contract for normalization components, candidate operators, evidence extractors, relationship vocabularies, profile policy, registry namespace rules, corpus manifests, projection mappings, and quality gates. Move behavior through that contract in dependency order while preserving public artifact semantics and benchmark results. Use at least two unrelated external packages to prove that the seam is real. Do not delete files or old behavior without the separate explicit authorization required by repository policy.

## Success Criteria
- A source scan has zero unexplained CMBS, Reg AB, sec10d, BDC, or structured-finance literals in generic runtime paths and defaults.
- Every inventoried special case has one named generic destination and parity evidence.
- The engine can load unknown opaque package and profile identifiers without recompilation.
- Current Reg AB and CMBS fixtures retain exact output parity and non-exact quality within the P12 gates through external packages.
- Two neutral domains exercise the same package contract without domain branches in core.
- Canon distributions do not point by default into a sibling repository or private corpus.
- Package manifests and digests are recorded in every project artifact and evaluation report.

## Test Plan
Snapshot the inventory before extraction; run source-firewall tests and denylisted literal scans; execute all current domain fixtures through old and packaged paths; compare canonical IDs, decisions, evidence, refusals, diagnostics, performance, and registry output. Test missing, unknown, tampered, stale, and incompatible packages. Run neutral-package conformance and public-binary subprocess tests.

## RESERVATIONS
- src/cli.rs
- src/entity/profile.rs
- src/entity/apply.rs
- src/namekit/tenant.rs
- tests/entity_profile_firewall_contract.rs
- tests/entity_fixture_manifest.rs
- docs/IDENTITY_ARCHITECTURE.md
- docs/ENTITY_CONTRACT.md

## Considerations
This is extraction, not deletion-by-cleanup. Domain expertise remains valuable; ownership moves to packages maintained by the consuming domain. Generic legal-name normalization may remain core only when justified across domains and provenance-backed.
notes:
## Cross-repository acceptance
sec10d bd-26s implements the first domain-owned Reg AB firm identity extension package. Extraction parity is incomplete until that package loads through the generic contract, reproduces the existing exact surface and projection behavior, and passes the empirical non-exact quality gates without Reg AB branches in Canon core.

title: [BDC/R6] Reconcile private decisions at canonical record grain
description: The private evaluator looks up target/reference material through lane + canonical RecordLinkInput record_id, then discards that record key and reconciles only by normalized issuer-surface material. This collapses distinct tranche/assignment rows for the same issuer and raises private_identity_conflict across valid row-level match/ambiguity outcomes. title: [CANON-V1/P09.3] Add an optional Splink candidate-and-evidence adapter
description:
## Background
Splink may provide scalable probabilistic linkage and useful comparison diagnostics for some operators. Its probabilities and learned parameters must remain suggestions within Canon's evidence/review boundary.

## Technical Approach
Implement a subprocess/file adapter that exports pinned observations and comparison configuration, invokes a pinned Splink environment through the bounded runner, and imports candidate pairs plus typed comparison/evidence records. Record model/training/config/software digests and map probabilities to context/support evidence under explicit policy; never auto-promote based solely on an adapter score.

## Success Criteria
- Splink candidates and comparisons are reproducible when the external environment declares deterministic behavior.
- Every score traces to model, parameters, input, and software version.
- Adapter failures or absence do not affect native workflows or registry state.
- Canon review/explain shows Splink evidence distinctly from native and trusted-anchor evidence.

## Test Plan
Against a pinned local environment or frozen adapter output, test candidate parity, model/config changes, shuffled inputs, missing values, large outputs, timeout/resource failure, malformed probabilities, and registry no-mutation.

## RESERVATIONS
- `src/adapters/splink.rs`
- `tests/splink_adapter_e2e.rs`
- `docs/ADAPTERS.md`

## Considerations
Do not expose Python objects or Splink schemas as Canon's public contract; the adapter translates at the boundary.
close_reason: Retired: Splink wraps Fellegi-Sunter + EM (textbook). Ported native as bd-1rlk. Scale backend is its only unique asset, irrelevant at our scale. Reopen only if an operator brings a trained model via generic seam bd-3ofg. See docs/DECISION_PORT_TECHNIQUES_OVER_ADAPTERS.md.

title: [CANON-V1/P12.2] Build a sealed, leakage-resistant corpus and split conformance harness
description:
## Background
Entity-resolution metrics are meaningless when the same aliases, entities, documents, or derived labels leak across tuning and holdout partitions. Canon must standardize evaluation mechanics while leaving substantive corpora under domain ownership.

## Technical Approach
Extend the generic corpus contract with entity-grouped and time-aware splits, source-family grouping, immutable train/tune/holdout manifests, label confidence and adjudicator provenance, license/redaction metadata, and cryptographic commitments to hidden labels. Validate that canonical entities, alias surfaces, derived mutations, document families, and duplicated observations cannot cross forbidden split boundaries. title: [CANON-V1/P06.17] Prove an out-of-tree demanding deployment without Canon awareness
description:
## Background
The extension boundary is credible only if an operator can solve a complex real domain while Canon remains unaware of that domain. The initiating operator intends a large counterparty deployment, but its proprietary or industry-specific assets must stay outside the open-source product.

## Technical Approach
Create a black-box conformance journey whose external workspace supplies its ontology, roles, identifier namespaces, source mappings/providers, profiles, evidence policy, hard-negative corpus, review policy, temporal facts, registry recipe, and export projections. Canon receives only generic packages through public CLI/SDK contracts. Public CI uses an invented neutral twin; an optional local acceptance target can point at the operator's private deployment.

## Success Criteria
- No Canon source, built-in schema enum, default, fixture, or required documentation names the operator's industry.
- The external deployment can cluster entities, link datasets, preserve related/distinct and assignments, review/promote facts, compile exact snapshots, and export dbt/search outputs.
- Swapping to the neutral twin requires no engine changes.
- A source scan and command trace prove there are no domain conditionals or hidden plugin privileges.

## Test Plan
Run the public neutral journey in CI and the external local journey when assets are supplied. Exercise offline, read-only, interrupt/resume, shuffled inputs, hard negatives, package tampering, and query final outputs. Log only non-sensitive commands, digests, metrics, and filesystem deltas.

## RESERVATIONS
- `tests/extensions_end_to_end.rs`
- `tests/fixtures/extensions/neutral-domain`
- `docs/EXTENSIONS.md`

## Considerations
The application may be structured finance, healthcare, commerce, or anything else. Canon's acceptance claim is extension completeness, not built-in expertise.
notes:
## Demanding-deployment acceptance
Exercise all R1-R5 twice: license-safe invented neutral analogues in public CI and real BDC issuer cases in a private local target. The proof must include a core source scan for BDC/finance vocabulary and must succeed without a fork, domain conditional, private-data dependency, optional matcher, or transport-specific review workflow.

title: [CANON-V1/P04.9] Measure coverage gain, review yield, drift, and accretion velocity
description:
## Background
The flywheel must prove that each review and provider investment makes Canon more useful. Raw registry size can grow while true coverage or decision quality gets worse.

## Technical Approach
Define versioned metrics across frozen corpora and project receipts: weighted exact coverage, unique unresolved groups, ambiguity/contradiction rate, reviewed-to-promoted yield, median age, repeat recurrence after promotion, hard-negative regressions, cross-project reuse, and time/cost bands. Attribute deltas to registry and strategy versions without collecting raw identities by default.

## Success Criteria
- Metrics compare like-for-like corpora and visibly flag corpus or policy changes.
- Coverage gains are separated into new aliases, new entities, remaps, provider additions, and temporal effects.
- A promotion that improves recall but harms hard negatives or creates repeat unresolved events is visible.
- Reports are deterministic, privacy-aware, and queryable as JSON plus concise summary.

## Test Plan
Use synthetic histories containing genuine improvement, registry bloat, regression, corpus drift, and review backlog. Verify attribution math, missing intervals, redaction, and deterministic reports.

## RESERVATIONS
- `src/inbox/metrics.rs`
- `schemas/canon.accretion.metrics.v1.schema.json`
- `tests/inbox_metrics.rs`

## Considerations
Metrics guide investment; they must not become thresholds that pressure reviewers to accept uncertain matches.

title: [CANON-V1/P04.8] Project ranked inbox groups into the shared offline review artifact
description:
## Background
High-impact unresolved groups need usage context and prioritization before they enter review, but Canon should not build a second renderer or decision-import format for the inbox.

## Technical Approach
Compile selected inbox groups, ranking contributions, recurrence/source context, and registry-impact summaries into the canonical native review artifact owned by bd-14m6. Reuse its JSON/CSV decision schema, static offline HTML projection, hash bindings, import validator, and typed patches. This bead owns only inbox selection/context projection and the deterministic handoff back to inbox state after review.

## Success Criteria
- Inbox review uses exactly the same safe actions, decision IDs, import receipts, and renderer as entity cluster/link review.
- The generated pack includes priority, recurrence, source, privacy, and impact context without changing patch semantics.
- Stale inbox, ranking-policy, impact, run, or registry hashes refuse import atomically.
- Reviewed groups transition deterministically to planned, resolved, related/distinct, deferred, or rejected inbox states.

## Test Plan
Project ranked groups through the shared renderer under a network-disabled browser, validate accessibility and redaction, import JSON/CSV decisions through the authoritative validator, tamper each inbox-specific binding, replay imports, and prove no duplicate renderer/template or patch implementation exists.

## RESERVATIONS
- `src/inbox/review.rs`
- `src/entity/review_export.rs`
- `tests/inbox_review.rs`

## Considerations
bd-14m6 owns canonical review data/render/import; bd-11uf owns extension presentation policy; this bead only enriches that shared artifact with inbox context.

title: [SPLINK-STEAL/S7] review packets: additive per-pair score decomposition (evidence waterfall)
description:
## Problem this solves
Reviewers deciding escrow items need to see WHY a pair scored 31 against a backbone threshold of 32 — which operators contributed what — in one glance. canon entity explain has the data, but review artifacts do not present it additively, so reviewers context-switch to explain output per item. Fast per-item comprehension is what makes the residual (post-S1/S2) review queue cheap. The review-substrate decision doc (docs/DECISION_REVIEW_VIA_EMAIL_CROWDSOURCING.md) already names "self-contained evidence-waterfall packets" as core substrate — this bead implements that presentation.

## Build
Extend review export (queue + native-review JSON/CSV/HTML) with a per-item ordered contribution breakdown:
- Each evidence hit as (lane, operator, view/field, integer score units, running cumulative total).
- Threshold lines (backbone_score_min, attach_score_min, abstain_margin) rendered against the cumulative so the shortfall or surplus is visible at a glance.
- Static offline HTML renders it as a simple bar/waterfall table using the existing static projection (no new JS deps, no new renderer).
- Redaction follows the existing review-artifact contract; the decomposition must not leak values the artifact would otherwise redact.

## Splink reference (clone at /Users/zac/Source/opensource/splink)
- splink/internals/waterfall_chart.py and linker_components/visualisations.py waterfall_chart — additive log2 decomposition (prior + per-comparison + TF terms) with a remove_sensitive_data variant. Port the presentation concept onto canon integer score units.

## How to test
- Golden snapshot test of a review packet with decomposition.
- Integer invariant: sum of listed contributions equals the recorded pair score exactly, for every item in the fixture corpus (property test).
- Redacted variant contains no raw values (scan test).
- HTML projection renders with a network-disabled browser.
- Byte-stable ordering: (lane, operator, field) sort is deterministic under input shuffle.

## Doctrine constraints
Presentation of existing artifact data only — no new scoring, no semantics change, no new renderer or import format (bd-14m6 substrate rules apply).

## RESERVATIONS
- src/entity/review_export.rs (shared with S2 — serialize if both in flight)
- tests/entity_review_waterfall.rs

title: [CANON-V1/P00.1] Freeze executable contract inventory and incompatibility matrix
description:
## Background
Canon currently has overlapping legacy and artifact-backed entity types, hand-maintained machine metadata, stale org wording, and runbook commands that are not all accepted by Clap. Before changing behavior, freeze the actual state and name every incompatibility so the cutover cannot silently drop a capability.

## Technical Approach
- Enumerate every top-level and entity command, argument, output version, exit code, stdout/stderr route, side effect, and next-command contract from Clap and implementation dispatch.
- Map legacy SolveRunArtifact fields against the artifact-backed EntityRunArtifact and every downstream consumer.
- Inventory README, PLAN, operator.json, doctor, schema snapshots, fixtures, and downstream sec10d/edgar-ddp command references.
- Classify each surface as preserve, replace directly, migrate with new artifact version, or remove after explicit user permission.

## Success Criteria
- A machine-readable matrix covers every shipped command and artifact family.
- Every advertised-but-missing command and every stale org reference is named.
- The matrix identifies the exact cutover and test owner for each incompatibility.
- No production behavior changes in this bead.

## Test Plan
- Add a contract-inventory test that fails when a new command or artifact version lacks a matrix row.
- Assert all current operator.json subcommands and Clap variants are represented.
- Log the inventory counts and unresolved decisions under --nocapture.

## RESERVATIONS
- `tests/canon_v1_contract_inventory.rs`
- `tests/fixtures/canon_v1/contract_inventory.json`

## Considerations
- Do not normalize contradictions away; the purpose is to expose them.
- The matrix becomes temporary migration evidence, not a second permanent source of truth.
- No file deletion is authorized by this bead.

title: [CANON-V1/P06.9] Build a generic frozen-source provider materializer SDK
description:
## Background
Operators need to turn authoritative or vendor source files into identity facts, but Canon must not contain clients or parsers for specific public agencies and products.

## Technical Approach
Define a provider-materializer contract and SDK separating optional acquisition from deterministic offline build. Inputs are explicit frozen files plus source manifest; outputs are typed facts, quarantined rows, diagnostics, provenance locators, and a content-addressed package. Expose streaming parsers, schema mapping, checkpointing, limits, licenses, and semantic diff hooks.

## Success Criteria
- A third party can implement a provider outside the Canon crate and pass conformance tests.
- Offline build never performs network access or reads undeclared files.
- Every emitted fact traces to source digest and record locator.
- Parser changes and source revisions produce deterministic semantic diffs.

## Test Plan
Implement only a neutral fixture provider; test malformed records, schema drift, duplicate facts, quarantine, interruption/resume, resource limits, offline enforcement, package determinism, and external plugin conformance.

## RESERVATIONS
- `src/provider_sdk.rs`
- `schemas/canon.provider.manifest.v1.schema.json`
- `tests/provider_sdk_conformance.rs`

## Considerations
Real regulator, corporate-registry, vendor, or internal-system providers remain separate packages owned by their users.

title: canon geo: spatial evidence operators (within, intersects, distance_lt, area_ratio, iou_gt)
description:
Spatial predicates as STRATEGY OPERATORS in the existing YAML surface -- the
same shape as exact / tolerance_pct / range / prefix today. Core stays
domain-free; the spatial vocabulary lives in the strategy.

OPERATORS:
  within            point in polygon
  intersects        polygon overlap, non-empty
  distance_lt       centroid or edge distance under a bound
  area_ratio        footprint area ratio within a band (rejects wrong-size match)
  iou_gt            intersection-over-union above a threshold
  constellation_consistent   deferred to its own bead; harder and not v1

Each operator emits EVIDENCE with a score and a named reason, so explain.rs can
answer 'why did X match Y' by pointing at operator outputs. Per canon's final
rule: if you cannot explain the match by pointing at assertion scores, it does
not ship.

ALSO: within-source mutual exclusion and distance-based hard negatives should be
expressed through anti_merge rather than a bespoke mechanism.

Depends on: geometry decision, skeleton
Parent: bd-2kjx

comments.author: zac
comments.text:
NOTE 2026-08-14 from the measured NYC baseline (see bd-bmee): a point can legitimately fall inside MORE THAN ONE lot polygon — condo unit BBL overlapping the condo parent lot — so the 'within' operator must not assume a single containing polygon.

Two consequences for this bead:
1. 'within' returns a SET, not a boolean-plus-one-winner. Emitting one match silently discards a real ambiguity.
2. Within-source mutual exclusion is NOT universally true for NYC tax lots the way it is for building footprints. Two Overture buildings are not the same building, but a condo unit lot and its parent lot are legitimately overlapping records in the SAME source. Expressing lot overlap through anti_merge as a blanket rule would be wrong; the condo parent/unit relationship is a part_of relation (bd-3soj), not a distinctness violation.

The epic bd-2kjx lists WITHIN-SOURCE MUTUAL EXCLUSION as one of the five reasons geo is easier than person ER. That claim holds for building footprints and does NOT hold for NYC tax lots. Scope the assumption per source rather than globally.

comments.author: Zac
comments.text:
REALITY CHECK 2026-08-14 — THE "STRATEGY OPERATOR" PREMISE IS NOT SUPPORTED BY THE CODE.

This bead says: "Spatial predicates as STRATEGY OPERATORS in the existing YAML surface --
the same shape as exact / tolerance_pct / range / prefix today. Core stays domain-free;
the spatial vocabulary lives in the strategy."

Two problems, both verified.

1. THERE IS NO DECLARATIVE OPERATOR SURFACE. The ops named
   (exact/tolerance_pct/range/prefix) live in src/resolve/strategy.rs:8 as
   `const SUPPORTED_OPERATORS: &[&str]`, dispatched by a `match spec.op.as_str()` in
   src/resolve/assertions.rs:19-28 with `_ => Outcome::fail("unsupported_operator")`.
   That is a CLOSED VOCABULARY IN CORE RUST. "The vocabulary lives in the strategy" is
   false — the strategy only SELECTS from a list core defines. Every new operator is a
   core code change.

   The entity-side equivalent is the same shape: src/entity/profile.rs:855-886 defines
   SUPPORTED_SUPPORT_OPS (6 entries), SUPPORTED_CANNOT_LINK_OPS (10),
   SUPPORTED_RELATION_HINT_OPS (8). All closed. All textual. Not one takes a number.

2. THE SURFACE THIS BEAD POINTS AT IS THE ONE THE EPIC DISAVOWS. exact/tolerance_pct/
   range/prefix are in src/resolve/ — the two-tape CMBS tape matcher that bd-2kjx
   explicitly rejects as "the wrong substrate (see bd-3g5q, closed)". Do not build the
   spatial vocabulary there.

CORRECTED SHAPE: declare geo's operator vocabularies as THEIR OWN const arrays inside
src/geo/, parallel to entity's, sharing the artifact chain but not the vocabulary. Core
does change; that is unavoidable and is now the settled call (see bd-15ba). What stays
out of core is the DOMAIN CONVENTION layer — BBL semantics, condo parent/unit rules,
locale address conventions — which belongs in profiles and strategies.

OPERATOR SET — AMENDED FOR BYOP AND FOR THE MEASURED NYC FINDINGS:

  within          POINT-IN-POLYGON. Returns a SET, not a boolean-plus-winner (see the
                  2026-08-14 comment on this bead: a point can legitimately fall inside
                  a condo unit lot AND its parent lot). Emitting one match silently
                  discards a real ambiguity.
  intersects      polygon overlap, non-empty
  distance_lt     centroid or edge distance under a bound. NOTE: this is the operator
                  that carries the interpolated geocode tier — OC-0048 establishes that
                  range_interpolation and street_center points land in the right-of-way
                  where NO lot contains them. "Snap to nearest lot" is forbidden; this
                  operator GENERATES CANDIDATES which the address channel must then
                  corroborate or the cascade abstains.
  distance_gt     NEW — the spatial hard negative. Emits ScoreLane::AntiMerge with
                  hard_cannot_link=true. This is the "hard negatives exist" claim from
                  the epic, and it is NEW CODE: anti_merge.rs is two lexical helpers and
                  transfers only the lane, not the logic.
  area_ratio      footprint area ratio within a band (rejects wrong-size match)
  iou_gt          intersection-over-union above a threshold
  centroid_within NEW — cheap prefilter before exact PIP
  bbox_overlaps   NEW — the conservative filter stage; see bd-15ba on filtered
                  predicates. Must be provably conservative.

ATTRIBUTE OPERATORS THE CLIENT INPUT CONTRACT NOW REQUIRES (operator decision
2026-08-14: the six fields are geocode, address, geometry, building size, year built,
property type). These are NOT geometry but they are how wrong matches get REJECTED, and
canon has no numeric evidence operator at all today:

  size_ratio_within   building size agreement within a band. A 12,000 sf building is not
                      a 340,000 sf building even if the footprints overlap.
  year_built_within   year-built agreement within a tolerance. Cheap, strong negative
                      signal: a 1927 building and a 2019 building on the same footprint
                      means redevelopment, which is a TEMPORAL finding, not a match.
  category_compatible property type compatibility over a declared equivalence table
                      (office/mixed-use compatible; multifamily/industrial not).
                      Table lives in the profile, not core.

REQUIREMENT — EVERY OPERATOR EMITS STRUCTURED EVIDENCE, NOT PROSE. Verified problem:
existing helpers stuff their semantics into a format! string on EdgeEvidenceHit.explanation
(e.g. "relation hint relation=part_of left=... right=..."). A renderer or a downstream
consumer would have to PARSE PROSE. Geo operators must emit typed fields — measured
value, threshold, units, and the comparison outcome — alongside the human explanation.
bd-101v's card depends on this and cannot be built against explanation strings.

REQUIREMENT — GEOMETRY IS NOT A SUPPORTED VALUE TYPE YET. src/entity/record_link.rs:153
types features as Numeric|Date|Categorical. There is no geometry variant anywhere in the
evidence model. See the new geometry-typed-value bead; this bead is blocked on it.

ANTI-MERGE SCOPING — CORRECTED (reinforces the 2026-08-14 comment already on this bead):
within-source mutual exclusion is a PER-SOURCE DECLARED PROPERTY, not a global geo
invariant. It holds for building footprints. It does NOT hold for parcel/tax-lot sources
with condo aggregation. Under BYOP this becomes sharper still: WE DO NOT KNOW THE
CLIENT'S PARCEL LAYER SEMANTICS. The client must DECLARE whether their layer is
mutually exclusive; canon must refuse rather than assume. A wrong assumption here
suppresses true part_of relations (bd-3soj).

constellation_consistent is deferred to its own bead — THAT BEAD NOW EXISTS. It was
never created before this reality check.

title: [CANON-V1/P00.3] Cut the final entity CLI and dispatch scaffold against v1 artifacts
description:
## Background
Entity behavior must not depend on optional-flag accidents, and record linkage must not remain a sibling product. One CLI contract should select one artifact-backed engine and expose supported stages plus clear cluster/link entry points.

## Technical Approach
Define the final grammar under `canon entity`. Stage commands are `prepare`, `index build`, `block`, `evidence` (or the single contract-approved replacement for legacy `edge`), `solve`, `run`, `review`, `audit`, `promote`, `apply`, and `explain`. `canon entity link <REFERENCE> <TARGET>` is the ergonomic two-source linkage entry point and compiles into the same run/stage requests; project manifests may declare cluster, two-source link, or N-source link mode. Make profile/work-directory/project context explicit, centralize output/refusal routing, and pre-create narrow dispatch seams. Remove active legacy selection directly after parity; request deletion permission for obsolete files.

## Success Criteria
- The same invocation shape always selects the same engine.
- `entity link` retains cross-dataset functionality without a top-level `resolve` engine.
- Run/project mode and explicit stage execution share typed request boundaries.
- Help contains no org wording, ambiguous mode switch, or domain-specific command/default.
- Unknown/stale shapes produce actionable structured refusals.

## Test Plan
Parse and subprocess-smoke every command/mode and mutual exclusion; snapshot help; test intent/typo diagnostics; assert dispatch request types and stdout/stderr; and prove two-source shorthand compiles to the same plan/artifacts as an equivalent project manifest.

## RESERVATIONS
- `src/cli.rs`
- `src/lib.rs`
- `src/entity/mod.rs`
- `src/entity/runtime.rs`
- `tests/cli_smoke.rs`
- `tests/fixtures/canon_v1/help/entity_help.txt`
- `tests/fixtures/canon_v1/help/entity_link_help.txt`

## Considerations
This bead owns shared CLI files. P00.1 decides any edge-to-evidence naming from the executable inventory; there is one final public name, no compatibility alias. Preserve bare exact lookup plus registry and strategy command families.
close_reason: Completed final entity CLI/dispatch scaffold cutover with evidence/link/index/apply leaves, no edge alias, structured legacy run refusal, link dispatch plan tests, help goldens, focused tests, fmt, and clippy.

title: [CANON-V1/P07.R6d] Bind shared prepared surfaces to every record-link source lane
description: Public record_link_surface_bindings currently reduces each PreparedSurfaceRecord to one lexicographically first source_id. When the same normalized surface occurs in both record-link source lanes, provenance contains both source systems but only one lane receives a binding; the other side then refuses at block with missing_surface_binding. Emit deterministic RecordLinkSurfaceBindingInput entries per (surface_id, source_id), with source_row_ids restricted to provenance samples from that source. Preserve the source-row identity firewall: assignment IDs and record IDs remain non-authoritative. Add a neutral regression covering an exact shared surface across both sources plus repeated rows/assignments, prove both lanes bind, native link does not refuse, and output remains deterministic. No BDC/CMBS/domain-specific behavior.
notes: Private proof reproduced missing_surface_binding when one normalized surface spans both source lanes. First fix (per-source prepared-surface bindings) exposed the next required projection rule: dedicated record-link candidates may legitimately have identical left/right surface IDs at record grain, but generic block/edge artifacts must never receive self-pairs. Exact neutral regression currently fails with E_ENTITY_ARTIFACT_CONTRACT malformed_candidate_pair. Keep dedicated candidate/evidence/alignment artifacts intact; suppress only same-surface projection into generic block candidates and generic edge records, then prove native link and deterministic artifacts.
close_reason: Shared prepared surfaces bind deterministically per source lane with fail-closed missing/ambiguous handling and no generic self-pair projection; neutral public regression and full quality gates pass.

title: [CANON-V1/P01.7] Add registry package verify and package-aware lint
description:
## Background
Immutable packages need a single offline command that validates bytes, schemas, attachments, effective mappings, profile scope, and deployment projections before use or publication.

## Technical Approach
- Extend registry lint or add package verify with clear separation between source-registry findings and package-integrity failures.
- Recompute manifest digest and every descriptor hash; validate mapping precedence, entry count, canonical IDs/types, duplicate aliases, sidecar scopes, dependency pins, and signature references.
- Optionally verify declared dbt/search outputs against their hashes.
- Emit machine and human reports with exact recovery commands.

## Success Criteria
- Tampering is detected before lookup or export.
- Warnings versus errors are deterministic and policy-driven.
- Verification performs no network access and no mutation.
- Clean package reports contain enough provenance for release gates.

## Test Plan
- One mutation fixture per descriptor/metadata class.
- Mixed standard/entity/strategy attachment tests.
- No-write and no-network guards.
- Robot JSON and summary goldens.

## RESERVATIONS
- `src/registry_lint.rs`
- `src/registry/package.rs`
- `src/doctor.rs`
- `tests/registry_package_verify.rs`

## Considerations
- Signature cryptography lands in P08; this bead verifies structural references first.
- Do not conflate untrusted package integrity with semantic approval.
- Support large packages without loading unnecessary blobs.

title: [CANON-V1/P06.R1-R5] Freeze demanding-deployment requirements for the extension boundary
description:
## Background
The private BDC issuer-resolution deployment is a forcing function for Canon's domain-neutral P06 extension boundary. It contains difficult identity cases—legal and operating names, SPVs and holdcos, tranches, weak identifiers, relational context, and renames—without authorizing any structured-finance behavior in core.

The normative planning artifact is docs/BDC_ISSUER_EXTENSION_REQUIREMENTS.md. This bead freezes R1-R5 and maps each requirement to generic core contracts and acceptance evidence.

## Scope
- R1: preserve raw, legal-name, dba or operating-name, and other typed views from a source observation.
- R2: model issuer identity separately from facilities, tranches, holdings, and other assignments.
- R3: preserve distinguishing features and express authoritative or reviewed negative constraints without unsafe domain heuristics.
- R4: admit generic relational context such as repeated co-observation while preventing it from becoming identity authority.
- R5: represent temporal aliases, renames, source dates, and as-of resolution explicitly.
- Exercise invented neutral analogues in public CI and the real BDC deployment in private acceptance.
- Keep all BDC vocabulary, corpora, parsing, and policy outside Canon core.
- Exclude committing to Splink, Dedupe, OpenRefine, active learning, email review, or a native model port.

## Technical approach
Wire R1-R5 into the existing P06 contracts: typed normalization views; observations, assignments, and relationships; generic evidence operators and typed evidence IR; source-schema mapping; candidate-recall evaluation; temporal/as-of semantics; and the out-of-tree deployment proof. The demanding deployment owns its source parsing, labels, thresholds, and policy.

Safety corrections are mandatory. Never blanket-strip SPV, Bidco, Holdco, numbered-company, or similar legal terms. Industry classification is contextual negative evidence, not a universal hard cannot-link. Cross-BDC co-holding is an ablation-gated context feature, never promotion authority. Hard vetoes require authoritative identifiers, explicit constraints, or reviewed adjudication.

## Acceptance Criteria
- R1-R5 each map to one or more owned implementation beads and named acceptance evidence.
- Public fixtures exercise neutral analogues without finance vocabulary in core.
- Private acceptance can exercise real BDC cases without creating a Canon dependency on private data.
- No optional matcher or review transport blocks the P00-P12 core release path.
- The requirements document and active bead notes agree on the safety boundaries.

## Test plan
- Inspect the dependency graph to ensure all affected P06 tasks and bd-doe2 consumed the frozen requirements.
- Run the P06 domain-neutrality/source scan when implemented.
- Run typed-view, assignment-separation, protected-feature, relational-ablation, candidate-recall, and temporal-alias acceptance cases.
- Compare public neutral and private BDC results at the generic contract boundary.
- Verify P09 optional decisions remain downstream of bd-2i2q.

## File and reservation boundaries
This planning bead changes only the requirements document and bead metadata. Future implementation follows the exact-file reservation rules of its owning beads. Domain packs and private corpora remain out of tree or in explicitly scoped package fixtures.

## Considerations
The goal is not to make Canon know BDCs. The goal is to ensure a demanding BDC package can be built on Canon without forks, hidden authority, or loss of evidence.
close_reason: Requirements frozen in docs/BDC_ISSUER_EXTENSION_REQUIREMENTS.md; R1-R5 are wired into generic P06 owners and bd-doe2 acceptance, unsafe veto/normalization assumptions are corrected, and optional matcher or review choices are explicitly out of scope.

title: [CANON-V1/P05.4] Keep identity, hierarchy, and role relationships semantically distinct
description:
## Background
Parents, children, brands, divisions, branches, products, successors, and time-bounded assignees are related but not necessarily the same identity. Treating every relation as `same_as` is a general source of registry corruption.

## Technical Approach
Define a generic directed relationship fact with subject/object types, valid interval, provenance, policy reference, cardinality constraints, and identity implication set to none unless a separate equality fact exists. Support namespaced extension vocabularies without embedding their substantive rules.

## Success Criteria
- Relationship edges never become aliases solely because they connect records.
- Temporal hierarchy/role queries return provenance and intervals.
- Cardinality/cycle constraints are policy-driven and reviewable.
- Review distinguishes same, distinct, related, and uncertain.

## Test Plan

title: canon geo: the client-facing output surface — CSV column, typed answer sidecar, derived crosswalk view
description:
THE THING THE CLIENT ACTUALLY CONSUMES. Everything else in this epic produces evidence;
this bead produces the deliverable.

OC-0048 specifies the output shape and it is already half-built: "`canon --emit csv`
appends a `location__canon` column to the operator's own file — the identifier-provider
experience, ALREADY IMPLEMENTED. Behind each row, a typed answer rather than a boolean."

  relation:        same_parcel
  apn / bbl:       1-00995-0001
  buildings:       [BIN_a, BIN_b]
  rca_resolves_to: BIN_a
  nx_range_spans:  [BIN_a, BIN_b]
  score_units:     8700 / 10000
  evidence:        [pip_parcel, address_range_match, area_ratio]

THE TENSION THIS BEAD MUST RESOLVE: canon's registry is FLAT AND EXACT — one alias, one
canonical id, one row. The answer above is NOT flat. It carries a typed relation, a set of
buildings, a score, and an evidence list. OC-0048 flags this openly for the property case
("A property spanning three parcels cannot be one registry row without either fan-out or
collapse — the same pathology this document rejects when it rejects the wide crosswalk")
and bd-3soj leaves it open at the API boundary. The property bead decides whether the
relation graph is product or workbench state; THIS bead builds whichever surface that
decision implies.

SCOPE:
1. THE CSV COLUMN PATH IS UNCHANGED AND MUST STAY THAT WAY. `canon <INPUT> --registry ...
   --column ... --emit csv` appends the canonical column by EXACT REGISTRY LOOKUP. Nothing
   probabilistic, nothing spatial, no geometry at runtime. That invariant is canon's core
   promise and geo does not get to bend it. Verify by test that the geo path introduces no
   new behaviour into src/lookup.rs.
2. THE DERIVED CROSSWALK VIEW. bd-67wx sanctions it explicitly: "The crosswalk is still
   USEFUL — materialize it as a DERIVED CONVENIENCE VIEW off the registry, regenerable,
   never authoritative. Ergonomics without the pathology." Build it. It is the wide table
   clients will ask for, generated from the registry plus the relation graph, carrying a
   generation timestamp and the source registry version so nobody mistakes it for truth.
   Its regeneration must be deterministic from pinned inputs.
3. THE TYPED ANSWER ARTIFACT. The per-row structure above, emitted as a sidecar keyed to
   the input rows — the same relationship `--map-out` already has to `--emit csv`. This is
   where relation, member sets, score_units, evidence operator ids, abstention state, and
   coverage state live. REUSE THE EXISTING SIDECAR PATTERN rather than inventing a new
   output mode.
4. THE GRAPH SURFACE. canon already depends on petgraph, and the estate already has graph
   infrastructure (data-fabric, Oxigraph). DECIDE — and record — whether canon geo emits a
   graph projection directly or whether it emits the typed answer artifact and lets
   downstream build the graph. RECOMMEND THE LATTER: canon's boundary is identity
   compilation, not graph serving, and OC-0048's non-goals already say canon does not ship
   a renderer or a web surface. The same reasoning applies to a query engine. Emit the
   artifact; let data-fabric or the client's warehouse serve it.
5. EXPORT PARITY. `canon registry export --format dbt-seed|search-index` already exists and
   preserves the registry boundary. Geo must not need a third export format. Verify the geo
   registry exports cleanly through the existing formats, and if it cannot, that is a
   finding about the identifier scheme (bd-67wx), not a licence to add a format.

WHAT MAKES THIS THE HARDEST BEAD TO KEEP HONEST: every request from a client will be for a
wider, flatter, more convenient table, and every one of those requests is a request to
reintroduce the fan-out-or-collapse pathology the identifier scheme exists to prevent. The
derived view is the pressure valve. Ship it, regenerate it, and never let it become the
source of truth.

EXIT CRITERIA:
- Test proving the runtime lookup path is unchanged by geo
- Derived crosswalk view, deterministic from pinned registry + relation graph, stamped with
  provenance and marked non-authoritative
- Typed answer sidecar reusing the existing --map-out pattern, carrying relation, members,
  score_units, evidence ids, abstention and coverage state
- A recorded decision on emit-graph vs emit-artifact
- Geo registry exports through the existing dbt-seed and search-index formats without a new
  format
- One worked end-to-end example: a client CSV in, a canonicalized CSV plus typed sidecar
  out, including at least one abstention and one multi-candidate row

## Background

title: canon geo: artifact license containment — field classification and 'canon geo redact'
description:
BYOP MAKES THE ARTIFACT LICENSE-ENCUMBERED. FOUND BY REALITY CHECK 2026-08-14.

THE PROBLEM: bd-101v requires geometry at DECISION FIDELITY in the artifact, for every
candidate including the ones that lost, so the visual evidence card can be drawn without
a second query. Under bring-your-own-parcel (bd-2kjx) that geometry INCLUDES THE CLIENT'S
LICENSED PARCEL POLYGONS from ATTOM / Regrid / LightBox. So the artifact that makes the
decision checkable is also an artifact we may have no right to receive.

CONSEQUENCES, WHICH MUST BE DESIGNED FOR RATHER THAN DISCOVERED IN A SUPPORT TICKET:
- We cannot debug a client's run by asking them to send the artifact.
- We cannot score a client's results centrally, so our own quality telemetry has a hole
  exactly where the paying customers are.
- bd-2jfj (evidence-signature grouping) CANNOT BE A HOSTED SERVICE for licensed layers.
  Its "one card per pattern instead of per pair" economics — which OC-0048 identifies as
  what makes visual review affordable at all — must work with the card rendered
  CLIENT-SIDE.
- OC-0048's non-goal "No APN corpus is redistributed; licensed parcel data stays the
  client's" is currently a statement of intent with NO MECHANISM. This bead is the
  mechanism.

TASK:
1. FIELD-LEVEL CLASSIFICATION. Classify every field of every geo artifact as
   ENCUMBERED or SHAREABLE. First cut:
     SHAREABLE   evidence scores, operator ids, reason codes, lanes, thresholds,
                 abstention states and reasons, tile ids, halo flags, coverage states,
                 multi-containment counts, OUR geometry, our minted cluster ids,
                 candidate counts, timing/diagnostics
     ENCUMBERED  client geometry, client row values, client addresses, vendor parcel
                 identifiers, and any derived value from which the source geometry could
                 be reconstructed (note: a sufficiently precise bbox plus area plus
                 vertex count may be reconstructive — think about this, do not wave at it)
   The reconstruction question is the subtle one. A "shareable" summary that leaks the
   polygon in aggregate is not shareable.
2. `canon geo redact` — A PROJECTION, NOT A DELETION. Produce the shareable subset as a
   first-class derived artifact that PRESERVES CONTENT-ADDRESSING INTEGRITY: the redacted
   artifact must carry a verifiable link to the full artifact's digest, so a decision can
   be discussed and audited by reference without the encumbered payload travelling. This
   is the same shape as canon's existing `--explicit` / masked-by-default behaviour on
   the lookup path, which already defaults input and canonical_id to [REDACTED] with
   "redacted": true in the envelope — REUSE THAT DOCTRINE AND VOCABULARY rather than
   inventing a second redaction model.
3. DEFAULT DENY. Redaction is the DEFAULT for any artifact containing a source marked
   licensed. Sharing the full artifact requires an explicit operator action. Getting this
   backwards means the first support ticket ships us data we should not hold.
4. LICENSE DECLARATION AT INGEST. The client-layer ingest bead requires a vendor
   descriptor; extend it with a license posture: shareable / internal-only / redact-always.
   Canon must refuse to run rather than assume a default posture.
5. WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE PROVING GROUND. bd-bmee uses MapPLUTO, which is public, so the
   proving ground runs UNREDACTED and is fully shareable. That is convenient and it also
   means the redaction path will be UNTESTED by the proving ground. The BYOP integration
   test bead must exercise redaction explicitly.
6. WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE CARD. bd-101v's card renders from the artifact. A redacted
   artifact can still render: the tile geometry from OUR sources, the evidence waterfall,
   the abstention state, and the candidate topology are all shareable. What it cannot draw
   is the client's parcel outline. Decide whether a redacted card is USEFUL ENOUGH TO BE
   WORTH RENDERING — RECOMMEND YES, because the evidence waterfall and the tie structure
   are most of the persuasive content, and a card that says "two client parcels contained
   this point, here is why neither won" is still checkable by the client against their own
   layer.

EXIT CRITERIA:
- Written field-level classification for every geo artifact, including an explicit
  analysis of which shareable aggregates could reconstruct encumbered geometry
- `canon geo redact` producing a verifiable, digest-linked shareable projection
- Default-deny behaviour with an explicit opt-out

comments.text:
TILE PRE-STITCHING IS ALREADY UNDER WAY IN cmdrvl-curves, LANDING NOW 2026-08-14. Verified
by reading the in-progress beads. This confirms the pre-resolved-tile architecture and
supplies hard facts that change several canon geo assumptions.

== WHAT IS ACTUALLY LANDING ==

  cmdrvl-curves bd-30ho   OVERTURE MAPS, release 2026-07-22.0. Themes buildings,
                          building_parts, PLACES, addresses, divisions. Snowflake DDL
                          APPLIED (OVERTURE_MAPS_FEATURES_HOT / _EXT /
                          OVERTURE_MAPS_FEATURE_H3_COVERAGE plus 14 per-type views);
                          manifest scan running, 0 rows landed yet.
  cmdrvl-curves bd-1ssr   FEMA USA STRUCTURES, 135,321,228 features nationally. National
                          landing IN PROGRESS; DC / AK / AL complete, AR running.
                          FEMA_USA_STRUCTURES_HOT loaded and read back (DC = 64,701 rows).
  cmdrvl-curves bd-3fyv   MICROSOFT GLOBALML FOOTPRINTS, release 2026-07-24. Landing IN
                          PROGRESS: 179 of 2,415 US files, 5,219,860 rows at 14:45Z.
  cmdrvl-curves bd-11uu   HUD USPS ADDRESS VACANCIES -- **BLOCKED**, and not a tile source.
                          HUD restricts it to registered governmental/non-profit users and
                          the sublicense forbids selling, licensing or distributing the
                          data. DO NOT PLAN ANY CANON GEO CAPABILITY ON IT.

NOTE ON "FOURSQUARE OS PLACES": it arrives as OVERTURE'S PLACES THEME, not a separate
Foursquare landing. That is the POI level in bd-2cbs, and it is in the same table family as
Overture buildings.

== FINDING 1: THE LANDED H3 GRAIN IS r4 / r7 / r8. THERE IS NO r9. ==
All three sources partition by h3_r4 and carry H3_R7 and H3_R8 columns. The epic's default
tile is res-9 and it is NOT precomputed anywhere.

AND THERE IS A CONVENIENT COINCIDENCE WORTH DELIBERATELY EXPLOITING: an r8 cell is
approximately 0.737 km2 -- which is almost exactly the area the epic specifies for its WORK
UNIT (an r9 cell plus k-ring 1 = 7 cells = 0.737 km2). So the already-landed H3_R8 column is
essentially the intended work-unit size.
ACTION FOR bd-2b9d: reconsider r9-plus-k-ring versus r8-plus-k-ring as the work unit, now
that r8 is precomputed across every source and r9 is not. This does not change the
requirement to compute cells in canon with a vetted Rust library -- the Snowflake H3 helper
defects (edgar-elt br-2wir) still stand -- but it does mean the warehouse can prefilter at
r8 for free, and the resolution decision now has a third input alongside node count and
human legibility.

== FINDING 2: POLYGON-TO-CELLS RETURNS EMPTY FOR SMALL BUILDINGS. LIVE, MEASURED. ==
From bd-3fyv: "H3_POLYGON_TO_CELLS alone inserted only 116 coverage rows for 354,804 hot
rows because small buildings often contain no H3 r8 cell centroid." Fixed there by using a
guaranteed CENTROID_H3_R8 plus H3_TRY_POLYGON_TO_CELLS.

THIS IS DIRECTLY THE MEMBERSHIP QUESTION bd-10s2 AND bd-2b9d SPECIFY. At r8 or r9 a
building is much smaller than a cell, so "which cells does this polygon cover" is
degenerate: the standard polygon-to-cells contract returns cells whose CENTRES fall inside
the polygon, and for a building that set is almost always EMPTY.
CONSEQUENCE: membership must be CENTROID-ANCHORED with polygon coverage as a supplement for
the large-feature case (parcels, campuses, complexes), NOT the other way round. My earlier
recommendation on bd-10s2 -- "full intersection cover for membership plus a single
deterministic anchor cell" -- is right in intent but inverted in emphasis, and applying it
naively with polygon_to_cells would have silently produced empty membership for nearly every
building. Correct it there.

== FINDING 3: OUR OWN SOURCES CARRY LICENSE OBLIGATIONS. bd-pq5w IS SCOPED TOO NARROWLY. ==
I framed license containment entirely around the CLIENT's licensed parcel layer. The landed
research shows OUR side has obligations too, and they differ per source:
    Overture buildings, divisions      ODbL-1.0            <-- SHARE-ALIKE
    Overture places                    per-source mix of CDLA-Permissive-2.0, Apache-2.0,
                                       CC0-1.0; source license must be retained
    Overture addresses                 source-specific, incl. NAD Access and Usage License
    FEMA USA Structures                CC-BY-4.0, attribution to ORNL and FEMA Geospatial
                                       Response Office REQUIRED
    Microsoft GlobalML                 CDLA-Permissive-2.0 current release; older vintages
                                       need per-release revalidation
bd-30ho states plainly: "License segmentation by source array is REQUIRED before any derived
product ships. Treat as a build-time gate, not a later cleanup."

ODbL SHARE-ALIKE IS THE COMMERCIAL ISSUE AND IT NEEDS AN OPERATOR DECISION, NOT AN
ENGINEERING ONE. A tile is a derived product. If it mixes ODbL Overture buildings with
everything else, the derived tile may inherit share-alike obligations that are
incompatible with a paid distribution model. Options to evaluate deliberately:
  (a) segregate ODbL-derived features into a separately-licensed layer of the tile, with
      the license class carried per feature -- note OVERTURE_MAPS_FEATURES_EXT ALREADY HAS
      LICENSE_CLASS AND LICENSE_TERMS COLUMNS, so the substrate for this exists;
  (b) build the commercial tile from the permissive sources only (FEMA CC-BY, Microsoft
      CDLA) and treat Overture as an internal enrichment;
  (c) accept share-alike and publish the tile openly.
REQUIRED IN bd-pq5w AND bd-1uld: license class per FEATURE in the tile artifact, and a
declared per-tile license posture that composes our obligations with the client's. The
artifact license boundary now has TWO directions, not one.

== FINDING 4: THE ATTRIBUTE CHANNELS FOR bd-272d ARE REAL, AND ONE IS MODELLED ==
Attribute anchoring needs class, size, floors, year. What is actually arriving:
    FEMA        OCC_CLS, PRIM_OCC (occupancy class), SQFEET, PROP_ADDR, UUID, BUILD_ID
    Overture    building class, height, num_floors, GERS id
    Microsoft   height (subset only), confidence, NO ID
    MapPLUTO    BLDGCLASS, LANDUSE, BLDGAREA, LOTAREA, NUMBLDGS, NUMFLOORS, YEARBUILT
So the six-field client contract has a counterpart on the tile side for every field except
YEAR BUILT, which only MapPLUTO supplies -- meaning year-built anchoring works in NYC and
degrades outside it until a national year source exists. Record that as a known national
limitation rather than discovering it later.

CRITICAL: FEMA OCCUPANCY IS MODELLED, NOT SURVEYED. bd-1ssr requires a provenance flag
"so downstream never treats it as surveyed." Attribute anchoring MUST carry that flag into
the evidence and weight modelled attributes below observed ones. A modelled occupancy class
driving a hard eliminative filter (bd-2zdz's assemblage type filter) would be a silent error
generator -- the filter is HARD, so a wrong modelled class removes the correct candidate
before anything is scored. Use modelled occupancy as SUPPORT evidence, never as a hard
filter, unless corroborated.

== FINDING 5: NO STABLE ID CONFIRMED FOR TWO SOURCES ==
Microsoft has no id at all -- bd-3fyv derives "a deterministic feature hash because no
stable id." Overture ADDRESSES are alpha with no stable GERS id either. This confirms
bd-2cbs rule 4 (alias-less participants) and extends it: the alias-less set is Microsoft
footprints AND Overture addresses, not just Microsoft.
A derived feature hash is NOT an alias and must not be minted into a registry -- it will
change whenever the geometry changes, which violates the tile identifier stability contract
in bd-12gh.

== FINDING 6: OVERTURE ADDRESSES CANNOT BE THE ADDRESS-SET SOURCE ==
bd-30ho: "Addresses theme is ALPHA -- do not build a contract against it yet," no stable
GERS id, multi-source licensing including NAD terms. US count 127,719,691.
So bd-35qg's address-set acquisition is NOT solved by Overture. NYC PAD or the per-BIN
addresses in the landed footprints file (bd-397d) remain the path, and the national story
stays open. Do not let the size of the Overture addresses count create false confidence.

== WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE WORKED-CASE CORPUS (bd-tccn) ==
The corpus can now stage its non-MapPLUTO pulls against REAL TABLE NAMES rather than
placeholders:
    EDGAR_DB.SOURCE.FEMA_USA_STRUCTURES_HOT              partially loaded (DC, AK, AL)
    EDGAR_DB.SOURCE.MICROSOFT_GLOBALML_BUILDING_FOOTPRINTS_HOT   partially loaded
    EDGAR_DB.SOURCE.OVERTURE_MAPS_FEATURES_HOT           DDL applied, 0 rows
    plus the *_FEATURE_H3_COVERAGE tables for each
NEW YORK IS NOT YET LOADED IN ANY OF THE THREE. FEMA is alphabetical by state and is at AR;
Microsoft is 179/2415 files; Overture has not started landing. So the full-tile version of
every case remains blocked, exactly as the corpus bead predicted -- but the blocker is now
a KNOWN COMPLETION DATE rather than an unlanded dataset, and the table names and column
shapes are already fixed enough to write the extraction queries against.

WHAT THE BODY ASSUMES: that license encumbrance flows one way — the CLIENT's licensed parcel

ODbL SHARE-ALIKE IS A COMMERCIAL DECISION, NOT AN ENGINEERING ONE. A tile is a derived
product. If it mixes ODbL Overture buildings with everything else, the derived tile may
inherit share-alike obligations incompatible with paid distribution. Three options to
evaluate deliberately:
  (a) SEGREGATE ODbL-derived features into a separately-licensed layer, carrying license
      class PER FEATURE. The substrate already exists — OVERTURE_MAPS_FEATURES_EXT carries

  (b) Build the commercial tile from permissive sources only (FEMA CC-BY, Microsoft CDLA)
      and treat Overture as internal enrichment.
  (c) Accept share-alike and publish the tile openly.
This needs an operator decision before the tile artifact format freezes (bd-1uld).

REQUIRED ADDITIONS TO THIS BEAD:
1. LICENSE CLASS PER FEATURE in the tile artifact, not per tile. Mixed-license tiles are

2. A DECLARED PER-TILE LICENSE POSTURE that COMPOSES our obligations with the client's.

comments.author: Zac
comments.text:
CORRECTION 2026-08-14 — THE ACCRETION FLYWHEEL DOES NOT SPIN FROM CLIENT USAGE. I overstated
it, and the operator caught it.

"We're not gonna get to keep our clients' properties. We're gonna run canon on their side.
We could offer it as an empty MCP server and get the info for ourselves, but we're mostly
offering for them to run canon on their side, so we won't be picking up addresses."

WHAT I IMPLIED: that resolving corpora compounds generally, as though every run added to the
registry.
WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE: accretion is bounded to CORPORA WE HOLD AND RESOLVE OURSELVES.
Canon runs on the client's machine, their artifacts are license-encumbered (bd-pq5w), and
their book never comes back. So:

  ACCRETES     HUD, Ginnie, Fannie, Freddie, CMBS conduit, REIT Schedule III, NAIC --
               everything we acquire and resolve on our own compute.
  DOES NOT     bank balance sheets, CRE CLOs, SASBs, and every other client corpus. Every
               client BENEFITS from our accretion; NO client CONTRIBUTES to it.

THE MOAT THEREFORE COMPOUNDS WITH ACQUISITION, NOT WITH ADOPTION. That is a real flywheel and
a weaker one than I described. It grows when we land another corpus, not when we sign
another client. Worth stating plainly because it changes what investment actually widens the
lead: buying and resolving more property corpora, not selling more seats.

TWO CONSEQUENCES THAT NEED HANDLING.

1. THE ADDRESS-SET ACCRETION PATH IS BOUNDED TOO (see bd-35qg). It still works -- HUD plus
   the agencies plus CMBS conduit is a large share of US institutional CRE addresses, and it
   is genuinely national. But it will never reach the addresses that exist only in client
   books, so it cannot fully substitute for landing an authoritative address-set source.
   The two paths remain complementary rather than one superseding the other.

2. WE ARE BLIND TO OUR OWN PRODUCT'S PERFORMANCE, AND THIS IS THE SERIOUS ONE.
   This bead makes the STAGE-1 HIT RATE against a real client book "the number that decides
   how much this actually buys." UNDER CLIENT-SIDE EXECUTION WE CANNOT MEASURE IT. Same for
   precision, abstention rate, coverage and false merges on live books -- bd-pq5w already
   records that we cannot debug or score a client's run centrally, and this is the same
   blindness applied to the metrics that would tell us where to improve.

   MITIGATION, AND IT IS ALREADY SCOPED: bd-pq5w's field classification separates SHAREABLE
   from ENCUMBERED. Evidence scores, operator ids, reason codes, abstention states, coverage
   states, candidate counts and tile ids are all shareable; client geometry and row values
   are not. So an OPT-IN REDACTED RUN SUMMARY gives us hit rates, abstention distributions
   and residual taxonomy WITHOUT their data ever leaving their machine.
   REQUIRED: make that redacted telemetry a first-class, opt-in, clearly-labelled output of
   the client run rather than something bolted on later. Design it as part of the artifact
   contract, and make what it contains inspectable by the client before they send it --
   trust is the product here, and a telemetry channel that is not fully legible would cost
   more than the metrics are worth.

   PROXY IN THE MEANTIME: hold out one of our own corpora, resolve the rest, and measure
   stage-1 hit rate of the held-out set against the accreted registry. That is a real
   number we can compute without any client, and it bounds the expected benefit before the
   first deployment.

3. THE HOSTED-MCP ALTERNATIVE IS A DELIBERATE PRODUCT DECISION, NOT A FALLBACK. Offering a
   hosted server that resolves on our side WOULD let us capture addresses -- and it inverts
   the privacy posture that the client-side design exists to provide. It is a different
   product with a different trust story and a different licensing exposure (their parcel
   vendor's terms may forbid sending the layer to us at all). Do not let it arrive by
   accident as a support convenience; if it is offered, it is offered explicitly.

title: [CANON-V1/P01.4] Define deterministic registry export backend interface
description:
## Background
dbt seed and search index are successful exports but currently implemented as one command-specific module. A backend boundary lets project compilation and packages produce multiple verified projections without alternate semantics.

## Technical Approach
- Define a typed export request containing verified package snapshot, filters, namespace, canonical IRI policy, output targets, and provenance.
- Define backend metadata, deterministic write planning, output hashes, refusal behavior, and common summary fields.
- Adapt existing dbt-seed and search-index implementations without changing their user-visible semantics.
- Allow project manifests to request multiple exports atomically after promotion.

## Success Criteria
- All backends consume the same effective mapping snapshot and precedence rules.
- Filters and normalized search keys cannot diverge silently between formats.
- Existing CLI commands continue to work.
- A failed backend cannot leave another backend falsely reported as complete.

## Test Plan
- Shared conformance harness for export backends.
- Filter and precedence metamorphic tests.
- Atomic multi-export failure tests.
- Existing golden artifact parity.

## RESERVATIONS
- `src/registry/export.rs`
- `src/lib.rs`
- `tests/registry_export_conformance.rs`

## Considerations
- Do not make export formats part of core lookup.
- Keep backend API narrow enough for future formats.
- Shared CLI wiring should be coordinated with P00 dispatch ownership.
close_reason: Implemented deterministic registry export backend interface with shared snapshot planning and conformance validation; focused tests/clippy green, repo-wide fmt blocked by unrelated active-tree drift
