title: canon geo: name-and-region resolution — the cascade entered from the other end (Schedule III, NAIC)
description:
OPERATOR CORRECTION 2026-08-14: NAME-ONLY RESOLUTION IS A CAPABILITY, NOT AN EDGE CASE. I
recorded it as a limitation on bd-14hu and that framing was wrong.

"A Schedule III that says 'Mall of Louisiana' with a city, state and ZIP -- we should be
able to use our data sources and get that. Resolving our data sources should really be good
at helping us resolve names, especially if we have the property type and the year built. I
don't see why we couldn't get pretty close to where a human would just have to adjudicate a
few decisions."

== WHY THIS IS RIGHT, AND WHY IT INVERTS THE DESIGN ==
OC-0048 states the doctrine as: "The attributes do not FIND the match -- geometry does. They
REJECT the wrong one."
THAT IS TRUE FOR ADDRESS AND GEOCODE INPUTS AND FALSE FOR NAME-ONLY INPUTS. With no point
and no street address there is nothing for geometry to start from. The correct statement for
this population is the mirror image:

    THE NAME FINDS THE MATCH. GEOMETRY AND ATTRIBUTES REJECT THE WRONG ONE.

Same evidence, same operators, opposite order. That symmetry is the whole design, and it
means name-only resolution is not a bolt-on -- it is the cascade entered from the other end.

== A SECOND ENTRY POINT INTO THE CASCADE ==
Everything scoped so far starts: geocode -> tile -> candidates -> score -> decide/abstain.
Name-only starts:  name + region -> TILE SET -> candidate POIs and buildings -> narrow by
attributes -> descend the level ladder -> confirm with geometry.

  1. REGION RESOLVES TO A TILE SET, NOT A TILE. City/state/ZIP is a coarse spatial filter
     yielding many cells rather than one. Overture's DIVISIONS theme (division_area,
     division_boundary) is landing in bd-30ho and is exactly the source for administrative
     boundaries -> cell coverage. A ZIP is on the order of tens of r8 cells; bounded and
     tractable, especially with a name filter applied first.
  2. NAME MATCHING IS WHERE canon ENTITY'S EXISTING MACHINERY GENUINELY TRANSFERS UNCHANGED
     (bd-2cbs rule 3). namekit, rapidfuzz, tfidf_cosine, alias_patch_match, and the
     cmbs_tenant_label profile pattern all apply directly to POI and place names. This is
     the strongest instance in the whole epic of reuse actually being reuse.
  3. ATTRIBUTES NARROW HARD. Property type plus year built plus size, against a region
     rather than a tile. A mall in one ZIP is close to unique.
  4. DESCEND THE LADDER TO CONFIRM. POI -> containing building -> parcel (bd-2cbs). Then
     check the building's size and year against the assertion. Found by name, CONFIRMED by
     geometry -- and disagreement at the confirm step is a strong abstention signal, not a
     tiebreak.

== RARITY IS THE FEASIBILITY TEST, AND IT IS COMPUTABLE ==
"Mall of Louisiana" works because it is unique in its region. "Holiday Inn Express" or
"Walmart Supercenter" is not -- a metro carries dozens. So name-only resolution is feasible
exactly where the name is DISCRIMINATING IN THE REGION, and that is computable from the
region's own POI population, the same way bd-272d computes attribute rarity from the tile's
own population.
REQUIRED: score by name rarity IN THE REGION, ABSTAIN when the name is not discriminating,
and REPORT the region's discriminating power so "we could not resolve it" distinguishes
"the name is generic" from "nothing matched." Chains and brands should route to review by
construction rather than being attempted and silently mismatched.

== FOUR HARD PARTS, RECORDED HONESTLY ==
1. CHAIN AND BRAND NAMES are the failure population, per the rarity point above.
2. NAMES DRIFT. Malls are renamed and rebranded; a 2015 Schedule III name may not match a
   2026 POI name. This is the temporal problem from bd-1oy8 arriving through the name
   channel, and prior names are themselves accretable knowledge (bd-14hu).
3. THE POI IS NOT THE BUILDING. A mall POI is one point; the mall spans multiple parcels
   and multiple buildings. So "Mall of Louisiana" resolves to a SET -- which makes a mall a
   canonical instance of BOTH the property-as-set model AND corpus case 7 (M parcels to N
   buildings). Do not let the POI point become the answer.
4. OVERTURE PLACES LICENSING is a per-source mix (CDLA-Permissive-2.0 / Apache-2.0 / CC0)
   requiring source license retention, per bd-30ho. Name-only resolution leans hardest on
   the theme with the most fragmented licensing; carry license class per feature (bd-pq5w).

== WHAT IT UNLOCKS: TWO WHOLE CORPORA ==
  REIT SCHEDULE III (bd-14a8)    property NAME only, no address field. Currently
                                 unaddressable by any geometry-first design.
  NAIC SCHEDULE A/B (naic-2wt)   the insurer's own descriptor, quality varies.
Both are name/descriptor-only and both are listed in OC-0048's corpus table as things this
outcome is supposed to key. Without this path they simply never resolve.

== GINNIE MAE IS A DIFFERENT MECHANISM AND SHOULD BE VERIFIED, NOT ASSUMED ==
The operator grouped Ginnie with the name cases. It is probably NOT a name problem: Ginnie's
native key is a pool number with no address and no property name, so there is no name to
match. The likely path is an IDENTIFIER JOIN rather than a name match -- Ginnie multifamily
pools reference FHA case numbers, and HUD's property inventory carries FHA numbers WITH
addresses, so GNMA -> FHA number -> HUD -> address would resolve it through a corpus we
already hold.
I HAVE NOT VERIFIED THAT CHAIN. Confirm the FHA-number linkage exists in the landed Ginnie
and HUD data before scoping work on it. If it holds, Ginnie is cheap and needs none of this
bead's machinery; if it does not, Ginnie may be genuinely unresolvable at the property level
and that should be stated plainly rather than left implied.

== SEQUENCING ==
This depends on Overture places and divisions landing (bd-30ho, not started) and on the
entity-level model (bd-2cbs). It does NOT depend on the geometry cascade being finished --
the name path can be proven independently, and proving it early de-risks two corpora that
the geometry-first design cannot touch at all.

EXIT CRITERIA:
- A name+region entry point distinct from the geocode entry point, with its own blocking
  strategy (region -> tile set, then name)
- Region-to-cell coverage derived from Overture divisions
- Name matching reusing canon entity's existing operators rather than new ones
- Name rarity computed per region, with abstention when not discriminating and the
  region's discriminating power reported
- Descend-and-confirm: POI -> building -> parcel, with attribute disagreement at the confirm
  step producing abstention rather than a tiebreak
- A worked case on a real Schedule III row -- "Mall of Louisiana" or equivalent -- resolving
  to a SET of parcels and buildings, not a point
- A negative case: a chain name in a dense metro that correctly abstains and routes to review
- The Ginnie FHA-number chain either verified and scoped, or documented as unavailable

title: canon geo: research all imagery and elevation sources from primary sources, catalog the survivors at provider and channel level
description:
Research every candidate imagery and elevation source carefully, then CATALOG THE SURVIVORS
at provider and channel level so the estate can draw on them later without re-researching.

CONTEXT: PLAN_CANON_GEO.md Appendix A establishes that a frozen-weight observer (the
cmdrvl-tabfm / FrankenWhisper / FrankenOCR pattern — open weights reimplemented in pure Rust
with hard-coded weights, bit-identical forever) satisfies canon's determinism requirement.
The model is a SOURCE, not a solver: it emits typed observations (a structure count, a roof
outline, a floor count) which enter as constraints like any other evidence. So imagery
becomes another source class, and any imagery source is admissible once it has a license
posture, a vintage, and a characterized error.

ONLY NAIP HAS BEEN VERIFIED. Everything else in Appendix A.5 is from general knowledge and
explicitly marked unverified. This bead closes that.

== WHAT TO RESEARCH, PER SOURCE ==

For each candidate below, establish from PRIMARY SOURCES (agency pages, license text, actual
bucket or endpoint listings — not blog posts, not model recall):

  1. LICENSE POSTURE, exactly. Public domain / permissive with attribution / licensed and
     resolvable but not redistributable / prohibited for our use. Quote the operative
     clause. This is the gate — see the FCC Fabric precedent, where a high-value dataset
     turned out to restrict use to "statutory broadband-related obligations" and was
     therefore unusable for commercial CRE despite ranking #4 on an earlier list.
  2. COVERAGE — national, regional, spotty. Which states/counties, and how is coverage
     reported.
  3. RESOLUTION and bands. Is it adequate to resolve an individual building footprint.
  4. VINTAGE AND CADENCE. Per-tile date, refresh schedule, and whether historical vintages
     are retained. Temporal identity depends on this (bd-1oy8, Allen interval constraints).
  5. ACCESS MECHANISM. Bulk download / COG plus HTTP range requests / STAC catalog / tile
     server / authenticated API. COG-plus-range is strongly preferred: it fetches only the
     window covering an H3 cell and needs no key or rate limit.
  6. PINNABILITY. Can a specific asset be content-addressed — object version, ETag, checksum
     — so a re-render years later is byte-identical? A source that cannot be pinned cannot
     enter a reproducible evidence artifact.
  7. COST at national scale, including egress.
  8. ERROR CHARACTERIZABILITY. Is there published accuracy metadata, and is the error
     plausibly measurable by us? Per Appendix A.3, no characterization means no rho band
     means no admission.

== CANDIDATES ==

VERIFIED ALREADY, re-confirm coverage years only:
  NAIP (USDA FPAC-BC). Public domain, 1m 2003-17 / 0.6m from 2018 / 0.3m coastal option.
  Three public S3 buckets: naip-visualization (3-band COG), naip-analytic (4-band MRF),
  naip-source (raw GeoTIFF). STAC exists. OPEN QUESTION: the AWS registry describes
  2011-2018 for one bucket while STAC catalogs claim 2010-present — confirm current coverage
  against the live bucket. Known limitation: leaf-on growing-season imagery, so canopy
  obscures structures in tree-heavy areas, which is the dominant term in its rho band and is
  seasonal and geographic.

ASSESS FIRST, AND POSSIBLY BEFORE IMAGERY AT ALL:
  USGS 3DEP LiDAR. Height is MEASURED rather than inferred; building extraction from point
  clouds is classical geometry, so there may be NO MODEL TO CHARACTERIZE — which would
  collapse the entire Appendix A.3 admission gate to ordinary sensor accuracy. Distinguishes
  building from parking lot trivially and yields floor-count estimates directly against
  NUMFLOORS. Public domain, on AWS Open Data. Coverage incomplete and vintage varies widely
  by county. THIS MAY BE THE RIGHT SENSOR AND IT IS RANKED FIRST FOR THAT REASON.

REMAINING CANDIDATES:
  Sentinel-1 SAR (ESA). ~10m radar, all-weather, free and open. Too coarse for footprints,
  but buildings have distinctive double-bounce signatures — assess for PRESENCE AND CHANGE
  DETECTION, which is what the temporal constraints currently have no observation source for.
  Sentinel-2 (ESA). ~10m optical, free and open. Change detection and land cover.
  State and municipal orthoimagery. Several states and NYC specifically fly higher resolution
  than NAIP, often public. Likely the best resolution available for the NYC proving ground —
  check NYC first.
  USGS High Resolution Orthoimagery (HRO). Public domain, higher res where covered.
  NOAA emergency response imagery. Post-disaster, high-res, public domain. Narrow but
  valuable for change events.
  Commercial: Maxar, Planet, Nearmap, Vexcel, Airbus. Better resolution and cadence,
  licensed. Record terms precisely — resolvable-under-license versus redistributable is the
  distinction that matters, and it is the same containment discipline as bd-pq5w.
  Mapbox / Google / Esri basemaps. EXPECTED TO FAIL — terms generally forbid caching, which
  is incompatible with a pinned evidence artifact. Confirm and record so nobody re-proposes
  them.

Add any source the research turns up that is not listed. The list is a starting point, not a
boundary.

== CATALOG THE SURVIVORS ==

Every source that passes scrutiny gets registered in the metadata catalog using the `catalog`
skill, at BOTH levels:
  data_provider://<agency or vendor>
  data_channel://<provider>/<dataset>/<access method>
with license_terms recorded verbatim, required attribution captured, access mechanism and
pinning strategy described, coverage and cadence stated, and a data-location plus lineage
stitched where we land anything.

Follow the existing pattern from the geo landings — cmdrvl-curves bd-30ho, bd-1ssr and
bd-3fyv each registered provider, channel, data-location, prefix and per-table lineage, with
license_terms and required attribution carried through. Match that shape.

Sources that FAIL scrutiny are recorded too, with the reason and the operative license
clause, so the finding is not re-litigated. A rejected source with a documented reason is a
deliverable.

Use the `catalog-eval` skill to score each registered provider/channel against the
four-dimension quality rubric, and `provider-data-enrich` to write the data dictionary onto
the channel description. A channel without a data dictionary is an incomplete registration.

== EXIT CRITERIA ==
- Every candidate researched from primary sources, with the license clause quoted
- A ranked recommendation, with 3DEP assessed explicitly against imagery rather than assumed
  to be secondary
- Survivors registered at provider and channel level with license_terms and attribution
- Failures recorded with reasons
- Each registered channel scored via catalog-eval and enriched with a data dictionary
- A written note on which single source to land first for the NYC proving ground, and why

title: [CANON-V1/REVIEW] Prove v1 contracts through the public crate API
description:

title: [CANON-V1/P08.5] Enforce content-addressed publication and optimistic concurrency
description:
## Background
Two writers can otherwise publish divergent next registry versions and silently lose updates. Versioned files alone do not guarantee a single ancestry.

## Technical Approach
Require every mutation/promotion to name expected base digest and version; build the candidate package completely; verify it; then publish with compare-and-swap or create-if-absent semantics. Define backend capabilities and deterministic conflict receipts. Tags/channels update only after immutable package publication and use their own expected-current digest.

## Success Criteria
- Concurrent writers from the same base produce at most one accepted successor for a linear channel.
- The loser receives the actual head and a safe rebase/semantic-merge plan; no data is overwritten.
- Filesystem publication is atomic and crash-safe within documented platform guarantees.
- Package history remains immutable and ancestry-verifiable.

## Test Plan
Race many subprocess writers, inject crashes at every publication boundary, test stale bases, identical candidates, divergent candidates, tag races, and recovery. Verify directory/object inventories and ancestry.

## RESERVATIONS
- `src/registry/transaction.rs`
- `src/distribution/backend.rs`
- `tests/registry_concurrency_e2e.rs`

## Considerations
Some stores provide weaker primitives. Backends must advertise capabilities and refuse unsafe mutation rather than emulate CAS with a race.
close_reason: Implemented filesystem-first content-addressed publication backend and registry publication transaction in reserved files only. Evidence: cargo test --test registry_concurrency_e2e passed 6/6; cargo test --test registry_concurrency passed 6/6 after rerun; cargo fmt --check passed; cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings passed. - Enforce max_candidates from strategy/CLI and refuse with E_TOO_MANY_CANDIDATES when a target has too many surviving candidates.

title: [CANON-V1/P02.5] Execute project DAGs with content-addressed resumability
description:
## Background
Large identity runs will be interrupted, rerun, and extended. A monolithic all-or-nothing command wastes compute and makes partial state opaque.

## Technical Approach
Implement a deterministic runner that executes ready DAG nodes, commits each artifact atomically, records a hash-linked receipt, and resumes only when all declared inputs and tool contracts match. Support bounded parallelism for independent read-only nodes, explicit stage selection, fail-fast or collect-independent-failures policy, and cancellation without corrupting prior results.

## Success Criteria
- Interrupted runs resume from validated artifacts and never repeat a valid completed node.
- Changed inputs invalidate exactly the affected node and descendants.
- Failed/cancelled nodes leave no artifact that can be mistaken for complete.
- Receipts record node hashes, durations, resource observations, outcomes, and next actions without sensitive data.

## Test Plan
Inject failures before, during, and after artifact publication for every node class; restart and compare final bytes with uninterrupted runs; test poisoning, stale tool versions, bounded parallelism, cancellation, and disk-full refusal.

## RESERVATIONS
- `src/project/run.rs`
- `src/project/receipt.rs`
- `schemas/canon.project.run.v1.schema.json`
- `tests/project_resume.rs`

## Considerations
Resumability is content validation, not existence checking. Temporary files stay inside the owned work directory and publication is atomic.
close_reason: Completed project DAG runner/resume layer in reserved files. Evidence: rustfmt --edition 2024 --check src/project/run.rs src/project/receipt.rs tests/project_resume.rs passed; cargo test --test project_resume --test project_plan passed (18 tests); cargo clippy --test project_resume --test project_plan -- -D warnings with command-line allowances for pre-existing unreserved src/project/plan.rs warnings passed. title: [CANON-V1/P04.4] Attach usage and blast-radius context to unresolved groups
description:

Occurrence count alone is a poor prioritizer. One missing identity used across many critical records and downstream models may matter more than a noisy high-frequency free-text label.

Define a content-addressed usage-context artifact derived from project manifests, typed field/assignment roles, exact-lookup/apply lineage, dbt/search consumers, source criticality, exposure or row-count bands, and downstream dependency counts. Build neutral fixtures where frequency and business impact disagree; test missing lineage, redacted measures, duplicated projects, stale references, and policy changes; verify joins and contribution breakdowns.

- `schemas/canon.usage_context.v1.schema.json`
- `tests/inbox_context.rs`

title: canon registry export: first-class provenance-stamped seed materialization (dbt-seed format)
description:
Promote the registry->dbt-seed promotion pattern (proven 2026-07-06 in edgar-elt, cmbs_servicer_alias_map.csv, firms@1.0.12->1.1.17) from a session-driven workbench process to a first-class canon subcommand, e.g.:

  canon registry export --format dbt-seed --namespace <ctx> --out <seed.csv>

Requirements distilled from the edgar-elt promotion:
- Deterministic output: stable row ordering so git diffs of re-exports are meaningful.
- Per-row provenance stamp: registry_version + content hash (drift tripwire), match_source (canon / registry_exact / registry_brand).
- Context/namespace filtering is FIRST-CLASS, not optional: full-registry export is what produced CRM false merges (NEWMARK->ORG-006, CRED IQ->ORG-005); the fix was servicer-context-restricted matching. Related: edgar-elt br-2n9x (shared alias namespace false-merge risk).
- Confident-only inclusion; abstentions are excluded so consumers fail closed to NULL.
- Optional scaffolds: companion dbt schema.yml (column docs + not_null tests) and an anti-collapse singular test template (one normalized key -> exactly one canon id).
- dbt coupling stays thin: the format is a conventions-following CSV; no dbt runtime dependency in canon.

Why first-class: canon boundary doctrine is "judgment in the workbench, deterministic SQL downstream; registry crosses into transform tools only as a frozen versioned snapshot." This command IS that boundary, and it is generic to any dbt user with messy entity strings -- a strong OSS adoption surface.

Capture-only bead: no build scheduled.

title: canon geo: worked-case corpus — six cases end to end before any code, from landed data
description:
OPERATOR DECISION 2026-08-14: NO CODE UNTIL THIS EXISTS. THIS BEAD BLOCKS bd-3ccc.

"Before we write a line of code, tee up a corpus of use cases that give an exact case, pull
all of the data from all of our datasets, look at it together, and see what the answer
should be and what techniques would arrive at that answer. Easiest to most complex, worked
through beginning to end, and what does it reveal about how canon should operate."

WHY THIS IS THE RIGHT MOVE NOW. Thirty-three geo beads currently settle their design
questions BY ARGUMENT. Six worked cases settle them BY EVIDENCE. Every open decision in the
epic — does `within` return a set, is the relation graph product or workbench state, can a
property's member set mix entity types, what does the assemblage subset-sum actually have
to tolerate, where does abstention genuinely belong — becomes a matter of looking at a real
case rather than reasoning about a hypothetical one.

== THIS ARTIFACT HAS FIVE USES, WHICH IS WHY IT IS WORTH BUILDING PROPERLY ==
1. DESIGN FORCING FUNCTION. Where a case cannot be adjudicated by hand, that is a genuine
   capability gap, not a modelling preference.
2. THE EVALUATION SUITE. canon already takes `--suite <DIR>` and `--gold <JSONL>`. These
   cases become the fixtures, so the corpus is not throwaway analysis.
3. bd-101v's WORKED EXAMPLES. The visual evidence card needs real artifacts to render; this
   produces six, including the abstention cases which are the hardest to design blind.
4. A SALES ARTIFACT THAT EXISTS BEFORE THE PRODUCT DOES. OC-0048's target reaction is
   "you put a BBL on every one of our New York properties, and I checked three of them
   myself." Six worked cases ARE that conversation, and they can be shown to Newmark or
   CRED iQ before a line of canon geo is written. That de-risks the build commercially, not
   just technically.
5. ACQUISITION PRIORITISATION. See the landed/not-landed section below.

== THE PROPOSED LADDER — SIX CASES, EACH FORCING A DISTINCT DECISION ==
Adjust the specific properties, but preserve the property that each case forces something
different. A corpus where all six are variations of one problem teaches nothing.

CASE 1 — CLEAN. Rooftop geocode, one building, one lot, address agrees, size agrees.
  FORCES: what "unambiguous" looks like; the shape both baselines get right; the floor.
CASE 2 — MULTI-CONTAINMENT. 237 Park Avenue: a ROOFTOP geocode inside TWO genuine MapPLUTO
  lots (BBL 1012920026 and 1012920001), both ST_CONTAINS true. Geometry scores them
  identically and must abstain; the address channel breaks the tie. 157 five-borough CMBS
  points fall in more than one lot, max 4. A mock already exists.
  FORCES: `within` returning a SET not a winner; abstention as an explicit state; the
  condo unit-vs-parent population, which is the bulk of the measured fan-out.
CASE 3 — ONE BUILDING OVER MANY LOTS. A single tower built over an assemblage of older tax
  lots — the most common Manhattan pattern.
  FORCES: typed relations in the many-to-one direction; why a BBL column cannot express the
  answer; the BBL/BIN split as the resolution, not a complication.
CASE 4 — RANGE-ADDRESS ASSEMBLAGE. A "100-105 Broadway"-shaped property: mixed office and
  retail in the tile, both address parities present, several candidate lots.
  FORCES: assemblage as a third solve mode (bd-2zdz); the interval structure; subset-sum
  over building areas; parity as a locale convention; the NRA-vs-gross size mismatch.
CASE 5 — INTERPOLATED GEOCODE. A range_interpolation or street_center point sitting in the
  right-of-way where NO lot contains it. OC-0048 identifies this tier as the actual canon
  geo workload.
  FORCES: proximity candidate generation bounded by tile rather than radius; the refusal to
  snap-to-nearest; the address channel as the corroborator — and it will expose the
  address-SET gap (bd-35qg) in the most visible possible way.
CASE 6 — MULTI-CORPUS SHARED PARCEL, TEMPORAL. A parcel bare in year 0 carrying several
  buildings a year later, with positions in DIFFERENT corpora — one in a REIT, one in a
  CMBS trust, one carrying an RCA sales comp.
  FORCES: the entity-level model (bd-2cbs); the FALSE-MERGE finding; existence intervals
  and temporal containment (bd-1oy8); and it demonstrates that bd-bmee's BBL metric can
  pass while the product fails.

AT LEAST ONE CASE MUST BE GENUINELY UNDECIDABLE. If all six resolve cleanly the corpus
teaches the wrong lesson and reads as cherry-picked. Include one where a domain expert
would abstain on the available evidence, and record WHY — that case calibrates what
abstention is supposed to look like and is the most valuable one in the set.

== REQUIRED CONTENT PER CASE — FIXED SCHEMA, NOT PROSE ==
1. THE ASSERTION. The client-side row with all six contract fields (bd-uilx), verbatim.
2. EVERY OBSERVATION IN THE TILE, from every landed dataset, at every level (poi / building
   / parcel), with source, vintage, native identifier, and geometry.
3. THE ADJUDICATED ANSWER as a TYPED STRUCTURE: member set with entity levels, typed
   relations between members, as-of date, and abstention state where applicable. Not a BBL
   string.
4. THE REASONING TRACE. Which signals decided it, IN WHAT ORDER, and — critically — WHAT
   THE ANSWER WOULD HAVE BEEN WITHOUT EACH SIGNAL. That ablation is what reveals which
   operators are load-bearing versus decorative, and it is the single most useful output of
   this exercise.
5. WHAT CANON WOULD HAVE TO DO: the operator sequence, the thresholds, the abstention
   points. Where no currently-scoped operator reaches the answer, NAME THE GAP.
6. WHAT EACH BASELINE PRODUCES: naive address-string match, and spatial join plus address
   tiebreak. The corpus therefore doubles as a qualitative companion to bd-14co's
   quantitative baselines.

== ADJUDICATION MUST NOT BE CIRCULAR — THE METHODOLOGICAL TRAP ==
If the hand-adjudicated answer is derived from the same signals canon will use, the corpus
proves nothing; it just restates the algorithm as truth. Adjudicate using INDEPENDENT
evidence wherever possible:
  ZoLa visual inspection (public, per-BBL, and it is what a client analyst would check)
  ACRIS recorded documents — landed, ~100.76M rows, and independent of the address channel
  the actual loan or offering documents where obtainable
  certificates of occupancy for building existence and dates
RECORD THE ADJUDICATION, NOT ONLY THE ANSWER. An answer key without reasoning is a test;
an answer key with reasoning is a specification.

== ON THE DATA NOT ALL BEING LANDED — THIS IS A FEATURE OF THE EXERCISE ==
LANDED and usable today: MapPLUTO 26v1 (856,614 lot polygons, H3-indexed), PLUTO 26v1
(858,602 rows), NYC Building Footprints / the BBL-to-BIN bridge (bd-397d), ACRIS
(~100.76M rows), and the CMBS geocode book (68,603 rows with accuracy_type and parsed
address parts).
NOT LANDED or unverified: the national footprint layers (Overture GERS, FEMA USA
Structures, Microsoft GlobalML), Foursquare OS Places, NYC PAD / any address-SET source
(bd-35qg), the MapPLUTO version archive (cmdrvl-curves bd-33t6, still open — only the
current release landed), and the DOB permit / certificate-of-occupancy channels.

CONSEQUENCE: cases 1 through 4 are constructible TODAY on the landed NYC spine. Cases 5 and
6 will run into missing sources — AND THAT IS THE POINT. A case that cannot be completed
because a dataset is absent is a RESULT, not a blocker: it identifies precisely which
un-landed source is load-bearing for which capability, which turns acquisition sequencing
into an evidence-backed decision instead of an intuition. Record every such stop explicitly
as "this case requires X, which is not landed, for reason Y."

Case 6 in particular needs the version archive (bd-33t6) to be honest about the temporal
arc; if only the current release exists, construct the case as far as it goes and record
the stop.

== WHAT THIS BEAD IS NOT ==
It is not a design document and it is not a plan. It is SIX WORKED CASES WITH THEIR DATA
ATTACHED. Every general statement in it must be traceable to a specific row in a specific
dataset. If a conclusion cannot be pointed at a case, it does not belong here — it belongs
in whichever bead it actually modifies.

EXIT CRITERIA:
- Six cases, spanning the ladder, at least one genuinely undecidable
- Complete tile extract per case from every landed dataset, at every level, with vintages
- Typed adjudicated answer per case, independently sourced, with the adjudication recorded
- The signal-ablation trace per case — what the answer would be without each signal
- Named gaps where no scoped operator reaches the answer
- Both baselines' outputs per case
- An explicit list of un-landed datasets, each tied to the case and capability it blocked
- A written "what this reveals about how canon geo should operate" summary, with every

comments.text:
OPERATOR CASE LADDER 2026-08-14 — SUPERSEDES THE PROPOSED LADDER IN THIS BEAD'S BODY.

Operator-supplied, grounded in observed data shapes rather than in which design decision
each case forces. Use these. They are better because they are ENUMERABLE FROM THE DATA — a
query can find instances of each shape — where the original proposal described shapes we
hoped existed.

  CASE 1  SINGLE ADDRESS, ROOFTOP GEOCODE
          The clean case. One address, one building, one lot, everything agrees.
          FORCES: the control for every ablation trace; what "unambiguous" means; the floor
          both baselines clear. Expected: rooftop tier, 99.92% lot-hit.

  CASE 2  SINGLE ADDRESS, GEOCODE TO THE MIDDLE OF THE STREET
          The point sits in the right-of-way. NO parcel contains it.
          FORCES: proximity candidate generation bounded by the tile rather than a radius;
          the explicit refusal to snap-to-nearest (on a narrow Manhattan block the nearest
          lot is frequently across the street, and a 20 m interpolation error is three lots);
          the address channel as the ONLY discriminator. This is the tier OC-0048 calls the
          actual canon geo workload. It will expose the missing address-SET source (bd-35qg)
          more clearly than any other case.

  CASE 3  SPLIT / RANGE ADDRESS -- "100 to 105"
          FORCES: assemblage as a third solve mode (bd-2zdz); the interval structure;
          subset-sum over member building areas; odd/even parity as a locale convention;
          the NRA-versus-gross size mismatch.

  CASE 4  COMMA-SEPARATED ADDRESS ON TWO DIFFERENT STREETS
          One address field carrying two addresses on different streets.
          FORCES: the address parser must handle MULTI-ADDRESS FIELDS, not only ranges —
          currently unscoped in bd-1zph, which models normalization and ranges only.
          Also: WHICH ONE DID THE GEOCODER PICK, and did it silently drop the other? A
          single lat/lon from a two-address field is a lossy choice made upstream by
          Geocodio, and canon should be able to detect that it happened.
          AND IT BREAKS A TRACTABILITY CLAIM — see the correction filed on bd-2zdz.

  CASE 5  TWO ADDRESSES, SAME BUILDING, DIFFERENT CORNERS
          A corner building with legitimate frontages on two streets, appearing as two
          different addresses. Already measured on bd-1zph: geocode "9 WEST FORDHAM ROAD"
          against MapPLUTO "2167 GRAND CONCOURSE" is exactly this.
          FORCES: THE INVERSE OF CASES 3 AND 4. Here the address channel ACTIVELY MISLEADS
          — two rows with completely different addresses are the SAME building, and address
          disagreement is NOT evidence against the match. Geometry has to win and the
          address channel has to be allowed to lose.
          Cases 4 and 5 together are the most valuable pair in the corpus: they show the
          address channel as signal and as noise, on the same tile, which is what any
          honest channel-agreement rule (bd-uilx) has to be calibrated against.

  CASE 6  DENSE URBAN BLOCK -- MULTIPLE BUILDINGS TO ONE PARCEL
          N buildings : 1 parcel.
          FORCES: geometry CANNOT discriminate — every candidate building is inside the same
          parcel, so point-in-polygon is useless past the first step. Size, type, and
          POI/tenant evidence carry it. This is where the entity-level model (bd-2cbs) bites
          and where the false-merge risk lives: resolving to the BBL merges buildings that
          may sit in different corpora entirely.

  CASE 7  DENSE MULTIFAMILY -- MULTIPLE PARCELS TO ONE SET OF BUILDINGS
          M parcels : N buildings. The hardest cardinality, and the inverse of case 6.
          A garden-apartment complex or campus: the property spans parcels AND contains
          multiple buildings, and no single containment relation expresses it.
          FORCES: the property-as-SET model (see bd-67wx / bd-1oid comments 2026-08-14) —
          this is the case that model exists for. Also forces the decision on whether a
          member set may MIX entity levels.

TWO CASES THE OPERATOR LIST DOES NOT COVER. Recommend adding both; decide explicitly rather
than by omission.

  CASE 8  MULTI-CONTAINMENT -- ONE POINT INSIDE TWO LEGITIMATE PARCELS
          237 Park Avenue: a ROOFTOP geocode inside BBL 1012920026 and 1012920001, both
          ST_CONTAINS true. 157 five-borough CMBS points fall in more than one lot, max 4,
          and the population is largely condo unit BBLs overlapping their parent lot.
          DISTINCT FROM 6 AND 7: the ambiguity is at the PARCEL level, not the building
          level, and geometry scores the candidates IDENTICALLY rather than uselessly.
          FORCES: `within` returning a SET rather than a winner; abstention as an explicit
          state; and the condo case that breaks assemblage additivity. A mock already exists,
          so this is the cheapest case in the corpus to construct.

  CASE 9  MULTI-CORPUS SHARED PARCEL, WITH A TEMPORAL ARC
          The operator's own earlier case: a parcel bare in year 0 carrying several
          buildings a year later, with one building in a REIT, one in a CMBS trust, and one
          carrying an RCA sales comp.
          FORCES: the false-merge finding — the single most consequential result in the
          epic. It demonstrates that bd-bmee's BBL metric PASSES while the product question
          goes untested, and that parcel-level resolution poisons the cross-corpus join this
          outcome exists to enable. Also forces existence intervals and temporal containment
          (bd-1oy8).
          NOTE: needs the MapPLUTO version archive (cmdrvl-curves bd-33t6, still open) to be
          honest about the arc. Build it as far as the current release allows and record the
          stop.

AT LEAST ONE CASE MUST BE GENUINELY UNDECIDABLE on available evidence, with the reason
recorded. Cases 7 and 8 are the most likely candidates. If every case resolves cleanly the
corpus reads as cherry-picked and teaches the wrong lesson about abstention.

CONSTRUCTIBILITY AGAINST LANDED DATA:
  Cases 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 8   constructible TODAY on MapPLUTO + PLUTO + footprints + the CMBS
                           geocode book. Case 5 has a measured instance already.
  Case 4                   constructible, but confirm the geocode book actually contains
                           comma-separated multi-street address fields before committing to
                           it — if it does not, the case may live in HUD or the GSE corpora
                           instead.
  Case 7                   constructible for geometry; the property-side truth may need the
                           loan documents.
  Case 9                   partially blocked on the version archive. Record the stop.

EACH CASE SHOULD BE FINDABLE BY QUERY, NOT BY MEMORY. Write the selector that identifies
instances of each shape and record it with the case, so the corpus can be regenerated and
expanded rather than being seven hand-picked rows. Runtime-selected subjects with a
recorded selection rule, per the proof-class discipline in AGENTS.md.

comments.text:
REAL CASE INSTANCES FOUND IN LANDED NYC DATA 2026-08-14, via Loom against
WRGL_EDGAR_CMBS_GEOCODES__STRUCTURED and NYC_DCP_MAPPLUTO_HOT. These are actual rows, not
hypotheticals. Selection was by query pattern, so each is regenerable.

=========================================================================
POPULATION COUNTS — MULTI-ADDRESS SHAPES ARE ~7-8% OF THE NYC BOOK, NOT A TAIL
=========================================================================
Five-borough CMBS geocode rows (county_fips 36005/36047/36061/36081/36085):

  hyphen in parsed NUMBER      756 rows   -- and the sample is ENTIRELY Queens (36081)
  '/' in PROPERTY_ADDRESS      297 rows
  ',' in PROPERTY_ADDRESS      129 rows
  '&' in PROPERTY_ADDRESS       93 rows
  ' AND ' in PROPERTY_ADDRESS   44 rows
  ' A/K/A ' in PROPERTY_ADDRESS  9 rows

CONFIRMS bd-1zph's QUEENS FINDING WITH A COUNT. The 756 hyphenated NUMBER rows are Queens
GRID addresses (47-27 Little Neck Pkwy), NOT ranges. A range-parsing rule applied to that
population produces garbage on 756 rows. The RANGE population lives in PROPERTY_ADDRESS
under a different set of separators entirely.

THE SEPARATOR VOCABULARY IS SIX PATTERNS, NOT ONE. bd-1zph currently scopes normalization
and ranges. It does not scope multi-address FIELDS at all. Required separators observed in
the wild: '/', ',', '&', ' AND ', ' A/K/A ', and bare whitespace
("54-40   54-44 Little Neck Parkway").

=========================================================================
CASE 2 + CASE 3 + THE SILENT-ERROR POPULATION, ALL IN ONE PROPERTY
"241/249 West 74th Street" -- THE SINGLE BEST CASE IN THE CORPUS
=========================================================================
This one property produces TWO geocode rows that disagree, and both are wrong in
different, instructive ways.

  ROW A   lat 40.7777640  lon -73.9755480   accuracy_type = range_interpolation
          parsed NUMBER 241, STREET "W 74th St"
          NO MapPLUTO LOT CONTAINS IT. The point is in the roadbed.
          Nearest lot is 8.4 m away: BBL 1011260038, "10 WEST 74 STREET",
          BLDGCLASS D1, LOTAREA 10,217, BLDGAREA 71,890, NUMBLDGS 1, YEARBUILT 1941.
          23 LOTS WITHIN 50 METRES.

  ROW B   lat 40.7615050  lon -73.9859030   accuracy_type = ROOFTOP
          parsed NUMBER 241, STREET "W 49th St"   <-- WRONG STREET
          A 74 -> 49 transposition. The point is roughly 25 blocks from the property,
          AT THE HIGHEST CONFIDENCE TIER.

WHAT THIS ONE ROW PAIR PROVES, WITH RECEIPTS:
1. SNAP-TO-NEAREST IS CATASTROPHIC, DEMONSTRATED RATHER THAN ASSERTED. OC-0048 argues
   "on a narrow Manhattan block the nearest lot is frequently across the street." Here the
   nearest lot is 8.4 m away and is 10 WEST 74 STREET -- a different building on a
   different part of the block from 241/249. With 23 lots inside 50 m, proximity alone is
   nearly uninformative.
2. THE ROOFTOP TIER IS NOT SAFE. bd-bmee names nearest_rooftop_match as the tier to
   distrust. This row is plain ROOFTOP and is 25 blocks wrong. The silent-error population
   is larger than the one tier previously identified, and any calibration keyed only on
   accuracy_type will miss it.
3. ONE PROPERTY, MULTIPLE INCONSISTENT GEOCODE ROWS. The row-to-point relation is not
   many-to-one; it is many-to-many AND INTERNALLY INCONSISTENT. Cross-row disagreement
   within a single property is itself a detectable signal and is currently unmodelled.
4. Address channel and geometry channel would DISAGREE on both rows. The correct output
   for both is abstention, which makes this the calibration case for bd-uilx's
   channel-agreement rule.

=========================================================================
CASE 6 -- N BUILDINGS TO ONE PARCEL, WITH THE ADDRESS-SET GAP ON TOP
"305 East 72nd Street A/K/A 301-305 East 72nd Street A/K/A 1392-1396 2nd Avenue
 A/K/A 1398-1402 2nd Avenue A/K/A 300-302 East 73rd Street"
=========================================================================
  geocode  lat 40.7688430  lon -73.9580550   accuracy_type = rooftop
           parsed NUMBER 305, STREET "E 72nd St"
  CONTAINED BY  BBL 1014477501
           MapPLUTO ADDRESS "305 EAST 72 STREET"
           BLDGCLASS RM (residential hotel), LOTAREA 37,800, BLDGAREA 194,949,
           NUMBLDGS 2, YEARBUILT 1961, UNITSTOTAL 178
           11 lots within 50 m

WHY IT IS VALUABLE:
1. FIVE ASSERTED ADDRESSES ACROSS THREE STREETS (E 72nd, 2nd Ave, E 73rd) RESOLVE TO ONE
   BBL. This is a through-block corner property.
2. MapPLUTO CARRIES EXACTLY ONE OF THE FIVE. Comparing the property's address against
   MapPLUTO's ADDRESS scores 4 of 5 as DISAGREEMENT when all five are correct. This is
   bd-1zph's measured address-set problem, on a specific named property, and it is the
   clearest justification for bd-35qg.
3. NUMBLDGS = 2 ON ONE LOT. The BBL is not the answer if only one of the two buildings is
   collateral. Needs the BBL-to-BIN bridge (landed, bd-397d) to go further -- which makes
   this the concrete instance of the false-merge risk in bd-1oy8.
4. It is ALSO a through-block property, which is the shape that broke the single-frontage
   interval assumption corrected on bd-2zdz.

=========================================================================
CASE 4 -- THE CHIMERA PARSE. A NEW FAILURE MODE, NOT PREVIOUSLY NAMED.
"199, 201, 203, 205 FIRST AVENUE AND 349 & 351 EAST 12TH STREET 197 1ST AVENUE
 A/K/A 351-353 EAST 12TH STREET, 199 1ST AVENUE, 201 1ST AVENUE, 203 1ST AVENUE,
 205 1ST AVENUE, 349 EAST 12TH STREET"
=========================================================================
  parsed NUMBER 199, parsed STREET "E 12th St", accuracy_type = range_interpolation

THE PARSER TOOK THE HOUSE NUMBER FROM ONE STREET AND THE STREET NAME FROM ANOTHER. 199 is
a First Avenue number; E 12th St is the cross street. The resulting parsed address
"199 E 12th St" DOES NOT APPEAR ANYWHERE IN THE SOURCE and may well exist as a real
address belonging to someone else.

This is distinct from "the parser picked the first of several addresses" -- it is a
SYNTHESIZED address that no source asserts. Neither bd-1zph nor bd-uilx models it.
REQUIRED: the address channel must be able to detect that a parsed address is not a member
of the asserted address set, and refuse rather than corroborate. Same shape seen on
"241/249 West 74th Street" -> "241 W 49th St".

Other confirmed instances of the same family:
  "280-290 Lafayette Street a/k/a 115 Crosby Street"  -> NUMBER null, STREET "Crosby St",
                                                         street_center (took the SECOND
                                                         address's street, dropped number)
  "129-139 NORTH 3RD STREET A/K/A 248-252 BEDFORD AVENUE A/K/A 195-205 BERRY STREET"
                                                      -> NUMBER 139, STREET "N 3rd St",
                                                         nearest_rooftop_match
  "47-19/47-27 a/k/a 47-27 Little Neck Parkway"       -> NUMBER 47-10 (appears in NO
                                                         source address), nearest_rooftop_match

=========================================================================
CASE 7 -- M PARCELS TO N BUILDINGS. THE HARDEST INSTANCE, AND IT NEVER GEOCODED.
"95-38, 95-40 to 95-44, 96-42 to 96-70 & 95-56 to 95-60 Queens Boulevard,
 63-73 to 63-79 Saunders Street, 94-14 to 94-24 and 95-11 to 95-19 63rd Drive"
=========================================================================
  parsed NUMBER null, parsed STREET null, accuracy_type = PLACE

Three streets, multiple ranges per street, Queens-grid hyphenates throughout, and it
degraded to a place centroid with nothing parsed.

THIS IS THE CASE THAT SHOULD BE UNDECIDABLE, and it is the required "genuinely
undecidable" member of the corpus. It combines every hard feature at once: multi-street,
multi-range, Queens grid convention, and no usable geocode.

IT ALSO EXPOSES A DENOMINATOR PROBLEM. Rows that degrade to accuracy_type = 'place' with
null NUMBER and STREET NEVER ENTER THE GEOMETRIC PIPELINE AT ALL. They are not part of the
95.49% hit-rate calculation in either direction -- they are invisible. bd-14co must count
and report them explicitly, because they are the population where the property is MOST
complex and the answer matters MOST. A coverage number that silently excludes the hardest
rows is the denominator dishonesty OC-0048 already forbids.

=========================================================================
CASE 5 CANDIDATES -- CORNER BUILDINGS, TWO ADDRESSES, ONE STRUCTURE
=========================================================================
Confirmed present; MapPLUTO pull still needed (the query response truncated before
returning them):
  "66 Crosby Street a/k/a 514 Broadway"                       rooftop, Manhattan
  "271 EAST 197TH STREET A/K/A 2825 BAINBRIDGE AVENUE"        rooftop, Bronx
  "57 PRINCE STREET A/K/A 273-279 LAFAYETTE STREET"           rooftop, Manhattan
  "305 East 24th Street a/k/a 420-438 Second Avenue"          rooftop, Manhattan
  "171 & 173 ELIZABETH STREET AND 14 SPRING STREET"           rooftop, Manhattan
Also confirmed from bd-1zph's earlier measurement:
  geocode "9 WEST FORDHAM ROAD" vs MapPLUTO "2167 GRAND CONCOURSE"

These are the cases where THE ADDRESS CHANNEL ACTIVELY MISLEADS -- two entirely different
addresses, same structure, and address disagreement must be allowed to LOSE to geometry.
Pair with case 4 (where address decides) to calibrate bd-uilx's agreement rule.

=========================================================================
STILL TO PULL FROM LANDED DATA
=========================================================================
- CASE 1 (clean rooftop, single lot, everything agrees). Trivial to select; needed as the
  ablation control.
- CASE 5 MapPLUTO lots for the five corner candidates above.
- CASE 8 (multi-containment): 237 Park Avenue, BBL 1012920026 and 1012920001. A mock
  exists; pull the real lot rows and confirm both ST_CONTAINS true.
- CASE 9 (multi-corpus shared parcel): requires joining CMBS geocodes to REIT Schedule III
  / HUD / GSE property rows on BBL. Confirm whether those corpora carry NYC rows with
  usable geometry before committing to this case.
- BBL-to-BIN expansion for 305 E 72nd (BBL 1014477501, NUMBLDGS 2) from the landed
  footprints file (bd-397d), to make case 6 a building-level case rather than a
  parcel-level one.

=========================================================================
WHEN THE REMAINING DATASETS LAND -- PULL THE SAME TILE FOR EACH CASE
=========================================================================
Each case above currently has only the CMBS assertion plus the MapPLUTO parcel layer. The
full tile requires the rest. For EVERY case in the corpus, pull the H3 r9 cell plus k-ring
1 and extract:

  [ ] OVERTURE MAPS -- building footprints and GERS ids. Gives the BUILDING level an
      identifier and a footprint independent of NYC's own data. Needed for cases 5, 6, 7.
  [ ] FEMA USA STRUCTURES -- footprints with OCCUPANCY. Occupancy is an independent
      property-type channel, which is the hard eliminative filter in assemblage mode
      (bd-2zdz). Needed for cases 3, 4, 7.
  [ ] MICROSOFT GLOBALML -- footprints with HEIGHTS. Height gives gross area, which feeds
      the assemblage subset-sum. NOTE: no stable ids, so geometry-and-attributes only,
      never an alias (bd-2cbs rule 4).
  [ ] FOURSQUARE OS PLACES -- POI level. This is where canon entity's EXISTING name
      machinery applies (bd-2cbs rule 3). Needed for case 6, where geometry cannot
      discriminate between buildings on one parcel and tenant/POI evidence must.
  [ ] NYC BUILDING FOOTPRINTS / BIN -- LANDED (bd-397d) but not yet pulled into any case.
      The BBL-to-BIN bridge. Highest priority of this list because it is already available
      and it is what turns case 6 from parcel-level into building-level.
  [ ] NYC PAD or per-BIN ADDRESSES -- NOT LANDED (bd-35qg). This is the address SET that
      makes case 6 scoreable rather than a manufactured disagreement, and it is the
      corroboration channel case 2 depends on. The 305 E 72nd case is the receipt for why
      this acquisition matters.
  [ ] DOB PERMITS + CERTIFICATES OF OCCUPANCY -- building lifecycle dates. Required for
      case 9 and for distinguishing demolition from coverage gap (bd-1oy8).
  [ ] MAPPLUTO VERSION ARCHIVE -- NOT LANDED (cmdrvl-curves bd-33t6, open). Only the
      current release exists, so case 9's temporal arc cannot be built yet. Record the
      stop rather than faking it.
  [ ] ACRIS -- LANDED (~100.76M rows). Not a tile layer, but the ADDRESS-INDEPENDENT
      GROUND TRUTH for adjudication. Use it to break the circularity: a recorded mortgage
      on a BBL matched to a known CMBS loan by amount and date gives a BBL for that loan
      without using the address channel at all.

comments.author: Zac
comments.text:
CORRECTION 2026-08-14 — THE GEOCODE TABLE'S GRAIN, AND WHY "241/249 WEST 74TH STREET" HAS
TWO ROWS. Operator questioned the earlier claim; the earlier claim was wrong about the
mechanism.

WHAT I SAID: "one property, two geocode rows that disagree — the row-to-point relation is
many-to-many AND INTERNALLY INCONSISTENT," framed as a single geocoder behaving
inconsistently.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE (verified against the table): the two rows are the output of TWO
DIFFERENT GEOCODING SERVICES run at different times. The ETL APPENDS results rather than
upserting them.

  GRAIN: PROPERTY_NAME + PROPERTY_ADDRESS + PROPERTY_CITY + PROPERTY_STATE + SOURCE + ASOF
  There is NO deal, loan, or property identifier column in this table AT ALL.

THREE CONSEQUENCES, ALL MORE USEFUL THAN THE CLAIM THEY REPLACE:

1. THE ROW COUNT IS NOT A PROPERTY COUNT. 68,603 rows nationally and 6,682 in the five
   boroughs are property x SOURCE x ASOF, not properties. The previously observed
   6,682 rows / 6,255 distinct points gap is partly this, not solely multi-lot fan-out.
   EVERY DENOMINATOR IN bd-14co AND bd-bmee MUST DEDUPLICATE TO A DECLARED GRAIN FIRST and
   state which grain it used. A coverage or precision rate computed over appended
   geocoder outputs is not a rate over the book.

2. THE TABLE CANNOT BE ATTRIBUTED TO A DEAL ON ITS OWN. With no loan or deal identifier,
   this table cannot answer "which CMBS position does this resolution belong to." bd-bmee's
   scored set, and the whole false-merge analysis in bd-1oy8 (which turns on positions from
   DIFFERENT corpora sharing a parcel), require joining upstream to a table that carries
   deal identifiers. IDENTIFY THAT UPSTREAM TABLE BEFORE THE SCORED SET IS BUILT — this is
   a prerequisite nobody had noticed.

3. INDEPENDENT GEOCODERS DISAGREEING IS BETTER EVIDENCE THAN ONE GEOCODER WAVERING.
   The finding survives and gets stronger. Two INDEPENDENT services producing points ~25
   blocks apart for the same asserted address is a strong, free disagreement signal, and it
   is exactly what the tile can adjudicate (see the geocode-plausibility bead). The usual
   remedies — take the highest ACCURACY_SCORE, the most recent ASOF, or a preferred SOURCE
   — all pick a winner WITHOUT EVIDENCE. Canon can do better by asking the tile which point
   its own neighbourhood supports.

WHAT SURVIVES UNCHANGED FROM THE ORIGINAL FINDING: one of the two points is ROOFTOP tier
and parses to "241 W 49th St" against a source address of "241/249 West 74th Street" — a
confident, high-tier, ~25-block error. The silent-error population is still larger than the
single nearest_rooftop_match tier bd-bmee identified, and calibration keyed only on
accuracy_type still misses it.

comments.author: Zac
comments.text:
CORRECTION 2026-08-14 (SECOND) — "COMPETING GEOCODING SERVICES" WAS NOT ESTABLISHED. IT
CAME FROM AN LLM INTERPRETATION, NOT FROM THE DATA. Operator caught it.

WHAT THE BEAD SAID: that the geocode table carries points from "SEVERAL candidate points
from INDEPENDENT services," and that their independence is what makes cross-source
disagreement valuable evidence.

THE PROVENANCE OF THAT CLAIM: Loom asserted "the ETL pipeline runs multiple geocoding
services (NYC and Census TIGER)." I did not verify it before writing it down. OC-0048
states plainly that the CMBS geocodes come from GEOCODIO — a single service — and records
a frozen Geocodio account (br-1zo6) as the backfill blocker.

THE LITERAL VALUES, NOW VERIFIED, for the two "241/249 West 74th Street" rows:
                   ROW 1                                          ROW 2
  SOURCE           "TIGER/Line(R) dataset from the US Census      "City of New York"
                    Bureau"
  ASOF             2025-01-01                                     2026-08-01
  CENSUS_YEAR      2024                                           2025
  PROPERTY_NAME    "Alfie Arms Corp."   (trailing period)         "Alfie Arms Corp"
  LAT/LON          40.7777640 / -73.9755480                       40.7615050 / -73.9859030
  ACCURACY_TYPE    range_interpolation                            rooftop
  ACCURACY_SCORE   1.00                                           0.92
  STREET           "W 74th St"                                    "W 49th St"

MOST LIKELY READING, STILL UNVERIFIED AND FLAGGED AS SUCH: those SOURCE strings are
GEOCODIO'S UNDERLYING-ADDRESS-DATASET ATTRIBUTION, not separate vendors. Geocodio returns a
per-result `source` naming the dataset that produced the match, and "TIGER/Line(R) dataset
from the US Census Bureau" is one of its stock strings. One service, two runs, different
underlying datasets matched.
DO NOT HARDEN THIS EITHER. Verify against Geocodio's documentation. It is the same class of
unverified-vendor-semantics problem bd-bmee already flags for accuracy_type ("asserted from
general knowledge, NOT verified against their documentation"), and both should be settled
in the same pass.

THE ACTUALLY VERIFIED AND MORE USEFUL FINDING — A TRAILING PERIOD DUPLICATES THE ROW.
PROPERTY_NAME is part of the table's grain. "Alfie Arms Corp." and "Alfie Arms Corp"
differ by ONE PUNCTUATION MARK, and that is what makes this two rows rather than one. Two
upstream records naming the same property slightly differently, geocoded 19 months apart,
landing 1.8 km apart.
This is a NAME-NORMALIZATION problem sitting upstream of the geo problem — and it is
squarely what canon entity's existing machinery is for (bd-2cbs rule 3). Deduplicating the
book by normalized property name BEFORE geo runs is cheap, uses shipped capability, and
directly shrinks the denominators bd-14co has to report. Add it to the corpus as its own
observation.

ALSO VERIFIED AND WORTH KEEPING: ACCURACY_SCORE and ACCURACY_TYPE DISAGREE about which row
to trust. Score says row 1 (1.00 vs 0.92); tier says row 2 (rooftop beats
range_interpolation). The tier — the field every convention trusts, and the one bd-bmee's
tier analysis is built on — points at the WRONG row. Neither field alone is a safe selector.

WHAT SURVIVES IN THIS BEAD, UNCHANGED AND STILL THE POINT:
The capability does not depend on WHY multiple rows exist. Whatever the mechanism —
separate vendors, one vendor across vintages, or duplicate upstream records — a property
can carry SEVERAL candidate points that disagree, and THE TILE CAN ADJUDICATE BETWEEN THEM
WITH EVIDENCE where accuracy_score, accuracy_type, most-recent-asof and preferred-source
all pick a winner without any. The 241/249 proof case stands exactly as written: the tile at
the West 49th point contains no West 74th Street and refutes it; the tile at the West 74th
point supports it.

REQUIRED EDIT: strike "independent services" from the adjudication section and replace with
"multiple candidate points for one property, whatever their provenance." Do not claim
independence as a property of the evidence until the mechanism is verified — independent
sources disagreeing IS stronger evidence than one source varying, but that strength has to
be earned by verification, not assumed.

PROCESS NOTE FOR THIS CORPUS: two claims in this session came from Loom's prose
interpretation rather than from returned values, and both were wrong. When building the
worked-case corpus (bd-tccn), TAKE LITERAL COLUMN VALUES AND RECORD THE QUERY. Prose
summaries from any LLM tool are a lead to verify, never a finding to cite. This matters
more here than usual because the corpus is meant to be the thing everything else is
designed against.

comments.text:
VERIFIED FACTS FROM STRUCTURED TOOL OUTPUT 2026-08-14. Method: `cmdrvl --json orchestrator
query --tenant salt --raw`, reading `.data.response.tool_responses[].structuredContent`
rather than Loom's prose answer. The underlying tool is `data__edgar_data_run_query`, which
returns the literal SQL it ran plus `{ok, columns, rows}` or `{ok:false, error}`. Every
fact below is a literal returned value.

THIS METHOD CHANGE IS THE FINDING THAT MATTERS MOST. Three claims earlier in this session
came from Loom's prose and were wrong. The structured path caught the third one
immediately, and the skill documentation already prescribed it ("prefer
tool_responses[*].structuredContent from --raw over prose"). ALL CORPUS EXTRACTS MUST USE
THE STRUCTURED PATH AND RECORD THE EMITTED SQL.

=========================================================================
1. THE LANDED MapPLUTO TABLE PROJECTS A SUBSET OF FIELDS. `UNITSTOTAL` DOES NOT EXIST.
=========================================================================
A prior extract reported "UNITSTOTAL 178" for BBL 1014477501. The structured output shows
that query FAILED: `invalid identifier 'UNITSTOTAL'`. The value was fabricated in prose.

LITERAL COLUMN LIST of EDGAR_DB.SOURCE.NYC_DCP_MAPPLUTO_HOT:
  RELEASE, RELEASE_DT, VARIANT, SOURCE_ROW_NUMBER, VALID_FROM_RELEASE_DT,
  VALID_TO_RELEASE_DT, IS_CURRENT_RELEASE, COUNTRY, STATE, BOROUGH_PARTITION, OBJECTID,
  BOROUGH, BLOCK, LOT, BBL, ADDRESS, BLDGCLASS, LANDUSE, YEARBUILT, LOTAREA, BLDGAREA,
  NUMBLDGS, NUMFLOORS, OWNERNAME, PLUTOMAPID, GEOM_GEOG, CENTROID_GEOG, CENTROID_LON,
  CENTROID_LAT, BBOX_XMIN, BBOX_YMIN, BBOX_XMAX, BBOX_YMAX, H3_R7, H3_R8, GEOM_CRS,
  SOURCE_GEOM_CRS, SOURCE_CHANNEL, SOURCE_FILENAME, ROW_PAYLOAD, LOADED_AT

CONSEQUENCES:
- MapPLUTO publishes roughly ninety fields; the landed table projects about twenty and puts
  the remainder in ROW_PAYLOAD. Anything not projected requires digging into ROW_PAYLOAD,
  which is a different access pattern and a different cost.
- THE SIX-FIELD CLIENT CONTRACT IS SATISFIED BY PROJECTED COLUMNS, which is good news:
  building size -> BLDGAREA, year built -> YEARBUILT, property type -> BLDGCLASS + LANDUSE.
  No ROW_PAYLOAD dig needed for the core cascade.
- UNIT COUNTS (UnitsTotal, UnitsRes) ARE NOT PROJECTED. Assemblage subset-sum for
  multifamily (case 7) may want them. Confirm they exist in ROW_PAYLOAD before designing
  around them.

=========================================================================
2. BBL IS STORED AS A STRING WITH A TRAILING ".0" AND IS NOT JOIN-READY.
=========================================================================
Literal returned value: "BBL": "1014477501.0"

This is a direct problem for canon. Core lookup is EXACT BYTE MATCH AFTER ASCII-TRIM, so
"1014477501" would NOT resolve against "1014477501.0". Any registry built from this column
without normalization silently fails to match the identifier every other NYC source uses,
and every downstream join against ACRIS, PLUTO, or the footprints file has the same
exposure.
REQUIRED: BBL normalization is a declared, versioned step in the ingest, not an incidental
cast. It belongs in the geo profile's normalization vocabulary alongside the geometry
canonicalization, and it needs a negative test.

=========================================================================
3. CASE 6 IS A CONDO, AND THE CONDO TRAP IS LIVE IN IT.
=========================================================================
Literal rows for BBL prefix 10144775:

  BBL 1014477501.0  "305 EAST 72 STREET"  BLDGCLASS RM  LOTAREA 37,800
                    BLDGAREA 194,949  NUMBLDGS 2  NUMFLOORS 17  YEARBUILT 1961
                    OWNERNAME "305/72 CONDOMINIUM"
  BBL 1014477502.0  "1355 1 AVENUE"       BLDGCLASS RM  LOTAREA  5,100
                    BLDGAREA 102,719  NUMBLDGS 1  NUMFLOORS 31  YEARBUILT 2009
                    OWNERNAME "UNAVAILABLE OWNER"

FOUR THINGS THIS ESTABLISHES:
a) OWNERNAME "305/72 CONDOMINIUM" and the 75xx lot range confirm these are CONDO BILLING
   BBLs. The condo trap named in OC-0048 and measured in the multi-lot fan-out is present
   in the very property picked to illustrate a different case.
b) A PRIOR CLAIM IS CORRECTED. I wrote that five asserted addresses "resolve to ONE BBL."
   Not established. At least two condo BBLs sit here with DIFFERENT street frontages —
   East 72 Street and 1 Avenue. The property's a/k/a set names E 72nd, 2nd Avenue and
   E 73rd; 1 Avenue is a fourth frontage not in that set. The containment test still has to
   be run properly.
c) YEARBUILT 1961 vs 2009 ON ADJACENT CONDO LOTS IS A LIVE REDEVELOPMENT SIGNAL — exactly
   the case hypothesised on bd-gs6n, that a large year-built spread on overlapping or
   adjacent footprints is a TEMPORAL finding rather than a match failure. It is real and it
   is in the first property examined closely.
d) NUMBLDGS 2 on one condo BBL. The building level is still needed and the BBL-to-BIN
   bridge (landed, bd-397d) is still the next pull.

=========================================================================
4. THE TABLE IS STRUCTURALLY BITEMPORAL ALREADY.
=========================================================================
RELEASE, RELEASE_DT, VALID_FROM_RELEASE_DT, VALID_TO_RELEASE_DT, IS_CURRENT_RELEASE are all
present. The landing contract (cmdrvl-curves bd-qbno) was built for multiple releases even
though OC-0048 records that only the current one is loaded.
CONSEQUENCE: the as-of machinery bd-12gh and bd-1oy8 need does not require a schema change,
only additional releases. Check `SELECT DISTINCT RELEASE, RELEASE_DT` before assuming case
9's temporal arc is blocked — cmdrvl-curves bd-33t6 may be closer to done than the outcome
document states.

=========================================================================
5. REPROJECTION PROVENANCE IS ALREADY RECORDED. THIS DIRECTLY SERVES bd-3nc7.
=========================================================================
GEOM_CRS and SOURCE_GEOM_CRS are projected columns. So the EPSG:2263 -> WGS84 transform
that the predicate-regime bead has to reason about is documented in the table itself rather
than needing archaeology. Read those columns first when starting bd-3nc7.

=========================================================================
6. H3_R7 AND H3_R8 ARE PRESENT. H3_R9 IS NOT.
=========================================================================
The epic's default tile is res-9. It is not precomputed. Canon computes it itself, which is
what bd-2b9d already requires for a separate reason — the Snowflake H3 helpers returned
malformed boundaries and a bad k-ring (edgar-elt br-2wir). Both reasons now point the same
way: compute r9 in canon with a vetted Rust H3 library, and treat the warehouse H3 columns
as a coarse prefilter at most.

=========================================================================
7. GEOCODIO SOURCE SEMANTICS — CONFIRMED BY OPERATOR.
=========================================================================
Geocodio reports the underlying address dataset that produced each match. So SOURCE values
like "TIGER/Line(R) dataset from the US Census Bureau" and "City of New York" are
per-result attribution from ONE service, not competing vendors — and MULTIPLE SOURCED
GEOCODES PER PROPERTY ARE EXPECTED AND NORMAL.
This VINDICATES the capability in bd-1a12 while keeping the retraction of the mechanism.
SOURCE becomes usable EVIDENCE: a local authoritative dataset and a national interpolated
one carry different reliability.
BUT NOTE THE COUNTEREXAMPLE ALREADY IN HAND: on "241/249 West 74th Street" the
"City of New York" sourced row is the WRONG one (W 49th St, rooftop, score 0.92) and the
TIGER/Line row is right (W 74th St, range_interpolation, score 1.00). So SOURCE is not a
safe selector either, any more than ACCURACY_TYPE or ACCURACY_SCORE are. Three fields, none
individually decisive, all disagreeing — which is precisely the argument for letting the
tile adjudicate.

comments.text:
TILE PRE-STITCHING IS ALREADY UNDER WAY IN cmdrvl-curves, LANDING NOW 2026-08-14. Verified
by reading the in-progress beads. This confirms the pre-resolved-tile architecture and
supplies hard facts that change several canon geo assumptions.

== WHAT IS ACTUALLY LANDING ==

  cmdrvl-curves bd-30ho   OVERTURE MAPS, release 2026-07-22.0. Themes buildings,
                          building_parts, PLACES, addresses, divisions. Snowflake DDL
                          APPLIED (OVERTURE_MAPS_FEATURES_HOT / _EXT /
                          OVERTURE_MAPS_FEATURE_H3_COVERAGE plus 14 per-type views);
                          manifest scan running, 0 rows landed yet.
  cmdrvl-curves bd-1ssr   FEMA USA STRUCTURES, 135,321,228 features nationally. National
                          landing IN PROGRESS; DC / AK / AL complete, AR running.
                          FEMA_USA_STRUCTURES_HOT loaded and read back (DC = 64,701 rows).
  cmdrvl-curves bd-3fyv   MICROSOFT GLOBALML FOOTPRINTS, release 2026-07-24. Landing IN
                          PROGRESS: 179 of 2,415 US files, 5,219,860 rows at 14:45Z.
  cmdrvl-curves bd-11uu   HUD USPS ADDRESS VACANCIES -- **BLOCKED**, and not a tile source.
                          HUD restricts it to registered governmental/non-profit users and
                          the sublicense forbids selling, licensing or distributing the
                          data. DO NOT PLAN ANY CANON GEO CAPABILITY ON IT.

NOTE ON "FOURSQUARE OS PLACES": it arrives as OVERTURE'S PLACES THEME, not a separate
Foursquare landing. That is the POI level in bd-2cbs, and it is in the same table family as
Overture buildings.

== FINDING 1: THE LANDED H3 GRAIN IS r4 / r7 / r8. THERE IS NO r9. ==
All three sources partition by h3_r4 and carry H3_R7 and H3_R8 columns. The epic's default
tile is res-9 and it is NOT precomputed anywhere.

AND THERE IS A CONVENIENT COINCIDENCE WORTH DELIBERATELY EXPLOITING: an r8 cell is
approximately 0.737 km2 -- which is almost exactly the area the epic specifies for its WORK
UNIT (an r9 cell plus k-ring 1 = 7 cells = 0.737 km2). So the already-landed H3_R8 column is
essentially the intended work-unit size.
ACTION FOR bd-2b9d: reconsider r9-plus-k-ring versus r8-plus-k-ring as the work unit, now
that r8 is precomputed across every source and r9 is not. This does not change the
requirement to compute cells in canon with a vetted Rust library -- the Snowflake H3 helper
defects (edgar-elt br-2wir) still stand -- but it does mean the warehouse can prefilter at
r8 for free, and the resolution decision now has a third input alongside node count and
human legibility.

== FINDING 2: POLYGON-TO-CELLS RETURNS EMPTY FOR SMALL BUILDINGS. LIVE, MEASURED. ==
From bd-3fyv: "H3_POLYGON_TO_CELLS alone inserted only 116 coverage rows for 354,804 hot
rows because small buildings often contain no H3 r8 cell centroid." Fixed there by using a
guaranteed CENTROID_H3_R8 plus H3_TRY_POLYGON_TO_CELLS.

THIS IS DIRECTLY THE MEMBERSHIP QUESTION bd-10s2 AND bd-2b9d SPECIFY. At r8 or r9 a
building is much smaller than a cell, so "which cells does this polygon cover" is
degenerate: the standard polygon-to-cells contract returns cells whose CENTRES fall inside
the polygon, and for a building that set is almost always EMPTY.
CONSEQUENCE: membership must be CENTROID-ANCHORED with polygon coverage as a supplement for
the large-feature case (parcels, campuses, complexes), NOT the other way round. My earlier
recommendation on bd-10s2 -- "full intersection cover for membership plus a single
deterministic anchor cell" -- is right in intent but inverted in emphasis, and applying it
naively with polygon_to_cells would have silently produced empty membership for nearly every
building. Correct it there.

== FINDING 3: OUR OWN SOURCES CARRY LICENSE OBLIGATIONS. bd-pq5w IS SCOPED TOO NARROWLY. ==
I framed license containment entirely around the CLIENT's licensed parcel layer. The landed
research shows OUR side has obligations too, and they differ per source:
    Overture buildings, divisions      ODbL-1.0            <-- SHARE-ALIKE
    Overture places                    per-source mix of CDLA-Permissive-2.0, Apache-2.0,
                                       CC0-1.0; source license must be retained
    Overture addresses                 source-specific, incl. NAD Access and Usage License
    FEMA USA Structures                CC-BY-4.0, attribution to ORNL and FEMA Geospatial
                                       Response Office REQUIRED
    Microsoft GlobalML                 CDLA-Permissive-2.0 current release; older vintages
                                       need per-release revalidation
bd-30ho states plainly: "License segmentation by source array is REQUIRED before any derived
product ships. Treat as a build-time gate, not a later cleanup."

ODbL SHARE-ALIKE IS THE COMMERCIAL ISSUE AND IT NEEDS AN OPERATOR DECISION, NOT AN
ENGINEERING ONE. A tile is a derived product. If it mixes ODbL Overture buildings with
everything else, the derived tile may inherit share-alike obligations that are
incompatible with a paid distribution model. Options to evaluate deliberately:
  (a) segregate ODbL-derived features into a separately-licensed layer of the tile, with
      the license class carried per feature -- note OVERTURE_MAPS_FEATURES_EXT ALREADY HAS
      LICENSE_CLASS AND LICENSE_TERMS COLUMNS, so the substrate for this exists;
  (b) build the commercial tile from the permissive sources only (FEMA CC-BY, Microsoft
      CDLA) and treat Overture as an internal enrichment;
  (c) accept share-alike and publish the tile openly.
REQUIRED IN bd-pq5w AND bd-1uld: license class per FEATURE in the tile artifact, and a
declared per-tile license posture that composes our obligations with the client's. The
artifact license boundary now has TWO directions, not one.

== FINDING 4: THE ATTRIBUTE CHANNELS FOR bd-272d ARE REAL, AND ONE IS MODELLED ==
Attribute anchoring needs class, size, floors, year. What is actually arriving:
    FEMA        OCC_CLS, PRIM_OCC (occupancy class), SQFEET, PROP_ADDR, UUID, BUILD_ID
    Overture    building class, height, num_floors, GERS id
    Microsoft   height (subset only), confidence, NO ID
    MapPLUTO    BLDGCLASS, LANDUSE, BLDGAREA, LOTAREA, NUMBLDGS, NUMFLOORS, YEARBUILT
So the six-field client contract has a counterpart on the tile side for every field except
YEAR BUILT, which only MapPLUTO supplies -- meaning year-built anchoring works in NYC and
degrades outside it until a national year source exists. Record that as a known national
limitation rather than discovering it later.

CRITICAL: FEMA OCCUPANCY IS MODELLED, NOT SURVEYED. bd-1ssr requires a provenance flag
"so downstream never treats it as surveyed." Attribute anchoring MUST carry that flag into
the evidence and weight modelled attributes below observed ones. A modelled occupancy class
driving a hard eliminative filter (bd-2zdz's assemblage type filter) would be a silent error
generator -- the filter is HARD, so a wrong modelled class removes the correct candidate
before anything is scored. Use modelled occupancy as SUPPORT evidence, never as a hard
filter, unless corroborated.

== FINDING 5: NO STABLE ID CONFIRMED FOR TWO SOURCES ==
Microsoft has no id at all -- bd-3fyv derives "a deterministic feature hash because no
stable id." Overture ADDRESSES are alpha with no stable GERS id either. This confirms
bd-2cbs rule 4 (alias-less participants) and extends it: the alias-less set is Microsoft
footprints AND Overture addresses, not just Microsoft.
A derived feature hash is NOT an alias and must not be minted into a registry -- it will
change whenever the geometry changes, which violates the tile identifier stability contract
in bd-12gh.

== FINDING 6: OVERTURE ADDRESSES CANNOT BE THE ADDRESS-SET SOURCE ==
bd-30ho: "Addresses theme is ALPHA -- do not build a contract against it yet," no stable
GERS id, multi-source licensing including NAD terms. US count 127,719,691.
So bd-35qg's address-set acquisition is NOT solved by Overture. NYC PAD or the per-BIN
addresses in the landed footprints file (bd-397d) remain the path, and the national story
stays open. Do not let the size of the Overture addresses count create false confidence.

== WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE WORKED-CASE CORPUS (bd-tccn) ==
The corpus can now stage its non-MapPLUTO pulls against REAL TABLE NAMES rather than
placeholders:
    EDGAR_DB.SOURCE.FEMA_USA_STRUCTURES_HOT              partially loaded (DC, AK, AL)
    EDGAR_DB.SOURCE.MICROSOFT_GLOBALML_BUILDING_FOOTPRINTS_HOT   partially loaded
    EDGAR_DB.SOURCE.OVERTURE_MAPS_FEATURES_HOT           DDL applied, 0 rows
    plus the *_FEATURE_H3_COVERAGE tables for each
NEW YORK IS NOT YET LOADED IN ANY OF THE THREE. FEMA is alphabetical by state and is at AR;
Microsoft is 179/2415 files; Overture has not started landing. So the full-tile version of
every case remains blocked, exactly as the corpus bead predicted -- but the blocker is now
a KNOWN COMPLETION DATE rather than an unlanded dataset, and the table names and column
shapes are already fixed enough to write the extraction queries against.

EXTRACTION QUERIES STAGED 2026-08-14 — scripts/geo_corpus/ in canon.

  00_discovery.sql       table/column confirmation, landing progress, MapPLUTO release
                         inventory, geocode grain, reprojection provenance
  01_case_selectors.sql  finds real instances of each case shape BY QUERY
  02_tile_assembly.sql   pulls every source at every level for one case's tile
  README.md              run order, landing status, the rules the queries encode

01_case_selectors.sql RUNS TODAY on the geocode book plus MapPLUTO. It covers all nine
cases, including the two headline rates bd-bmee needs (multi-lot distribution deduplicated
to distinct points, and the multi-assertion-per-BBL exposure that sizes the false-merge
risk). 02_tile_assembly.sql runs its MapPLUTO block today and returns empty for the
national sources until New York lands.

THREE RULES THE QUERIES ENCODE, EACH FROM A MISTAKE MADE IN THIS SESSION:
1. Take literal values and record the query. Read tool_responses[].structuredContent, not
   the answer markdown. Three claims this session came from LLM prose and all three were
   wrong.
2. Dedupe to a declared grain before computing any rate. The geocode table is
   property x SOURCE x ASOF with NO deal or loan identifier, so 6,682 rows are not 6,682
   properties and case 9 needs an upstream join that is not yet identified.
3. Never collapse a set with MAX / LIMIT 1 / first-returned. `within` returns a set.

TWO TECHNICAL DECISIONS RECORDED IN THE FILES SO THEY ARE NOT RE-LITIGATED:
- Tile extent is ST_DWITHIN in metres, NOT an H3 k-ring call. H3_R8 prunes partitions; it
  does not define the answer. Reason: edgar-elt br-2wir malformed boundaries and a k-ring
  listing a neighbour three times. Canon computes its own cells (bd-2b9d).
- Membership is centroid-anchored with polygon overlap as a supplement, because
  polygon-to-cells returns cells whose CENTRES fall inside the polygon and a building
  almost never contains an r8 cell centre (measured live on cmdrvl-curves bd-3fyv: 116
  coverage rows for 354,804 buildings).

02_tile_assembly.sql also emits the TILE DISCRIMINATING POWER query bd-272d needs — the
per-tile frequency of each class x area x year bucket, which is the exact denominator for
tile-relative rarity weighting. No global corpus statistics required; the tile bounds the
population.

ONE COLUMN NAME IS STILL UNCONFIRMED AND IT BLOCKS THE HIGHEST-VALUE AVAILABLE PULL: the
NYC building footprints / BBL-to-BIN table, landed per cmdrvl-curves bd-397d. Q6 in
00_discovery.sql resolves it. That table is what turns case 6 from a parcel-level case into
a building-level one, and unlike the national sources it is available right now.
